# Verification log

Before any specification was written, eighteen factual claims underpinning the plan were
each investigated twice against the source on disk — once by an engineer reading the code,
then again by a second engineer told to take a *different route* and to catch
over-confidence in the first. This is the raw record.

**Verdicts: 1 confirmed, 17 partially confirmed, 0 refuted.** No claim was outright wrong;
almost every one was imprecise in a way that changes an implementation detail, and several
were imprecise in ways that change a design decision. The corrections are the point of this
document — read them, not the verdicts.

> **Provenance note.** The workflow stage that would have written this document with its
> claim-by-claim headings died on a session limit, and the run journal does not preserve
> the mapping from each result back to its claim id. Rather than guess that mapping and
> publish a log whose only value is being trustworthy, each investigation below is
> reproduced **verbatim as returned**, ordered by verdict then by how much it corrected.
> Every file path and line number here was cited by an agent that read that file; spot-check
> before relying on any single one.

---

## Investigation 1 — `partially_confirmed`

Every endpoint named in the claim exists in the on-disk gigapipe tree and is registered exactly at the path given — so no path in the claim is invented. But the claim is incomplete and imprecise in ways that matter for a gateway written directly against it: it omits roughly two thirds of the actual route table (Datadog, Influx, Elastic, Zipkin ingest; the entire OTLP/gRPC receiver; most Loki/Pyroscope/Tempo read routes; ruler and common routes), it states no HTTP methods (several read routes are GET-only where Loki/Prometheus normally allow POST), and it lists `/loki/api/v1/patterns` unconditionally when that route only registers under `LOG_DRILLDOWN`. gigapipe is one gorilla/mux router shared by writer, reader, ruler and view, gated by `MODE`/`READONLY`, `LOG_DRILLDOWN`, `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED` and the `view` build tag. The full enumerated table with methods and conditionals is in the findings below.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- Incomplete on ingest. The full writer table (all POST unless noted) is: /loki/api/v1/push; /influx/api/v2/write; /cf/v1/insert; /api/v2/series (Datadog metrics); /api/v2/logs (Datadog logs); /v1/logs; /v1/metrics; GET /influx/api/v2/write/health; GET /influx/health; /v1/prom/remote/write; /api/v1/prom/remote/write; /prom/remote/write; /api/prom/remote/write; /api/prom/push; GET /prom/remote/write (probe, 200 OK); /{target}/_doc; /{target}/_create/{id} (POST and PUT); PUT /{target}/_doc/{id}; /_bulk; /{target}/_bulk; /tempo/spans; /tempo/api/push; /api/v2/spans; /v1/traces; /ingest; /v1development/profiles.
- The claim omits the OTLP/gRPC receiver entirely. All four OTLP signals (traces, logs, metrics, profiles) are also accepted over gRPC on the same port, dispatched by HTTP/2 + Content-Type: application/grpc*, mounted only when the writer boots. Tenant selection there is gRPC metadata x-ch-dsn / x-scope-meta / x-ttl-days rather than headers.
- '/api/prom/push' is a Prometheus remote-write alias in gigapipe (writer/router/prom.go:13 -> WriteStreamV2), NOT a Loki push alias. Sending a Loki JSON push body there will fail to parse.
- /loki/api/v1/patterns is conditional: it is registered only when DRILLDOWN_SETTINGS.LogDrilldown is true (env LOG_DRILLDOWN), together with /loki/api/v1/index/volume, /loki/api/v1/detected_labels and /loki/api/v1/detected_fields. The claim lists it as unconditionally available. LogDrilldown is a plain bool, so it is false unless LOG_DRILLDOWN or a config file turns it on.
- HTTP methods are not as a Loki/Prometheus client would assume. /loki/api/v1/query_range, /loki/api/v1/query, /loki/api/v1/tail and /loki/api/v1/index/stats are GET+OPTIONS only — no POST, so long LogQL queries cannot be sent in a body. /api/v1/label/{name}/values is GET+OPTIONS only. /api/v1/query, /api/v1/query_range, /api/v1/labels and /api/v1/series do accept POST.
- /loki/api/v1/tail is a WebSocket upgrade (gorilla/websocket), not a normal HTTP response — a plain fetch-based read client cannot consume it.
- /api/metrics/query_range is a Tempo TraceQL-metrics endpoint (alias of /tempo/api/metrics/query_range), not a Prometheus one, and it has a sibling /api/metrics/query (instant) the claim omits. Grouping it with the Prometheus read endpoints is misleading.
- /api/v1/query_exemplars exists but is wired to the metadata handler (reader/router/prometheus_labels.go:23 -> qrCtrl.Metadata) — it is a stub, not an exemplar API.
- The claim's Loki read list omits /loki/api/v1/query (instant), /loki/api/v1/label, /loki/api/v1/labels, /loki/api/v1/label/{name}/values and /loki/api/v1/series; its Prometheus list omits /api/v1/metadata and /api/v1/status/buildinfo.
- The claim omits the Pyroscope read surface: ten POST routes named by gRPC full-method paths (/querier.v1.QuerierService/... and /settings.v1.SettingsService/Get) plus GET /pyroscope/render and /pyroscope/render-diff.
- The claim omits the ruler routes (/loki/api/v1/rules*, /api/prom/rules*, /api/v1/rules*, /prometheus/api/v1/rules), which are conditional on QRYN_RULER_ENABLED and on MODE being all/unset, and the always-on common routes GET /ready, GET /config, GET /metrics, GET /api/status/buildinfo.
- The whole table is mode-gated: MODE=reader (or READONLY=true) drops every ingest route and the gRPC receiver; MODE=writer drops every read route, the ruler and the view; the ruler only exists at MODE=all/unset. A `view`-tagged build additionally registers a catch-all PathPrefix("/") static file server.
- Content types are not uniform. /v1/metrics accepts ONLY application/x-protobuf or application/json (400 'Content-Type not supported' otherwise); /v1/logs and /v1/traces accept any content type; /loki/api/v1/push takes JSON by default and snappy-framed protobuf under application/x-protobuf; /ingest accepts only multipart/form-data and binary/octet-stream; /v1development/profiles rejects application/json with 415. Success codes also differ: 204 for loki push, remote write and /v1/logs; 200 (proto ExportResponse) for /v1/traces and /v1/metrics; 202 for Zipkin spans; 200 '{}' for /ingest.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Root-level wildcard ingest routes (/{target}/_doc, /{target}/_create/{id}, /{target}/_doc/{id}, /{target}/_bulk) are registered on the same mux before all reader routes. They do not currently shadow any read route (the second segment is a literal _doc/_create/_bulk), but they mean the OpenPanel gateway must allowlist exact upstream paths — a prefix-proxy of '/' would expose an unauthenticated Elasticsearch-shaped ingest surface on any first path segment.
- GET /metrics on the same port exposes gigapipe's own Prometheus registry (shared/commonroutes/routes.go:13-18), including the per-tenant write-rate gauges pushed by StartPushStat (writer/plugin/utils.go:175-197). Since the gauge names derive from stat keys, this is a cross-tenant information leak if the port is ever reachable. It reinforces the plan's 'gigapipe is never exposed' decision and means the gateway must not forward /metrics, /ready or /config.
- gorilla/mux resolves by registration order, and /api/v1/metadata is registered twice (reader/router/prometheus_labels.go:22 wins over reader/router/misc.go:14). Any future OpenPanel-side patch or plugin that adds routes must respect reader.go:106-113 ordering — this is exactly the kind of silent shadowing the boot-order comment in main.go:344-354 warns about.
- The ruler's own file header states alerting endpoints are deliberately absent and gigapipe stores but never evaluates alerting rules (ruler/router/router.go:1-3). That independently confirms the plan's position that alert evaluation must live in OpenPanel's worker. Note the ruler DOES evaluate *recording* rules in-process (ruler/router/init.go:88-99 builds LogQL and PromQL managers and starts them), so if OpenPanel enables it, gigapipe will be writing back series on its own schedule.
- Per-request tenancy on the write path is the X-CH-DSN header (writer/controller/middleware.go:165), which selects a whole ClickHouse DSN, and there is no per-request database selection on the read path — consistent with the plan's premise, and worth restating: any header the client can set that reaches the writer is a tenancy control, so the gateway must strip X-CH-DSN, X-Scope-Meta and X-Ttl-Days from inbound requests, not just set them.
- Both /v1/metrics HTTP and OTLP/gRPC metrics report dropped data points via OTLP partial_success rather than an error status (writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:97-104, writer/grpc/metrics.go:37-45). A gateway that only checks the HTTP status will silently lose delta-temporality and invalid points; the plan's ingest metering should read RejectedDataPoints out of the response body.
- /v1/metrics and the OTLP/gRPC receiver are only days-old commits at HEAD (60e22ea, e7484e9). The plan should pin a gigapipe image by digest at or after these commits, since the metrics ingest path the whole P2 phase depends on does not exist in released qryn v3/v4 images.
- Unverified: the default value of DRILLDOWN_SETTINGS.LogDrilldown is defined in the external github.com/metrico/cloki-config module, which is not vendored on disk. I inferred 'false' from the Go zero value and the in-repo comment at cmd/gigapipe/main.go:239-240 ('Default is "false"'), not from reading cloki-config's source.
- Unverified: I did not confirm what the Tempo search/trace handlers accept as query parameters, nor whether the reader's Tempo routes honour any label matcher that could carry op_project_id. That matters for the P4 label-enforcement boundary on traces and should be verified separately.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's gateway and read-client design survives — every endpoint it names is real and at the stated path — but three things must change before code is written against this list. (1) The route table in the plan must be replaced with the full enumerated table above, with methods: writing a read client that POSTs LogQL to /loki/api/v1/query_range, or that expects /loki/api/v1/tail to be a normal HTTP response, will fail. (2) /loki/api/v1/patterns must be treated as a feature-flagged endpoint — the P3 logs surface either requires LOG_DRILLDOWN=true in the self-hosting compose template and gigapipe deployment docs, or must degrade gracefully when it 404s. (3) The security boundary is wider than the plan assumes: gigapipe additionally exposes Elastic-shaped root wildcard ingest, Datadog, Influx, Zipkin, an OTLP/gRPC receiver on the same port, /metrics with per-tenant gauges, and (if enabled) a ruler CRUD API. The gateway must be an explicit path+method allowlist that strips X-CH-DSN/X-Scope-Meta/X-Ttl-Days, not a reverse proxy of a prefix, and the deployment must run gigapipe on a private network with MODE deliberately chosen (MODE=all is required if the ruler is ever wanted; MODE=reader/READONLY silently removes every ingest route). Additionally, pin the gigapipe image at or after commit 60e22ea/e7484e9 — /v1/metrics and OTLP/gRPC do not exist in older builds — and prefer OTLP/gRPC or explicitly set Content-Type: application/x-protobuf on /v1/metrics, since that route rejects any other content type with a 400.

## Investigation 2 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived this from the runtime path, git history, and the gigapipe side rather than from the helper definitions, and I reach the same headline verdict as the first engineer: the numbered TS runner and the createDatabase/createTable/createMaterializedView helpers all exist as described, they branch on an explicit `isClustered` boolean (never on SELF_HOSTED), and `createDatabase` will emit `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS <anything>`. Their evidence is accurate — I spot-checked every line number they cited and found no fabrications. But two of their *corrections* are themselves overstated, and they missed the fact that settles the practical question: gigapipe creates its own ClickHouse database at boot (`ctrl/ctrl.go:17` → `ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:40-49` → `ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:47-61`, `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS`), so OpenPanel's migration runner does not need to create or populate a second database at all. Separately, the repo already contains a fully-qualified `db.table` migration (`4-add-sessions.ts:123,127` — `INSERT INTO openpanel.sessions ... FROM openpanel.events`), so "nothing in this repo does it" is false, and in the non-clustered path (the shipped default) `createTable({ name: 'gigapipe.foo' })` would in fact emit valid working DDL.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/code-migrations/migrate.ts:19-34, 36, 65-70, 76-84, 93-110` — Runner confirmed verbatim. `fs.readdirSync` filtered on `!Number.isNaN(Number.parseInt(file.split('-')[0]))` && `.endsWith('.ts')`, sorted by `aVersion - bVersion`. Ledger read at :36 `db.codeMigration.findMany()`. `if (!getIsSelfHosting())` at :65 gates only the 10s countdown. `runMigration` at :93-95 does `await import(...)` then `await migration.up()`; :96-107 upserts the filename unless `--dry`/`--no-record`; catch at :108-110 prints and `process.exit(1)`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/code-migrations/helpers.ts:19-33` — Confirmed exactly as quoted: `getIsCluster()` = `--cluster || CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER==='true' || ==='1'`; `getIsSelfHosting()` = `SELF_HOSTED === 'true' || !!process.env.SELF_HOSTED`; `getIsDry()`; `getShouldIgnoreRecord()`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:32-33, 37, 56, 68, 114, 174-187, 364, 412, 420` — Every line number the first engineer cited is correct. :32 CLUSTER_REPLICA_PATH contains the literal `/openpanel/`; :37 `chMigrationClient = createClient({ url: process.env.CLICKHOUSE_URL, request_timeout: 3600000, ... })`; :56 createDatabase; :68 createTable; :114 and :412 `Distributed('{cluster}', currentDatabase(), ...)`; :177 `SELECT name FROM system.tables WHERE database = 'openpanel'`; :364 createMaterializedView; :420 runClickhouseMigrationCommands. `grep -n SELF_HOSTED migration.ts` returns nothing — confirms migration.ts never reads it.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/code-migrations/4-add-sessions.ts:123-127` — THE FIRST ENGINEER MISSED THIS. A shipped migration already executes fully-qualified cross-database-style SQL through chMigrationClient: `INSERT INTO openpanel.sessions WITH unique_sessions AS (SELECT session_id, min(created_at) ... FROM openpanel.events ...)`. Their statement 'nothing in this repo does it — treat as unverified in-repo' is factually wrong. Qualified `db.table` naming demonstrably passes through the executor unchanged.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/ctrl.go:11-37 and /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:40-49 and /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:47-61` — THE DECISIVE FACT, ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FIRST REVIEW. gigapipe bootstraps its own database. `ctrl.Init` loops `config.Setting.DATABASE_DATA` calling `maintenance.InitDB`, which early-returns for name ''/'default', connects, then calls `InitDBTry` → `fmt.Sprintf("CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `%s` %s %s", dbName, onCluster, engine)` (with `ON CLUSTER` when ClusterName is set), then `SHOW CREATE DATABASE`, then `proj.upgrade` (maintenance.UpgradeAll) for the schema. So the second database and all gigapipe tables are created by gigapipe, not by packages/db/code-migrations.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:88-98` — Non-clustered createTable emits a single `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ${tableName} (...)` with tableName interpolated raw. **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's phrase 'clustered vs self-hosted deployments' is wrong, and I confirm the first engineer's correction independently: migration.ts contains zero references to SELF_HOSTED; every helper takes an explicit `isClustered: boolean`. git commit bcfb4f25 is the proof — getIsCluster() used to be `!getIsSelfHosting()` and was deliberately decoupled on 2025-10-23.
- The two cluster predicates have opposite defaults (getIsCluster false-by-default at helpers.ts:20-24; isClickhouseClustered true-by-default at client.ts:83-99). Confirmed, and bcfb4f25 shows this drift was introduced by that commit and never propagated to client.ts.
- AGAINST THE FIRST ENGINEER: their claim that 'nothing in this repo does' cross-database-qualified naming is false. packages/db/code-migrations/4-add-sessions.ts:123,127 runs `INSERT INTO openpanel.sessions ... FROM openpanel.events` through chMigrationClient. Qualified `db.table` names demonstrably work through this executor.
- AGAINST THE FIRST ENGINEER: 'the runner cannot usefully populate a second database as-is' is too strong. In the non-clustered branch — the shipped default for every self-hosted deployment, since CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER is set in neither compose template — createTable (migration.ts:88-98) interpolates `name` raw into `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ${tableName}`, so `name: 'gigapipe.foo'` emits valid DDL. Their objection is real only for the clustered branch, where `Distributed('{cluster}', currentDatabase(), gigapipe.foo_replicated, ...)` would be doubly wrong (wrong db argument, and a dotted identifier in the table argument).
- AGAINST THE FIRST ENGINEER: the ZooKeeper-collision claim is overstated. CLUSTER_REPLICA_PATH (migration.ts:32-33) ends in `/{table}`, a ClickHouse-side macro expanded to the table name — so two databases collide only if they contain identically-named tables. gigapipe's table names (samples_v3, time_series, tempo_traces) do not overlap OpenPanel's. The hardcoded `openpanel` path segment is semantically misleading, not automatically a collision.
- AGAINST THE FIRST ENGINEER: 'the guard nearly every ClickHouse migration uses' overstates getExistingTables' reach. Only 4 of 23 migrations call it (3, 13, 14, 20-cohort-summary-mv-sort-key); the two most recent ClickHouse migrations (18, 19) hand-write `WHERE database = currentDatabase()` instead. The hardcoded 'openpanel' at migration.ts:177 is a legacy helper, not a load-bearing convention.
- Refinement on rollback: five migrations DO export `down()` (13:136, 14:86, 15:248, 18:130, 19:218), but migrate.ts:94-95 calls only `up()` and exposes no flag to call `down()`. Dead code, not a rollback mechanism.
- `--dry` is not a runner-level dry run — confirmed independently. getIsDry() is consumed at migrate.ts:66 (skip countdown) and :96 (skip recording), and inside exactly two Postgres-only migrations (20-invite-project-access-levels.ts:69, 21-wind-down-onboarding-pointer.ts:24). Passing --dry to a ClickHouse migration still executes the DDL.
- Version prefixes are not unique — confirmed by directory listing: 20-cohort-summary-mv-sort-key.ts / 20-invite-project-access-levels.ts, and 21-backfill-cohort-summary-mvs.ts / 21-wind-down-onboarding-pointer.ts. The comparator returns 0 for ties, so order falls back to readdirSync order (V8 sort is stable, so it is deterministic per-filesystem but not specified by the code). There is no collision detection.
- One nuance neither the claim nor the first engineer stated precisely: chMigrationClient is built from the raw @clickhouse/client `createClient` re-exported at client.ts:13, so it inherits none of CLICKHOUSE_OPTIONS — notably not `distributed_product_mode: 'allow'` or `date_time_input_format: 'best_effort'` from getClickhouseSettings(). Any DDL needing those settings must pass them inline.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe creates its own ClickHouse database at startup: ctrl/ctrl.go:29-33 loops DATABASE_DATA calling maintenance.InitDB, which reaches ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:53 `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `<name>` [ON CLUSTER `<cluster>`]`, then runs maintenance.UpgradeAll for the schema. The plan should therefore NOT depend on packages/db/code-migrations to create or populate the gigapipe database — that would duplicate work gigapipe does itself and risk schema drift against gigapipe's own migration ledger. The load-bearing question is not 'can OpenPanel's runner create a second database' but 'does the ClickHouse user OpenPanel hands gigapipe hold CREATE DATABASE grant', which I could not verify (self-hosting/clickhouse/clickhouse-user-config.xml not inspected for grants; and the container sets CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1 at docker-compose.template.yml:96).
- gigapipe's InitDB early-returns when the database name is '' or 'default' (maintain.go:41-43), so CLICKHOUSE_DB must be set to a real non-default name (the plan's `gigapipe`) or no database is created at all.
- gigapipe's ON CLUSTER behavior is driven by its own ClusterName config, entirely independent of OpenPanel's getIsCluster()/isClickhouseClustered(). A clustered OpenPanel deployment would need that configured on the gigapipe side separately; nothing wires the two together.
- Because chMigrationClient is bound to the CLICKHOUSE_URL path database at module load (migration.ts:37), any OpenPanel-side read of gigapipe tables must use fully-qualified `gigapipe.<table>` names. Migration 4 proves qualified names work through this client; whether the CH user has SELECT grants on a second database is unverified.
- If the plan does add a migration for anything telemetry-adjacent, it must take a fresh unique numeric prefix (22+) since 20 and 21 are already doubled, and it must not rely on getExistingTables() (hardcoded to `database = 'openpanel'`) — the 18/19 pattern of an explicit `system.tables WHERE database = '<db>'` query is the correct model.
- createMaterializedView's placeholder rewrite is `query.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, ...)` (migration.ts:385-387); `\w` does not match `.`, so a `{gigapipe.samples_v3}` placeholder would silently not be substituted. Another reason not to route gigapipe DDL through these helpers.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim is safe to keep in the plan as a description of the runner's shape, but two plan positions need adjusting. First, drop any dependency on packages/db/code-migrations creating or populating the gigapipe database — gigapipe does it itself (ctrl/ctrl.go:17 → shared.go:53) and owns its own schema upgrades; duplicating that in an OpenPanel migration invites drift. Reframe the OpenPanel-side requirement as a grants/provisioning concern (does the CH user gigapipe connects as have CREATE DATABASE) plus, at most, a read-side grant so apps/api can query `gigapipe.<table>` with qualified names. Second, wherever the plan proposes conditional per-signal TTL via an OpenPanel migration against samples_v3, note it would be modifying a table gigapipe's own UpgradeAll manages, in a database the runner's helpers cannot idempotency-check (getExistingTables is pinned to 'openpanel') and whose clustered path the helpers emit incorrectly (Distributed uses currentDatabase()). Write that DDL by hand against chMigrationClient with an explicit `system.tables WHERE database = 'gigapipe'` guard, or better, drive it through gigapipe's own config. Also: do not plan to validate any of it with `--dry` (it still executes), do not plan on `down()` for rollback (the runner never calls it), give any new migration a unique prefix ≥22, and be aware that a cloud deployment with neither SELF_HOSTED nor CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER set will have runtime code assuming clustered tables that the migration runner did not create.

## Investigation 3 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived this from the runtime path (mount points → ReportChart → renderer index → tRPC procedure → engine) rather than from the type definitions, and checked tests, git history, the Prisma schema and the serialization layer. The first engineer's verdict is correct and their evidence holds: I independently confirmed every citation I checked, including the exact type at packages/validation/src/types.validation.ts:66-109, format.ts being the sole producer, index-based previous alignment, `count: undefined` at the top level, and all four gigapipe facts (15s floor/ceil, 11000-point cap, float-seconds + string values, Go-map label order, `s.Floats` only, `LookbackDelta: 0`). The type half of the claim is exact; the "maps on cleanly" half is overstated for the reasons they give. I found one piece of evidence that settles their most contested correction definitively — apps/start/src/components/chat/tool-results/chat-report-result.tsx already holds a `{report, data}` pair and throws `data` away, passing only `report` so ReportChart refetches — proving there is no data-injection prop anywhere in the tree. I also found five substantive gaps they missed: FinalChart is an explicitly deprecated shape with an unused successor type, it has zero test coverage, chartType is a Postgres enum behind a closed switch, there is no sub-minute interval anywhere in OpenPanel, and the engine already has a non-finite convention (collapse to 0, round to 2dp) that would silently destroy small gauge values.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/validation/src/types.validation.ts:66-109` — Verified verbatim. `PreviousValue`, `Metrics` (with `count: number | undefined` and optional `previous`), `IChartSerie = { id; names: string[]; event: { id?; name; breakdowns? }; metrics; data: {date;count;previous}[] }`, `FinalChart = { series: IChartSerie[]; metrics: Metrics }`. The claim's quoted type is character-for-character correct.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/engine/types.ts:57-84` — MISSED BY THE FIRST ENGINEER. A complete successor type `ChartResponse` is defined here — `{ series: [{id, name, data: [{date, value, previous?}], summary: {total, average, min, max, count?}, context?}], summary }`. `grep -rn ChartResponse` across both repos returns exactly two hits: this definition and the TODO in format.ts:16. It is entirely unused. So FinalChart is not the codebase's chosen contract; it is the one format.ts:15-16 labels `(backward compatible)` with `TODO: Migrate frontend to use cleaner ChartResponse format`. Decision 4 bets the metrics engine on a shape the team has already written down its intent to replace.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/start/src/components/chat/tool-results/chat-report-result.tsx:11-13,55,74-76` — SETTLES THE 'RENDERERS WORK UNCHANGED' QUESTION. The header comment says the tools 'all return `{ report, data }` we can plug into `<ReportChart>`'. But the code does `const report = value.report;` and then `<ReportChart report={report as unknown as IReportInput} lazy={false} .../>` — `data` is never passed. The one call site in the app that already has a computed FinalChart in hand discards it and lets ReportChart refetch through tRPC. There is no `data` prop on ReportChartProps (context.tsx:37-40) and no injection path anywhere. The first engineer's correction is not just right, it is stronger than they stated.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/start/src/components/report-chart/{line,area,metric,histogram,map}/index.tsx:16-17 and {bar,pie}/index.tsx:17` — Verified independently by reading all seven files. line/area/metric/histogram/map call `trpc.chart.chart.queryOptions({...chartInput, shareId})`; bar/pie call `trpc.chart.aggregate.queryOptions(...)`. `chartInput` comes from `useChartInput()` (context.tsx:58-64), which is `report` minus `visibleSeries`. Confirms the fetch layer is hard-wired.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/start/src/components/report-chart/index.tsx:20,41-60` — MISSED. `ReportChart` is a closed `switch (props.report.chartType)` over linear/bar/area/histogram/pie/map/metric/funnel/retention/conversion/sankey. Combined with the enum below, a metric report is not a data-shape change — it is a Postgres enum migration + a zod enum value + a new switch arm + a new renderer index component.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:377-397,415-423,425-448` — MISSED. `enum Interval { hour day month minute week }`, `enum ChartType {...}` and `enum Metric { sum average min max count }` are real Postgres enums, and `model Report` stores `interval Interval`, `chartType ChartType`, `metric Metric`, `unit String?`, `events Json`, `breakdowns Json`. The report persistence layer — which the public share path reads via `getReportById` (chart.ts:112-116) — is enum-constrained, not free-form JSON.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/constants/index.ts:236-242,281-295` — MISSED, AND MATERIAL FOR OBSERVABILITY. `intervals` is exactly `{minute, day, hour, week, month}`. There is no second-level or 15s bucket. gigapipe floors every range query to a 15s UTC boundary (prom_query_range.go:55-56) and Prometheus users routinely want 15s/30s steps. `isMinuteIntervalEnabledByRange` returns true ONLY for range '30min' or 'lastHour'. Note this gating is enforced in the FRONTEND ONLY — apps/start/src/components/report/reportSlice.ts:231-241 downgrades minute→hour and hour→day on range change, and ReportInterval.tsx:53,62 disables the options; `zTimeInterval` in zReportInput does not clamp, so the server would accept `interval:'minute'` with `range:'30d'`. Still, minute is the floor.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:4,57` — MISSED, AND IT STRENGTHENS THEIR POINT. `import superjson from 'superjson'` / `transformer: superjson`. The frontend type is `IChartData = RouterOutputs['chart']['chart']` (apps/start/src/trpc/client.ts:16), not `FinalChart` directly. Because the transformer is superjson rather than plain JSON, `count: undefined` and `previous: undefined` genuinely survive the wire as `undefined` instead of being stripped to absent keys — so the 'N/A' path in metric-card.tsx:64-66 really does fire on the client.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/engine/compute.ts:154-162 and formula.ts:177-186` — MISSED, AND IT BOTH SUPPORTS AND SHARPENS THEIR NaN CORRECTION. `evaluateFormula` returns `undefined` when the result is not a finite number (formula.ts:185-186), and compute.ts:158 then writes `count: result === undefined ? 0 : round(result, 2)`. So (a) the engine's established convention for non-finite is collapse-to-zero, which is exactly wrong for a gauge where 0 is a real value, and (b) it rounds to 2 decimals — a CPU fraction of 0.00123 or an error ratio of 0.004 becomes 0. Also a partial correction to their 'integer-biased' framing: `data[].count` already carries decimals today via the formula path (formula.test.ts:11 asserts `A/B` → 2.5), so float values per se are not novel; the loss is in `round(_,2)` and the axis, not the field type.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/common/src/math.ts:8-33` — Verified, with a precision note. `average` DOES guard non-finite — `isNumber(n) && !Number.isNaN(n) && Number.isFinite(n) && (includeZero || n !== 0)` — and does drop zeros by default. `sum`, `min` and `max` use bare `arr.filter(isNumber)` with no NaN/Infinity guard, and mathjs `isNumber` is a typeof check, so `typeof NaN === 'number'` passes. The first engineer scoped their NaN claim to `sum` specifically, which is exactly right; `average` is safe.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/engine/format.ts:101,139-148,153,159-165` — Verified independently. `id: slug(cs.id)`. `previous: previousSerie?.data[index] ? getPreviousMetric(item.count, previousSerie.data[index]?.count ?? null) : undefined` — previous alignment is BY ARRAY INDEX. `series.sort((a,b) => b.metrics.sum - a.metrics.sum)`. Global metrics literally `count: undefined as number | undefined` with no `previous` key. All four first-engineer claims confirmed.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/engine/fetch.ts:125 and plan.ts:26 and packages/common/src/slug.test.ts:5-9` — THE ID-COLLISION CLAIM, NOW WITH ITS CONSTRUCTION SITE. The first engineer asserted slug collisions but never cited where the id is built. It is `id: `${placeholder.id}-${grouped.name.join('-')}`` (fetch.ts:125), where `placeholder.id` is `` `${slug(event.name)}-${event.id ?? index}` `` (plan.ts:26); the aggregate path uses `` `${event.name}-${grouped.name.join('-')}-${i}` `` (engine/index.ts:200,311). format.ts:101 then slugs the whole thing. The id is therefore a function of the label VALUES. slug.test.ts asserts `slug('Hello || World, | Test å å ä ä') === 'hello-world-test-a-a-a-a'`, demonstrating lowercasing, punctuation stripping and pipe collapsing. `{path="/api/v1/Users"}` and `{path="/api/v1/users"}` collide to one recharts dataKey, React key and persisted visibleSeries id.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/common/src/group-by-labels.ts:61-72` — MISSED, AND IT BREAKS THE MOST COMMON METRICS QUERY. `return result.filter((group) => group.name.length > 0).map(...)` — a group with an EMPTY label array is dropped entirely. A fully-aggregated PromQL expression (`sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))`, the single most common observability query) returns a matrix entry with an empty label set. If the metrics engine reuses `groupByLabels` that series disappears; if it bypasses it, `slug('')` still yields an empty id. The zero-fill claim itself is confirmed at lines 67-70: `Array.from(timestamps).map(date => group.data.find(dp => dp.date === date) || {date, count: 0, total_count: 0})`, and `Array.from(timestamps)` preserves Set INSERTION order (SQL row order), not sorted order.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/start/src/hooks/use-rechart-data-model.ts:22-43` — Confirmed, and sharpened. `series[0]?.data.map(({date}) => ...)` then `if (item.date === date)`. Combined with format.ts:153 sorting series by `metrics.sum` DESCENDING, `series[0]` is the HIGHEST-SUM series — arbitrary with respect to which series has the widest time coverage. Under Prometheus lookback semantics every series shares the step grid but may start late or have holes, so a big late-starting series silently truncates the entire x-axis for every other series. That is worse than 'sparse'.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/engine/formula.test.ts, packages/common/src/slug.test.ts, packages/common/src/object.test.ts` — MISSED. `find packages/db/src/engine packages/common/src -name '*.test.ts'` returns exactly these three. There is NO test anywhere that exercises `format()`, `FinalChart`, `groupByLabels`, or the engine pipeline end to end. A metrics engine claiming to emit FinalChart has no executable contract to validate against — the 'same type' guarantee is compile-time only, and every runtime invariant the frontend relies on (dense grid, identical date strings, sorted-by-sum, stable ids) is unenforced.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/controller/prom_query_range.go:55-71,170-210,242-283` — All gigapipe claims verified independently. `req.Start = time.Unix(req.Start.Unix()/15*15, 0)`; `req.End = ceil(End/15)*15`; reject `Step <= 0`; reject `End.Sub(Start)/Step > 11000`. `writeResponse` (170-210) emits the envelope `{"status":"success","data":{"resultType":"<type>","result":[...]}}`. `writeMatrix` iterates `for name, value := range s.Metric.Map()` (Go map order, non-deterministic), writes `stream.WriteFloat64(float64(v.T)/1000)` then `stream.WriteString(strconv.FormatFloat(v.F,'f',-1,64))`, and loops only `s.Floats` — `s.Histograms` is never emitted, so native histograms silently vanish.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/router/prometheus_query_range.go:24-43` — Verified. `promql.NewEngine(promql.EngineOpts{... MaxSamples: <MetricsMaxSamples>, Timeout: 30s, LookbackDelta: 0, NoStepSubqueryIntervalFn: 1m, EnableAtModifier: true, EnableNegativeOffset: false})`. `LookbackDelta: 0` means the upstream default (5m) applies, which is precisely what makes a series emit no point where the last sample is older than 5m — the source of the holes.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/services/chart.service.ts:828-846 and packages/db/src/clickhouse/client.ts:108-123,344-356` — Verified. `sb.select.uc_state = 'uniqState(profile_id) as _uc_state'` and `uniqMerge(_uc_state) OVER (PARTITION BY label_1, ...) as total_count` — confirms `metrics.count` is whole-range unique profiles, deliberately non-summable. `getClickhouseSettings()` sets only `distributed_product_mode`, `date_time_input_format: 'best_effort'` and the join flag; `chQueryWithMeta` coerces to number ONLY when `meta?.type.includes('Int')`, so `date` stays a raw string. Small correction: the settings object spreads `...additionalSettings` parsed from the `CLICKHOUSE_SETTINGS` env JSON, so `date_time_output_format` is unset by default but IS operator-overridable.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/start/src/components/report-chart/common/report-table-utils.ts:419-435 and apps/start/src/components/report-chart/line/chart.tsx:286,316` — Verified, with a line-number correction. report-table-utils: `serieName: serie.names[0] ?? ''`, `breakdownValues: serie.names.slice(1)`, `count: serie.metrics.count ?? 0` — confirms both the names[0]/names[1..] positional semantics and the silent coercion of an undefined count to 0. The recharts `dataKey={`${serie.id}:count`}` is at line/chart.tsx:286 (and `:prev:count` at 316), not 275 as the first engineer wrote — substance unaffected.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's first half is exactly right and I confirm it; the second half ('a Prometheus matrix response maps onto it cleanly') is the overstated part, for the reasons the first engineer gave and five more below. I agree with their verdict of partially_confirmed.
- MISSED BY BOTH THE CLAIM AND THE FIRST ENGINEER: FinalChart is explicitly deprecated in-repo. format.ts:15-16 calls it '(backward compatible)' with 'TODO: Migrate frontend to use cleaner ChartResponse format', and that successor — `ChartResponse` at packages/db/src/engine/types.ts:60-84 — is fully written and referenced nowhere. Decision 4 is 'reuse the legacy shape the team intends to retire', which is still probably the right call for leverage but should be stated as such, not as 'reuse the chart contract'.
- MISSED: there is zero test coverage for format(), FinalChart, or groupByLabels. The only tests under packages/db/src/engine and packages/common/src are formula.test.ts, slug.test.ts and object.test.ts. The 'same type' guarantee is compile-time only; every runtime invariant the frontend depends on (dense identical date grid, sorted-by-sum, stable slugged ids) is unenforced. A metrics engine emitting FinalChart needs its own conformance tests written from scratch.
- MISSED, AND IT IS A SCHEMA COST NOT A TYPE COST: `chartType`, `interval` and `metric` are Postgres enums (schema.prisma:377-397, 415-423), and apps/start/src/components/report-chart/index.tsx:41-60 is a closed switch on `report.chartType`. Adding a metric report type is a Prisma migration plus a zod enum value plus a switch arm plus a renderer index component — none of which FinalChart buys you.
- MISSED, AND MATERIAL: OpenPanel has no sub-minute interval. `intervals` (packages/constants/index.ts:236-242) and `enum Interval` (schema.prisma:377-383) are exactly {minute, hour, day, week, month}. gigapipe floors every range query to a 15s UTC boundary. Sub-minute resolution — routine for observability — has no representation in IReportInput at all. Minute itself is UI-gated to ranges '30min'/'lastHour' (constants:281-285, reportSlice.ts:231-241), though I verified that gating is frontend-only and the server does not clamp.
- MISSED: `groupByLabels` drops any group with an empty label array (group-by-labels.ts:62). A fully-aggregated PromQL result such as `sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))` has an empty label set — the single most common observability query would vanish if the metrics engine reuses that helper, and would produce an empty slugged id even if it does not.
- SHARPENING their sparse-grid point: format.ts:153 sorts series by `metrics.sum` descending and use-rechart-data-model.ts:22 builds the x-axis from `series[0]`. So the axis is defined by whichever series has the largest sum, which is unrelated to which has the widest time coverage. Under Prometheus's 5m lookback a high-volume series that started recently would truncate the x-axis for every other series on the chart.
- PARTIAL CORRECTION to the first engineer's 'integer-biased' framing: `data[].count` already carries non-integers today via the formula path (compute.ts:158 `round(result, 2)`; formula.test.ts:11 asserts A/B === 2.5). Float values are not novel. What is lossy is the fixed `round(_, 2)` — a CPU fraction of 0.00123 becomes 0 — and the `allowDecimals: false` y-axis (axis.tsx:38), not the field's type.
- PARTIAL CORRECTION on NaN: their statement is right but worth bounding. `average` in packages/common/src/math.ts:8-18 explicitly guards `!Number.isNaN(n) && Number.isFinite(n)`. Only `sum`, `min` and `max` (lines 20-33) use bare `filter(isNumber)` and would propagate NaN/±Inf. They scoped the claim to `sum`, which is accurate.
- Minor: the recharts dataKey is at apps/start/src/components/report-chart/line/chart.tsx:286, not 275. And `unit` in zReportInput spans packages/validation/src/index.ts:303-308, not 305-311. Neither affects the substance.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The strongest single piece of evidence for the first engineer's most contested correction is one they did not find: apps/start/src/components/chat/tool-results/chat-report-result.tsx:11-13,55,74-76 receives `{ report, data }` from an MCP tool, throws `data` away, and passes only `report` to `<ReportChart>` so it refetches over tRPC. There is no `data` prop on ReportChartProps and no injection path in the tree. 'Every chart renderer works unchanged' is therefore false in the strongest possible sense — the app already has a code path holding the finished chart and it cannot hand it to the renderer.
- The plan should state explicitly which pieces FinalChart actually buys, since that list is short and verifiable: the inner `Chart` components (line/area/histogram via useRechartDataModel + useVisibleSeries), report-table-utils.ts, report-chart-tooltip.tsx, serie-name.tsx, and packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts shapeChart. The fetch layer, the chartType switch, the Prisma enums and the share/embed plumbing all need new code regardless.
- packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:71-85 sorts the pivot's date axis with `dates.sort()` — plain lexicographic. That works for 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' and would silently misorder any other date encoding (epoch-seconds-as-string, ISO-with-offset, or a mix). Whatever the metrics engine emits for `date` must remain a zero-padded lexicographically-sortable local wall-clock string, or the MCP payoff quietly breaks. Note shapeChart at 71-79 already defensively takes the union of dates rather than trusting series[0], so it is more robust than the recharts hook.
- The public-share and embed path is not a separate risk surface: chartProcedure (packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:83-141) resolves shares by loading the persisted Report row via getReportById and substituting it as `ctx.report`, then runs the same ChartEngine. So sharing a metric report requires the metric query spec to round-trip through the enum-constrained `model Report` columns (events Json / breakdowns Json / chartType enum / metric enum), or requires a parallel share path.
- A concrete decision the plan owes an answer to, given gigapipe emits labels in Go map order (prom_query_range.go:263): the metrics engine must impose a deterministic label ordering BEFORE building `names` and `id`, because `id` feeds a recharts dataKey, a React key, and the persisted `visibleSeries` string array on the Report row (schema.prisma:446). Non-deterministic ordering would make saved visible-series selections decay across identical requests.
- Because gigapipe caps range queries at 11,000 points per series and floors to 15s, while OpenPanel's finest bucket is a minute and its widest ranges are months, the two point-budget models never bind at the same time. The compiler needs an explicit interval→step mapping plus a guard, since a naive `range: '3m', interval: 'minute'` (which the server accepts, only the UI blocks it) is ~130,000 points and would be rejected by gigapipe with a 500, not a graceful degradation.

**Impact on the plan.** Decision 4 survives, but three things in the plan need rewording or new work. (1) Reframe the leverage claim honestly: FinalChart buys the inner chart components, the report table, the tooltip, and the MCP shapeChart — it does not buy the fetch layer, the chartType switch, the Prisma enums, or the share plumbing. Budget for a new `trpc.metrics.chart` procedure plus a `data`-accepting variant of ReportChart (or a `data` prop on the existing one), since chat-report-result.tsx shows the app already wants one. (2) Add a phase-0 item acknowledging FinalChart is marked legacy with an unused `ChartResponse` successor, and decide explicitly whether to adopt FinalChart anyway (recommended, for the MCP/table/tooltip payoff) or to accelerate the ChartResponse migration; either way write the conformance tests that do not currently exist. (3) The interval model needs design work the plan does not currently contain: OpenPanel has no sub-minute bucket while gigapipe floors to 15s, so the zMetricQuery compiler needs an explicit interval→step mapping, a point-budget guard against gigapipe's 11,000-point limit, a deterministic label ordering imposed before names/id are built, a policy for empty label sets (which `groupByLabels` drops today), and a policy for NaN/±Inf and for small gauge values that the engine's existing `round(_, 2)` convention would flatten to zero. None of these are reasons to abandon the bet; all of them are work the plan currently reads as free.

## Investigation 4 — `partially_confirmed`

Every individual assertion in the claim is true and I confirmed each in Go source, not just docs. QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD set HTTP basic auth (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:172-183, applied at main.go:322-326 via reader/utils/middleware/basic_auth.go), 3100 is the default port (main.go:301-303 and Dockerfile ENV PORT 3100), docs/configuration.md documents the env surface, and MODE selects all/reader/writer/init_only (main.go:207-220, 305-311, 353-370). The claim is imprecise in ways that matter for deployment: a config file IS supported via a `-config` flag (main.go:50, 290-296) so it is not "entirely" env-driven; basic auth is OFF unless BOTH vars are non-empty; CLOKI_* overrides rather than aliases QRYN_*; MODE is unvalidated so a typo silently boots a server with no subsystems; and READONLY only downgrades mode `all`. Two facts the plan should absorb: the ruler runs only in MODE=all, and OTLP/gRPC is multiplexed onto the same cleartext port with no server-side TLS anywhere.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:172-183` — All four auth env vars, read in this order: `if os.Getenv("QRYN_LOGIN") != "" { cfg.Setting.AUTH_SETTINGS.BASIC.Username = ... }`, then CLOKI_LOGIN, then QRYN_PASSWORD, then CLOKI_PASSWORD. Later assignments win, so CLOKI_* overrides QRYN_*.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:322-326` — Basic auth is conditional: `if cfg.Setting.AUTH_SETTINGS.BASIC.Username != "" && cfg.Setting.AUTH_SETTINGS.BASIC.Password != "" { app.Use(middleware.BasicAuthMiddleware(...)) }`. No credentials configured = no auth at all.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/utils/middleware/basic_auth.go:8-42` — RFC 7235 basic auth via `r.BasicAuth()`, comparing SHA-256 digests with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` (constant-time, length-hiding), returning 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Restricted"`. Single static credential pair — no per-tenant users, no token scheme.
- `/Users/drew/go/pkg/mod/github.com/gorilla/mux@v1.8.1/mux.go:138-149` — `Router.Match` builds the middleware chain at match time (`for i := len(r.middlewares)-1; i>=0; i-- { match.Handler = r.middlewares[i].Middleware(match.Handler) }`), independent of route-registration order. So the basic-auth middleware added at main.go:325 also covers the routes registered earlier at main.go:317 — /ready, /config, /metrics, /api/status/buildinfo (shared/commonroutes/routes.go:10-19). Health and Prometheus scrapes therefore need credentials too once auth is on.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:184-196` — `PORT` parsed with strconv.Atoi into `cfg.Setting.HTTP_SETTINGS.Port` (invalid value returns an error that main.go:298-300 panics on); `HOST` into `.Host`, defaulting to `0.0.0.0` when empty. `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` enables CORS.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:301-303` — The 3100 default, applied after both config file and env are read: `if cfg.Setting.HTTP_SETTINGS.Port == 0 { cfg.Setting.HTTP_SETTINGS.Port = 3100 }`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/Dockerfile:14-16` — The image also hard-sets it: `ENV PORT 3100` / `EXPOSE 3100` / `STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM`, `CMD ["/gigapipe"]`. So in Docker PORT is always explicitly present, not falling through to the code default.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:207-220` — MODE resolution: `mode := "all"; if os.Getenv("MODE") != "" { mode = os.Getenv("MODE") }`; READONLY (via boolEnv) downgrades `all` -> `reader` only; then `cfg.Setting.SYSTEM_SETTINGS.Mode = mode` unconditionally. No validation of the string.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:305-311` — `initDB` (table creation + rotation via ctrl.Init/ctrl.Rotate) runs for modes all/writer/init_only, then `if os.Getenv("MODE") == "init_only" { return }`. MODE=reader never creates tables — a reader-only node against an uninitialized database will fail at query time.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:353-370` — bootSequence: writer for all/writer/""; reader for all/reader/""; ruler ONLY for all/""; view for all/reader/"". Comment documents the ordering as a correctness constraint (ruler needs writer's CH client and reader's registry; view registers a catch-all "/"). Confirms the ruler cannot run in a split reader/writer deployment.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:64-79,282-296` — `initDB` honors `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES` via boolEnv; `start()` does `distconfig.Init(); tables.InitDistTableNames()`, conditionally appends `*appFlags.ConfigPath` to configPaths, then `clconfig.New(...)` + `cfg.ReadConfig()` BEFORE portEnv layers env on top.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:46-51` — CLI flags: `-initialize_db`, `-help`, `-version`, `-config <path>`. Only `-config` is actually consumed in start(); `appFlags.InitializeDB`, ShowHelpMessage and ShowVersion are parsed but never read anywhere in the repo (grep for InitializeDB returns only these two lines plus an unrelated help string in writer/plugin/utils.go:50) — so `-initialize_db` is dead and MODE=init_only is the real initialization path.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/grpc/server.go:69-116` — gRPC honors the SAME basic credentials, passed from main.go:330-333 as `writergrpc.Options{BasicAuthUser: cfg...BASIC.Username, BasicAuthPass: ...Password}`; interceptors added only `if opts.BasicAuthUser != "" && opts.BasicAuthPass != ""`. MaxRecvMsgSize = controller.OTLPMaxMessageSize().
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/grpc/auth.go:21-60` — gRPC auth expects `authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)>` metadata (what the OTel Collector `basicauth` extension sets), returns a deliberately generic "invalid credentials" / codes.Unauthenticated, and its doc comment warns the port is cleartext.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/grpc/mux.go:28-49` — `Mux` dispatches HTTP/2 + `application/grpc*` to the gRPC server and everything else to the mux router; `Protocols()` enables HTTP/1 plus unencrypted HTTP/2. gRPC requests bypass the mux middleware chain entirely — which is exactly why basic auth had to be re-implemented as an interceptor.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/grpc/tenant.go:32-62` — The writer's per-request tenancy metadata, gRPC side: `x-ch-dsn` (tenant DSN), `x-scope-meta`, `x-async-insert`, `x-ttl-days` (uint16), mirroring the HTTP middleware. Confirms the writer takes a per-request ClickHouse DSN and a per-request TTL.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/docs/configuration.md:30-79` — The doc sections the claim refers to: Authentication (QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD + CLOKI_* legacy), HTTP Settings (PORT default 3100, HOST default 0.0.0.0, CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN), Mode (all default / reader / writer / init_only, plus READONLY), Storage and Retention (SAMPLES_DAYS default 7 — a single global TTL, no per-signal setting).
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/docs/configuration.md:81-92` — Ruler section states it "is single-tenant and recording-only (alerting rules may be stored but are never evaluated)" and "runs only in modes all/\"\"" — matching bootSequence at main.go:365-367. QRYN_RULER_ENABLED default disabled; when disabled the rule endpoints 404.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/scripts/test/e2e/docker-compose.yml:16-30` — A working reference deployment using exactly these knobs: CLUSTER_NAME, CLICKHOUSE_SERVER, CLICKHOUSE_AUTH, QRYN_LOGIN: a, QRYN_PASSWORD: b, QRYN_RULER_ENABLED, BULK_MAX_AGE_MS, PORT: "9080" — i.e. PORT is genuinely overridable and basic auth genuinely enabled by env alone.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/test/integration/docker-compose.yml:12-27` — Second reference: image built from the working tree, env CLICKHOUSE_SERVER/CLICKHOUSE_PORT/PORT=3100/BULK_MAX_AGE_MS, ports 3100:3100, no config file mounted anywhere.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:406-448` — httpStart: `net.Listen("tcp", httpURL)` then `httpServer.Serve(listener)` — plain TCP, no TLS. Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT with a 30s timeout, then rulerrouter.Stop / writer.Stop / reader.Stop per mode.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/go.mod:1-2,38` — Module is still `github.com/metrico/qryn/v5` (go 1.27.0) and config comes from `github.com/metrico/cloki-config v0.0.96`. HEAD is d4b91b1; recent commits e7484e9/60e22ea added the OTLP/gRPC receiver and OTLP metrics on /v1/metrics.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "Configured entirely by environment variables" is imprecise. A YAML/JSON config file IS supported: `cmd/gigapipe/main.go:50` defines a `-config` flag, and `main.go:290-296` stats that path, passes it to `clconfig.New(clconfig.CLOKI_READER, configPaths, "", "")` and calls `cfg.ReadConfig()`. Env vars are then layered on top by `portEnv()` (main.go:163-279). Docs also reference config-file keys directly (`docs/configuration.md`: "Also settable in the config file as `system_settings.otlp_max_message_size`"), and `writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:31-32` names the same key. The accurate statement: env vars are the primary and fully sufficient configuration surface, and they override the config file for everything portEnv touches.
- MODE is env-only in practice, not merely "selected by MODE". `main.go:207-220` computes `mode` (default `"all"`, overridden by `os.Getenv("MODE")`) and then UNCONDITIONALLY assigns `cfg.Setting.SYSTEM_SETTINGS.Mode = mode` (main.go:220) — so a mode set in a config file is always clobbered back to `all`. Related asymmetry: the init-and-exit short-circuit at `main.go:310` reads `os.Getenv("MODE") == "init_only"`, not the resolved config value.
- The MODE value set is `all` (default) | `reader` | `writer` | `init_only`, plus an undocumented empty-string alias. `bootSequence` (main.go:353-370) treats `""` as equivalent to `all`, but `""` is unreachable via env because `main.go:209` only overrides when `MODE != ""`. Also: MODE is NOT validated. A typo (e.g. `MODE=read`) yields zero boot steps, `initDB` is skipped, and the process still binds the port and serves only `/ready`, `/config`, `/metrics`, `/api/status/buildinfo` — a silent no-op deployment, not an error.
- READONLY is not exactly "equivalent to MODE=reader" as the docs say. `main.go:216-218` downgrades to reader ONLY when `mode == "all"`; `READONLY=true` together with `MODE=writer` leaves the node a writer. Also `boolEnv` (main.go:54-62) accepts only lowercase `true/1/yes/y` / `false/0/no/n/""` and PANICS on anything else (e.g. `READONLY=TRUE` or `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=True` crash the process at boot). Note the ruler's own parser is different and more lenient — `ruler/router/init.go:30-36` lowercases/trims and accepts `1|true|yes|on`.
- Basic auth is OFF by default and only engages when BOTH credentials are non-empty: `main.go:322-326` gates `middleware.BasicAuthMiddleware` on `Username != "" && Password != ""`, and `writer/grpc/server.go:101-103` gates the gRPC interceptors identically. Setting only QRYN_LOGIN silently leaves the instance fully open.
- `CLOKI_LOGIN`/`CLOKI_PASSWORD` are not passive aliases — they are checked AFTER the QRYN_* vars (main.go:172-183), so if both are set the legacy CLOKI_* value WINS.
- The port serves both HTTP and OTLP/gRPC; there is no separate gRPC port. `main.go:329-335` builds one `httpURL` and `httpRoot` (main.go:400-405) wraps the router in `writergrpc.Mux` with `writergrpc.Protocols()` (h2c). `writer/grpc/mux.go:28-36` dispatches on `r.ProtoMajor == 2 && Content-Type` prefix `application/grpc`. Confirmed by `docs/otlp-grpc.md:11`.
- gigapipe's own listener is cleartext only — there is no TLS/HTTPS option for the server. `main.go:412` uses `net.Listen("tcp", httpURL)` and `httpServer.Serve(listener)`; there is no `ListenAndServeTLS` or server-side `tls.Config` anywhere (the only `tls.Config` hits are ClickHouse client connections in `reader/registry/registry.go:72`, `writer/chwrapper/*`). Credentials on both HTTP and gRPC travel in the clear unless TLS is terminated in front (`writer/grpc/auth.go:31-33`, `docs/otlp-grpc.md:107-109`).
- `docs/configuration.md` is not a complete env-var reference. `CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER` is read in production code at `ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:31` but appears nowhere in the doc.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The ruler runs ONLY in MODE=all (or empty) — `cmd/gigapipe/main.go:365-367` gates the ruler boot step on `in("all", "")`, unlike writer (all/writer) and reader (all/reader). If the plan splits gigapipe into separate reader and writer containers (which decision #2 implies, since only the writer accepts a per-request DSN), NEITHER container runs the ruler. This reinforces the plan's position that alert/rule evaluation must live in OpenPanel's worker, and additionally means gigapipe's recording rules are unavailable in a split deployment too.
- MODE is silently unvalidated (main.go:207-220 + 353-370). `MODE=readonly` or `MODE=read` produces a process that starts cleanly, logs "Server is listening on ...", answers /ready with 200 (watchdog permitting), and serves no ingest or query routes at all. Any compose template or health check in the plan should assert on a real API route, not /ready.
- Basic auth is a single global static credential pair, not per-tenant. There is exactly one Username/Password on `cfg.Setting.AUTH_SETTINGS.BASIC` (main.go:172-183) checked by one middleware/interceptor. This is fine for the plan's model (only apps/api talks to gigapipe) but confirms gigapipe itself can never be the project-isolation boundary — all isolation must be the label enforcement in apps/api, as decision #2 states.
- Turning auth on affects observability plumbing: because gorilla/mux applies middleware at match time regardless of registration order, /ready, /metrics, /config and /api/status/buildinfo all sit behind basic auth once QRYN_LOGIN+QRYN_PASSWORD are set. A Docker healthcheck or Prometheus scrape of the gigapipe container must carry the credentials.
- The writer's per-request DSN mechanism is confirmed on both transports: `x-ch-dsn` metadata on gRPC (writer/grpc/tenant.go:43) with the comment that it mirrors the HTTP middleware. Also confirmed per-request `x-ttl-days` (uint16) — potentially relevant to the plan's per-signal retention problem, since TTL can be set per write request rather than only globally via SAMPLES_DAYS. I did not trace how x-ttl-days is applied at the ClickHouse level, so treat that as a lead, not a solution.
- OTLP/gRPC shares PORT with HTTP via h2c (writer/grpc/mux.go, main.go:400-405). One published port (3100) covers Loki push, Prometheus remote-write, OTLP/HTTP and OTLP/gRPC — the compose service needs no second port. Max OTLP payload is 64 MiB by default, tunable via QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:26-42).
- The built-in web UI is behind a Go build tag, not an env var: `view/static.go` (`//go:build view`) vs `view/static_no.go` (`//go:build !view`), and the Dockerfile builds with `-tags view` only when `ARG VIEW=1`. The default `ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe:latest` behavior w.r.t. that build arg is not determinable from this repo. Since view registers a catch-all "/" route (main.go comment at 351-352), it is worth pinning explicitly rather than inheriting.
- `docs/configuration.md` claims READONLY is "equivalent to MODE=reader" and that CLOKI_LOGIN is an "alias" for QRYN_LOGIN. Both are subtly wrong against the source (READONLY only downgrades `all`; CLOKI_* overrides QRYN_* rather than aliasing it). Do not treat that doc as authoritative when writing the compose template — main.go's portEnv is the contract.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan's five load-bearing decisions has to change; the deployment and auth story holds. Four refinements are needed in the P0 stack section. (1) Write the compose service against `cmd/gigapipe/main.go`'s portEnv, not `docs/configuration.md` — pin PORT, MODE, QRYN_LOGIN, QRYN_PASSWORD, CLICKHOUSE_* explicitly, use only lowercase `true`/`false` for boolean env vars (boolEnv panics otherwise), and set QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD as a pair or not at all, since one alone yields a wide-open instance. (2) Do not describe gigapipe as env-only configured; it accepts a `-config` file, and env overrides it — but note MODE specifically is always overwritten from env, so mode cannot be set in a file. (3) Health-checking: if auth is enabled, /ready and /metrics require credentials, and /ready answers 200 even for a typo'd MODE that boots no subsystems, so the compose healthcheck should hit a real API route with the credentials. (4) The ruler-only-in-MODE=all finding strengthens, and should be cited in, the plan's decision to put alert evaluation in OpenPanel's worker: a split reader/writer topology has no ruler at all, so gigapipe recording rules are also off the table there — the plan should state whether it runs one MODE=all instance or a split pair, because that choice decides it. Separately, the confirmed per-request `x-ttl-days` header is worth investigating as an alternative to the plan's conditional-TTL approach for per-signal retention.

## Investigation 5 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-checked every citation the first engineer made and all of them exist and say what they claim — I found no fabricated path, line number, or symbol, and I confirmed their sharpest correction (the `get_latest_images` sed collision) empirically by running the regex rather than reading it. Their verdict of partially_confirmed is right and I agree with it. The mechanical core holds: the self-hosting template has no `networks:` block so a new service reaches ClickHouse as `op-ch`, self-hosting's `op-ch` already publishes no ports, gigapipe defaults `HOST` to `0.0.0.0` so container-to-container works with no `ports:` key, and neither the ClickHouse config nor the user config nor init-db.sh restricts the server to one database. My independent additions are three: gigapipe's boot-time DB creation `panic()`s on failure so any incompatibility is a crash-loop against `restart: always`, not a degraded start; the maintenance connection unconditionally sends the deprecated session setting `allow_experimental_database_replicated`, and gigapipe is tested only against ClickHouse 24.9.1/25.3 while OpenPanel ships 25.10.2.65/26.1.3.52 — an unverified compatibility risk neither the claim nor the first engineer raises; and `quiz.ts` does clean dangling `depends_on` when it removes `op-ch`, but it cleans no environment variables, so a hardcoded `CLICKHOUSE_SERVER: op-ch` survives into a compose file where `op-ch` no longer exists.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:67-90` — Verified. `op-ch` has image `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65`, the three read-only ./clickhouse mounts, `CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1`, a `clickhouse-client --query "SELECT 1"` healthcheck, and no `ports:` key. I read the whole 174-line file: the only top-level keys are `version`, `services`, `volumes` (line 164) — no `networks:`, so every service is on the compose default network. Confirms the first engineer exactly.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/clickhouse/clickhouse-config.xml:1-29` — The config file the first engineer did NOT cite (they only cited the user-config). It contains `<listen_host>0.0.0.0</listen_host>` and `<interserver_listen_host>0.0.0.0</interserver_listen_host>`, removes the system log tables, and declares `<macros>` with `<cluster>openpanel_cluster</cluster>`. It does not remove `tcp_port`, so stock native 9000 stays live and gigapipe's default native port works. Two additions: (a) no `<remote_servers>` is defined anywhere, so gigapipe's `CLUSTER_NAME` must be left UNSET or its `ON CLUSTER \`%s\`` DDL fails; (b) still no per-database restriction of any kind, independently confirming the second half of the claim.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/clickhouse/clickhouse-user-config.xml:1-8 and /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/clickhouse/init-db.sh:1-6` — Verified verbatim. **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- I confirm all of the first engineer's corrections; I could not falsify any of them. What follows are additions and sharpenings, not disagreements.
- NEW — the highest unverified risk in 'pointed at op-ch' is ClickHouse version compatibility, which neither the claim nor the first engineer raises. gigapipe's boot path sends the deprecated session setting `allow_experimental_database_replicated` on every maintenance connection (ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:32-35), and gigapipe is CI-tested only against ClickHouse 24.9.1 and 25.3 (its two compose files), while OpenPanel ships 25.10.2.65 (self-hosting/smoke), 26.1.3.52 (dev) and 24.3.2-alpine (coolify). UNVERIFIED: I cannot run docker, so I do not know whether CH 25.10/26.1 rejects that setting or merely warns. Flagging it as the risk to test first, not asserting it breaks.
- NEW — the failure mode is harsh. ctrl/ctrl.go:30-33 does `panic(err)` if `InitDB` fails, so any DB-creation failure kills the process rather than degrading. Combined with the template's `restart: always`, a misconfigured or version-incompatible gigapipe is an unbounded crash loop inside the operator's stack. The plan should specify `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES` handling or a one-shot `MODE=init_only` container so schema init is a separate, observable step.
- NEW — `CLUSTER_NAME` must be left unset. self-hosting/clickhouse/clickhouse-config.xml:24-28 declares `<macros>` naming `openpanel_cluster`, but no `<remote_servers>` is defined anywhere in the repo. Setting gigapipe's CLUSTER_NAME (main.go:98-101) makes InitDBTry emit `CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER \`openpanel_cluster\``, which would fail against a cluster that does not exist. The macros comment even says 'Not used anymore, but kept for backwards compatibility' — an easy trap.
- SHARPENING of their quiz.ts point — I read `removeServiceFromDockerCompose` (quiz.ts:95-136), which they cited only for the copy. It DOES clean `depends_on` in both array and object form and DOES drop `serviceName`-prefixed volumes, so a gigapipe service depending on op-ch degrades gracefully when an operator brings their own ClickHouse. But it cleans no `environment:` block, so a hardcoded `CLICKHOUSE_SERVER: op-ch` survives into a compose file where op-ch was deleted — which, per the panic above, crash-loops. Their 'something has to translate' correction is right and this is the concrete mechanism by which it bites.
- SHARPENING of their `./update` point — `--remove-orphans` cuts the other way too. An operator whose gitignored docker-compose.yml predates the gigapipe addition will have `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans` actively tear down any gigapipe container they added by hand outside that file.
- NEW — gigapipe's own docs contradict its code on the ClickHouse protocol default. docs/configuration.md:22 says `CLICKHOUSE_PROTO` '(default: `http`)', but cmd/gigapipe/main.go:130-140 only switches to HTTP when the var is explicitly set. Anyone wiring this from the docs will silently get native TCP 9000.
- NEW — the claim and the first engineer both treat this as greenfield. OpenPanel already ships an OTLP tracing SDK (apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts, commit d19c5298) gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY, with metrics explicitly left on prom-client. Neither compose surface wires it, but the plan needs a position on whether gigapipe replaces, coexists with, or receives from this existing path.
- MINOR — 'the ClickHouse init/config files there permit a second database' is true but is the wrong frame twice over: the files never restricted anything (so 'permit' implies a gate that does not exist), and gigapipe would not use init-db.sh even if edited, since /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d runs only on a fresh data directory. The first engineer got both halves right.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe's DB-init failure path is `panic(err)` (ctrl/ctrl.go:30-33), not a returned error — so under the template's `restart: always` any ClickHouse incompatibility becomes a silent crash loop inside the operator's stack rather than a degraded start. The plan should isolate schema init behind `MODE=init_only` or `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES` so it fails once, visibly.
- Three different ClickHouse versions ship across OpenPanel's own surfaces — 25.10.2.65 (self-hosting template + CI smoke), 26.1.3.52 (dev), 24.3.2-alpine (coolify.yml:36) — and gigapipe is CI-tested against neither of the first two (its compose files pin 24.9.1 and 25.3). The plan needs a supported-version matrix, and the coolify surface may need a ClickHouse bump before gigapipe can run there at all.
- `CLUSTER_NAME` must be explicitly left unset. clickhouse-config.xml:24-28 defines `<macros>` with `<cluster>openpanel_cluster</cluster>` but no `<remote_servers>` exists in the repo; setting CLUSTER_NAME would make gigapipe emit `ON CLUSTER` DDL against a nonexistent cluster.
- quiz.ts's `removeServiceFromDockerCompose` cleans `depends_on` and volumes but never `environment:`. Any gigapipe env pointing at `op-ch` must therefore be templated the same way `$OP_WORKER_REPLICAS` is (via `searchAndReplaceDockerCompose`, quiz.ts:414), or derived at runtime from CLICKHOUSE_URL — not hardcoded — so the bring-your-own-ClickHouse path does not break.
- gigapipe supports HTTP basic auth via `QRYN_LOGIN`/`QRYN_PASSWORD` (docs/configuration.md:38-40). Since the plan makes 'gigapipe is never exposed' a security boundary, these are worth setting as defense-in-depth against a future operator adding a `ports:` key or a misconfigured reverse proxy — the network-only posture is currently the sole control.
- gigapipe's `MODE` env (all/reader/writer/init_only, docs/configuration.md) plus `READONLY` directly serve plan decision 1's split — the plan can run separate reader and writer containers rather than one `all` process, which also lets the writer take a per-request DSN while the reader stays pinned, matching decision 2's stated constraint.
- OpenPanel already has an OTLP path: apps/api and apps/worker boot `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry` gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY, with `disableMetrics: true` because 'Metrics stay on prom-client/Grafana' (apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts:1-27). The plan's claim of adding observability without an external stack has to reconcile with this existing external dependency.
- gigapipe's docs and code disagree on the ClickHouse protocol default (docs say http, main.go:130-140 defaults to native 9000). Whatever the plan writes into the compose template should set CLICKHOUSE_PROTO explicitly rather than rely on either.
- `apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx` documents CLICKHOUSE_URL in two places (lines 70-80 and a summary list at 1227) and is the canonical doc surface for any new telemetry env var — the first engineer's doc audit named the four deploy-*.mdx files but not this one, nor deploy-dokploy.mdx, which neither of us has read.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's P0 (stack) step should not be written as "add a gigapipe service to docker-compose.template.yml." Concretely: (1) P0 must enumerate five delivery surfaces, not two — the self-hosting template, coolify.yml, .github/smoke/docker-compose.yml (so CI actually exercises the new service), the dev docker-compose.yml with plain-list `depends_on: [op-ch]` since dev's op-ch has no healthcheck, and the documented-but-unsourced Kubernetes path. (2) P0 must include changes to quiz.ts (env translation from the single CLICKHOUSE_URL into gigapipe's five vars, plus a `$GIGAPIPE_URL` replace in writeEnvFile), to .env.template, and to environment-variables.mdx — none of which the claim counts. (3) `get_latest_images` needs its sed anchored (e.g. `image:.*openpanel[-/]${component}` or matching only the known service keys) BEFORE any image containing the substring "api" enters a compose file, or the updater will silently rewrite gigapipe's image to OpenPanel's api image. (4) An upgrade path for existing self-hosters must be designed, since docker-compose.yml is gitignored and `./update` cannot reach it — the plan needs either a migration script or an explicit "re-run the quiz" step with a warning that it overwrites customisations. (5) Before any of this, P0 should carry a spike: run gigapipe against clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65 and confirm the `allow_experimental_database_replicated` session setting and gigapipe's DDL are accepted, because the boot path panics on failure and gigapipe has no CI coverage at that version. Nothing here invalidates decisions 1-5; it moves cost from "one added service" into a real P0 with a version spike and five surfaces. Delete the claim's implication that ClickHouse init/config files need any edit — they do not.
