## Investigation 6 — `partially_confirmed`

Two of the three named packages are already resolved in the monorepo's lockfile — `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.57.2` and `protobufjs@7.4.0`, both pulled transitively by `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry` (catalog `^0.10.3`). The other two needs are not backed by anything on disk: there is no snappy implementation of any kind in `pnpm-lock.yaml` or the stray `package-lock.json`, and no `@prometheus-io/*` package anywhere — I could not verify that `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql` exists, is maintained, or what it exports, because no lockfile entry, no `node_modules` (the repo is not installed) and no package manager cache for it is present on this machine. More importantly, reading gigapipe's actual ingest handlers changes the shape of the requirement: gigapipe accepts **OTLP JSON** on `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/logs` and **Loki JSON** on `/loki/api/v1/push`, and its remote-write middleware silently falls back to the raw body when snappy decoding fails — so the OpenPanel→gigapipe hop needs neither protobuf nor snappy. Protobuf decode and snappy decompress are needed only on the *inbound* leg (an OTel SDK or a Prometheus server talking to apps/api), which the claim does not distinguish.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-lock.yaml:6078, 25771-25780` — `'@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.57.2'` is a resolved package, with its own dependency block listing `protobufjs: 7.4.0` plus api-logs/core/resources/sdk-logs/sdk-metrics/sdk-trace-base at 0.57.2/1.30.1. It is present *transitively*, not as a direct dependency of any workspace package.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-lock.yaml:16344, 38333-38346` — `protobufjs@7.4.0` resolved, deps are the ten pure-JS `@protobufjs/*` helpers plus `long@5.2.3` and `@types/node@20.19.24`. No native/optional binary dependency in the tree.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-lock.yaml:24010-24030` — The importer that drags all of this in is `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry`, which depends on `@opentelemetry/exporter-{logs,metrics,trace}-otlp-{grpc,http,proto}@0.57.2` — those are what depend on otlp-transformer. `@grpc/grpc-js@1.11.2` arrives the same way (pnpm-lock.yaml:4740, 25288).
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-workspace.yaml:87, 107-127` — Catalog pins `"@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry": ^0.10.3`. The `allowBuilds:` block sets `protobufjs: false` (line 116) alongside sharp/esbuild/prisma etc. — every dependency install script is denied. protobufjs is fine with that (pure JS); a *native* snappy would not be.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-lock.yaml (whole file, 42235 lines)` — `grep -n "snappy\|snappyjs\|lezer-promql\|@prometheus-io"` returns zero matches for any of them. The only `@prometheus-io` string in the file is inside the deprecation notice on `prom-client@15.1.3` at line 16305: `deprecated: prom-client has been replaced by @prometheus-io/client`. `package-lock.json` (7560 lines, stale, lockfileVersion 2) likewise has no snappy and no lezer-promql.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-lock.yaml:5153-5166, 24346-24366` — `@lezer/common@1.5.0`, `@lezer/highlight@1.2.3`, `@lezer/lr@1.4.7` ARE present — but only via `@codemirror/language@6.12.1`, i.e. through `apps/start/package.json:21-26,102` (codemirror in the dashboard). They are not in apps/api's graph, where the plan puts the compiler.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:18-60` — gigapipe's OTLP/HTTP metrics handler registers TWO parsers: `otlpContentTypeProto = "application/x-protobuf"` via `proto.Unmarshal`, and `otlpContentTypeJSON = "application/json"` via `protojson.UnmarshalOptions{DiscardUnknown: true}.Unmarshal`. Routed at `writer/router/insert.go:16` (`/v1/metrics`), with `/v1/logs` alongside it (line 15). So OpenPanel can forward OTLP as JSON and never encode protobuf outbound.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/insert.go:47-56` — Loki push: `withSimpleParser("*", Parser(unmarshal.DecodePushRequestStringV2))` is the default for ANY content type; protobuf is only reached via `withComplexParser("application/x-protobuf", …, withUnsnappyRequest)`. Logs can be pushed to gigapipe as plain JSON.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/prom.go:39-46 and writer/controller/middleware.go:111-143` — Remote-write is the one path that is protobuf-only: `withUnsnappyRequest` then `withSimpleParser("*", Parser(unmarshal.UnmarshallMetricsWriteProtoV2))` — no JSON fallback. But `withUnsnappyRequest` is tolerant: if `snappy.DecodedLen`/`snappy.Decode` errors it puts the ORIGINAL body back on the context ("Sending the compressed body back", middleware.go:135-137). An uncompressed prompb payload is accepted.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/utils/unmarshal/metrics_protobuf.go:74-77 and writer/utils/proto/prompb.proto` — `UnmarshallMetricsWriteProtoV2 = Build(withBufferedBody, withParsedBody(func() proto.Message { return &prompb.WriteRequest{} }), …)` — remote-write v1 only. The schema is checked into gigapipe as a 68-line `.proto` (`package prometheus`, `message WriteRequest/TimeSeries/Sample/Label/LabelMatcher`), so it can be fed straight to protobufjs. `writer/utils/proto/loki.proto` (36 lines, `PushRequest/StreamAdapter/EntryAdapter`) is there too.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/go.mod:42-44, 49-51 and reader/promql/promql_parser/parser.go:1-13` — gigapipe vendors the real Prometheus PromQL parser (`github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.314.0`) and wraps it: `parser.NewParser(parser.Options{}).ParseExpr(query)`. Also `go.opentelemetry.io/proto/otlp v1.11.0` and `github.com/golang/snappy v1.0.0`. A grep for `LabelMatchers = append|AddMatcher|injectMatcher|enforce` across `reader/` finds NO matcher-injection code — gigapipe parses PromQL but does not rewrite selectors for tenancy today.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/tsdown.config.ts:5-16` — `noExternal: [/^@openpanel\/.*$/u, /^@\/.*$/u]` and `external: ['@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry','pino','pino-pretty','@node-rs/argon2']`, `platform: 'node'`, `shims: true`. Only workspace packages are bundled — every npm dependency stays external and is resolved from node_modules at runtime. So bundling under tsdown is a non-issue for protobufjs; a native addon would just need adding to `external` the way `@node-rs/argon2` is. apps/worker/tsdown.config.ts is identical plus `@aws-sdk/client-s3`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/Dockerfile:67-79` — The prod stage sets `ENV npm_config_build_from_source=true`, installs python3/make/g++, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod && pnpm rebuild`. pnpm-workspace.yaml:107-127 documents that flipping `allowBuilds` to true here already broke the image once (sharp tried to compile via node-gyp: "Please add node-gyp to your dependencies"). A native snappy binding lands squarely in that failure mode.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/app.ts:88, 128 and apps/api/src/routes/webhook.router.ts:15` — `bodyLimit: 1_048_576 * 500`; `await fastify.register(import('fastify-raw-body'), { global: false })`, opted into per-route with `rawBody: true`. There is NO `addContentTypeParser` anywhere in apps/api/src — and the existing rawBody consumer treats it as a string (`request as FastifyRequest & { rawBody?: string }`, app.ts:422). A binary `application/x-protobuf` parser is net-new work.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/package.json:4 / apps/api/Dockerfile:1` — apps/api is `"type": "module"` and runs on `NODE_VERSION=24.19.0` (same for worker and start). Relevant to any CJS-only dependency choice; tsdown's `shims: true` covers __dirname/require in the bundle itself.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/grpc/register.go:5-11 and writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:22-40` — gigapipe also serves OTLP over gRPC for all four signals (trace, logs, metrics, profiles). `OTLPMaxMessageSize()` defaults to 64 MiB (`defaultOTLPMaxMessageSize = 64 << 20`), configurable via `system_settings.otlp_max_message_size` / env `QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`, and bounds both the HTTP body (413) and the gRPC MaxRecvMsgSize.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "The Node ecosystem provides…" overstates what is verified. Only 2 of the 3 named things are confirmed present: @opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.57.2 and protobufjs@7.4.0 (pnpm-lock.yaml:6078, 16344). snappy and @prometheus-io/lezer-promql have zero presence in either lockfile, in node_modules (not installed), or in any pnpm/npm cache on this machine — I cannot confirm the latter package even exists under that name.
- Both confirmed packages are TRANSITIVE, not direct. They are reachable today only because @hyperdx/node-opentelemetry (catalog ^0.10.3, pnpm-workspace.yaml:87) pulls the OTLP exporters. apps/api/package.json declares neither. Importing them without adding explicit dependencies is a phantom-dependency bug that breaks the moment the hyperdx pin moves — and note that @hyperdx/node-opentelemetry is in apps/api's `external` list (apps/api/tsdown.config.ts:9), so it is deliberately NOT bundled.
- @opentelemetry/otlp-transformer is an export-side serializer library — it exists to turn SDK ReadableSpan/ResourceMetrics/LogRecord objects into OTLP wire bytes for exporters. The claim needs the opposite direction: decoding an inbound ExportTraceServiceRequest into an object the gateway can mutate (overwrite op_project_id) and re-emit. I could NOT verify from source whether 0.57.2 exposes any decode entry point, because node_modules is not installed on this machine. Treat "otlp-transformer gives you decode" as unverified; assuming it does is the single riskiest line in the claim.
- "protobufjs against opentelemetry-proto" glosses over where the .proto files come from. There are NO OTLP .proto files anywhere on disk: `find` over gigapipe returns only its own 7 protos, and the Go module cache (~/go/pkg/mod/go.opentelemetry.io/proto/otlp@v1.11.0) ships generated .pb.go, not .proto. Those schemas would have to be vendored from an external source and version-tracked. By contrast the Prometheus and Loki schemas ARE on disk in gigapipe (writer/utils/proto/prompb.proto, loki.proto) and are directly consumable by protobufjs.
- The claim treats "snappy for Prometheus remote-write" as one need; gigapipe's code splits it in two. Outbound (OpenPanel→gigapipe) snappy is optional — middleware.go:135-137 restores the raw body when decode fails, so an uncompressed prompb.WriteRequest is accepted. Inbound (a customer's Prometheus → apps/api) snappy is mandatory, because Prometheus always snappy-compresses remote-write. Only the inbound leg justifies the dependency.
- The claim implies protobuf encode is needed for the write-out to gigapipe. It is not, for OTLP: gigapipe's /v1/metrics and /v1/logs accept application/json via protojson (otlp_metrics.go:55-58), and /loki/api/v1/push defaults to JSON for any content type (insert.go:50). Only /v1/prom/remote/write is protobuf-only (prom.go:44-45, no JSON parser registered).
- "bundling under tsdown" is listed as an open caveat but is already settled by the repo: apps/api/tsdown.config.ts:6 sets noExternal to workspace packages only, so npm dependencies are never bundled. The real packaging risk is not tsdown — it is the Docker prod stage (apps/api/Dockerfile:67-79: npm_config_build_from_source=true + pnpm rebuild) combined with pnpm-workspace.yaml's blanket allowBuilds:false, which the file itself documents as having already broken the image over sharp. That risk applies to a native snappy and to nothing else in this list.
- The claim's PromQL-rewriting premise omits that gigapipe already embeds the canonical parser (github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.314.0, reader/promql/promql_parser/parser.go). It exposes no matcher-injection API today (verified: no such code in reader/), so a JS parser is a legitimate choice — but "we must parse PromQL in Node" is a design decision, not a forced one; adding an enforcement hook to the Go reader is the alternative the plan should at least name.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe's remote-write path is Prometheus remote-write **v1 only** (metrics_protobuf.go:76 constructs `&prompb.WriteRequest{}`; prompb.proto has no symbol-table/v2 messages). It also drops everything but labels + float samples — `msg` is filled with empty strings and every sample is tagged `model.SAMPLE_TYPE_METRIC` (metrics_protobuf.go:39-45). Native histograms, exemplars and metric metadata are not ingested. Any plan promising Prometheus-parity ingest needs to say this out loud.
- gigapipe's per-request ClickHouse DSN is an HTTP header, `X-CH-DSN`, read in `WithOverallContextMiddleware` (writer/controller/middleware.go:164), alongside `X-Scope-Meta`, `X-Ttl-Days` and `X-Async-Insert`. That corroborates the plan's decision #2 (writer takes a per-request DSN, reader does not) and gives the exact header names — and it means those headers must be stripped from anything a customer can influence.
- `withUnsnappyRequest` hard-caps the decompressed remote-write body at 10 MiB (`if uncompressedLen > 10*1024*1024 { return errors.New400Error("body is too long") }`, middleware.go:122-125) — and on that error it falls through to passing the still-compressed body to the protobuf parser, which will fail confusingly rather than returning a clean 413. OTLP has a separate, much larger 64 MiB bound (otlp_metrics.go:25, OTLPMaxMessageSize). The gateway should enforce its own limits before forwarding.
- `prom-client@15.1.3` is already a direct dependency of apps/worker (apps/worker/package.json:35) and `fastify-metrics@^12.1.0` of apps/api — and the lockfile carries an upstream deprecation notice: "prom-client has been replaced by @prometheus-io/client" (pnpm-lock.yaml:16305). If OpenPanel is going to self-instrument into its own metrics store, that migration is adjacent work worth sequencing.
- `@grpc/grpc-js@1.11.2` is already resolved in the tree (pnpm-lock.yaml:4740) via the OTLP gRPC exporters, and gigapipe serves OTLP over gRPC for all four signals (writer/grpc/register.go:6-11). If the gateway ever needs to accept OTLP/gRPC rather than OTLP/HTTP, the Node-side transport is at least present — though again transitively, and gRPC ingest through Fastify is a separate server, not a Fastify route.
- gigapipe's OTLP handlers already implement the spec's partial-success semantics (`ExportMetricsPartialSuccess{RejectedDataPoints, ErrorMessage}`, otlp_metrics.go:96-101) and encode errors as `google.rpc.Status` in the request's content type (writeOTLPStatus/writeOTLPMessage, otlp_metrics.go:106-120). A gateway that terminates OTLP must reproduce this response shape or SDKs will retry-storm; proxying gigapipe's response body through is the cheaper path.
- apps/api currently has no binary content-type parser at all (no `addContentTypeParser` in apps/api/src), and its only rawBody consumer, the Svix webhook path, treats rawBody as a string (app.ts:422, webhook.controller.ts:416). fastify-raw-body is registered with `global: false` (app.ts:128), so the ingest routes will need their own buffer-mode parser registration — small, but it is not free reuse of the webhook machinery.
- The pnpm-workspace.yaml header comments (lines 1-127) are an unusually explicit record of this repo's dependency scar tissue: unused patches, `verifyDepsBeforeRun: false`, the seroval/embla overrides, and the allowBuilds rationale. Any new dependency for this plan — especially a native one — should be justified against that file, because it is where the next reviewer will look.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim is safe to keep as a direction but not as a dependency list. Three concrete changes to the plan:

(1) Split the wire-format requirement by leg. Inbound (SDK/Prometheus → apps/api) genuinely needs OTLP protobuf decode and snappy decompress. Outbound (apps/api → gigapipe) needs neither: send OTLP as `application/json` to /v1/metrics and /v1/logs and Loki JSON to /loki/api/v1/push. That halves the codec surface and removes protobuf *encode* from P1 entirely. Prometheus remote-write is the sole exception — protobuf-only, but tolerant of uncompressed bodies.

(2) De-risk the two unverified packages before committing to them in P1. `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer` must be confirmed to expose a *decoder* (not just serializers) at 0.57.2 — if it does not, the fallback is protobufjs plus vendored opentelemetry-proto `.proto` files, which nothing on disk supplies today and which is therefore a real task with a versioning obligation, not a library import. And add both as explicit `dependencies` of apps/api rather than relying on the @hyperdx transitive.

(3) Treat snappy as a packaging decision, not a package name. If the chosen implementation is a native addon it collides with `allowBuilds: {...: false}` (pnpm-workspace.yaml:107-127) and `npm_config_build_from_source=true` in the api prod stage (Dockerfile:68) — the exact combination that already broke this image over sharp. Prefer a pure-JS snappy decoder, or scope P1's inbound Prometheus support to "OTLP first, remote-write in a later phase" so the dependency is deferred until it is actually earning its keep.

Separately, the raw-PromQL phase (P6) should record that gigapipe already links the canonical Prometheus parser and that adding matcher enforcement in Go is a viable alternative to a JS rewriter — @prometheus-io/lezer-promql could not be verified to exist from anything on disk, so committing the plan to it now is committing to an unchecked assumption.

I re-derived this from the runtime path (browser → procedure → engine) rather than from the definitions, and every line number and quotation the first engineer gave checks out exactly. `chartProcedure` (chart.ts:83-143) is real, `cacher = cacheMiddleware(60)` is real (chart.ts:54), and `chart` (588) / `aggregate` (612) are both `chartProcedure.use(cacher)` ending in `ChartEngine.execute` / `AggregateChartEngine.execute` (chart.ts:609,633), which return `FinalChart` (types.validation.ts:106). Their three criticisms all hold: no `Report.dataSource` exists anywhere, `zReportInput` is a strip `z.object` so a client-sent discriminator is silently dropped, and `ChartEngine.execute` has five call sites with hand-rolled `chartType === 'funnel'|'metric'` dispatch. I disagree with one of their corrections and I found four gates and surfaces they missed, all of which make the "chart.ts is the natural seam" framing weaker, not stronger: a `dataSource` value has to survive four separate hand-written field whitelists (zReport → report.create → report.update → transformReport) plus a Prisma migration, and the *client* renderer switch is a second, independent dispatch keyed on `chartType`.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- I disagree with one of the first engineer's corrections. They wrote: 'Any new metrics procedure that does not reuse `chartProcedure` gets no access check by default.' That is wrong as stated. `protectedProcedure` (trpc.ts:176-180) includes `enforceAccess`, which at trpc.ts:102-112 calls `requireProjectAccess({ level: 'read' })` for any procedure whose raw input has a top-level `projectId` — and the comment there says it 'Fails closed: any procedure that takes a top-level projectId requires write access to mutate, including ones added later.' The accurate statement is: a metrics procedure built on `publicProcedure` gets no check; one built on `protectedProcedure` gets the standard project read check but no share path.
- The first engineer said a `dataSource` column 'would be undefined until transformReport is extended.' True but incomplete — it also never gets WRITTEN. `report.create` (report.ts:54-75) and `report.update` (report.ts:97-119) each spell out the Prisma `data` object field by field. So the discriminator has to be added in four hand-maintained whitelists — `zReportInput`/`zReport`, `report.create`, `report.update`, `transformReport` — plus the Prisma model and a migration, before chart.ts can branch on it at all.
- 'chart.ts is not the only seam' understates it by one axis. Beyond the five server-side `ChartEngine.execute` call sites, there is a *client-side* dispatch that chart.ts cannot reach: `apps/start/src/components/report-chart/index.tsx:39-63` switches on `report.chartType` to pick the renderer, and the renderer picks the procedure. Adding a server-side `dataSource` branch inside `chart.chart` changes what data comes back but not which component asks for it, so a metrics report still renders through `ReportLineChart`/`ReportMetricChart` unless the client switch is extended too.
- The public share page is a sixth surface the first engineer did not enumerate. `apps/start/src/routes/share.report.$shareId.tsx:22-26,80-83` fetches the report through `trpc.share.report` (share.ts:266-297, `publicProcedure` → `transformReport`), not through chartProcedure. That route must also carry the discriminator for plan decision #4's 'public share works unchanged' claim to hold.
- `runReportFromConfig` (mcp/reports.ts:307-351) is materially different from the other four duplicated dispatches: it takes an arbitrary config object with no DB lookup (`config: { chartType, interval, startDate, endDate, [key: string]: unknown }`), so it is fed by the LLM, not by a Report row. The first engineer counted it as 'a second ad-hoc executor' but did not note that a DB-only discriminator is structurally unreachable there — the discriminator has to exist on the *input schema* for this path to work at all.
- Neither the claim nor the first engineer notes that `chartProcedure` has zero test coverage: there is no chart.test.ts in packages/trpc (only access.test.ts, rate-limit.test.ts, routers/share.test.ts). Since the plan calls project isolation 'a SECURITY BOUNDARY' and this procedure is the one place in chart.ts where authorization happens, an untested seam is a real cost of choosing it.
- Minor, on the caching seam: `.use(cacher)` is applied AFTER chartProcedure's auth middleware, so cached values are served only post-authorization — good. But the key is `JSON.stringify(rawInput)` (trpc.ts:203-206) while the *data* on the share path comes from `ctx.report` (the DB), so the key does not vary with report content. Any tenant/label scoping a metrics branch relies on must appear in the raw input or two tenants collide on one cache entry.
- Minor, on error surface: `validateShareAccess` throws a plain `Error` (share.service.ts:110, 146, 184, 210) for missing or non-public shares, which chartProcedure does not catch. Only the passworded-without-cookie case reaches the `TRPCForbiddenError`. A metrics branch reusing chartProcedure inherits this — a bad shareId surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, not FORBIDDEN.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- `report.create` and `report.update` (packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:54-75, 97-119) are two additional hand-written field whitelists between `zReport` and the Prisma row. A `dataSource` value would never be persisted without editing both.
- `transformReport` demonstrably drops real columns today — `criteria`, `funnelGroup`, `funnelWindow`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` all exist on the Prisma `Report` model (schema.prisma:425-459) and none appear in the returned literal (reports.service.ts:91-115). This is empirical proof of the whitelist behavior, not an inference from reading the code.
- The public share page path is `trpc.share.report` (share.ts:266-297) → `transformReport` → client `<ReportChart>`, entirely separate from chartProcedure. Plan decision #4's promise that 'public share works unchanged' depends on this second read path carrying the discriminator.
- `overviewProcedure` (packages/trpc/src/routers/overview.ts:57-96) is a second, pre-existing copy of the exact chartProcedure share-validation pattern, with a comment reading 'The chart path does the same check.' The pattern is a convention with two instances; a metrics procedure has a template to copy rather than needing to be merged into chartProcedure.
- There is no test file covering chart.ts anywhere in packages/trpc — only access.test.ts, rate-limit.test.ts and routers/share.test.ts exist. The adjacent share router, by contrast, has a hostile-caller regression suite. Any change to chart.ts's security-relevant dispatch lands untested.
- `export.controller.charts()` hardcodes `chartType: 'linear'` at apps/api/src/controllers/export.controller.ts:215 and authenticates by client token via `getProjectId(request)`, not tRPC. It has no chartType or dataSource input at all today, so making it metrics-aware is a schema change to its Fastify querystring, not a dispatch tweak.
- `chartType: 'metric'` is routed by the browser to `trpc.chart.chart` (report-chart/metric/index.tsx:16), i.e. `ChartEngine.execute`, while every server-side dispatch (reports.service.ts:214, mcp/reports.ts:301, agents/tools/dashboard.ts:101) maps 'metric' to `AggregateChartEngine.execute`. The in-app path and the MCP/agent/REST paths already disagree about what a 'metric' report means — worth knowing before adding a second orthogonal discriminator on top.
- `enum ChartType` (schema.prisma:385-397) is a Postgres enum. If the design alternative is a 12th chartType instead of a `dataSource` column, the repo's own comment on `enum Metric` (schema.prisma:419-421) documents the constraint: new values must be appended last to match `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` or `prisma migrate` reports drift.
- Confirmed the installed zod is v4 (`pnpm-workspace.yaml:77` — `zod: ^4.1.8`), so the 'unknown keys are stripped' argument rests on the actual dependency, not on a zod-3 assumption. `zReportInput.and(z.object({shareId, id}))` is a ZodIntersection of two strip objects; the merged output carries shareId/id and nothing else unknown.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's premise survives — `chart.ts` genuinely is where share-aware, cached, `FinalChart`-returning execution lives, and `chartProcedure` is the right authorization primitive to reuse for a metrics procedure that must enforce project isolation as a security boundary. But the plan should stop describing this as "add a discriminator and branch in one place" and budget for the real shape of the change: (1) `dataSource` must be added to `zReportInput`/`zReport`, `report.create`, `report.update`, `transformReport`, and the Prisma model with a migration — five hand-maintained whitelists, not one; (2) the browser's `switch (report.chartType)` in report-chart/index.tsx is a second dispatch chart.ts cannot influence, so either metric reports reuse existing chartTypes or a client branch ships alongside; (3) five server-side executors (chart.ts, reports.service.getReportDataCore, mcp runReport, mcp runReportFromConfig, agents/tools/dashboard.ts) plus the client-token REST `export.controller.charts()` each need the branch, and `runReportFromConfig` takes an LLM-supplied config with no DB row, so an input-level discriminator is mandatory, not optional; (4) the share page reads through `trpc.share.report`, a separate procedure. Two lower-cost alternatives the plan should weigh explicitly: model metrics as new `ChartType` enum values (one enum migration, and every existing chartType-keyed dispatch already has a default branch to extend), or introduce a sibling `metrics.*` router modeled on `overviewProcedure` (overview.ts:57) and leave the event dispatches alone entirely. Finally, because the plan calls label enforcement a SECURITY BOUNDARY and chart.ts has zero test coverage today, any metrics procedure landing there should ship with a router test in the style of packages/trpc/src/routers/share.test.ts.

## Investigation 8 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived gigapipe's route table from scratch with a repo-wide grep for every route registration call, and every path the claim names exists exactly as stated — no invented paths. I also spot-verified the first engineer's citations line by line and found them accurate: main.go's bootSequence, the writer's six route files, the reader's eight registration calls, the ruler's QRYN_RULER_ENABLED gate, commonroutes, the view build tag, and the never-called RegisterRoutePlugin all say what they said. Their verdict of partially_confirmed is right and their correction list is substantially correct. I disagree with two of their framings (the Elastic wildcard shadowing risk is narrower than described, and RouteMiscApis is called — it is its body that is empty), and I found five things neither the claim nor their answer covers: a fourth MODE (init_only) that serves zero routes, gorilla/mux returning 405 rather than 404 on method mismatch, gorilla/mux 301-redirecting non-canonical paths before any handler runs, basic auth covering /ready and /metrics too, and the shared 64 MiB OTLP body cap with its env var.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim is accurate as far as it goes — every path it names is registered at exactly that path — but it is incomplete and states no HTTP methods, which matters because a gateway written against it will make wrong assumptions. I reach the same verdict as the first engineer by an independent route.
- Two disagreements with the first engineer's framing, neither of which changes their verdict. (1) They wrote that writer/plugin/utils.go registers "RouteMiscApis (the last is entirely commented out)". The CALL is live at utils.go:165; it is the function body in writer/router/misc.go:8-18 that is commented out. (2) They wrote that the Elastic wildcard routes "match any first path segment, so any proxy in front must allowlist exact paths rather than pass a prefix through". gorilla/mux matches on segment count and literal segments, so /{target}/_doc only captures two-segment paths whose second segment is literally _doc, and /{target}/_create/{id} only three-segment paths whose middle segment is literally _create. No gigapipe read route is shadowed by them. The allowlisting advice is still right — POST /anything/_doc and POST /_bulk are live log-ingest paths — but the stated mechanism overstates the risk.
- MODE has a fourth value neither the claim nor the first engineer mentions: init_only. main.go:310-312 returns before the router is even constructed (line 314), so an init_only node serves zero routes — not even /ready. It is documented at docs/configuration.md:69 as "Initialize database and exit" and appears in cmd/gigapipe/main_test.go:154.
- gorilla/mux returns 405, not 404, when the path matches but the method does not (mux.go:203-205, methodNotAllowedHandler). Since /loki/api/v1/query_range and friends are GET-only, a gateway that POSTs a long LogQL query gets a 405 with no body — worth handling distinctly from a 404 when probing which routes a given gigapipe build serves.
- gorilla/mux cleans the request path and issues a 301 Moved Permanently before any route is matched (mux.go:180-195). A gateway that forwards a path with a doubled slash or a dot segment (e.g. //loki/api/v1/push) gets a redirect, and most HTTP clients will not replay a POST body against a 301. Paths must be forwarded in canonical form.
- Basic auth, when QRYN_LOGIN/CLOKI_LOGIN and QRYN_PASSWORD/CLOKI_PASSWORD are both set, applies to every matched route including GET /ready, GET /metrics, GET /config and GET /api/status/buildinfo. gorilla applies Use middlewares at match time (mux.go:143-145), so the fact that commonroutes are registered at main.go:319 before app.Use(BasicAuthMiddleware) at 321-326 does not exempt them. Container health probes and any Prometheus scrape of gigapipe's own /metrics need credentials.
- /v1development/profiles is not protobuf-only. It gates application/json with an explicit 415 (profile.go:54-61) but then registers both an application/x-protobuf parser and a "*" fallback (profile.go:63-64), so any other content type is accepted. /ingest is the genuinely restrictive one: only multipart/form-data and binary/octet-stream, with its "*" fallback commented out at profile.go:45.
- Both OTLP transports share one body-size ceiling: 64 MiB by default, configurable via system_settings.otlp_max_message_size / QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (otlp_metrics.go:23-40). HTTP returns 413 above it, gRPC returns ResourceExhausted. A gateway that re-batches events before forwarding needs to respect this.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The plan's position that gigapipe's ruler is recording-only is confirmed in gigapipe's own prose, not merely inferred from code: docs/configuration.md's Recording Rules section states the ruler "is single-tenant and recording-only (alerting rules may be stored but are never evaluated)". Single-tenant is the second half of that sentence and is at least as load-bearing for this plan as recording-only — a per-project alerting design cannot delegate any part of evaluation to the ruler.
- Every subsystem registers onto the single root *mux.Router created at main.go:314; there is no subrouter and no path prefix anywhere in writer, reader, ruler or commonroutes. The gateway can therefore address gigapipe with the literal paths above and nothing else, but it also means there is no prefix the gateway could rely on to separate read from write traffic — MODE is the only separation mechanism.
- MODE=writer serves neither /ready's siblings nor any read route, but it does serve GET /ready, /config, /metrics and /api/status/buildinfo, because commonroutes are registered in main() before bootSequence runs and are ungated by mode. So a writer-only node is still health-checkable. Conversely MODE=reader still exposes /ready etc. but mounts no gRPC receiver (main_test.go:145-160).
- Running MODE=all with READONLY unset — the natural single-container choice — mounts the Elastic wildcard ingest routes (POST /{target}/_doc, POST /_bulk, /{target}/_bulk) alongside every read route on one port. If the plan's gateway ever proxies a path it did not construct itself, these are unauthenticated writes into the same database. An exact-path allowlist in apps/api, plus gigapipe basic auth, are both worth treating as part of the label-enforcement security boundary rather than as hardening extras.
- The gRPC receiver is not configurable — docs/otlp-grpc.md: "There is no environment variable to set... it is always on for nodes running in writer mode." A plan that intends every write to pass through apps/api first must therefore prevent network reachability of gigapipe's port (compose network isolation, no published port), because there is no in-process switch that turns the gRPC ingest path off while keeping HTTP ingest on.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim is safe to keep as a starting point but must not be used as the gateway's route contract. Three concrete changes to the plan. First, pin the gigapipe image at or after commit 60e22ea (/v1/metrics) and e7484e9 (OTLP/gRPC) — anything older 404s the metrics ingest path the plan depends on. Second, treat the endpoint list as method-and-condition-qualified rather than path-only: the metrics read path (/api/v1/query, /api/v1/query_range, /api/v1/labels, /api/v1/series) accepts POST, but the logs read path is GET-only, so the compiled-LogQL query string has to survive a URL, and /loki/api/v1/tail is a WebSocket the P3 logs explorer cannot consume with a plain fetch. If the P3 explorer wants patterns or detected fields, LOG_DRILLDOWN must be set in the compose template or those routes 404. Third, note the operational details that bite at P0: MODE=all plus no READONLY mounts wildcard Elastic write routes and an always-on cleartext-HTTP/2 gRPC ingest receiver on the same port, so the port must not be published and apps/api must allowlist exact paths; enabling gigapipe basic auth also locks GET /ready and GET /metrics, so health checks and any scrape of gigapipe's own process metrics need credentials; and paths must be forwarded canonically or gorilla/mux answers with a 301 that will silently drop a POST body.

## Investigation 9 — `partially_confirmed`

Same headline as the first engineer, but the substance differs on four points and I overturn three of their specific conclusions. Verified independently (via the npm registry, the on-machine npm/pnpm caches, and an extracted tarball rather than the lockfile alone): `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql` **does exist** — v0.314.0, exporting `parser: LRParser` plus `VectorSelector`/`LabelMatchers`/`MatchOp`/`LabelName` term constants, zero runtime deps, and versioned in lockstep with the very Prometheus release gigapipe vendors — so the claim's third leg is confirmed, not unverifiable. Conversely, `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer` is now verified **not** to do what the claim needs: its whole public surface is `ISerializer<ResourceMetrics, IExportMetricsServiceResponse>`, i.e. serialize-from-SDK-object and deserialize-the-*response* only, with no wire-request decoder in either 0.57.2 or 0.218.0. That is a refutation, not an open question. The claim's protobuf leg therefore rests entirely on `protobufjs` + vendored OTLP `.proto` files, which are absent from both repos. The first engineer's native-snappy risk analysis is wrong (snappy is napi-rs with no install scripts, and apps/api already ships the identical mechanism via `@node-rs/argon2`), and their statement that gigapipe takes OTLP JSON on `/v1/logs` is wrong — only `/v1/metrics` is dual-encoded; `/v1/logs` and `/v1/traces` are binary-protobuf-only.

**Evidence**

- `/private/tmp/.../otlp/package/build/src/i-serializer.d.ts (extracted from ~/.npm/_cacache, @opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.218.0)` — The library's complete contract: `serializeRequest(request: Request): Uint8Array | undefined;` and `deserializeResponse(data: Uint8Array): Response;` — the latter documented as "Deserialize the response from the backend." There is no `deserializeRequest`. This is the decisive file: it settles the question the first engineer marked unverifiable, and settles it against the claim.
- `/private/tmp/.../otlp/package/build/src/metrics/protobuf/metrics.d.ts` — `export declare const ProtobufMetricsSerializer: ISerializer<ResourceMetrics, IExportMetricsServiceResponse>;` with `import type { ResourceMetrics } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics'`. The `Request` generic is an SDK in-memory type, not an OTLP wire message — so even the encode direction is unusable for a gateway holding decoded wire data. `json/metrics.d.ts` is identical for `JsonMetricsSerializer`.
- `/private/tmp/.../otlp/package/build/src/common/protobuf/protobuf-reader.d.ts` — The only decoder in the package, and it is internal and deliberately partial: "Minimal binary protobuf reader. Only implements the wire-types that we currently need; this is not intended to be a general-purpose protobuf reader." `grep` shows it is consumed solely by `metrics|trace|logs/protobuf/response-deserializer.js`. Not re-exported from `build/src/index.d.ts`. (Also note 0.218.0 has dropped the protobufjs dependency entirely in favour of this hand-rolled reader/writer.)
- `https://unpkg.com/@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.57.2/build/src/index.d.ts` — The version actually pinned in this repo's lockfile exports the same surface as 0.218.0: six serializers (Protobuf/Json × Logs/Metrics/Trace), the `IExport*Response`/`IExport*PartialSuccess` response types, and `ISerializer`. Confirms the no-request-decoder finding is not an artifact of reading a newer release.
- `npm registry: https://registry.npmjs.org/@prometheus-io%2flezer-promql` — Refutes the first engineer's "cannot confirm it exists". Package exists; description "lezer-based PromQL grammar"; dist-tags latest `0.314.0`; 50+ versions; `main: dist/index.cjs`, `module: dist/index.es.js`, `types: dist/index.d.ts`, `exports: { import, require }`; no runtime dependencies; peerDeps `@lezer/lr ^1.2.3`, `@lezer/highlight ^1.1.2`.
- `https://unpkg.com/@prometheus-io/lezer-promql@0.314.0/dist/index.d.ts` — Exports `export const parser: LRParser` plus ~150 numeric term constants, including `VectorSelector`, `MatrixSelector`, `LabelMatchers`, `LabelName`, `MatchOp`, `MetricName`. This is precisely the API the plan's decision #3 requires for offset-based selector rewriting.
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prometheus/prometheus/v0.314.0/web/ui/module/lezer-promql/src/promql.grammar` — `VectorSelector { Identifier LabelMatchers | Identifier | LabelMatchers }`. The bare-`Identifier` alternative is an implementation trap the plan should record: for `up` the rewriter must synthesise a whole `{...}` block, not append into an existing one. `LabelMatchers` also admits `QuotedLabelMatcher`/`QuotedLabelName`, so the rewriter must handle UTF-8 quoted label syntax.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/utils/unmarshal/builder.go:516-529` — The line that refutes "gigapipe accepts OTLP JSON on /v1/logs": `func withParsedBody(fn func() proto.Message) buildOption { ... err := proto.Unmarshal(ctx.bodyBuffer, obj) ... }`. Binary protobuf only — there is no protojson branch in this helper.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/insert.go:142-153 and writer/utils/unmarshal/otlplogs.go:163-168` — `OTLPLogsV2` registers exactly one parser for all content types — `withSimpleParser("*", Parser(unmarshal.UnmarshalOTLPLogsV2))` — and `UnmarshalOTLPLogsV2 = Build(withBufferedBody, withParsedBody(func() proto.Message { return &otlplogs.LogsData{} }), ...)`. Hence `/v1/logs` is protobuf-only.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/tempo.go:37-55 and writer/utils/unmarshal/otlp.go:162-166` — The traces endpoint the first engineer never mentioned. `/v1/traces` (writer/router/tempo.go:12) → `OTLPPushV2` → `withSimpleParser("*", Parser(unmarshal.UnmarshalOTLPV2))` → `withParsedBody(func() proto.Message { return &tracev1.TracesData{} })` — protobuf-only. Its JSON sibling `PushV2` (tempo.go:17-24) parses **Zipkin** JSON, not OTLP: `withSimpleParser("ndjson", ...UnmarshalZipkinNDJSONV2)`, `withSimpleParser("*", ...UnmarshalZipkinJSONV2)`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:36-57` — Confirms metrics is the one genuinely dual endpoint: `withOTLPMetricsParser(otlpContentTypeProto, ... proto.Unmarshal ...)` and `withOTLPMetricsParser(otlpContentTypeJSON, ... protojson.UnmarshalOptions{DiscardUnknown: true}.Unmarshal ...)`, keyed into `ctx.Parser[contentType]`. The doc comment states it "accepts binary protobuf and JSON payloads, dispatched on Content-Type".
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/middleware.go:111-145` — Confirms the snappy-tolerance claim. `withUnsnappyRequest` calls `snappy.DecodedLen` then `snappy.Decode`; on error it takes the `ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, utils.ContextKeyBodyStream, bytes.NewBuffer(compressed))` branch marked `// Sending the compressed body back`. Also caps decompressed size at `10*1024*1024` with a 400 — a limit the first engineer did not mention and that bounds remote-write batch size.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-lock.yaml:24742-24752 and /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/package.json` — The in-repo precedent that kills the native-snappy objection. apps/api declares `"@node-rs/argon2": "^2.0.2"`, and the lockfile resolves it via `optionalDependencies:` over `@node-rs/argon2-{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-arm64-gnu,linux-arm64-musl,linux-x64-gnu,linux-x64-musl,...}: 2.0.2` — the identical napi-rs prebuilt-binary mechanism `snappy@7.4.2` uses, already shipping in this image.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/pnpm-workspace.yaml:89-116` — The comment says the opposite of the first engineer's reading: "under pnpm 10.6.2 not one of these scripts ran, and the images worked anyway (prebuilt binaries + the explicit `pnpm rebuild` and `pnpm codegen` steps in the Dockerfiles do the real work)." The breakage came from "Flipping them to true" so that "sharp's newly-running install script tried to compile via node-gyp". `allowBuilds` is an install-script allowlist; snappy has no install scripts (npm registry, 7.4.2), so it is out of scope.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/Dockerfile:1-3, 69-83` — `ARG NODE_VERSION=24.19.0` / `FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-slim` — Debian/glibc, so the `-gnu` napi-rs prebuilds apply and the musl variants are irrelevant. The prod stage's `ENV npm_config_build_from_source=true` + `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod && pnpm rebuild` is the same stage `@node-rs/argon2` already survives.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/promql/promql_transpiler/transpiler_v2.go:84-85` — The concrete Go-side enforcement hook the plan should name: the recursive walk handles every expression type and reaches `case *parser.VectorSelector:` followed by a bare `// No-op`. Every selector in a parsed query passes through this exact line.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/promql/promql_transpiler/optimizer/substitute.go:17-26 and reader/promql/promql_parser/nodes.go:38-58` — Refines the first engineer's "gigapipe ... does not rewrite selectors" — it does: `substituteSelector` clones a `*prom_parser.VectorSelector`, sets `sub.Name` and clears `sub.LabelMatchers = nil`. What is genuinely absent is tenancy policy, not rewriting machinery: the `nodes.go` wrapper is read-only (`GetLabelMatchers`, `GetOp`, `GetLabel`, `GetVal` — no setters).
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/go.mod:27, 44, 51 and writer/utils/proto/prompb.proto:1-40` — `github.com/golang/snappy v1.0.0`, `github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.314.0`, `go.opentelemetry.io/proto/otlp v1.11.0`. The Prometheus pin exactly matches `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql`'s latest 0.314.0 — same PromQL dialect on both sides. `prompb.proto` declares `message WriteRequest { repeated prometheus.TimeSeries timeseries = 1; }` with no metadata field, i.e. remote-write v1, and is directly consumable by protobufjs.
- `Filesystem survey (find/grep, read-only)` — Zero `.proto` files anywhere under /Users/drew/projects/openpanel; gigapipe has exactly seven, none OTLP; the Go module cache under ~/go/pkg/mod/go.opentelemetry.io contains no OTLP `.proto` (only jaegerremote's `sampling.proto`). Separately, /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/node_modules does not exist (0 entries), but a 4.9G pnpm store (3824 packages) and 7.4G npm cacache DO exist on this machine — contra the first engineer's "no package manager cache for it is present". Neither cache contains snappy, lezer-promql, or any `@prometheus-io/*`; the pnpm store does hold 18 `@lezer/*` grammars and `protobufjs@8.8.0` from unrelated projects.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- OVERTURNS THE FIRST ENGINEER (and confirms the claim): `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql` exists and is current. They said they "could not verify that [it] exists, is maintained, or what it exports." The npm registry returns it: description "lezer-based PromQL grammar", dist-tags latest `0.314.0` (plus an `rc` 0.314.0-rc.0), 50+ published versions, dual CJS/ESM (`dist/index.cjs` / `dist/index.es.js`) with bundled `dist/index.d.ts`, **zero runtime dependencies**, peerDeps `@lezer/lr ^1.2.3` and `@lezer/highlight ^1.1.2`. Both peers are already resolved in this monorepo (`@lezer/lr@1.4.7` pnpm-lock.yaml:5165, `@lezer/highlight@1.2.3` pnpm-lock.yaml:5156). Its `dist/index.d.ts` exports `parser: LRParser` and ~150 numeric term constants including `VectorSelector`, `MatrixSelector`, `LabelMatchers`, `LabelName`, `MatchOp`, `MetricName` — exactly the surface a selector rewriter needs. Their negative was an artifact of searching only on-disk lockfiles for a package the repo has never installed.
- OVERTURNS THE FIRST ENGINEER, and REFUTES the claim's first leg: `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer` cannot decode OTLP requests, and this is now verified rather than "unverified". They flagged it as "the single riskiest line in the claim" but could not check because node_modules is absent. I extracted the real tarball from this machine's npm cacache. The entire contract is `i-serializer.d.ts`: `serializeRequest(request: Request): Uint8Array | undefined` and `deserializeResponse(data: Uint8Array): Response`, where the docstring says Response is "the response from the backend". `build/src/metrics/protobuf/metrics.d.ts` pins the generic: `ISerializer<ResourceMetrics, IExportMetricsServiceResponse>` — `Request` is `ResourceMetrics` from `@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics`, an SDK in-memory type, not an OTLP wire message. So it encodes only *from SDK objects* and decodes only the tiny partial-success *response*. The version pinned in the lockfile (0.57.2) has an identical export list. There is no wire-bytes-to-mutable-object path in either. A gateway that must decode an inbound ExportTraceServiceRequest, overwrite `op_project_id`, and re-emit gets nothing from this library.
- OVERTURNS THE FIRST ENGINEER: their claim that "a native snappy binding lands squarely in that [allowBuilds/node-gyp] failure mode" is wrong on both halves. (a) `snappy@7.4.2` is a **napi-rs** module with **no install or postinstall scripts at all**; it ships prebuilt per-platform binaries as `optionalDependencies` (`@napi-rs/snappy-linux-x64-gnu`, `-linux-arm64-gnu`, `-linux-x64-musl`, etc.). `allowBuilds` governs *install-script* approval, so snappy would never appear on that list. (b) apps/api **already depends on an identical napi-rs package today**: `"@node-rs/argon2": "^2.0.2"` (apps/api/package.json), resolved in pnpm-lock.yaml:24742-24752 as `optionalDependencies` over per-platform binaries — and it ships successfully in the very Dockerfile they cite as dangerous. The workspace comment they quoted actually says the opposite of their reading: the images "worked anyway (prebuilt binaries + the explicit `pnpm rebuild` ...)" under allowBuilds:false; the sharp breakage happened when allowBuilds was flipped **to true**, letting sharp's install script run under `npm_config_build_from_source=true`. Base image is `node:24.19.0-slim` (Debian/glibc), so the `-gnu` prebuilds apply and musl is irrelevant.
- OVERTURNS THE FIRST ENGINEER on a load-bearing point: "gigapipe accepts OTLP JSON on `/v1/metrics` **and `/v1/logs`**" is half wrong, and the conclusion they drew from it ("the OpenPanel→gigapipe hop needs neither protobuf nor snappy") only holds for metrics. `/v1/logs` → `OTLPLogsV2` (writer/controller/insert.go:142-153) registers a **single** parser for all content types, `withSimpleParser("*", Parser(unmarshal.UnmarshalOTLPLogsV2))`; that resolves to `withParsedBody(func() proto.Message { return &otlplogs.LogsData{} })` (writer/utils/unmarshal/otlplogs.go:163-168), and `withParsedBody` is **`proto.Unmarshal` only** (writer/utils/unmarshal/builder.go:516-529) — no protojson anywhere in that path. `/v1/traces` is identical (tempo.go:37-55 → otlp.go:162-166 → same `withParsedBody`). Only `/v1/metrics` has the bespoke dual dispatch (otlp_metrics.go:36-57). So OTLP logs and traces to gigapipe require binary protobuf **encode** in Node. The JSON escape hatches that do exist are not OTLP — they are Loki JSON (`/loki/api/v1/push`) and Zipkin JSON (`/tempo/spans`, `/api/v2/spans`), different schemas needing a lossy translation step in the gateway. That is more work than protobuf encode, not less.
- The claim's phrase "@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer **or** protobufjs against opentelemetry-proto" presents two options where only one is real. Given the finding above, protobufjs + vendored `.proto` is the only viable route — and I confirm the first engineer's point that the schemas are missing: `find` returns **zero** `.proto` files anywhere in /Users/drew/projects/openpanel, and gigapipe has exactly seven, none of them OTLP. The Go module cache holds no OTLP `.proto` either (only an unrelated jaeger-idl `sampling.proto`). OTLP schemas must be vendored from open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto and version-tracked. By contrast `writer/utils/proto/prompb.proto` and `loki.proto` are on disk and directly consumable by protobufjs.
- The claim treats "snappy for Prometheus remote-write" as one requirement; it is two, and only one is mandatory — I confirm the first engineer here. Outbound (OpenPanel→gigapipe) is optional because `withUnsnappyRequest` restores the original body when `snappy.DecodedLen`/`snappy.Decode` fails (writer/controller/middleware.go:111-145, the `// Sending the compressed body back` branch at 135-137), so an uncompressed `prompb.WriteRequest` is accepted. Inbound (a customer's Prometheus → apps/api) is mandatory, since Prometheus always snappy-compresses. Only the inbound leg justifies the dependency — and note `snappyjs@0.7.0` is a pure-JS zero-dependency alternative, though it was last published June 2022 and is effectively unmaintained.
- Both confirmed npm packages are TRANSITIVE, not direct — I confirm this and verified the exact citations. `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.57.2` (pnpm-lock.yaml:6078) and `protobufjs@7.4.0` (pnpm-lock.yaml:16344) arrive only via `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry` (catalog `^0.10.3`). I corroborated the dependency edge from an independent source — the cached npm registry document for otlp-transformer lists 0.57.2's deps as `protobufjs: ^7.3.0` plus core/api-logs/sdk-* — so it is not merely a lockfile artifact. apps/api/package.json declares neither. Relying on them without explicit dependencies is a phantom-dependency bug.
- Minor citation drift in their evidence, all in their favor but worth correcting for a plan doc: `PushStreamV2` is writer/controller/insert.go:**49-60**, not 47-56; the OTLP metrics dual-parser block is otlp_metrics.go:**36-57**; `withUnsnappyRequest` is middleware.go:**111-145**. Their pnpm-lock and pnpm-workspace line numbers (6078, 16344, 16305, 107-127, 116) are exact, and `grep -c` confirms **zero** matches for `snappy` and `lezer-promql` in pnpm-lock.yaml.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql` is published from the prometheus/prometheus monorepo (`web/ui/module/lezer-promql`) and versioned with the Prometheus release itself — latest 0.314.0, byte-for-byte the same version gigapipe vendors at go.mod:44. The plan should turn this into a policy: pin the grammar to gigapipe's Prometheus version and gate upgrades on both moving together. A dialect skew between the Node rewriter and the Go executor is not a cosmetic bug — if the rewriter fails to recognise a selector form the executor accepts, the mandatory `op_project_id` matcher is silently omitted, which is a cross-tenant read.
- The grammar's `VectorSelector { Identifier LabelMatchers | Identifier | LabelMatchers }` production has three shapes, and only one is an append. A bare `up` requires synthesising `{op_project_id="..."}`; a bare `{__name__="up"}` requires insertion into an existing brace list; and `QuotedLabelMatcher`/`QuotedLabelName` mean UTF-8 quoted label syntax must be handled too. Any rewriter that assumes "find the `{` and insert" is wrong for two of the three cases.
- gigapipe exposes a trace ingest endpoint the first engineer's review never mentions: `/v1/traces` at writer/router/tempo.go:12, plus `/tempo/spans` and `/api/v2/spans` (Zipkin JSON) and `/tempo/api/push`. P4 depends on this and the plan should record that the OTLP form is protobuf-only while the Zipkin form is JSON.
- `withUnsnappyRequest` rejects any remote-write body whose *decompressed* size exceeds `10*1024*1024` with a 400 "body is too long" (middleware.go:133-135). That is a hard 10 MiB cap on the inbound remote-write path, unrelated to and much smaller than the 64 MiB `OTLPMaxMessageSize` the first engineer cited for OTLP. It also sits well under apps/api's own `bodyLimit: 1_048_576 * 500` (~500 MB, app.ts:88), so the gateway must chunk or reject oversized remote-write batches itself rather than relying on either limit matching.
- A pure-JS escape hatch exists for the inbound snappy requirement: `snappyjs@0.7.0`, zero dependencies, no native bindings, exporting `compress`/`uncompress`. But it was last published in June 2022 and is effectively unmaintained — a supply-chain tradeoff the plan should state explicitly rather than leave implicit, especially since the napi-rs `snappy` is now shown to carry no packaging risk.
- Newer `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer` releases (0.218.0) have dropped the `protobufjs` dependency entirely in favour of a hand-rolled minimal reader/writer. So the transitive `protobufjs@7.4.0` the plan currently leans on is an artifact of the old 0.57.2 pin and will vanish if `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry` ever bumps its OTel range. This makes the phantom-dependency risk concrete rather than theoretical: protobufjs must be a direct dependency of apps/api.
- The gateway needs a binary body parser that does not exist yet. `grep` confirms there is no `addContentTypeParser` anywhere in apps/api/src, and the sole `fastify-raw-body` consumer treats the body as a string (`request.rawBody!` at apps/api/src/controllers/webhook.controller.ts:416, registered per-route via `rawBody: true` at apps/api/src/routes/webhook.router.ts:15). Accepting `application/x-protobuf` as a Buffer is net-new work on the inbound leg regardless of which decode library wins.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's node-libraries line must be rewritten in three places. (1) Drop `@opentelemetry/otlp-transformer` from the decode/encode story entirely — it is an export-side serializer over SDK types with no request decoder. The gateway's OTLP codec is `protobufjs` plus OTLP `.proto` files vendored from open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto and pinned to a stated version; that vendoring is a real P1 task with an ongoing upstream-tracking cost, not a dependency line. (2) Restore `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql` as a confirmed, low-risk choice: it exists at 0.314.0, has zero runtime deps, ships its own types, and its two peers are already in the monorepo — but they sit in apps/start's graph via codemirror, so apps/api needs its own explicit `@lezer/lr` + `@lezer/highlight` entries. Its version tracking Prometheus releases is a genuine asset the plan should exploit: pin the grammar to the same Prometheus version gigapipe vendors (both are 0.314.0 today, go.mod:44) and treat divergence as a release-gate check, since a dialect skew between the JS rewriter and the Go executor is a silent tenancy-bypass risk. (3) Delete the native-module packaging caveat for snappy; it is unfounded, and `@node-rs/argon2` is the in-repo precedent that settles it. The larger correction is to P3/P4 sequencing: the plan cannot assume a uniform "forward everything to gigapipe as JSON" write path. Metrics can go as OTLP JSON, but logs and traces over OTLP are protobuf-only, so either the gateway gains a protobuf encoder (making protobufjs load-bearing on the outbound leg too, not just inbound) or logs/traces route through Loki-JSON and Zipkin-JSON with a schema translation that loses OTLP fidelity. Decide that explicitly per signal rather than inheriting a false "JSON everywhere" premise. Finally, the plan should name the Go-side alternative concretely: gigapipe's transpiler already walks every node type and has a literal empty `case *parser.VectorSelector: // No-op` at reader/promql/promql_transpiler/transpiler_v2.go:84 — that is where a mandatory-matcher hook belongs, and it is a materially smaller and safer surface than a JS rewriter, since enforcement would sit inside the engine that actually executes the query rather than in a string transformation upstream of it.

## Investigation 10 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived gigapipe's route table independently — a repo-wide grep for every `HandleFunc`/`Handle`/`PathPrefix` registration, then the runtime path from `cmd/gigapipe/main.go`'s `start()` outward through middleware, plus `cmd/gigapipe/main_test.go`, `docs/`, and git log — and I reach the same verdict as the first engineer. Every path in the claim exists and is registered at exactly the path stated; none is invented. But the claim enumerates roughly a third of the real route table, states no HTTP methods (which are genuinely non-obvious: the Loki read routes are GET-only), lists `/loki/api/v1/patterns` unconditionally when it is gated on `LOG_DRILLDOWN`, and misfiles `/api/metrics/query_range` as a Prometheus endpoint when it is Tempo's TraceQL-metrics handler. I verified essentially every one of the first engineer's ~25 evidence citations by opening the files: all of them exist and say what they claim, with correct line numbers. I found four things they missed that bear on the plan: a global HTTP Basic auth gate (`CLOKI_LOGIN`/`CLOKI_PASSWORD`) applied to every route including `/ready` and `/metrics` and mirrored onto the gRPC receiver; a fifth `MODE=init_only`; a `Content-Type`-matching detail that makes an absent header a hard 400 on `/v1/metrics`; and direct confirmation (by absence) that the reader accepts no per-request tenant header at all.

**Evidence**

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim is incomplete, not wrong: every path it names is real and registered at exactly that path, but it covers roughly a third of the route table. I confirm the first engineer's full enumeration by independent grep and endorse all their corrections — I found no error in any of their ~25 citations, and their line numbers are accurate.
- Missing from the first engineer's answer, and the most consequential omission for this plan: gigapipe has a GLOBAL HTTP Basic auth gate. CLOKI_LOGIN/CLOKI_PASSWORD (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:175-182) feed app.Use(middleware.BasicAuthMiddleware(...)) at main.go:322-326. Because gorilla/mux applies Use to every matched route irrespective of registration order, this covers the entire table including the commonroutes /ready, /config and /metrics — so a naive liveness probe against /ready will 401 once credentials are set. The same credentials are ported onto the gRPC receiver as interceptors (writer/grpc/server.go:101-103), whereas CORS and response gzip deliberately are NOT (writer/grpc/mux.go:19-21). Setting these is how the plan keeps gigapipe unexposed, and the gateway must send the header on every call.
- There is a fifth MODE the first engineer's gating analysis omits: MODE=init_only (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:306-312). It runs initDB to bootstrap the ClickHouse schema and then returns BEFORE mux.NewRouter() is called — zero routes, no listener. For a plan that provisions a second database on an existing ClickHouse instance, this is the intended schema-bootstrap entry point.
- Sharper than the first engineer's content-type note: because builder.go:135 matches with strings.HasPrefix(contentType, k), an ABSENT or empty Content-Type header matches no registered key, and /v1/metrics has no "*" fallback — so a POST /v1/metrics with no Content-Type is a hard 400 'Content-Type not supported', not a default-to-protobuf. The gateway must set it explicitly on every metrics forward. Separately, that same loop is a Go map range with a break, so any endpoint whose parser keys overlap as prefixes would resolve nondeterministically; none currently do, but it is a latent hazard for anyone patching in a parser.
- The Prometheus query engine has a real capability limit neither the claim nor the first engineer mentions: reader/router/prometheus_query_range.go:41-42 sets EnableAtModifier: true but EnableNegativeOffset: FALSE. The plan's zMetricQuery -> PromQL compiler (and any later raw-PromQL parser gate) must reject negative offsets, which stock Prometheus accepts.
- OTLP payload size is bounded at 64 MiB by default, shared across HTTP and gRPC, configurable via system_settings.otlp_max_message_size / QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:25-42). Oversize HTTP bodies get 413. The gateway's own body limits should be set at or below this.
- Minor precision fix to the first engineer's evidence, not a disagreement: they wrote that RouteMiscApis on the writer side is 'entirely commented out'. The CALL is live at writer/plugin/utils.go:166; it is the function BODY at writer/router/misc.go:9-17 that is commented out. Same zero routes registered, but the phrasing would mislead someone grepping for the call site.
- Default listen port is 3100 (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:302-304), overridable by PORT; HOST defaults to 0.0.0.0 (main.go:193-200). Neither the claim nor the first engineer states the port, which the self-hosting compose template will need.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Global Basic auth via CLOKI_LOGIN/CLOKI_PASSWORD wraps every route including /ready, /config and /metrics (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:175-182, 322-326), and is mirrored onto the gRPC receiver via interceptors (writer/grpc/server.go:101-103). The plan should use it and must account for authenticated health checks.
- gigapipe implements NO read-time tenant header. X-Scope-OrgID appears exactly once repo-wide, in ruler/controller/controller.go:3 as 'single-tenant — no X-Scope-OrgID is read.' X-CH-DSN/X-Scope-Meta exist only on writer HTTP paths and gRPC metadata. This is affirmative confirmation that label enforcement is the only available isolation mechanism on the read side.
- MODE=init_only (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:306-312) bootstraps the ClickHouse schema and exits without registering routes or binding a listener — the natural one-shot migration step for standing up the second database.
- EnableNegativeOffset is false in the reader's PromQL engine (reader/router/prometheus_query_range.go:42). The zMetricQuery compiler and any future raw-PromQL gate must reject negative offsets that stock Prometheus would accept. EnableAtModifier is true; MaxSamples is ADVANCED_PROMETHEUS_MAX_SAMPLES; query timeout is a fixed 30s (not configurable), which bounds the worst-case dashboard query.
- OTLP payloads are capped at 64 MiB across both transports via system_settings.otlp_max_message_size / QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:25-42); oversize HTTP bodies return 413.
- A POST to /v1/metrics with no Content-Type header returns 400, not a protobuf default — builder.go:135 matches by strings.HasPrefix, which never matches an empty string, and /v1/metrics registers no "*" fallback.
- grpc-web is explicitly unsupported on the gRPC receiver (writer/grpc/mux.go:11-15), and gRPC requests bypass the HTTP middleware chain entirely — so CORS and response gzip do not apply there. If the plan ever wants browser-side OTLP, it is OTLP/HTTP only.
- The boot ordering and mode gating are pinned by tests (cmd/gigapipe/main_test.go), which cite two real shipped regressions. This raises confidence that the mode semantics the plan depends on are stable, not incidental.
- Default port 3100, default host 0.0.0.0 (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:193-200, 302-304) — needed for the self-hosting compose template.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's five load-bearing decisions all survive; nothing here forces a redesign. Three concrete adjustments follow. (1) Add Basic auth to the P0 stack decision: set CLOKI_LOGIN/CLOKI_PASSWORD on the gigapipe service and have apps/api send the Authorization header on every ingest and query call. This is a second, cheap layer under the 'gigapipe is never exposed' decision, but it also means the health check the compose template uses cannot be a bare GET /ready — it must carry credentials. (2) Decision #2's premise is now confirmed by absence rather than inference: X-Scope-OrgID appears nowhere in the repo except a comment denying it, and X-CH-DSN exists only on writer paths. Label enforcement is not merely the better option, it is the only one — the reader has no tenant input at all. Write that up as the justification rather than the reader's single-database binding alone, which is the weaker argument. (3) The P2 metrics compiler must (a) always set Content-Type on /v1/metrics forwards or get a 400, (b) never emit negative offsets, and (c) treat 64 MiB as the ingest ceiling. For P3 logs, plan for GET-only Loki read routes — long LogQL queries go in the query string, and if they exceed the proxy's URL limit the fix is a shorter compiled query, not a POST body. Live tailing needs a WebSocket proxy, not fetch, so if P3 scopes tail, budget for it; if not, say so explicitly. If the logs explorer wants pattern detection, LOG_DRILLDOWN must be set at boot. For P5 alerts, the ruler's own package doc confirms alert evaluation belongs in OpenPanel's worker. Finally, pin the gigapipe image at or after e7484e9 — /v1/metrics and the gRPC receiver are the 3rd and 4th commits from HEAD.

Every one of the first engineer's ~25 cites exists and says what they said it says, including the three-valued type constant, the tp==3→0 collapse, the eight tables touched by Rotate, the absence of any TTL clause in the CREATE statements, and samples_v3 being the one table whose ORDER BY was left as (timestamp_ns). I also found four things neither the claim nor they mention that bear on the plan: the 7-day default is applied only on the pure-env config path, DefaultTtlDays is a dead template var, ADVANCED_SAMPLES_ORDERING is a fresh-install-only knob, and the fingerprint/type collision hazard is stronger than they stated.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's shape is right: one samples_v3 table (fingerprint, timestamp_ns, value, string, + type UInt8 added by ALTER) holds logs and metrics; time_series holds the JSON label set per fingerprint and time_series_gin is the (key,val)->fingerprint inverted index; metrics_15s + metrics_15s_mv is the 15-second AggregatingMergeTree rollup. I confirmed all of this independently from ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql and from both writer insert services.
- `type` has three values, not two: 0 = UNDEF/both, 1 = LOG, 2 = METRIC (writer/model/insert_request.go:8-12). Value 0 is actively written whenever a Loki-JSON entry carries both a line and a numeric value (unmarshal.go:163-165 and 225-228, `if tp == 3 { tp = 0 }`), and every reader predicate is `type IN (n, 0)` (sql_misc.go:213-220). Anything that assumes equality will silently drop rows.
- SAMPLES_DAYS is not scoped to samples_v3. ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:122-208 applies the same scalar as a MODIFY TTL to eight tables across three signals: samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, metrics_15s, patterns, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv. The profiles tables are not rotated at all.
- The default retention is not in any CREATE statement. `grep -rni 'ttl' ctrl/qryn/sql/*.sql` returns zero matches; retention is asserted only by ctrl.Rotate on every boot (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:66-82) and skipped wholesale when OMIT_CREATE_TABLES is set.
- I DISAGREE with the first engineer's correction that metrics_15s reads carry 'no type predicate' and that 'type isolation on the rollup depends solely on the type-filtered fingerprint subquery'. That is true only of the PromQL path. reader/logql/logql_transpiler/clickhouse_planner/planner_metrics15s_shortcut.go:57 puts GetTypes(ctx) directly into the WHERE of a query whose FROM is ctx.Metrics15sDistTableName (line 71). LogQL rate/count_over_time over the rollup IS type-filtered; PromQL (bucket_producer.go:52-56, downsample_values.go:32) is not. The behaviour is path-dependent, not absolute.
- The first engineer's cite of tables.go:44-55 as where 'the reader picks the _dist name' is imprecise. That function only rewrites map entries. Selection happens in PopulateTableNames: line 74 assigns SamplesDistTableName from the NON-dist key, and only the `if db.Config.ClusterName != ""` branch at lines 99-115 substitutes the suffixed distributed name. In the single-node topology the plan assumes, dist and local table names are identical.
- 'metrics_15s as a 15-second aggregate MV' is misleading if read as metrics-only. metrics_15s_mv (log.sql:146-158) has no WHERE and groups by (fingerprint, timestamp_ns, type), so log rows are rolled up too; its `bytes` column is sumSimpleState(length(string)), which exists to serve LogQL volume queries.
- samples_v3 is the one table where `type` was NOT added to the sort key — it keeps ORDER BY (timestamp_ns) (log.sql:32 + 119-120, with SAMPLES_ORDER_RUL defaulting to "timestamp_ns" at update.go:214), while time_series, time_series_gin and metrics_15s all got type appended. Per-type filtering on samples_v3 is a scan within the day partition.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The 7-day default only applies on the pure-env config path. cmd/gigapipe/main.go:84-86 makes portCHEnv return immediately when cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA is already populated, and `TTLDays = 7` lives inside that function (line 146). If OpenPanel ships gigapipe with a config file supplying database_data rather than env vars, TTLDays is whatever the file says, and maintain.go:28-29 hard-errors 'ttl_days should be set for node#' at boot when it is 0. The plan should pin gigapipe to env-only configuration or explicitly set ttl_days.
- There is a `DefaultTtlDays` template variable (update.go:212, 229, 338, defaulting to "30") that no .sql file ever references. It is dead. Anyone reading the maintenance code could mistake it for a schema-level TTL default; it is not one.
- ADVANCED_SAMPLES_ORDERING (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:123-124 -> SamplesOrdering -> update.go:221-223 -> {{.SAMPLES_ORDER_RUL}} at log.sql:32) is the ONLY lever over samples_v3's ORDER BY, and it is interpolated only into the CREATE TABLE statement. It is therefore a fresh-install-only knob: once samples_v3 exists in the OpenPanel ClickHouse instance, its sort key is frozen. If the plan wants op_project_id-adjacent locality or `type` in the sort key, that decision must be made at first boot, before any telemetry lands.
- There is a latent read-correctness hazard stronger than the first engineer stated. fingerprintLabels (unmarshal.go:250-270) hashes only label key/value pairs, so a log stream and a metric series with an identical label set collide on one fingerprint. The PromQL rollup read (bucket_producer.go:52-56) selects from metrics_15s filtered only by timestamp range and `fingerprint IN (fp)`, and the fp subquery (planner_stream_select.go:72-80) returns the fingerprint because it exists with type 2 — but metrics_15s rows for that same fingerprint with type 1 (log rollups, value 0) are then aggregated in as well. In practice metrics carry __name__ and logs do not, so collisions are unlikely, but this is a real failure mode the label-enforcement design should not make more likely (e.g. by stamping the same op_project_id-only label set on both signals).
- Type assignment is universal across ingest protocols, wider than the first engineer enumerated: datadog_json.go:95, datadog_cf_json.go:46 and elastic.go:35,114 -> LOG; datadog_metrics_json.go:40 -> METRIC; influx.go:99 -> LOG and :121 -> METRIC; otlplogs.go:82 -> LOG; otlp_metrics.go:307 -> METRIC; metrics_protobuf.go:46,61 -> METRIC; logs_protobuf.go:33 -> LOG. Only the Loki-JSON both-fields case produces type 0. If OpenPanel restricts ingest to OTLP + Prometheus remote-write + Loki push protobuf, type 0 never occurs and the two-value mental model becomes safe — but that is a constraint the gateway must actually enforce, not an assumption.
- The `type_v2` ALIAS exists on the LOCAL tables too (log.sql:162-172), not just the _dist ones. That is what lets reader/service/query_range.go:853 use type_v2 on a single-node install. Worth knowing if the plan ever inspects or extends these tables directly.
- Migration ordering means a fresh install produces exactly the same schema as an upgraded one: updateScripts (update.go:258-285) replays every statement in log.sql in file order from the `ver` watermark, so CREATE TABLE samples_v3 runs and is then immediately ALTERed to add `type` without a sort-key change. There is no 'new install gets a better schema' escape hatch.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's per-signal retention item stands and is slightly harder than written: there is no per-type TTL, no per-tenant TTL (X-Ttl-Days and __ttl_days__ are parsed but never reach an INSERT — verified across all seven INSERT statements in writer/service/insert/), and one SAMPLES_DAYS value drives eight tables including traces. Conditional ClickHouse TTL on samples_v3 will also be a scan rather than a prefix seek, because samples_v3 alone kept ORDER BY (timestamp_ns); and any hand-written TTL will be silently overwritten by ctrl.Rotate on the next gigapipe boot unless OMIT_CREATE_TABLES is set, which also disables schema upgrades. Two additions the plan should absorb: (1) if OpenPanel wants type or project locality in samples_v3's sort key, ADVANCED_SAMPLES_ORDERING must be set before the very first boot, since it only affects CREATE TABLE; (2) configure gigapipe by env vars only, or explicitly set ttl_days, because the 7-day default is skipped entirely when a config file supplies database_data and boot then fails. Finally, correct the first engineer's note in the plan doc: metrics_15s reads ARE type-filtered on the LogQL path and are NOT on the PromQL path, so a metrics-only reading of the rollup is unsafe for PromQL specifically.

## Investigation 12 — `partially_confirmed`

I reach the same top-line verdict as the first engineer but for materially different reasons, and two of their load-bearing corrections are wrong. Settled from source: `@prometheus-io/lezer-promql` definitively exists, is actively maintained (135 published versions, latest 0.314.0 — exactly matching gigapipe's vendored `github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.314.0`), and its tarball is on this machine in `~/.npm/_cacache`, which the first engineer missed while asserting no cache existed. Their biggest error is the assertion that gigapipe accepts OTLP JSON on `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/logs`: only `/v1/metrics` has a protojson branch; `/v1/logs` and `/v1/traces` are binary-protobuf-only for every content type, so protobuf encode IS required outbound for two of three OTLP signals. snappy remains the one genuinely unverifiable item — zero presence in either lockfile, the pnpm store index, or the npm cache.
