**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "SAMPLES_DAYS applies globally to the table" is doubly imprecise. It reaches eight tables across three signals (rotate.go:155-210: samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv, metrics_15s, patterns) — so raising it for log retention also extends trace and label retention — and it is not read at all unless DATABASE_DATA is empty at startup (main.go:84-87), i.e. a config-file deployment ignores the env var entirely.
- The `type` column has three values, not the two the claim implies: 0 = UNDEF/both, 1 = LOG, 2 = METRIC (writer/model/insert_request.go:8-12). 0 is actively written for Loki-JSON entries carrying both a line and a value (unmarshal.go:163, 225), and every reader predicate is `type IN (n, 0)` (sql_misc.go:213-220). Any per-type retention, per-type read, or type-based metering that assumes equality drops or misattributes the type-0 rows.
- `type` discriminates the signal logically but not physically on samples_v3: it is in neither the sort key (log.sql:119-120 adds the column with no MODIFY ORDER BY; SAMPLES_ORDER_RUL defaults to "timestamp_ns", update.go:214) nor the partition key (PARTITION BY toStartOfDay). Combined with ttl_only_drop_parts=1 (rotate.go:78-79), per-signal retention on samples_v3 is not expressible as a partition drop, and any per-type filter is a scan within the day partition.
- "metrics_15s as a 15-second aggregate MV" reads as metrics-only and is not. metrics_15s_mv has no WHERE and rolls up log rows too (log.sql:146-158), its `bytes` column exists to serve LogQL volume, and LogQL's rate()/count_over_time() reads it directly (planner_metrics15s_shortcut.go:71). It is a shared rollup for both signals.
- The claim's implicit column split — `value` for metrics, `string` for logs — no longer holds. OTLP metric data points write an exemplar trace id into samples_v3.string (otlp_metrics.go:293-308, docs/otlp-metrics.md:68-72). Metric rows therefore have a non-empty string, and metrics_15s.bytes = sumSimpleState(length(string)) accumulates 32 bytes per exemplar-bearing metric sample. Any "log bytes ingested" metering read off metrics_15s.bytes without a type filter over-counts metrics.
- The claim omits that none of this retention is in the DDL. No file under ctrl/qryn/sql contains the string TTL; the TTL is asserted by ALTER on every boot via ctrl.Rotate (ctrl.go:40-55, main.go:66-83) and skipped entirely under OMIT_CREATE_TABLES.
- "time_series / time_series_gin for labels" flattens a distinction the plan will need: time_series holds the whole JSON label set (plus, since the metadata migration, a `metadata` JSON column and `updated_at_ns`, log.sql:189-193) and is what the label-rendering and empty-label paths read; time_series_gin is the (key,val)->fingerprint inverted index populated by time_series_gin_view via ARRAY JOIN JSONExtractKeysAndValues, and is what every label matcher reads.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Where I disagree with the first engineer: their statement that metrics_15s carries "no type predicate" and that "type isolation on the rollup depends solely on the type-filtered fingerprint subquery" is over-general. reader/logql/logql_transpiler/clickhouse_planner/planner_metrics15s_shortcut.go:57 applies GetTypes(ctx) to the metrics_15s read on the LogQL path, and reader/promql/promql_transpiler/planner/values.go:27 applies it to the PromQL raw-samples read. The gap is confined to the two PromQL rollup planners (bucket_producer.go:51-58, downsample_values.go:32-35). Their conclusion still stands for the PromQL path the metrics plan depends on, but the plan should not be written as if metrics_15s is universally unfiltered.
- A second type-filter gap neither the claim nor the first engineer found: planner_stream_select.go:105-116 (processEmptyLabels) resolves fingerprints FROM time_series with only a date bound and simpleJSONHas() conditions, and intersects with the type-filtered gin result only when other label matchers exist. Under the plan's label-enforcement security boundary, a selector reduced to empty-label matchers is a case the injected op_project_id matcher must be proven to survive.
- The whole `NewMetricsInsertService` write path is dead code in this tree. GetMetricsService (registry/static.go:84-86) has no caller; ResolveMetricServices delegates to ResolveLogServices (writer/controller/services.go:59-66) and every protocol resolves GetSamplesService. So metrics.go's 4-column `INSERT INTO samples_v3 (type, fingerprint, timestamp_ns, value)` never runs — all signals go through samples.go's 5-column insert. The plan's "one table, two signals" premise is stronger than the claim states, but any reasoning about two distinct writer paths is wrong.
- Per-request TTL is advertised but inert. X-Ttl-Days (writer/controller/middleware.go:167-207), the x-ttl-days gRPC metadata key (writer/grpc/tenant.go:53-58, documented at docs/otlp-grpc.md:45) and the `__ttl_days__` label (builder.go:333-338) all populate MTTLDays, which no insert service and no column consumes. If the plan wants per-project or per-signal retention, this hook cannot deliver it without a writer plugin (the extension point is plugins.GetSamplesInsertServicePlugin, samples.go:48-51) plus a schema change to an APPEND-ONLY migration file.
- OTLP metrics ingest rejects delta temporality outright: Sum/Histogram/ExponentialHistogram data points with DELTA or unspecified aggregation temporality are counted as rejected_data_points (docs/otlp-metrics.md:52-58), as are exponential histograms with negative buckets, bucket_counts/explicit_bounds length mismatches, and zero timestamps. OpenPanel's gateway will need to either require cumulative from SDKs or run a deltatocumulative step, and must surface partial_success back to the caller.
- There is a third copy of the log/metric DDL the plan's schema review should include: ctrl/qryn/sql/log_read_dist.sql, used when CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER is set, which recreates samples_v3/time_series/time_series_gin/metrics_15s/patterns as Distributed tables with the same `type UInt8` back-fill (lines 45-51). log.sql and log_dist.sql are not the whole story.
- rotate.go:135 and rotate.go:196-197 both key their idempotence marker on settings row (type='rotate', name='metrics_15s'). If STORAGE_POLICY is set, the storage-policy update and the TTL update overwrite each other's stored value, so both ALTER TABLE statements re-issue on every gigapipe boot against the shared ClickHouse instance. With STORAGE_POLICY unset (the likely default here) storagePolicyUpdate returns early and the collision is dormant.
- The `profiles`, `profiles_series` and `profiles_series_gin` tables are created (ctrl/qryn/sql/profiles.sql) but appear in no rotateTables call — profiling data has no retention at all. Not on the plan's critical path today, but it means enabling gigapipe's profile endpoints against OpenPanel's ClickHouse creates unbounded growth.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's P0/P3 retention design has to stop treating SAMPLES_DAYS as a per-signal knob: one scalar sets the drop TTL on logs, metrics, labels, the rollup, patterns and all three trace tables, and it is only read when gigapipe is configured purely from env. The claim's own instinct ("per-signal retention needs conditional ClickHouse TTL") is right, but the conditional expression must handle `type IN (1,0)` / `type IN (2,0)` rather than equality, and must accept that `type` is in neither samples_v3's sort key nor its partition key — so a conditional TTL there is a scan, and ttl_only_drop_parts=1 (which rotate.go re-asserts on every boot) would have to be turned off, at a real merge cost. Any such TTL is also re-overwritten by ctrl.Rotate at every gigapipe start unless OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=true is set, which then also disables schema upgrades — that trade-off needs to be an explicit P0 decision. For P2 metrics: the exemplar trace id landing in samples_v3.string means metrics_15s.bytes cannot be used as a log-volume meter without a type filter, which matters directly to the plan's "meter telemetry volume separately for billing" position; and OTLP delta rejection means the ingest gateway must guarantee cumulative temporality and propagate partial_success. For the label-enforcement security boundary, the two unfiltered read sites found here (PromQL's metrics_15s planners, and processEmptyLabels' time_series scan) are the places where an injected op_project_id matcher must be proven to still bind — fingerprints are hashed from labels only (unmarshal.go:250-270), so a log stream and a metric series with identical labels share a fingerprint, and any read that skips both the gin type filter and the matcher can cross signals.

## Investigation 18 — `partially_confirmed`

The claim's syntax half is CONFIRMED — and more strongly than the first engineer allowed. ClickHouse's own documentation gives the grammar `TTL expr [DELETE|RECOMPRESS|TO DISK|TO VOLUME][, ...] [WHERE conditions]` and an explicit multi-clause example (`TTL time + INTERVAL 1 MONTH DELETE WHERE event != 'error', time + INTERVAL 6 MONTH DELETE WHERE event = 'error'`) that is exactly the shape per-signal retention needs; the feature merged 2020-05-27 (ClickHouse PR #10537), far below every version this repo pins. The claim's feasibility half is REFUTED on this table, and the first engineer identified the right blocker: gigapipe forces `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` on samples_v3 (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:78-79). But three of their supporting statements are wrong. There is no single pinned ClickHouse version — the repo pins four, spanning 24.3.2-alpine to 26.1.3.52. `materialize_ttl_after_modify` IS set in gigapipe, to "0", on the exact connection the rotation path uses (ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:34), and git history shows a deliberate 2021 attempt to set it to 1 and a rollback two days later. And "a DELETE WHERE clause would delete nothing" overstates it: under ttl_only_drop_parts=1 a part drops once all its rows expire, so per-signal retention degrades to max(log_ttl, metric_ttl), not to never-delete. I also found, via git history, that gigapipe once shipped an actual `ttl_days UInt16` column on samples_v3 and removed it — the per-row TTL path is not merely unwired, it was written and retracted, while docs/otlp-grpc.md:45 still advertises the header.

**Evidence**

- `https://clickhouse.com/docs/engines/table-engines/mergetree-family/mergetree (ClickHouse official docs, fetched)` — Grammar verbatim: `TTL expr [DELETE|RECOMPRESS codec_name1|TO DISK 'xxx'|TO VOLUME 'xxx'][, ...] [WHERE conditions] [GROUP BY key_expr ...]`. "DELETE action can be used together with WHERE clause to delete only some of the expired rows based on a filtering condition" and "Data with an expired TTL is removed when ClickHouse merges data parts." Example given: `TTL time_column + INTERVAL 1 MONTH DELETE WHERE column = 'value'`. This is vendor documentation, not an executed parse against the pinned image.
- `https://clickhouse.com/docs/guides/developer/ttl (ClickHouse official docs, fetched)` — Confirms MULTIPLE comma-separated DELETE WHERE clauses in one TTL, the exact shape per-signal retention needs: `TTL time + INTERVAL 1 MONTH DELETE WHERE event != 'error', time + INTERVAL 6 MONTH DELETE WHERE event = 'error'`. The first engineer never checked this; the MergeTree reference grammar shows WHERE only as a single trailing clause, so it was a live open question.
- `https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/10537 (fetched)` — "Support of WHERE and GROUP BY in TTL expressions" — merged into master May 27, 2020. Version floor is ClickHouse 20.x, i.e. well below every image this repo runs. The first engineer's 'treat the syntax and its version floor as UNVERIFIED' is over-cautious.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/docker-compose.yml:25, /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/.github/workflows/docker-build.yml:62, /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/coolify.yml:36, /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:68, /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/.github/smoke/docker-compose.yml:35` — FOUR different ClickHouse pins, not one: dev compose and CI use `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.1.3.52`; the Coolify self-host path uses `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.3.2-alpine`; the self-hosting template and the smoke test use `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65`. The first engineer cited only 25.10.2.65 as "the pinned version".
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:32-35` — Refutes the first engineer directly. `ConnectV2` sets client options `Settings: map[string]interface{}{"allow_experimental_database_replicated": "1", "materialize_ttl_after_modify": "0"}`. They wrote that the setting "could not be confirmed from any file in either repo — neither repo sets or mentions that setting." It does.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:113-131` — `rotateDB` opens its connection via `maintenance.ConnectV2(dbObject, true)` (line 114) and then calls `Rotate(connDb, ...)` (lines 130-131). So every MODIFY SETTING and MODIFY TTL gigapipe issues runs on the connection carrying materialize_ttl_after_modify=0 — gigapipe's TTL changes apply to new parts only and never mutate existing parts.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe git history: 99d5043 (2021-11-19) and 8c1771e (2021-11-21)` — 99d5043 "materialize_ttl_after_modify TTL (#60)" added `materialize_ttl_after_modify = 1` to the samples/time_series MODIFY SETTING, with the commit body "Patch intended to apply TTL to existing data (drop)". 8c1771e "rollback materialize_ttl_after_modify — pending version check" removed it two days later. The project tried retroactive TTL materialization and backed out.
- `https://kb.altinity.com/altinity-kb-queries-and-syntax/ttl/modify-ttl/ (fetched)` — "You can disable this step completely by using `materialize_ttl_after_modify` user session setting (by default it's 1, so materialization is enabled)" and "If you will disable materialization of TTL, it does mean that all old parts will be transformed according OLD TTL rules." So a hand-applied MODIFY TTL from OpenPanel's own ClickHouse client would kick off a heavy materialization mutation unless OpenPanel also sets it to 0.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:73-95` — Verified verbatim. Guard at 73-76: `val, err := getSetting(db, distributed, "rotate", settingName)` / `if err != nil || val == rotateTTLStr { return err }`. Then per table, line 78-79 `ALTER TABLE %s %s MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1, merge_with_ttl_timeout = 3600, index_granularity = 8192`, then line 87 `ALTER TABLE %s %s MODIFY TTL %s`. Note the guard gates BOTH statements — a point the first engineer missed.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:155-163` — samples_v3 is rotated with settingName `v3_samples_days`, time expression `toDateTime(timestamp_ns / 1000000000)`, and drop expression `logDefaultTTLString(...)` = `<expr> + toIntervalDay(dropTTLDays)` (lines 140-144). rotateTables (48-66) joins the move-to-disk clauses with that one unconditional drop clause; no WHERE is ever emitted.

- `/opt/homebrew/bin/clickhouse` — Confirms their inability to test empirically: `broken symbolic link to /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/clickhouse/26.6.1.1193-stable/clickhouse-macos-aarch64`. The Caskroom version directory exists but is empty of the binary. No ClickHouse source or binary is vendored in either repo, and the Go module cache holds only client libraries. Their "no parse test was possible" is accurate.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The first engineer's 'treat the syntax and its version floor as UNVERIFIED' is over-cautious and should not go into the plan as an open risk. ClickHouse's own docs publish the grammar `TTL expr [DELETE|...][, ...] [WHERE conditions]` AND a multi-clause conditional example (`TTL time + INTERVAL 1 MONTH DELETE WHERE event != 'error', time + INTERVAL 6 MONTH DELETE WHERE event = 'error'`), and the feature merged in PR #10537 on 2020-05-27. Every ClickHouse image this repo runs is years past that. The multi-clause form specifically — which the MergeTree reference grammar does NOT obviously permit, since it shows WHERE only as one trailing clause — is the form the plan needs, and it is documented. Caveat: this is vendor documentation, not an executed parse against 25.10.2.65; nothing on disk allows an empirical test.
- There is no single 'pinned ClickHouse version'. The repo pins four: `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.1.3.52` (docker-compose.yml:25, .github/workflows/docker-build.yml:62), `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65` (self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:68, .github/smoke/docker-compose.yml:35), and `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.3.2-alpine` (self-hosting/coolify.yml:36). The Coolify self-host path is nearly two years behind the others. Any ClickHouse-version-sensitive decision in the plan must clear 24.3, not 25.10.
- FLATLY WRONG: 'whether ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL triggers a mutation to materialize TTL metadata over existing parts (the materialize_ttl_after_modify behaviour) could not be confirmed from any file in either repo — neither repo sets or mentions that setting.' gigapipe sets it. ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:32-35 puts `"materialize_ttl_after_modify": "0"` into the ClickHouse client options returned by ConnectV2, and ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:114 shows rotateDB gets its connection from exactly that function. Git history confirms the intent was deliberate: 99d5043 (2021-11-19) added `materialize_ttl_after_modify = 1` to the MODIFY SETTING and 8c1771e (2021-11-21) rolled it back 'pending version check'. Consequences for the plan, both real: (a) gigapipe's own MODIFY TTL never rewrites existing parts, so a SAMPLES_DAYS change only affects data ingested after it; (b) ClickHouse's default is 1 (Altinity KB), so a MODIFY TTL issued from OpenPanel's own client via packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:118-132 WILL launch a heavy materialization mutation across samples_v3 unless OpenPanel explicitly sets it to 0.
- 'A DELETE WHERE type = 1 clause would delete nothing' overstates the failure. Per ClickHouse docs, with ttl_only_drop_parts=1 a whole part is dropped once ALL rows in it are expired. samples_v3 parts mix logs and metrics (type is not in the partition key), so with two different per-signal TTLs a part survives until the LONGER one expires. The accurate statement is: per-signal retention collapses to max(log_ttl, metric_ttl) — logs get retained for the metrics window — not that deletion stops. Both outcomes defeat the plan, but the doc should state the real one.
- The first engineer missed that rotate.go's short-circuit guard (lines 73-76) gates BOTH the `MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` (line 78-79) and the `MODIFY TTL` (line 87) — they are inside the same loop after the same early return. Corollary they did not draw: if OpenPanel flips ttl_only_drop_parts back to 0 by hand, gigapipe will NOT restore it to 1 on restart, for the same reason a hand-applied TTL survives — the `v3_samples_days` settings row still matches. The setting and the TTL are clobbered together or not at all, which makes the workaround more durable than their write-up implies (though still fragile to any SAMPLES_DAYS or STORAGE_POLICY change).
- Their claim that `type` is merely 'bolted on later as a non-key column' understates it. `type` is absent from samples_v3's ORDER BY as well as its PARTITION BY, and that omission is specific to samples_v3: log.sql:117, 124 and 128 explicitly add `type` to the sort keys of time_series, time_series_gin and metrics_15s in the same migration block, while log.sql:119-120 gives samples_v3 the column with no MODIFY ORDER BY. The default sort key is just `(timestamp_ns)` (update.go:214). So a `DELETE WHERE type = N` predicate has neither partition pruning nor primary-index support.
- Path/line imprecisions worth fixing before the plan cites them: the SAMPLES_TYPE constants are at reader/logql/logql_transpiler/shared/types.go:12-14, not `shared/types.go:12-14`. The samples_v3 INSERT is at writer/service/insert/samples.go:60 (acquirer 13-33), not 57-58. The `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS type UInt8` on samples_v3 is at ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:119-120; their cited 26-32 is the CREATE only.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe once shipped per-row TTL in the schema and removed it. Commit d5b5ce6 ("ttl_days updates for tables", 2025-04-30) added `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ttl_days UInt16` to samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin and metrics_15s (plus their _dist counterparts in log_dist.sql) and put ttl_days into three sort keys. A grep for `ttl_days` across ctrl/qryn/sql/*.sql at HEAD returns zero hits. The plan should not treat per-request TTL as a feature that is 'nearly there' — it was written into the schema and pulled back out.
- The retracted feature is still documented and still has a green test. docs/otlp-grpc.md:45 advertises `x-ttl-days` / `X-Ttl-Days` as 'Per-request TTL in days'; writer/grpc/tenant.go:53-58 parses it into ContextKeyTTLDays; writer/grpc/tenant_test.go:28-47 (`TestDSNCtx_ParsesTTLDays`) asserts the parse succeeds. The header is accepted, validated, tested, documented — and silently discarded before the INSERT. Anyone planning per-tenant or per-signal retention off gigapipe's docs will build on a no-op.
- There is a real escape hatch neither engineer surfaced: gigapipe's DDL is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {{.DB}}.samples_v3` (log.sql:25), and the sort key is env-controlled by ADVANCED_SAMPLES_ORDERING (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:123-124 -> update.go:221-222). OpenPanel can therefore pre-create samples_v3 itself, before gigapipe's first boot, with its own PARTITION BY including `type` — gigapipe will leave it alone. With type-homogeneous partitions, `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` stops being a blocker and part-level per-signal retention works without fighting gigapipe's rotation. Constraints: it must happen before first boot (PARTITION BY cannot be altered afterwards), and gigapipe will still overwrite the TTL expression itself on the next SAMPLES_DAYS/STORAGE_POLICY change. UNVERIFIED: exactly how ClickHouse resolves a multi-clause conditional TTL under ttl_only_drop_parts=1 over homogeneous parts — I could not test this, and the plan should.
- samples_v3 is created WITHOUT ttl_only_drop_parts. update.go:213 sets CREATE_SETTINGS to "" and line 218 only ever fills it with `SETTINGS storage_policy = '...'`. ClickHouse's own default for ttl_only_drop_parts is 0. So the value on samples_v3 is 1 purely as a side effect of rotate.go:79 — it is not baked into the schema, and it is not what a freshly created, never-rotated samples_v3 has. (The `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` occurrences in reader/model/sample.go:35 and writer/model/sample.go:43 are stale comment blocks describing the legacy `samples` table keyed on timestamp_ms, not samples_v3 — do not cite them as schema.)
- `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE WHERE` already appears in OpenPanel (packages/db/src/services/delete.service.ts:61, import.service.ts:183 and :199, scripts/find-duplicate-events.ts:308) but as a lightweight-delete mutation, not as a TTL clause. A grep confirming 'DELETE WHERE exists in the repo' would be a false positive for this claim; the two constructs are unrelated.

**Impact on the plan.** Two things in the plan need to change, one relaxes and one tightens.

RELAX: drop 'conditional TTL syntax is unverified / needs a version check' as an open risk. The grammar and the multi-clause `DELETE WHERE` form are both in ClickHouse's published docs, and the feature landed in 2020 — below the 24.3.2-alpine floor that self-hosting/coolify.yml:36 actually implies. What the plan should carry instead is the correct version floor statement: the repo runs 24.3.2, 25.10.2.65 and 26.1.3.52 across its four compose/CI files, so any ClickHouse-version-dependent decision must clear 24.3, not 25.10.

TIGHTEN: the plan's line that 'per-signal retention needs conditional ClickHouse TTL' is necessary but not sufficient, and must be restated as a three-part requirement. (1) `ttl_only_drop_parts` must be forced back to 0 on samples_v3 — gigapipe sets it to 1 at rotate.go:79 — with the consequence spelled out honestly: not 'nothing is deleted' but 'retention collapses to max(log_ttl, metric_ttl)', plus the row-level merge cost gigapipe deliberately avoided. (2) `materialize_ttl_after_modify` must be set explicitly on whichever connection issues the ALTER: gigapipe pins it to 0 (ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:34) while ClickHouse defaults it to 1, so the same statement behaves differently depending on whether gigapipe or OpenPanel's own client (packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:118-132) issues it — silently no-op-on-old-parts in one case, heavy full-table mutation in the other. (3) The TTL expression must handle type=0 explicitly, since GetTypes emits `type IN (requested, 0)`.

The plan should also evaluate the pre-create alternative before committing to conditional TTL: because log.sql:25 uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, OpenPanel can own samples_v3's PARTITION BY (adding `type`) at P0 provisioning time, which makes gigapipe's own ttl_only_drop_parts=1 harmless and gives part-level per-signal retention with no row-level merge cost. That decision is only available before gigapipe's first boot, so it belongs in P0, not P6.

Finally, delete any dependence on gigapipe's `X-Ttl-Days` / `x-ttl-days` header or `__ttl_days__` label. docs/otlp-grpc.md:45 documents it and writer/grpc/tenant_test.go tests it, but git history (d5b5ce6, then removed) shows the backing `ttl_days` column was pulled from the schema, and writer/service/insert/samples.go:60 inserts five columns that do not include it. Per-request TTL is a documented no-op.

## Investigation 19 — `partially_confirmed`

I reached the same verdict as the first engineer by a different route (tests first, then the registry consumer side, then the connection factories, then git history), and I independently reproduced every citation they gave — all of them exist and say what they claim. The transport half of the claim is correct: `X-CH-DSN` (writer/controller/middleware.go:165) and `x-ch-dsn` (writer/grpc/tenant.go:42) are read on every ingest path and stored under `utils.ContextKeyDSN`. The routing half is wrong: the value is used only as an opaque key compared against `svc.GetNodeName()` in a static, boot-built registry, and an unmatched or empty value falls through to `r.rand.Intn(len(svcs))` — fail-open, and re-randomized per getter call (writer/service/registry/static.go:55-69). However, one of the first engineer's statements is too absolute and I disagree with it as phrased: they wrote "There is no code path anywhere in the writer that opens a connection from a caller-supplied DSN." The writer in fact carries a complete, working DSN-dialing implementation — `SmartDatabaseAdapter{Xdsn, DSN}` plus `NewGeneralPurposeClientWithXDSN` / `NewWriterClientWithXDSN`, which strip an `n-`/`c-` prefix and dial the rest as a real ClickHouse DSN. Nothing in the request path calls it (the plugin fields `DBConnWithXDSN`/`DBConnWithDSN` are declared and never assigned or read; the only callers are an env-gated unit test), so the conclusion survives — but the correct reason is "dead scaffolding for an unfinished per-tenant feature," not "no such code exists."

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/middleware.go:164-207` — Reproduced. `WithOverallContextMiddleware = WithPreRequest(func(w,r) error { dsn := strings.Clone(r.Header.Get("X-CH-DSN")) ... ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, utils.ContextKeyDSN, dsn) ... })`. Also reads X-Scope-Meta, X-Ttl-Days, X-Async-Insert and handles gzip/snappy decoding. The value is stored verbatim — never parsed, validated, or dialed here.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/grpc/tenant.go:33-60` — Reproduced. `dsn := mdFirst(md, "x-ch-dsn")` then `ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, utils.ContextKeyDSN, dsn)`. Its own doc comment says handlers "call dsnCtx(ctx) and then the signal-scoped resolver directly, e.g. controller.ResolveTraceServices(dsn)". Call sites: writer/grpc/metrics.go:28, trace.go:25, logs.go:25, profiles.go:24.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/service/registry/static.go:55-69` — The decisive code, reproduced verbatim: `func staticServiceRegistryGetService[T interface{ GetNodeName() string }](r *staticServiceRegistry, id string, svcs []T) (T, error) { if id != "" { for _, svc := range svcs { if svc.GetNodeName() == id { return svc, nil } } } r.mtx.Lock(); defer r.mtx.Unlock(); idx := r.rand.Intn(len(svcs)); return svcs[idx], nil }`. Unrecognized id is NOT an error — random fallback. Also note `r.rand.Intn(len(svcs))` panics if a signal's service slice is empty.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/services.go:22-78` — All four resolvers treat the value as a registry key only: `Registry.GetSpansSeriesService(dsn)`, `GetSpansService(dsn)`, `GetSamplesService(dsn)`, `GetTimeSeriesService(dsn)`, `GetProfileInsertService(dsn)`. `ResolveMetricServices` (line 63) delegates to `ResolveLogServices` verbatim.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/chwrapper/adapter.go:15-57` — NEW — contradicts the first engineer's absolute phrasing. `type SmartDatabaseAdapter struct { Xdsn string; DSN string; dbObject *config.ClokiBaseDataBase; ... }` and both `initGeneralClient`/`initWriteClient` branch: `if a.dbObject != nil {...} else if a.Xdsn != "" { NewGeneralPurposeClientWithXDSN(ctx, a.Xdsn, ...) } else if a.DSN != "" { NewGeneralPurposeClientWithDSN(...) }`. A real caller-supplied-DSN dialing path exists in the writer.

Confirmed `append(cfg.ExtraMiddleware, withTSAndSampleService, ...)` in writer/controller/{insert,prom,datadog,profile,otlp_metrics}.go, and writer/router/insert.go:8-16 mounts /loki/api/v1/push, /influx/api/v2/write, /cf/v1/insert, /api/v2/series, /api/v2/logs, /v1/logs, /v1/metrics through that config. The header is read on every ingest endpoint.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe git history` — `git log --oneline -S"X-CH-DSN"` returns only 7580d08 (qryn -> gigapipe rename) and 6b3467b (OTLP/gRPC ingest) — the header has never had a different implementation in this history. `git log --oneline -- writer/service/registry/static.go` shows four commits, all refactors/path renames, none touching the selection logic.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's phrase "routing inserts to that DSN" is wrong. The value is never parsed or dialed on the request path; it is an opaque id compared to `svc.GetNodeName()`, i.e. the `Node` field of a database entry fixed at boot (writer/service/registry/static.go:55-69, writer/service/generic_insert.go:130/366/512). I confirm the first engineer on this.
- The selector is fail-open. An empty or unrecognized id silently returns `svcs[r.rand.Intn(len(svcs))]` (static.go:65-68) rather than erroring. This alone disqualifies the header as a security boundary. I confirm the first engineer on this.
- Selection is not atomic per request — each `Get*Service` call re-randomizes independently, so samples and time_series can land on different nodes within one request, which the repo's own test comment (services_test.go:43-49) says can silently lose time_series rows. I confirm the first engineer on this.
- CORRECTION TO THE FIRST ENGINEER: their statement "There is no code path anywhere in the writer that opens a connection from a caller-supplied DSN" is too strong as written. `writer/chwrapper/adapter.go:15-57` plus `factory.go:71-81`, `171-183`, `246-257` implement exactly that — a `SmartDatabaseAdapter` that dials whatever `Xdsn`/`DSN` string it is handed (stripping an `n-`/`c-` prefix). What is true is that nothing in the request path reaches it: the plugin fields `DBConnWithXDSN`/`DBConnWithDSN` (writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:33-34) are declared and never assigned or read, and the only callers are the env-gated writer/chwrapper/unit_test.go:63,95. The correct framing is "dead scaffolding for an unfinished per-tenant DSN feature", which matters because it changes how likely upstream is to activate it.
- NUANCE the first engineer asserted without citing the gate: `portCHEnv` early-returns when DATABASE_DATA is already non-empty (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:85-87), and a `-config <file>` YAML can populate it with several named nodes (main.go:51, 290-294). So the header is inert only under env-var-only bootstrap, not categorically. (I could NOT read the `ClokiBaseDataBase` struct's yaml tags — github.com/metrico/cloki-config v0.0.96 is not in this machine's module cache and there is no sample YAML in the repo — so the exact key name for `Node` in a config file is UNVERIFIED. That the field exists and is per-database is confirmed by its use at writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:49 and reader/registry/registry.go:56,91.)
- The header cannot select a ClickHouse *database name* per request: the database is `dbObject.Name` baked into each connection at open time (writer/chwrapper/factory.go:20-31 `databaseName = dbObject.Name`; reader/registry/registry.go:110 `.../" + dbObject.Name`). I confirm the first engineer on this.
- The value is neither validated nor authorized (single global Basic credential), so in any multi-node deployment an unauthenticated-as-to-tenant caller can steer writes; the only containment is that the id can select only among already-configured nodes. I confirm the first engineer on this.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The reader's `DatabaseRegistryPlugin` hook is dead code: `reader/registry/registry.go:20-26` assigns `Registry = (*p)()` from the plugin and then unconditionally overwrites it with `Registry = InitStaticRegistry()` on the very next line. This is a stronger support for plan decision 2 than anything cited so far — the reader's only documented extension point for a dynamic registry cannot take effect, so 'the reader binds to a fixed set of databases at boot and ignores request context' holds even for a plugin build.
- Upstream states the gap itself. writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:65: `// TODO: move this all into a separate /registry module and add plugin support to support dynamic database registries`. Cite this in the plan doc — it is upstream's own admission that per-request database registries are unimplemented, and it is more durable than reasoning from absence.
- A latent per-tenant DSN feature exists in BOTH halves of gigapipe, disconnected at each end. The writer can dial an `n-`/`c-`-prefixed DSN (chwrapper/factory.go:71-81) but nothing supplies one; the reader BUILDS exactly that string at boot (reader/registry/registry.go:92-110, `prefix + "clickhouse://" + user + ":" + pass + "@" + host + ":" + port + "/" + name`) into `DataDatabasesMap.DSN` and nothing reads it. Implication for the plan: pin an exact gigapipe version/commit and re-audit on upgrade — if upstream ever wires `DBConnWithXDSN` to `ContextKeyDSN`, an unstripped X-CH-DSN header becomes a full SSRF-to-arbitrary-ClickHouse primitive, not merely a node-shuffle.
- Concrete gateway requirement not stated in the plan as summarized: apps/api must STRIP `X-CH-DSN` and `x-ch-dsn` (and `X-Ttl-Days` / `X-Scope-Meta` / `X-Async-Insert`, all read by the same middleware at writer/controller/middleware.go:165-168) from client requests before proxying, rather than merely not setting them. Header names are case-insensitive in HTTP/1.1 and gRPC metadata keys are lowercase — strip both forms.
- The log-pattern path ignores tenancy entirely: writer/pattern/controller/controller.go:172 calls `GetPatternInsertService("")` with a hardcoded empty id, always hitting the random fallback. If the plan enables pattern extraction, note that this signal has no tenant selection at all.
- `GetMetricsService` has no non-test caller in the tree (only the interface at registry/service.go:8, the impl at registry/static.go:85, and three test fakes). Metrics resolve via `ResolveMetricServices` -> `ResolveLogServices` -> samples + time_series, so the `MtrSvcs` services built at boot are unreachable on the OSS write path. Corroborates plan decision on shared storage: writer/service/insert/metrics.go:53-58 inserts into `samples_v3 (type, fingerprint, timestamp_ns, value)`.
- Two robustness notes on the static registry: (a) `r.rand.Intn(len(svcs))` (static.go:67) panics on an empty service slice rather than returning an error, so a signal with no configured service crashes the ingest goroutine; (b) services are keyed by `node.Node` in maps (`MtrSvcs[node.Node]` etc., writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:186-217), so two DATABASE_DATA entries sharing a Node value — including two blank ones — silently collapse into one. Both argue for the plan's single-node deployment shape.

**Impact on the plan.** Plan decision 2 stands and is if anything better supported than the plan states — label enforcement is the right call, and the reader's dead plugin hook plus upstream's own TODO make 'no per-request database selection exists' a documented fact rather than an inference. Three concrete changes to the plan document: (1) Restate the header's status precisely — 'X-CH-DSN selects a boot-configured node by name, fail-open to a random node, and is inert only because the env-var bootstrap configures exactly one unnamed node' — rather than 'gigapipe's writer supports per-request DSN tenancy'; the imprecise version invites someone to try building isolation on it. (2) Add an explicit gateway requirement to strip X-CH-DSN / x-ch-dsn (plus X-Ttl-Days, X-Scope-Meta, X-Async-Insert) from inbound client requests in apps/api before proxying to gigapipe, and a test asserting the strip — the fail-open random selector means a passed-through header is a live misrouting vector the moment anyone adds a second DATABASE_DATA entry. (3) Add a version-pin + re-audit note: the writer already contains working caller-supplied-DSN dialing code (chwrapper/adapter.go, factory.go:71-81/171-183) that is merely unwired, so a gigapipe upgrade could turn the header from inert into a connection-opening primitive. Also add a deployment constraint: keep the env-var bootstrap (never a -config YAML with multiple nodes), since cmd/gigapipe/main.go:85-87 shows a config file bypasses the single-entry path entirely.

## Investigation 20 — `partially_confirmed`

I independently reached the same verdict as the first engineer and confirmed essentially all of their load-bearing evidence by a different route (enumerating every `trpc.chart.*` call site in apps/start, then reading the resolvers, then the DB read mappers). FinalChart is real and is the shared contract, but only 7 of 11 renderers consume it; funnel/retention/conversion/sankey hit different procedures with different result shapes; ShareOverview and the embed widgets are not FinalChart surfaces at all; and the MCP tools do not work unchanged. However, the first engineer missed the single hardest blocker and got one evidence item backwards. The blocker they missed is `transformReport` / `transformReportEventItem` (packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:56-115) — an explicit field-whitelist mapper that every server-side report read passes through, which unconditionally rewrites any series item whose `type` is not `'formula'` into `{type:'event', name: item.name || 'unknown_event'}`. That means a metric series cannot survive a round-trip through Postgres even if the zod schema were opened up. The item they got backwards is their final one: `zReportInput` is a plain `z.object`, so zod strips unknown keys — a future metrics discriminator sent by `useChartInput` reaches the transport but never reaches the resolver, so "no frontend change needed" is not the same as "no schema change needed."

**Evidence**

- `apps/start/src/components/report-chart/index.tsx:41-61` — The `switch (props.report.chartType)` dispatch confirms exactly 11 renderers: linear, bar, area, histogram, pie, map, metric, funnel, retention, conversion, sankey.
- `apps/start/src/components/report-chart/{line,area,histogram,map,metric}/index.tsx (lines 16,17,17,17,16) and {bar,pie}/index.tsx (17,17)` — Exhaustive grep of `trpc.chart.` across apps/start/src returns exactly these seven calling `trpc.chart.chart` or `trpc.chart.aggregate`. The other four call `trpc.chart.funnel` (funnel/index.tsx:23), `trpc.chart.cohort` (retention/index.tsx:34), `trpc.chart.conversion` (conversion/index.tsx:18), `trpc.chart.sankey` (sankey/index.tsx:47). 7 of 11 confirmed, independently of the first engineer's method.
- `packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:56-80` — THE BLOCKER THE FIRST ENGINEER MISSED. `transformReportEventItem` is `if (item.type === 'formula') { ...return formula } return { type: 'event', segment: ..., filters: ..., id: ..., name: item.name || 'unknown_event', displayName, property }`. Any series item that is not a formula is unconditionally coerced to an event series with a fixed field set. A `{type:'metric', ...}` series persisted in the `events` JSON column comes back out of the DB as a bogus event named `unknown_event`.
- `packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:83-115` — `transformReport` returns an explicit object literal listing exactly 18 fields (id, projectId, name, chartType, lineType, interval, series, breakdowns, globalFilters, range, previous, formula, metric, unit, layout, options, visibleSeries, startDate, endDate). It is a whitelist, not a spread. Any new Report column or JSON field is dropped here unless the mapper is edited.
- `packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:131-145, 128` — Both DB read entry points funnel through that mapper: `getReportById` → `transformReport(report)` and `getReportsByDashboardId` → `reports.map(transformReport)`. `getReportById` is what `chartProcedure` puts on `ctx.report` for the share path, and `getReportsByDashboardId` is what `share.dashboardReports` returns (packages/trpc/src/routers/share.ts:262). So both public-share paths are gated by the whitelist.
- `packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:154-178` — A third whitelist the first engineer did not mention: `listReportsCore` re-projects each series to `{type:'formula',id,formula}` or `{type:'event',id,name,displayName,segment}` at line 174. This backs MCP's report listing and would flatten a metric series there too.
- `packages/validation/src/index.ts:233-308` — `zReportInput = z.object({...})` — a plain strip-mode object. Zod strips unknown keys by default, so an extra `source: 'metrics'` field sent from the client is removed before the resolver sees `input`. This contradicts the first engineer's last evidence bullet.
- `packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:202-208` — `cacheMiddleware` builds its Redis key from `await getRawInput()` — the pre-validation payload — not from the parsed `input`. So an unrecognised extra field silently fragments the 60s chart cache while having zero effect on the query. A footgun for anyone who assumes 'the field is harmless until the schema catches up'.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:588-635` — Confirmed verbatim: `chart:` and `aggregate:` both build `chartInput` from `ctx.report ?? input` and then `return ChartEngine.execute(chartInput)` / `return AggregateChartEngine.execute(chartInput)` with no discriminator. Any metrics routing must be inserted here to make the renderers work unchanged.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:554 and apps/start/src/components/report-chart/sankey/index.tsx:30-47` — Confirmed and strengthened: `sankey: protectedProcedure.input(zReportInput)` — and `protectedProcedure = t.procedure.use(enforceUserIsAuthed).use(enforceAccess)...` (packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:176-180). The sankey renderer's `input: IReportInput` literal contains no `shareId` at all, so it is not merely unsupported server-side — the client never even attempts a share request. Sankey reports are already broken on public shares today.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:83-141` — `chartProcedure` middleware confirmed: `if (rawInput.shareId)` → require `id`, `validateShareAccess`, `getReportById`, then `next({ ctx: { report } })`. Share rendering is driven entirely by the persisted, whitelist-mapped report row.
- `apps/start/src/routes/share.overview.$shareId.tsx:1-16, 119-135` — Confirmed: imports and renders a fixed set — OverviewMetrics, OverviewTopSources, OverviewTopPages, OverviewTopDevices, OverviewTopEvents, OverviewTopGeo, OverviewWeeklyTrends, OverviewUserJourney. No `ReportChart` import. `OverviewMetrics` queries `trpc.overview.stats` (overview-metrics.tsx:95), not `chart.chart`. ShareOverview is not a FinalChart surface.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/widget.ts:1-14, 118, 141, 184` — Independently confirmed: the widget router imports only `ch, clix, db, eventBuffer, getSettingsForProject, TABLE_NAMES` — no engine import. `counter`, `badge`, `realtimeData` are `publicProcedure`s querying ClickHouse/eventBuffer directly. `/widget/badge|counter|realtime` are not FinalChart consumers.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:299-304 and 345-351` — Confirmed (line numbers 299-304 / 345-351, marginally off the first engineer's 296-303 / 349-351): both `runReport` and `runReportFromConfig` do `if (chartType === 'funnel') funnelService.getFunnel; if (chartType === 'metric') AggregateChartEngine.execute; return ChartEngine.execute`. A metrics report is silently run through the event engine.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/dashboard-management.ts:15-17` — Confirmed: `const reportSchema = zReport.omit({projectId:true, limit:true, offset:true}).strict().superRefine(...)`, used as the `report` input to both `create_report` (line ~413) and `update_report` (line ~438). `.strict()` throws on any additional key.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:70-75` — A nuance the first engineer inverted: the comment says the engine zero-fills onto a common grid BUT `shapeChart` explicitly 'take[s] the union anyway so a short series can't silently truncate the axis'. MCP's shaping is more tolerant of a ragged date grid than the frontend is.
- `apps/start/src/hooks/use-rechart-data-model.ts:19-52` — Confirmed and it is the real fragility: `series[0]?.data.map(({date}) => ...)` establishes the x-axis, then every other series is matched with `if (item.date === date)` string equality. A metrics engine that emits a different or unfilled date grid loses points with no error.
- `packages/db/src/engine/index.ts:27-77, 31-38, 91` — Confirmed the two producers. Also unnoticed by the first engineer: BOTH `executeChart` (line 32) and `executeAggregateChart` (line 91) clamp `endDate` via `getOrganizationSubscriptionChartEndDate(input.projectId, normalized.endDate)`. A second engine that skips this would show metric data past the subscription cutoff that event charts hide — a billing-enforcement divergence.
- `apps/start/src/components/profiles/profile-charts.tsx:90,98 and apps/start/src/modals/insight-details.tsx:174 and apps/start/src/modals/overview-chart-details.tsx:18` — Three further `<ReportChart>` render sites neither the claim nor the first engineer enumerated. The full set of ReportChart consumers is: report-item.tsx:192,260 (dashboards + shared dashboards), share.report.$shareId.tsx:125, chat-report-result.tsx:75, profile-charts.tsx:90,98, insight-details.tsx:174, overview-chart-details.tsx:18.
- `packages/db/src/services/reports.service.test.ts:40-62 (and a repo-wide test grep)` — No test file anywhere in the repo references `FinalChart`, `ChartEngine`, or `executeChart` (verified by grepping all *.test.ts/*.spec.ts under packages and apps). reports.service.test.ts only covers `mergeGlobalFilters`. There is no regression net for the 'works unchanged' premise, and none of the five engine dispatch sites is covered.
- `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:385-397` — Confirmed: `enum ChartType { linear bar histogram pie metric area map funnel retention conversion sankey }` — a closed Postgres enum. Reusing an existing type avoids a migration; a metrics-specific type does not.
- `apps/api/src/agents/tools/dashboard.ts:100-105, apps/api/src/controllers/export.controller.ts:201-216, packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:212-219` — Confirmed the remaining direct engine call sites by repo-wide grep for `ChartEngine`. Total call sites needing a branch: chart.ts:609, chart.ts:633, mcp reports.ts:302, mcp reports.ts:304, mcp reports.ts:349, mcp reports.ts:351, reports.service.ts:215, reports.service.ts:219, agents/tools/dashboard.ts:102, agents/tools/dashboard.ts:104, export.controller.ts:201.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's "11 chart renderers" is wrong — confirmed independently. Exactly 7 consume FinalChart. My grep of every `trpc.chart.*` call site in apps/start/src returns line/area/histogram/map/metric → `chart.chart` and bar/pie → `chart.aggregate`; funnel/retention/conversion/sankey each hit a different procedure with a different result type.
- The claim's "works everywhere unchanged" is false as stated, and the deeper reason is not the one the first engineer gave. Even with server-side routing inside `chart.chart`/`chart.aggregate`, a saved metrics report cannot round-trip through Postgres: `transformReport` (packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:83-115) is an explicit 18-field whitelist and `transformReportEventItem` (:56-80) rewrites every non-formula series item into `{type:'event', name: item.name || 'unknown_event'}`. Both public-share paths, the dashboard list, MCP `runReport` and `getReportDataCore` all read through these two functions. This is a harder blocker than "no discriminator exists in the zod schema" and the first engineer did not find it.
- The first engineer's final evidence item is backwards. They wrote that `useChartInput` sends everything so "any future metrics discriminator [reaches the server], with no frontend change needed." `zReportInput` is a plain `z.object` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:233), and zod strips unknown keys, so the field is removed before the resolver's `input`. Worse, `cacheMiddleware` keys off `getRawInput()` (packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:202-208), so the stripped field still fragments the Redis cache — it has no effect except a wasted cache miss. The schema must change; the frontend behaviour is irrelevant.
- The first engineer's "sankey already cannot be shared" is correct but understated. Beyond `sankey` being a `protectedProcedure` (chart.ts:554), the sankey renderer's `input: IReportInput` literal (sankey/index.tsx:30-44) contains no `shareId` field at all, so the client never even attempts a share-scoped request. It is a two-sided gap.
- The claim's surface list is incomplete in a direction nobody has flagged. Three more `<ReportChart>` render sites exist: `profile-charts.tsx:90,98` (per-profile page-view and event charts), `modals/insight-details.tsx:174`, and `modals/overview-chart-details.tsx:18`. Any of them would inherit a metrics-routing decision made inside `chart.chart`/`chart.aggregate`.
- "A second engine returning FinalChart works everywhere" has zero test coverage backing it. No test in either repo references FinalChart, ChartEngine or executeChart; `reports.service.test.ts` covers only `mergeGlobalFilters`. Any claim of behavioural equivalence between two engines would have to be established by tests that do not currently exist.
- Minor line-number corrections to the first engineer: `runReport`'s dispatch is at packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:299-304 (not 296-303); `getReportDataCore` begins at packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:180 (not 178). Their `shapeChart` characterisation is also slightly unfair — the code at reports.ts:70-75 deliberately takes the *union* of dates rather than trusting the zero-fill, making MCP more tolerant of a ragged grid than `useRechartDataModel` is.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- `transformReport` and `transformReportEventItem` (packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:56-115) are the true chokepoint for the whole plan, and the plan does not account for them. Persisting a metric series requires editing three separate whitelist mappers (`transformReportEventItem`, `transformReport`, `listReportsCore`) in addition to `zChartEventItem` and `zReportInput`. Without that, a metrics report silently degrades to an event series named `unknown_event` on every share, dashboard, and MCP read.
- Both `executeChart` (packages/db/src/engine/index.ts:32) and `executeAggregateChart` (:91) clamp the query end date through `getOrganizationSubscriptionChartEndDate`. A gigapipe-backed metrics engine that does not replicate this would leak data past a lapsed subscription's cutoff on the metrics path while the event path correctly hides it — a billing-enforcement asymmetry the plan should call out explicitly.
- `cacheMiddleware` keys the 60s chart cache off `getRawInput()` (packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:205-208), the pre-validation payload. Two consequences for the plan: (a) an extra field the schema does not yet know about splits the cache without changing behaviour, and (b) once metrics routing is added, the cache key correctly varies with the discriminator only because it is in the raw input — but it also means share links and authenticated views cache under different keys for the same underlying data.
- There is no test coverage for the FinalChart contract anywhere: no test file references FinalChart, ChartEngine, or executeChart, and none of the eleven engine dispatch call sites is exercised. The plan's testing phase (docs/observability/11-testing-strategy.md exists) should treat 'FinalChart shape equivalence between the two engines' as a new test surface to be created, not an existing one to extend.
- The full ReportChart consumer set is eight render sites, not the three the claim names: report-item.tsx:192 and :260, share.report.$shareId.tsx:125, chat-report-result.tsx:75, profile-charts.tsx:90 and :98, insight-details.tsx:174, overview-chart-details.tsx:18. `profile-charts.tsx` is notable because it constructs synthetic reports client-side rather than loading saved ones — a metrics report can never reach it, but it does mean any change to ReportChart's props ripples further than the plan assumes.
- `share.dashboardReports` (packages/trpc/src/routers/share.ts:262) returns `getReportsByDashboardId(share.dashboardId)` with no chart-type filtering, so a sankey report saved onto a shared dashboard will render `ReportSankeyChart`, which calls a `protectedProcedure` with no shareId — an unauthenticated share viewer gets an error card today. Worth documenting as a pre-existing bug the observability work will sit next to rather than one it introduces.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's decision #4 ("the metrics engine returns FinalChart, therefore every renderer, dashboard, share, embed and MCP tool works unchanged") must be restated as a much narrower claim: it buys you five time-series renderers (line, area, histogram, map, metric) plus two aggregate renderers (bar, pie), the ReportLayout/GrafanaGrid layout, and ShareReport/ShareDashboard — and only if the metrics dispatch happens server-side inside `chart.chart` and `chart.aggregate`. It buys you nothing for funnel/retention/conversion/sankey, nothing for ShareOverview, and nothing for the embed widgets, all of which are separate query paths. Concretely the plan needs to add: (1) a persistence workstream covering `zChartEventItem`, `zReportInput`, and the three whitelist mappers in packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts (:56, :83, :154) — this is the item currently missing entirely and it gates every share and MCP surface; (2) eleven dispatch-site edits, including the public REST endpoint apps/api/src/controllers/export.controller.ts:201 which returns FinalChart to external API consumers and is an undocumented sixth surface; (3) removal of `.strict()` or a schema widening in packages/mcp/src/tools/dashboard-management.ts:15 before MCP can write a metrics report; (4) an explicit contract that the metrics engine reproduces the event engine's zero-filled, identically-formatted date grid, because apps/start/src/hooks/use-rechart-data-model.ts:19-52 takes the x-axis from series[0] and matches by exact string equality; (5) replication of the `getOrganizationSubscriptionChartEndDate` clamp; and (6) suppression of the "View Users" drilldown and honest handling of `metrics.sum`-based percent-of-total in bar/table renderers, which render but lie for gauges and ratios. Finally, the plan should not lean on "the existing surfaces already prove this works" — there are no tests over FinalChart at all, so equivalence between the two engines has to be newly established rather than inherited.

## Investigation 21 — `partially_confirmed`

The first engineer's evidence is real and I could reproduce essentially all of it from independent routes. `chartProcedure` (chart.ts:83-142) is a `publicProcedure`-based middleware that does its own share/member auth; `chart` (588) and `aggregate` (612) are `chartProcedure.use(cacher)` bodies whose entire content is a 3-line `ctx.report ? merge : input` then `ChartEngine.execute` / `AggregateChartEngine.execute`, both returning `FinalChart`. `Report.dataSource` does not exist anywhere in either repo, and the discriminator cannot live on the Prisma row alone because `ctx.report` is null on every non-shared query. Where I go further than they did: the plumbing cost is bigger than "extend transformReport" — a `dataSource` column has to be threaded through FOUR explicit field-by-field whitelists (report.ts:54 create, report.ts:97 update, report.ts:225 duplicate, reports.service.ts:83 transformReport), `chartType` is a Postgres ENUM so the alternative design needs an `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` migration, `overview.ts:57` is a second structurally identical share-aware seam they never mention, and there is ZERO test coverage of `chartProcedure` or either engine. I also disagree with one of their factual characterizations: chart.ts contains no `chartType === 'funnel' | 'metric'` dispatch at all, so "five call sites each with its own hand-rolled dispatch" is wrong — there are exactly four such dispatches in three files.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:54,83-142` — Confirmed verbatim. `const cacher = cacheMiddleware(60);` at 54. `const chartProcedure = publicProcedure.use(async ({ ctx, next, getRawInput }) => {...})` at 83. Share branch: requires `rawInput.id` (`throw new Error('reportId required with shareId')`), `validateShareAccess(rawInput.shareId, rawInput.id, { cookies, session })`, `if (!shareValidation.isValid) throw new TRPCForbiddenError(...)`, `getReportById(rawInput.id)`, `next({ ctx: { report } })`. **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's core mechanics are accurate but its conclusion overreaches: `chart.ts` is the natural seam only for the in-app dashboard's tRPC read path (7 of 11 chart types). It is not the seam for MCP, the in-app agent, the dashboard agent tool, or the REST `/export/charts` endpoint, none of which pass through tRPC.
- `Report.dataSource` does not exist. `grep -rn dataSource --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.prisma apps packages` returns zero hits in either repo. The identifier is entirely hypothetical.
- A discriminator on the Prisma row cannot drive the live path. At chart.ts:598 `chartInput = ctx.report ? {...} : input` and `ctx.report` is `null` for every authenticated in-app query (chart.ts:139). The editor and every non-shared tile send `zReportInput` from the browser (context.tsx:53-63). The discriminator MUST also exist on `zReportInput`.
- DISAGREEMENT WITH THE FIRST ENGINEER: their summary says `ChartEngine.execute` has 'five call sites ... each with its own hand-rolled `chartType === 'funnel' | 'metric'` dispatch'. That is wrong for two of the five. chart.ts:588-634 contains NO chartType dispatch whatsoever — the browser picks the procedure (report-chart/index.tsx:39-64), and `metric` charts actually call `trpc.chart.chart` (ChartEngine), not `chart.aggregate`. And export.controller.ts:201 hardcodes `chartType: 'linear', metric: 'sum'` and never dispatches. There are exactly FOUR chartType dispatches, in THREE files: reports.service.ts:209/214, mcp/reports.ts:300/302 and 347/349, agents/tools/dashboard.ts:97/101.
- The first engineer says a new column needs `transformReport()` extended. Understated — it needs FOUR whitelists: `transformReport` (reports.service.ts:83, read) plus three write-side `data: {...}` literals in report.ts (create:54, update:97, duplicate:225). Miss any write site and the field silently stops round-tripping.
- Neither the claim nor the first engineer notes that `chartType` is a Postgres ENUM (schema.prisma:385-397), so the obvious alternative design — a `metric`/`promql` chartType instead of a `dataSource` column — costs an `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` migration, a hazard the schema itself documents at schema.prisma:420-422.
- The claim's framing 'a chartProcedure with a cacher middleware' is loose in the way the first engineer noted, and I confirm it: `cacher` is a module-level `cacheMiddleware(60)` (chart.ts:54) applied per-procedure at 457, 499, 589, 613, 637. It is not part of `chartProcedure`.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The cohort/retention procedure is a hole in the plan. `cohort` (chart.ts:636) is a `chartProcedure` but takes a bespoke `z.object` input, not `zReportInput`. Adding `dataSource` to `zReportInput` reaches chart/aggregate/funnel/conversion but NOT cohort.
- `overview.ts:57` defines `overviewProcedure`, a second share-aware `publicProcedure` with the identical shareId/session branch and its own range-sensitive `cacher` (overview.ts:40-55). If telemetry ever appears on the project overview page (the default landing surface), that is a second seam requiring the same treatment. Its inline comment explicitly documents a prior bug class: ignoring `isValid` on a password-protected share leaves data open to anyone holding the link.
- ZERO test coverage on the seam. No test file in the repo references `chartRouter`, `chartProcedure`, `ChartEngine`, or `AggregateChartEngine`. Given the plan calls per-project label enforcement a SECURITY BOUNDARY, cloning an untested auth middleware as the template for that boundary is a risk worth naming; `packages/trpc/src/routers/share.test.ts` is the pattern to copy (it uses `router.createCaller` with a mocked `@openpanel/db`) and shows the maintainer already writes regression tests for share-access CVEs (GHSA-7gv7-c464-9wh8).
- `validateShareAccess` throws bare `new Error(...)` for missing/non-public shares (share.service.ts:148, 186, 214) instead of returning `{isValid:false}`. Through tRPC those become INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, not FORBIDDEN. A metrics procedure cloned from `chartProcedure` inherits that inconsistency.
- `runReportFromConfig` (mcp/reports.ts:307) types its config as `{ chartType: string; ...; [key: string]: unknown }` and casts `as unknown as Parameters<typeof ChartEngine.execute>[0]`. That index signature plus the double cast means a `dataSource` field passes through with no type checking and no validation — a metrics spec could reach the event engine here with no compile error.
- The redis cache key is `trpc:${path}:` + `JSON.stringify(rawInput)` (trpc.ts:203-206) with no userId component. It is only project-scoped because `projectId` happens to be in rawInput. If a metrics query spec is ever accepted where the project is derived server-side rather than present in the input, the 60s cache becomes cross-tenant. This directly constrains the plan's decision #2.
- The plan's decision #4 (metrics engine returns `FinalChart`) is mechanically sound: `executeChart` and `executeAggregateChart` both declare `Promise<FinalChart>` (engine/index.ts:27, 84-86) and `FinalChart` is `{ series: IChartSerie[]; metrics: Metrics }` (types.validation.ts:106-109). But the renderers are selected by `chartType` (a Postgres enum), so 'every chart renderer works unchanged' holds only if metric reports reuse existing chartType values.
- The existing extension point that costs no migration is `options` — `zReportOptions` is a `z.discriminatedUnion('type', ...)` (validation/index.ts:198-205) over a Json column annotated `/// [IReportOptions]` (schema.prisma:443-444), and it already round-trips through all four whitelists (`options: report.options`). If the goal is a discriminator with minimal plumbing, `options` is the path of least resistance the codebase already sanctions; a top-level `dataSource` column is the higher-cost option.
- `export.controller.ts:16-45` authorizes via `request.client?.type === ClientType.read` and `request.client?.organizationId`. This is the same `Client`/`ClientType` machinery the plan proposes to reuse for telemetry ingest tokens — so it is a live precedent, but note it is a REST/client-token path that bypasses tRPC entirely and would need its own telemetry equivalent.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan should stop describing chart.ts as "the" seam and describe it as "the seam for the dashboard read path", then explicitly enumerate the other four executors it must also branch (reports.service.getReportDataCore, mcp runReport, mcp runReportFromConfig, agents/tools/dashboard.ts) — otherwise MCP, the in-app chat, and the dashboard agent will execute a metric report as an event report and return an empty or wrong FinalChart with no error. Concretely: (a) the discriminator must live on `zReportInput` (validation/index.ts:233) as well as on the Prisma model, because `ctx.report` is null for every live editor query; (b) budget four whitelist edits (report.ts:54/97/225 write, reports.service.ts:83 read), not one; (c) decide up front between a `dataSource` column (needs a Prisma migration + four whitelists) and extending the existing `options` discriminated union (Json column, no migration, already round-trips) — the codebase's own convention is the latter; (d) if the design instead adds a chartType, budget a Postgres `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` migration; (e) the cohort procedure needs separate handling since its input is not zReportInput; (f) `overview.ts` is a parallel seam if metrics ever land on the overview page; (g) since the plan calls project isolation a security boundary and `chartProcedure` has zero tests, the metrics procedure should ship with a `createCaller`-style test modeled on packages/trpc/src/routers/share.test.ts; and (h) the 60s redis cache key contains no userId, so the metrics query spec must carry projectId in the raw input or the cache will leak across tenants.
