## Investigation 22 — `partially_confirmed`

I reach the same headline verdict as the first engineer but by a different route, and I found two of their evidence statements to be factually false. The syntax half of the claim (`TTL <expr> DELETE WHERE <cond>`) remains genuinely UNVERIFIABLE from anything on disk: neither repo vendors ClickHouse source, docs or a grammar; /opt/homebrew/bin/clickhouse is confirmed dangling (its Caskroom dir exists but is empty, and `clickhouse --version` fails with "no such file or directory"); and no server is listening on 127.0.0.1:8123 or :9000, so no parse test was possible. The feasibility half is correctly identified as blocked by gigapipe forcing `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:78-79) — but the first engineer's conclusion that "part-level retention cannot substitute" is wrong for the plan as actually written, because both samples_v3 and metrics_15s are `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:25, :83) and OpenPanel's own doc (docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:32) pre-creates them with `type` in PARTITION BY, which makes every part signal-homogeneous and therefore compatible with ttl_only_drop_parts=1. Their two false statements: gigapipe DOES set `materialize_ttl_after_modify` (to "0", ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:34, with git history showing it was set to 1 and rolled back), and `DELETE WHERE` does NOT return zero hits in OpenPanel (five real occurrences).

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:31-35` — REFUTES the first engineer's claim that "neither repo sets or mentions that setting". The clickhouse-go connection used by every maintenance operation sets `Settings: map[string]interface{}{ "allow_experimental_database_replicated": "1", "materialize_ttl_after_modify": "0" }`. ConnectV2 is the connection used by rotateDB (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:114) and upgradeDB (maintain.go:16), so every gigapipe `MODIFY TTL` runs with materialization explicitly disabled — the new TTL applies only to parts written or merged afterwards.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe git history: 99d5043 "materialize_ttl_after_modify TTL (#60)" and 8c1771e "rollback materialize_ttl_after_modify"` — Corroborates the above from history. 99d5043 (Nov 2021, lib/db/clickhouse.js) added `materialize_ttl_after_modify = 1` to the same `MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1, merge_with_ttl_timeout = 3600, ... index_granularity = 8192` statement that survives verbatim in today's Go code; 8c1771e reverted it two days later with the message "rollback materialize_ttl_after_modify pending version check". The project has deliberately chosen non-materializing MODIFY TTL twice.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/utils/unmarshal/unmarshal.go:146-165 and :206-227` — CORRECTS the characterization of type=0 as legacy rows. Both Loki push decoders do `tp |= model.SAMPLE_TYPE_LOG` when a line is present and `tp |= model.SAMPLE_TYPE_METRIC` when a numeric value is present, then `if tp == 3 { tp = 0 }` (lines 163 and 225). type=0 is therefore ACTIVELY WRITTEN TODAY for any entry carrying both a string and a value — it is not merely a pre-migration residue. Any conditional TTL or sweep predicate must treat type=0 as a first-class, currently-produced value.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:135 vs :192-200` — NEW FINDING the first engineer missed. `storagePolicyUpdate(db, clusterName, distributed, storagePolicy, "metrics_15s", "metrics_15s")` (line 135) and the metrics_15s `rotateTables(..., "metrics_15s", logger, "metrics_15s")` (lines 192-200) use the SAME bookkeeping setting name. getSetting/putSetting fingerprint on `{"type":"rotate", "name":"metrics_15s"` (rotate.go:17-18, 39-41), so both writers share one row and overwrite each other. When STORAGE_POLICY is set, each boot the storage-policy check sees the TTL string, re-applies and rewrites; then the rotate check sees the storage policy, re-applies `MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` and `MODIFY TTL` and rewrites. metrics_15s is therefore clobbered on EVERY restart, not only on config change. storagePolicyUpdate short-circuits on `storagePolicy == ""` (rotate.go:103), so the collision is dormant on a default self-host with no STORAGE_POLICY.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:73-94` — I confirm the guard and the clobber verbatim. `val, err := getSetting(db, distributed, "rotate", settingName); if err != nil || val == rotateTTLStr { return err }` (73-76), then per table `ALTER TABLE %s %s MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1, merge_with_ttl_timeout = 3600, index_granularity = 8192` (78-79) and `ALTER TABLE %s %s MODIFY TTL %s` (87), then putSetting (94). The generated TTL (51-66) is move-to-disk clauses plus one unconditional `<expr> + toIntervalDay(N)` drop clause — no WHERE is ever emitted. Confirmed for samples_v3 (155-165), time_series/time_series_gin (167), tempo_traces (175), tempo_traces_attrs_gin/tempo_traces_kv (184), metrics_15s (192), patterns (202).
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/maintenance/maintain.go:28-29 + /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:66-81, :146-152` — STRENGTHENS their opt-out conclusion. `SAMPLES_DAYS=0` is not an escape hatch in the Go build: TTLDays flows into upgradeDB which returns `fmt.Errorf("ttl_days should be set for node#%s", dbObject.Node)` when it is 0, and initDB panics on that error. (git 99d5043 shows SAMPLES_DAYS=0 DID disable rotation in the old JS build, so this is a behavioural regression worth knowing.) `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES` (main.go:67-72) returning before both ctrl.Init and ctrl.Rotate is confirmed as the only clean opt-out.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:25-32, :83-94, :115-128` — samples_v3 is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` with `PARTITION BY toStartOfDay(toDateTime(timestamp_ns / 1000000000))`; metrics_15s is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` AggregatingMergeTree with `PARTITION BY toDate(toDateTime(intDiv(timestamp_ns, 1000000000)))`. `type UInt8` arrives later via ALTER (119-120). NOTE the asymmetry the first engineer missed: time_series and metrics_15s get `MODIFY ORDER BY` to include type (115-117, 126-128), but samples_v3 gets ADD COLUMN only — so on samples_v3 `type` is in neither the partition key nor the sort key, and a `WHERE type = 1` TTL/sweep predicate cannot be index-pruned there.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/services/delete.service.ts:61, packages/db/src/services/import.service.ts:183,199, packages/db/scripts/find-duplicate-events.ts:308, test/fixtures.ts:388, test/retention-fixtures.ts:221` — REFUTES "a repo-wide grep for `DELETE WHERE` across OpenPanel returns zero hits". Five production/test occurrences exist, e.g. delete.service.ts:61 `? \`ALTER TABLE ${getReplicatedTableName(table)} DELETE WHERE ${where};\``. These are mutation DELETEs, not TTL clauses, so the engineer's underlying point about TTL syntax stands — but the statement as written is wrong, and it obscures that OpenPanel already owns a cluster-aware `ALTER … DELETE WHERE` helper the plan's shorter-tier sweep layer can reuse rather than reinvent.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/logql/logql_transpiler/clickhouse_planner/sql_misc.go:213-220 + /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/service/prom_queryable.go:170` — Confirms the read-side predicate, and fixes a bad citation: the constants live at reader/logql/logql_transpiler/shared/types.go:12-14, NOT at `shared/types.go` (no such file at the repo root). GetTypes emits `type IN (tp, 0)` and coerces BOTH→LOGS. prom_queryable.go:170 sets `Type: 2` for the PromQL path, so metric queries read `type IN (2, 0)` and log queries read `type IN (1, 0)` — type=0 rows are returned by both.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:68 and self-hosting/clickhouse/*.xml` — Confirmed: `image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65`, single node, no cluster env. Grepping the two mounted config files for `merge_tree` / `ttl_only_drop_parts` returns nothing (only `<profiles>` in clickhouse-user-config.xml:2), so server-side TTL defaults are unpinned — confirming the first engineer on this point.
- `local toolchain check (no repo file)` — `ls /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/clickhouse/26.6.1.1193-stable/` lists no files and `/opt/homebrew/bin/clickhouse --version` fails with "no such file or directory"; `nc -z 127.0.0.1 8123` and `:9000` both closed. Independently confirms that no empirical parse test of `TTL … DELETE WHERE` against any ClickHouse build was possible on this machine. The syntax and its version floor remain UNVERIFIED.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/model/sample.go:22-36 and reader/model/time_series.go:30-36` — Warning for anyone grepping after me: these two files contain `TTL toDateTime(timestamp_ms / 1000) + toIntervalDay(7)` and `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` inside dead COMMENT blocks describing the long-retired `cloki.samples` table (TableName() returns "samples"). They are not live DDL and must not be cited as evidence of current behaviour.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- FALSE STATEMENT IN THEIR EVIDENCE: "neither repo sets or mentions that setting" (materialize_ttl_after_modify). It is set, to "0", on the connection every maintenance operation uses — /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:34 — and git commits 99d5043/8c1771e show it was set to 1 and then rolled back. This flips their advice: the behaviour is not unknown, it is pinned OFF by gigapipe. A hand-applied `MODIFY TTL` from OpenPanel would inherit whatever the OpenPanel client sets, so the plan must decide materialization explicitly rather than treating it as an open question.
- FALSE STATEMENT IN THEIR EVIDENCE: "a repo-wide grep for `DELETE WHERE` ... across OpenPanel returns zero hits". There are five: packages/db/src/services/delete.service.ts:61, packages/db/src/services/import.service.ts:183 and :199, packages/db/scripts/find-duplicate-events.ts:308, plus test/fixtures.ts:388 and test/retention-fixtures.ts:221. Their point about TTL-clause syntax is unaffected, but the grep claim is wrong and it hides an existing cluster-aware `ALTER … DELETE WHERE` helper the plan's sweep layer should reuse.
- OVERSTATED: "Part-level retention cannot substitute, because samples_v3 partitions by day only." True of a gigapipe-created table, false of the plan as written. samples_v3 and metrics_15s are both `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:25, :83), and docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:32 already pre-creates them with `type` in the PARTITION BY before gigapipe's first boot. With signal-homogeneous partitions, ttl_only_drop_parts=1 and a conditional TTL are compatible: every row in a part shares one TTL clause, so the whole part expires together. Their correction would push the plan into flipping ttl_only_drop_parts to 0 and eating a merge-cost regression that the pre-create approach avoids.
- UNDERSTATED: they call type=0 rows "old pre-migration rows". They are actively written today. writer/utils/unmarshal/unmarshal.go:163 and :225 collapse `tp == 3` (line AND value present) to 0 in both Loki push decoders. A type=0 row is produced by live ingest and is visible to both log and metric queries, so a two-clause TTL must assign it deliberately (the plan's `type != 1` / `type = 1` split does exactly this) rather than treating it as a shrinking legacy tail.
- INCOMPLETE: "the clobber is config-change-triggered, not restart-triggered." Correct for samples_v3, wrong for metrics_15s when STORAGE_POLICY is set. rotate.go:135 and rotate.go:192-200 share the bookkeeping setting name "metrics_15s", so the storage-policy writer and the TTL writer overwrite each other's row and both ALTERs — including `MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` — re-run on every process start.
- BAD CITATION: they cite `shared/types.go:12-14`. No such file exists at the gigapipe repo root; the constants are at reader/logql/logql_transpiler/shared/types.go:12-14.
- UNCHANGED AND STILL CORRECT: the syntax half of the claim is UNVERIFIABLE from disk. I independently confirmed the dangling Homebrew symlink (Caskroom dir empty, binary exec fails) and additionally confirmed no ClickHouse is listening on 8123/9000, and that neither repo vendors a ClickHouse grammar or docs. Do not let the plan assert `TTL … DELETE WHERE` works on 25.10.2.65 without an actual `EXPLAIN`/DDL test against that image.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe's `MODIFY TTL` never materializes over existing parts, because ConnectV2 pins `materialize_ttl_after_modify = 0` at the connection level (ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:34). Whatever OpenPanel's TTL cron does is therefore NOT symmetric with gigapipe's own behaviour by default — docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:709-716 already reasons about this knob, and it should cite shared.go:34 as the reason gigapipe's own rotation is free.
- On samples_v3 specifically, `type` is in neither the partition key nor the sort key: log.sql:119-120 does ADD COLUMN only, whereas time_series (115-117) and metrics_15s (126-128) both get `MODIFY ORDER BY` to include type. Any sweep predicate `WHERE type = 1` on a gigapipe-created samples_v3 is a full scan of the touched partitions. Pre-creating with type in the partition key fixes this too.
- metrics_15s is an AggregatingMergeTree fed by `metrics_15s_mv` selecting FROM samples_v3 and grouping by (fingerprint, timestamp_ns, type) (log.sql:146-158). Deleting rows out of samples_v3 by TTL or by sweep does NOT retract the corresponding metrics_15s aggregates — the MV is insert-triggered only. Any per-signal retention design must apply to metrics_15s independently, which the plan does (D8), but the reason should be stated as MV semantics, not just table count.
- `SAMPLES_DAYS=0` is a hard startup failure, not a rotation opt-out: maintain.go:28-29 returns `ttl_days should be set for node#%s` and cmd/gigapipe/main.go:78-80 panics. This regressed from the JS build, where 99d5043 explicitly documented "LABELS_DAYS or SAMPLES_DAYS set to 0 will disable rotation/alter operations". OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=true is confirmed as the only clean opt-out, and it also disables schema creation — so pre-creating the full schema is a prerequisite for using it, not an alternative to it.
- time_series (the label/fingerprint table) is rotated on the same global dropTTLDays (rotate.go:167-173) and is partitioned by `date` only, mixing log and metric fingerprints. Unlike samples_v3 it does have `type` in its ORDER BY (log.sql:115-117), so a conditional TTL there would at least prune. The plan currently gives time_series/time_series_gin an unconditional TTL at the longest tier (docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:779-780) — that is the safe choice, but it means label cardinality is retained at the metrics window even for logs.
- reader/model/sample.go:22-36 and reader/model/time_series.go:30-36 contain TTL and ttl_only_drop_parts strings inside dead comment blocks for the retired `cloki.samples` table. They are grep noise that could easily be mis-cited as current schema.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's conditional-TTL section stands, but three things must change. (1) Stop treating `materialize_ttl_after_modify` as an unknown — cite ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:34, state that gigapipe pins it to 0, and make OpenPanel's TTL cron set it explicitly per direction (lengthen = 0, shorten = 1 once), which is what docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:709-716 already proposes. (2) Keep the pre-create-with-type-in-PARTITION-BY decision (D4) and do NOT adopt the first engineer's correction that ttl_only_drop_parts must be flipped to 0 — signal-homogeneous partitions make part-level TTL correct and cheap, and flipping the setting is a merge-cost regression the plan can avoid; keep the flip only as the documented fallback if pre-creation fails. (3) Add the metrics_15s setting-name collision (rotate.go:135 vs :192-200) to the risk list: the plan's claim at line 795-802 that \"our TTL survives gigapipe restarts\" is true for samples_v3 but false for metrics_15s whenever STORAGE_POLICY is configured, so either leave STORAGE_POLICY unset or have the nightly reconciler re-stamp metrics_15s unconditionally. Independently, the plan must not assert `TTL … DELETE WHERE` parses on clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65 until someone runs the DDL against that image — that remains the single unverified load-bearing premise, and the pre-create approach does not remove the need for it.

## Investigation 23 — `partially_confirmed`

I reached the same verdict by a different route (runtime scripts, docs, gigapipe's own test compose, and an empirical sed replay) and the first engineer's evidence is real and accurately quoted — I checked every file they cited and found no fabrication. The mechanical core holds: `self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml` has no `networks:` block and no `ports:` on `op-ch`, so a `op-gigapipe` service slots in and reaches `op-ch:9000` on the compose default network; nothing in the ClickHouse config or init files restricts a second database (no `<users>`, no `readonly`, no `default_database`), and gigapipe creates its own database at boot. Two things sharpen the picture beyond their answer: `apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/high-volume.mdx:16-70` already documents adding an extra service (`op-pgbouncer`) to the self-hosted compose by hand — a first-party precedent that both proves the mechanics and shows the intended delivery channel for existing installs — and `apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker-compose.mdx:32` tells operators to `git clone -b self-hosting`, meaning `./update`'s `git pull` tracks a *separate branch*, not `main`, which is a bigger delivery gap than the gitignore point they raised. One of their corrections is over-confident and wrong: gigapipe does **not** need `CLICKHOUSE_AUTH=default:` — gigapipe's own integration stack at `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/test/integration/docker-compose.yml:13-27` connects to a stock ClickHouse with no `CLICKHOUSE_AUTH` at all.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:67-90` — Verified independently. `op-ch` has image `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65`, three `:ro` mounts, `CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1`, a `clickhouse-client --query "SELECT 1"` healthcheck, ulimits, logging — and no `ports:` key. I read the whole 174-line file: the only top-level keys are `version`, `services`, and `volumes:` at line 164. No `networks:` block anywhere, so every service is on the compose default network and resolvable by service name.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/high-volume.mdx:16-70` — MISSED BY THE FIRST ENGINEER, and it is the strongest confirmation of the mechanical claim. Section heading: `### Add PGBouncer to docker-compose.yml`, followed by a full `op-pgbouncer:` service block (`image: edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.1-p0`, `depends_on: op-db: {condition: service_healthy}`, env, healthcheck, logging) with no `networks:` key, addressed by service name via `DB_HOST=op-db`. This is a shipped, first-party instruction to add a service to the self-hosted compose by hand — so the pattern the claim proposes is already the documented mechanism, and hand-editing `docker-compose.yml` is the supported delivery path for existing installs, not merely a defect.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker-compose.mdx:29-33` — MISSED BY THE FIRST ENGINEER. The install instruction is `git clone -b self-hosting https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel.git` then `cd openpanel/self-hosting`. Self-hosters track a branch named `self-hosting`, not `main`. So `./update`'s `git pull` (self-hosting/update:3) pulls that branch — a gigapipe service added to the template on `main` does not reach any operator until it is merged to `self-hosting`. This is a delivery gap on top of the gitignore one. (`git branch -a` in this checkout shows only `main` and `origin/main`, and `git ls-remote` returned nothing in this sandbox, so I could not confirm the branch exists remotely — the docs instruction is the verified fact; the branch's existence is UNVERIFIED here.)
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/test/integration/docker-compose.yml:4-27` — REFUTES one of the first engineer's corrections. gigapipe's own integration stack is exactly the shape the claim proposes: `clickhouse:` (stock `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.9.1`, no user config) plus `gigapipe:` with `depends_on: {clickhouse: {condition: service_healthy}}` and environment `CLICKHOUSE_SERVER: clickhouse`, `CLICKHOUSE_PORT: "9000"`, `PORT: "3100"`, `BULK_MAX_AGE_MS: "100"`. No `networks:`, no `CLICKHOUSE_AUTH`, no `CLICKHOUSE_DB` — so gigapipe connects to a stock ClickHouse as the empty-password default user and creates database `cloki` (its default) alongside whatever else is there. `CLICKHOUSE_AUTH=default:` is not required. `test/integration/run.sh:1-28` shows this stack is actually built and exercised (`docker compose up -d --build`, then `go test -tags integration`).
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/docs/otlp-grpc.md:8-21` — Strengthens the "no ports exposed" half beyond the first engineer's `EXPOSE 3100` citation. "There is no environment variable to set... the gRPC receiver is multiplexed onto the same port as OTLP/HTTP — `PORT` (default `3100`)." So gigapipe needs exactly one internal port for OTLP/HTTP *and* OTLP/gRPC; one unexposed service suffices. Caveat for the plan (not this claim): "The transport is cleartext HTTP/2 using prior-knowledge negotiation (no TLS, no ALPN). An HTTP/1.1-only proxy or load balancer placed in front of gigapipe will break gRPC traffic" — relevant if OTLP/gRPC is ever proxied through apps/api or Caddy.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/clickhouse/clickhouse-config.xml:1-29` — The first engineer quoted the *user* config but not this one, which is where a database restriction would most plausibly live. Full contents: logger level/console, `keep_alive_timeout`, eight `remove="remove"` log-table disables, `<listen_host>0.0.0.0</listen_host>`, `<interserver_listen_host>0.0.0.0</interserver_listen_host>`, `<interserver_http_host>op-ch</interserver_http_host>`, and macros (shard 1 / replica1 / cluster `openpanel_cluster`). No `default_database`, no `<remote_servers>`, nothing scoping the server to one database — confirms the second half of the claim. Note the absent `<remote_servers>`: the `openpanel_cluster` macro is labelled "Not used anymore", so gigapipe's `CLUSTER_NAME` must be left UNSET, or its `ON CLUSTER` DDL (ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:50-53) would target a cluster that is not defined. Neither engineer's answer flagged this.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:177` — Slight correction to the first engineer's phrasing ("Nothing in OpenPanel hardcodes the `openpanel` database name"). `getExistingTables()` runs `SELECT name FROM system.tables WHERE database = 'openpanel'` — the database name IS hardcoded, in the migration runner. This actually supports the claim: OpenPanel's migration enumeration is scoped to `openpanel`, so a second gigapipe database on the same server is invisible to it and cannot be picked up or dropped. The only other `system.tables` use, packages/db/code-migrations/19-event-property-values-projections.ts:111, scopes with `database = currentDatabase()` — also safe.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/get_latest_images:7,270-280` — CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, not just by reading. `COMPONENTS=("worker" "api" "dashboard")` (line 7); apply_tags does `sed -i "s|image:.*${component}.*|image: docker.openpanel.dev/openpanel-dev/${component}:main-${short_sha}|g"` (lines 276/279) over `${DOCKER_COMPOSE_FILE:-./docker-compose.yml}`. I replayed the exact loop in the scratchpad against a file containing `image: ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe:latest`; output was `image: docker.openpanel.dev/openpanel-dev/api:main-abc1234`. The gigapipe image line is silently rewritten to the OpenPanel API image. (Only `api` matches — `worker` and `dashboard` do not appear in "gigapipe".)
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/quiz.ts:89-139,389-414` — Confirms and extends the first engineer's regeneration point. `fs.copyFileSync(template -> docker-compose.yml)` at 390-393, then conditional `removeServiceFromDockerCompose(...)`. Crucially, that function is a full `yaml.load` -> mutate -> `yaml.dump` round trip (lines 94, 135), so it strips every comment and reformats the file. Added detail neither answer covers: at line 395, if the operator supplied their own `CLICKHOUSE_URL`, `op-ch` is *removed* from the compose, and lines 106-121 then strip `op-ch` out of every `depends_on`. A gigapipe service hardwired to `CLICKHOUSE_SERVER=op-ch` would survive that deletion and point at a host that no longer exists. gigapipe's five ClickHouse vars would have to be derived from the operator-supplied CLICKHOUSE_URL in that branch.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/.env.template:1-16 and quiz.ts:141-166` — Verified as claimed. 16 lines, and `writeEnvFile` does a fixed list of nine `.replace()` calls then `.filter(line => !line.includes('=""'))`. A new `GIGAPIPE_URL="$GIGAPIPE_URL"` line would be emitted with the literal `$GIGAPIPE_URL` unless a matching replace is added. Note `.replace()` (not `replaceAll`) is used throughout — single-occurrence only.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/coolify.yml:35-108` — Confirms the third-surface correction, and I read the part the first engineer only grepped. `opch:` uses `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.3.2-alpine` with all three ClickHouse files inlined as Coolify `content:` binds (config at 44-75, users at 76-88, init-db at 89-100), the same `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS openpanel;` at line 98, and — as they said — no `CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP`. Neighbours also differ: `postgres:16-alpine` (line 9) and `redis:7.4-alpine` (line 24) vs 14/7.2.5 in the template. Its users block is likewise profiles-only, no `<users>`, no `readonly` — so a second database is permitted here too.

Also confirmed their drift note: `op-ch-migrator` appears in the entire repo only at quiz.ts:397 — the service no longer exists in the template.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- WRONG in the first engineer's answer: "gigapipe would need `CLICKHOUSE_AUTH=default:`". It does not. gigapipe's own integration stack (/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/test/integration/docker-compose.yml:13-27) runs against a stock ClickHouse image with no CLICKHOUSE_AUTH set at all and works — main.go:117-123 simply leaves User/Password empty, which the ClickHouse client resolves to the default user. Combined with `CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1` on op-ch (which keeps `default` password-less), no auth var is required in the self-hosting compose. Setting it is harmless, but presenting it as a requirement is over-confident.
- INCOMPLETE in the first engineer's answer: they framed delivery-to-existing-installs purely as a defect (gitignored file, `git pull` can't touch it). apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/high-volume.mdx:16-70 shows OpenPanel already ships first-party instructions for hand-adding a service (`op-pgbouncer`) to the generated docker-compose.yml, with the exact `depends_on: {condition: service_healthy}` shape and no `networks:` key. So there is a supported, documented delivery path for a gigapipe service on existing installs — a docs page, not a template edit. That materially softens the "reaches nobody" framing.
- MISSED by the first engineer, and a larger delivery gap than the one they found: apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker-compose.mdx:32 instructs `git clone -b self-hosting`. Self-hosters track a `self-hosting` BRANCH. `./update`'s `git pull` therefore pulls that branch, not `main` — so a template change on main is invisible to operators regardless of the gitignore issue, until it is merged to that branch. (The branch's remote existence is UNVERIFIED in this sandbox; only the docs instruction is confirmed.)
- MISSED by both: quiz.ts:395-398 removes `op-ch` from the compose entirely when the operator brings their own ClickHouse, and lines 106-121 strip `op-ch` from every `depends_on`. A gigapipe service hardcoded to `CLICKHOUSE_SERVER=op-ch` survives that deletion pointing at a nonexistent host. Whatever translates OpenPanel's single CLICKHOUSE_URL into gigapipe's five vars must run in that branch too.
- MISSED by both: self-hosting/clickhouse/clickhouse-config.xml:24-28 declares a `cluster` macro (`openpanel_cluster`) but the file has NO `<remote_servers>` block, and the macro is explicitly commented "Not used anymore". gigapipe's CLUSTER_NAME must therefore be left unset — setting it flips `Cloud = true` (main.go:96-99) and makes every DDL `ON CLUSTER \`name\`` (ctrl/maintenance/shared.go:50-53) against a cluster that does not exist.
- MINOR imprecision: "Nothing in OpenPanel hardcodes the `openpanel` database name at connect time" — true of connect, but packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:177 hardcodes `WHERE database = 'openpanel'` in getExistingTables(). This cuts in the claim's favour (a second database is invisible to the migration runner and cannot be touched by it), but the phrasing as written is not accurate.
- The claim's own wording "the ClickHouse init/config files there permit a second database" is true but frames the wrong thing. Nothing needs to permit anything: no config in any of the four surfaces scopes the server to one database, and gigapipe creates its own at boot. init-db.sh could not help even if edited, since /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d only runs on a fresh data directory.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- `apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/high-volume.mdx:16-70` is the template to copy for a gigapipe docs page — it is the existing, shipped pattern for adding a service to a self-hosted OpenPanel compose, and the plan should follow its shape (service block + depends_on rewrite + env change) rather than inventing a new one.
- The delivery matrix is five surfaces, not two: self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml (-> generated, gitignored docker-compose.yml), the dev-root docker-compose.yml, self-hosting/coolify.yml, .github/smoke/docker-compose.yml, and the Kubernetes path documented in deploy-kubernetes.mdx with no chart in this repo. A P0 'add one service' task must name which of these it touches; the smoke stack in particular is what CI actually boots, so an unexercised gigapipe service gets no regression coverage.
- `self-hosting/get_latest_images` corrupting the gigapipe image line is real (verified by replaying the sed). The one-line fix is to anchor the sed to the service key or to `openpanel-dev/${component}` rather than `image:.*${component}.*` — worth calling out in the plan as a required, tiny prerequisite change.
- gigapipe multiplexes OTLP/gRPC onto the same PORT as OTLP/HTTP using cleartext HTTP/2 prior-knowledge (docs/otlp-grpc.md:8-21). That is good for 'one unexposed service', but it means any future decision to proxy OTLP/gRPC through Caddy or apps/api requires HTTP/2 prior-knowledge passthrough — an HTTP/1.1-only hop breaks gRPC while leaving OTLP/HTTP working, which is a silent partial failure.
- gigapipe's docs contradict its code on the ClickHouse default protocol (docs/configuration.md:23 says http; main.go:106-115 defaults to native TCP 9000). Any compose snippet in the plan should set CLICKHOUSE_PORT and CLICKHOUSE_PROTO explicitly rather than relying on either document's stated default.
- `environment-variables.mdx:746` already misdescribes 'the bundled docker-compose.yml' as containing Redpanda, which exists only in the dev-root compose. Existing docs drift on exactly this axis, so gigapipe documentation must name the file path explicitly every time.
- quiz.ts's removeServiceFromDockerCompose is a yaml.load/yaml.dump round trip (quiz.ts:94,135) — it destroys every comment in the generated compose. Any explanatory comment placed on a gigapipe service in the template is silently deleted for the majority of operators (anyone who answers the ClickHouse/Redis/Postgres/proxy questions in a way that triggers a service removal).

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's P0 'stack' phase should not be written as "add a gigapipe service to the compose template". Four things have to be scoped in alongside it. (1) Delivery: pick the mechanism explicitly — a docs page in the high-volume.mdx style is the honest path for existing installs, since the file operators run is gitignored and regenerated, and `./update` pulls the `self-hosting` branch rather than main. (2) Config translation: something must derive gigapipe's CLICKHOUSE_SERVER/PORT/DB/PROTO from OpenPanel's single CLICKHOUSE_URL, and it must handle the quiz.ts branch where op-ch is deleted because the operator brought their own ClickHouse. CLUSTER_NAME must be left unset (no remote_servers is defined). CLICKHOUSE_AUTH is optional, not required. (3) A one-line fix to self-hosting/get_latest_images so its `api` sed stops rewriting the gigapipe image tag. (4) Surface count: coolify.yml and the smoke stack need parallel edits or an explicit "not supported yet" note, and the ClickHouse init/config files need no edit at all — dropping that from the plan removes a step. Everything the claim asserts about network reachability, absent ports, and a second database being permitted stands and needs no rework.

## Investigation 24 — `partially_confirmed`

The structural core of the claim is correct: traces and profiles live in their own ClickHouse tables defined by `ctrl/qryn/sql/traces.sql` and `ctrl/qryn/sql/profiles.sql`, entirely separate from `samples_v3`, and each does have a `_dist.sql` and a `_read_dist.sql` companion, all embedded in `ctrl/qryn/sql/sql.go`. Precision corrections: the traces table is named `tempo_traces` (not `traces`), each signal is a *family* of tables rather than one, and all of them live in the SAME single database (`{{.DB}}`) — the separation is per-table, never per-database. The dist and read-dist variants are conditional, not always present: `_dist.sql` only runs in `CLUST_MODE_DISTRIBUTED` (cluster_name set) and `_read_dist.sql` only when `CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER` is set and differs from the write cluster, so a single-node OpenPanel deployment gets neither. Most consequential for the "why it matters" framing: separate tables do NOT give you per-signal retention out of the box — `Rotate()` drives every rotated table from one `TTLDays` value (`SAMPLES_DAYS`, default 7), and the `profiles*` tables are not rotated at all and receive no TTL and no storage policy.

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/docs/configuration.md:61` — "**`SAMPLES_DAYS`** - TTL in days for stored samples (default: `7`)" — the docs present it as a samples-only knob, but rotate.go applies it to traces and metrics_15s too.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The trace table is named `tempo_traces`, not `traces`. `traces_input` exists but is `Engine=Null` — an ingest-only funnel, not storage (traces.sql:53-65). Any direct-SQL path must target `tempo_traces`.
- Each signal is a table FAMILY, not one table. Traces = `tempo_traces` + `tempo_traces_attrs_gin` + `tempo_traces_kv` (+ `traces_input` Null + 3 MVs). Profiles = `profiles` + `profiles_series` + `profiles_series_gin` + `profiles_series_keys` (+ `profiles_input` Null + 4 MVs). Storage sizing has to count the GIN/series sidecars, which for traces carry every attribute key/value per span.
- "Separate ClickHouse tables" is true but "separate databases" is not — every DDL is `{{.DB}}.<table>`; traces, profiles, logs and metrics all land in the one database the reader binds to at boot. This is consistent with the plan's decision #2, but it means the table separation gives no isolation benefit.
- The `_dist` and `_read_dist` variants are NOT unconditional. `*_dist.sql` runs only under `CLUST_MODE_DISTRIBUTED`, i.e. when `cluster_name` is configured (update.go:56-75). `*_read_dist.sql` runs only when `CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER` is set AND differs from the write cluster AND distributed mode is on (update.go:93). A single-node OpenPanel deployment will have neither set of tables — only the base MergeTree tables exist.
- The claim's implied payoff — per-signal retention comes for free because the tables are separate — does not hold as stated. `Rotate()` derives one `dropTTLDays` from one `TTLDays`/`SAMPLES_DAYS` value (default 7) and applies the identical expression to `samples_v3`, `time_series`, `tempo_traces`, `tempo_traces_attrs_gin`, `tempo_traces_kv`, `metrics_15s` and `patterns`. Traces and logs get the same number out of the box.
- The `profiles*` tables receive NO TTL and NO storage policy at all — they are absent from `Rotate()` (rotate.go:122-212). Profile data would grow unbounded unless OpenPanel applies its own `ALTER TABLE … MODIFY TTL`.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Per-signal retention needs TWO different mechanisms, not one. Logs vs metrics genuinely share `samples_v3` and are separable only by the `type UInt8` column (log.sql:119-120), so that split does require the conditional TTL the plan calls for. Traces vs logs is a plain table-level TTL on `tempo_traces` + its two GIN/KV sidecars. Profiles need a TTL created from scratch. The plan should not describe these as one problem.
- gigapipe will fight a hand-applied TTL, but only intermittently. `rotateTables` short-circuits while the stored `settings` row for that `settingName` equals the newly computed TTL string (rotate.go:73-76), so a manual `MODIFY TTL` survives — until `SAMPLES_DAYS`/`ttl_days`/`ttl_policy` changes, at which point gigapipe recomputes, sees a mismatch, and overwrites every table in its list including `tempo_traces`. Any OpenPanel per-signal retention design must either pin `SAMPLES_DAYS` and never touch it, or reapply its own TTLs after every gigapipe config change.
- `rotateTables` also unconditionally issues `ALTER TABLE … MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 1, merge_with_ttl_timeout = 3600, index_granularity = 8192` on each rotated table (rotate.go:78-79) before the TTL. `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` means TTL deletes whole parts only — a row-level conditional TTL on `samples_v3` keyed by `type` will not evict rows until the entire day-partition part qualifies. This materially affects the plan's conditional-TTL approach for splitting log vs metric retention.
- Tenancy columns are asymmetric across signals, which bears directly on the plan's label-enforcement security boundary. `tempo_traces`, `tempo_traces_attrs_gin` and `tempo_traces_kv` all carry an `oid String` column and it is the leading `ORDER BY`/`PARTITION BY` key (traces.sql:8, 18-19, 21-32). The profiles tables have no `oid` column at all — isolation there could only ride in the `tags Array(Tuple(String,String))` and the derived `fingerprint`. And `samples_v3`/`time_series` have neither `oid` nor any tenant column; isolation for logs and metrics is purely a label inside the `labels` JSON string. So the enforcement mechanism differs per signal.
- `metrics_15s` is a rollup derived from `samples_v3` by materialized view (log.sql:96-107, 146-158) and is separately TTL'd with its own setting name (rotate.go:192-197) but the same day count. It also carries the `type UInt8` column (log.sql:126-128), so any conditional-TTL scheme must be applied to `metrics_15s` as well as `samples_v3` or the rollup will outlive its source rows.
- There is a naming collision hazard in the read-dist path. `CLICKHOUSE_READ_DIST_SUFFIX` defaults to `_dist` (maintain.go:32-35), which is exactly the suffix the ordinary `*_dist.sql` tables already occupy. Since every read-dist DDL is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, enabling `CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER` without also setting `CLICKHOUSE_READ_DIST_SUFFIX` would silently no-op against the existing write-cluster Distributed tables. I could not find code that guards against this — flagging as observed behavior of the literal code, not as a confirmed bug.
- `docs/configuration.md:61` describes `SAMPLES_DAYS` as "TTL in days for stored samples", which understates its reach — it is the retention for traces and the metrics rollup too. If the OpenPanel plan documents this env var for operators, it should say so.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim can stand in the plan with three edits. (1) Fix the names: `tempo_traces` (plus `tempo_traces_attrs_gin` and `tempo_traces_kv`), and `profiles` (plus `profiles_series`, `profiles_series_gin`, `profiles_series_keys`) — and say "separate tables in the same database", since decision #2 already establishes there is only one database. (2) Drop the inference that separate tables deliver separate retention. They make it POSSIBLE, but gigapipe's `Rotate()` actively drives `tempo_traces` and `samples_v3` from the same `SAMPLES_DAYS` value and will re-flatten any manual per-table TTL whenever its own config changes. The retention section needs an explicit owner for that: either OpenPanel pins gigapipe's `ttl_days` and manages every TTL itself, or it accepts one shared number for traces and logs. (3) Add profiles to the retention plan as an unretained signal — they get no TTL and no storage policy from gigapipe at all, so if OTLP profile ingest is ever enabled (writer/grpc/profiles.go exists), that data grows without bound. Separately, the conditional-TTL idea for splitting logs from metrics inside `samples_v3` should be re-checked against `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1`, which gigapipe sets on every rotated table and which prevents row-level TTL eviction — that may make the conditional TTL ineffective as designed.

## Investigation 25 — `partially_confirmed`

The reusable machinery is real and the shape of the claim is right: `Client` (uuid id, nullable scrypt-hashed `secret`, `type ClientType @default(write)`, nullable `projectId`, `organizationId`, `ignoreCorsAndSecret`) plus `getClientByIdCached` (Redis 5 min + 60 s per-process LRU) is exactly what `apps/api` track ingestion uses to resolve a projectId, and there is migration precedent for adding an enum value. But the claim is imprecise in two load-bearing ways. First, `cors` is not on `Client` — it is `Project.cors`, read as `client.project.cors`; `Client` only carries `ignoreCorsAndSecret`. Second, and more importantly, the ingest path never inspects `client.type` at all, and every other validator that does inspect it is a deny-list on `write` (or collapses everything non-`root` to `read`). So "adding a ClientType value" does not by itself isolate telemetry tokens — it silently grants a new `telemetry` client access to the Export, Import and MCP read surfaces, and it still passes `validateSdkRequest` for event ingestion. Real reuse means adding a new validator that reuses `getClientByIdCached` + `verifyPassword` + `getCache`, plus explicit allow-list checks retro-fitted into the four existing validators.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:353-375` — `enum ClientType { read write root }` and `model Client { id String @id @default(dbgenerated("gen_random_uuid()")) @db.Uuid; name; secret String?; type ClientType @default(write); projectId String?; project Project? ...onDelete: Cascade; organization/organizationId; ignoreCorsAndSecret Boolean @default(false); createdAt; updatedAt; @@map("clients") }`. There is no `cors` field on Client.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:257-269` — `cors String[] @default([])` lives on `model Project`, alongside `crossDomain`, `allowUnsafeRevenueTracking` and `filters Json`. The CORS allow-list the ingest auth checks is per-project, not per-client.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts:42-176` — `validateSdkRequest(req)` is the whole ingest auth path. It reads clientId/secret from `openpanel-client-id` / `mixan-client-id` headers OR from `req.body.clientId` (ramda `path`), sets `req.clientSecretAuth = true` when a secret is present, enforces a UUIDv4 regex, calls `getClientByIdCached(clientId)` (line 88), rejects when `!client.project` (94-96), applies `client.project.filters` IP and profile_id blocks (98-114), enforces the `allowUnsafeRevenueTracking` rule (117-131), short-circuits on `client.ignoreCorsAndSecret` (133-135), matches `client.project.cors` incl. `*.foo.com` wildcards and `'*'` (137-161), and only then verifies the secret. It NEVER reads `client.type`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts:163-176` — Secret verification: `getCache(`client:auth:${clientId}:${Buffer.from(clientSecret).toString('base64')}`, 60 * 5, () => verifyPassword(clientSecret, client.secret!), true)` — 5 min Redis + LRU, keyed on the base64 of the *plaintext* secret. Falls through to `throw createError('Ingestion: Invalid cors or secret')`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts:186-283` — The other three validators are header-only and are deny-lists, not allow-lists: `validateExportRequest` and `validateImportRequest` both reject only `client.type === ClientType.write` (lines 202, 237); only `validateManageRequest` uses an allow-list (`if (client.type !== ClientType.root) throw`, line 272). - `cors` is not a field on the Client model. It is `Project.cors String[]` (schema.prisma:265); the ingest auth reads it as `client.project.cors` (auth.ts:137-161). The only CORS-related field on Client is `ignoreCorsAndSecret` (schema.prisma:369). Restate the claim as: Client(id, name, secret, type, projectId, organizationId, ignoreCorsAndSecret) + Project(cors, filters, allowUnsafeRevenueTracking).
- "The auth path used by track ingestion" does not discriminate on ClientType at all. `validateSdkRequest` (auth.ts:42-176) never reads `client.type` — a `read` or `root` client can ingest events today, and a new `telemetry` value would be accepted for event ingestion too unless an explicit check is added. Adding the enum value is therefore NOT sufficient to make a telemetry token telemetry-only.
- The inverse also holds and is the security-relevant half: `validateExportRequest` and `validateImportRequest` reject only `ClientType.write` (auth.ts:202, 237), and `packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:99` rejects only `write`. A new `telemetry` value is therefore *granted* Export, Import and MCP access by default. Because `packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:124-130`, `apps/api/src/controllers/insights.controller.ts:87` and `resolveClientProjectId` (project.service.ts:163-176) all collapse "anything not root" to `read`, TypeScript will not flag any of these — they are typed `'read' | 'root'`, so the new value is coerced silently.
- `validateSdkRequest` requires `client.project` to be non-null (auth.ts:94-96). Telemetry tokens reusing this path must be project-scoped; an org-level (root-style, `projectId: null`) telemetry token would be rejected. If org-level telemetry tokens are wanted, a separate validator plus `resolveClientProjectId` is needed.
- Reuse of the *auth path* is not reuse of the *route*. `validateSdkRequest` is typed against `ITrackHandlerPayload | DeprecatedPostEventPayload` and pulls clientId/clientSecret out of the JSON body, applies project IP/profile_id filters and the `__revenue` rule; `duplicateHook` and `isBotHook` are likewise body-shape-specific. Only `getClientByIdCached`, `verifyPassword`, the `getCache` secret-verification pattern, `req.client` and `subscriptionHook` transfer cleanly.
- Adding the enum value touches at least five call sites beyond the schema + migration: packages/trpc/src/routers/client.ts:58, apps/api/src/controllers/manage.controller.ts:37, apps/start/src/modals/add-client.tsx:24 (plus its hard-coded Combobox items and help text at 113-140), admin/src/utils/display.ts:195, and the four validators in apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts. The migration itself must be standalone (`ALTER TYPE "ClientType" ADD VALUE 'telemetry';`) per the precedent comment in migrations/20260818090000_add_count_to_metric_enum.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The ingest path is credential-type-blind: `validateSdkRequest` never inspects `client.type`, so `read` and `root` clients can already write events. Any statement in the plan that ClientType gates ingestion is wrong for the current code.
- The type checks elsewhere are deny-lists keyed on `write` (auth.ts:202, 237; mcp/auth.ts:99), and every `read | root` narrowing collapses unknown values to `read` (mcp/auth.ts:129, insights.controller.ts:87, project.service.ts:169). Adding an enum value is therefore fail-OPEN across Export, Import, Insights and MCP — the compiler will not catch it.
- `/track` has no rate limiter at all, while `/export` (100/10s), `/insights` (100/10s), `/manage` and `/mcp` (60/min) do. Telemetry ingest volume per request is far higher than a track event, so the plan's quota/metering work is not optional at P1.
- There is no `addContentTypeParser` and no protobuf handling anywhere in apps/api/src; `fastify-raw-body` is registered with `global: false` (app.ts:128) and `bodyLimit` is 500 MB (app.ts:88). OTLP/protobuf ingest needs a new parser registration scoped to the telemetry router.
- Secrets are scrypt (`salt.hex` format, `timingSafeEqual`) via packages/common/server/crypto.ts, NOT argon2 as the repo's CLAUDE.md summary of packages/auth implies. Generated secrets are `sec_${randomBytes(10).toString('hex')}` (20 hex chars, 80 bits) in both trpc client.ts:69 and manage.controller.ts:314 — worth deciding whether telemetry tokens want more entropy, since they will be embedded in collector configs.
- The plaintext secret is base64'd directly into a Redis key in the ingest path (`client:auth:${clientId}:${base64(secret)}`, auth.ts:165). The MCP path deliberately hashes instead (sha256, first 16 hex, mcp/auth.ts:106). A telemetry route should follow the MCP pattern; the plan should note the existing ingest key as pre-existing debt rather than a template to copy.
- There are two independent client-CRUD surfaces that both mint secrets and both would need the new type: the dashboard tRPC router (packages/trpc/src/routers/client.ts, admin-gated by `requireOrganizationAdmin`) and the root-client REST Manage API (apps/api/src/controllers/manage.controller.ts createClient/updateClient/deleteClient). `updateClient` only accepts `name` — there is no way to change a client's type after creation, so telemetry tokens must be created as telemetry from the start.
- `subscriptionHook` (wind-down ingestion block) is fully reusable for telemetry as-is: it depends only on `req.client?.projectId` and answers 202 rather than 4xx so retrying clients quiet down. It also no-ops under `SELF_HOSTED=true`, which matters for the self-hosting story in the plan.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan can keep \"reuse Client/ClientType for telemetry ingest tokens\", but the P1 task list has to be rewritten from \"add a ClientType value\" to five concrete items. (1) Standalone migration `ALTER TYPE \"ClientType\" ADD VALUE 'telemetry'` and regenerate Prisma. (2) A new `validateTelemetryRequest(headers)` in apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts that reuses `getClientByIdCached` + `verifyPassword` + `getCache` but reads credentials from headers/Bearer only (not the body), hashes the secret into the cache key the way packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:106 does rather than base64'ing the plaintext as auth.ts:165 does, and requires `client.type === ClientType.telemetry` as an allow-list. (3) DEFENSIVE EDITS to the existing validators, which are the security-relevant part: `validateExportRequest` (auth.ts:202) and `validateImportRequest` (auth.ts:237) must become allow-lists (`type === read || type === root`) instead of `!== write`, `packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:99` must reject `telemetry` explicitly, `validateSdkRequest` must reject `telemetry` so a telemetry token cannot mint analytics events, and `export.controller.ts:26` must scope by projectId for any non-root type rather than only for `read`. Without these four edits the new enum value is a privilege escalation, not an isolation mechanism. (4) A separate telemetry router (there is no rate limiter on /track and no protobuf content-type parser anywhere in apps/api) that adds `addContentTypeParser` for OTLP and its own `activateRateLimiter`/quota; it can reuse `subscriptionHook` verbatim but not `duplicateHook`/`isBotHook`. (5) Plan the label-enforcement boundary around a projectId that is authoritative for up to 60 s after revocation: `getClientByIdCached.clear()` (cachable.ts:275-279) only clears the local LRU and Redis, so other API pods keep honouring a deleted telemetry token for up to the 60 s LRU TTL. If the plan needs immediate revocation for a telemetry credential, it needs a pub/sub invalidation or a shorter LRU, which does not exist today.

## Investigation 26 — `partially_confirmed`

The claim is substantially correct on shape and mostly correct on retention, but imprecise on the type column's cardinality and on how far SAMPLES_DAYS reaches. gigapipe does store logs and metrics in one samples_v3 table (fingerprint, timestamp_ns, value, string) discriminated by a `type UInt8` column added by migration, with time_series holding the JSON label set, time_series_gin as the (key,val)->fingerprint inverted index, and metrics_15s + metrics_15s_mv as a 15-second AggregatingMergeTree rollup. The type column takes three values, not two — 0 = UNDEF/both, 1 = LOG, 2 = METRIC (writer/model/insert_request.go:8-12) — assigned per-protocol in the writer's unmarshal decoders, and every reader predicate is `type IN (n, 0)` rather than equality. SAMPLES_DAYS does default to 7 (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:146-153), but it is not scoped to samples_v3: the same value is applied by ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go as a MODIFY TTL to samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, metrics_15s, patterns, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin and tempo_traces_kv. Two facts materially affect the plan: samples_v3 is the one table where `type` was NOT added to the ORDER BY (it stays `ORDER BY (timestamp_ns)`), and metrics_15s_mv rolls up log rows too, since it has no type filter.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "SAMPLES_DAYS applies globally to the table" understates it. It applies globally to EIGHT tables across three signals: samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, metrics_15s, patterns, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:122-200). Changing SAMPLES_DAYS to get longer log retention also lengthens trace and label retention. (The `profiles` table is not rotated at all.)
- The `type` column has three values, not two: 0 = SAMPLE_TYPE_UNDEF/both, 1 = LOG, 2 = METRIC (writer/model/insert_request.go:8-12). Value 0 is actively written for Loki-JSON entries that carry both a line and a value (unmarshal.go:163, 225), and every reader predicate is `type IN (n, 0)`, never equality. A retention or read-path design that assumes `type = 1` for logs and `type = 2` for metrics will silently drop the type-0 rows.
- The claim implies type distinguishes the signal inside samples_v3 at the storage level. It does, but the column is NOT in samples_v3's sort key — samples_v3 alone kept `ORDER BY (timestamp_ns)` while time_series, time_series_gin and metrics_15s all got type appended to their ORDER BY (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:115-128; default SAMPLES_ORDER_RUL = "timestamp_ns" at ctrl/qryn/maintenance/update.go:214). Any per-type SQL or per-type TTL on samples_v3 is a full-column scan within the day partition, not a prefix seek.
- "metrics_15s as a 15-second aggregate MV" is right about the mechanism but wrong if read as metrics-only: metrics_15s_mv has no WHERE and rolls up log rows as well, carrying type through and grouping by it (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:146-158). Its `bytes` column exists precisely to serve LogQL volume queries. metrics_15s is a shared rollup for both signals, not a metrics table.
- time_series_gin is described as being "for labels" alongside time_series. Precisely: time_series holds the whole JSON label set per fingerprint, and time_series_gin is an inverted index of (key, val) -> fingerprint populated by the time_series_gin_view MV via ARRAY JOIN JSONExtractKeysAndValues (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:62-80, 132-141). The label-matcher path reads gin; the label-rendering path reads time_series.
- The claim omits that the default retention is applied only by an ALTER at boot, not by a TTL clause in the CREATE statements — no .sql file in ctrl/qryn/sql contains the word TTL. It is asserted by ctrl.Rotate on every start (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:71-83) and skipped wholesale when OMIT_CREATE_TABLES is set.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The `type` column is NOT part of samples_v3's ORDER BY. samples_v3 is `ORDER BY ({{.SAMPLES_ORDER_RUL}})`, and the default substitution is the single column `timestamp_ns` (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/update.go:214), overridable only by ADVANCED_SAMPLES_ORDERING (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:123-125). time_series, time_series_gin and metrics_15s each got `MODIFY ORDER BY (..., type)` in the same migration, but samples_v3 only got `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS type UInt8` (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:119-128). Consequence for any direct-SQL read path: on samples_v3 neither `type` nor `fingerprint` is index-assisted; only the timestamp_ns primary key and the daily partition prune the scan.
- The `type` column takes THREE values, not two. writer/model/insert_request.go:8-12 defines SAMPLE_TYPE_UNDEF = 0, SAMPLE_TYPE_LOG = 1, SAMPLE_TYPE_METRIC = 2. 0 is a real stored value meaning 'both/ambiguous': the Loki-JSON push decoder ORs the bits per entry and collapses the both-set case to 0 (writer/utils/unmarshal/unmarshal.go:148,155,163 and 211,215,225 — `if tp == 3 { tp = 0 }`). Every reader type filter is therefore `type IN (<wanted>, 0)`, never `type = <wanted>` (reader/logql/logql_transpiler/clickhouse_planner/sql_misc.go:213-220).
- The type value is assigned in the writer's per-protocol decoders, not centrally: OTLP logs -> SAMPLE_TYPE_LOG (writer/utils/unmarshal/otlplogs.go:82), Loki protobuf push -> LOG (logs_protobuf.go:33), Datadog logs -> LOG (datadog_json.go:95, datadog_cf_json.go:46), Elastic -> LOG (elastic.go:35,114), OTLP metrics -> METRIC (otlp_metrics.go:307), Prometheus remote-write protobuf -> METRIC (metrics_protobuf.go:46,61), Datadog metrics -> METRIC (datadog_metrics_json.go:40), Influx -> LOG or METRIC per point (influx.go:99,121). The value flows as `types []uint8` into builder.go:358 -> TimeSamplesData.MType -> the `type` column of the samples_v3 INSERT (writer/service/insert/samples.go:59,92).
- Traces and profiles are NOT in samples_v3 and do not use the type column. Traces live in tempo_traces / tempo_traces_attrs_gin / tempo_traces_kv (ctrl/qryn/sql/traces.sql:7-42); profiles live in profiles / profiles_series (ctrl/qryn/sql/profiles.sql:19-31). So 'logs and metrics share a table' is true; traces are already physically separate.
- SAMPLES_DAYS is broader than samples_v3: the same value (DATABASE_DATA[0].TTLDays, default 7, cmd/gigapipe/main.go:146-153) is passed as `dropTTLDays` to Rotate and applied as `MODIFY TTL <ts expr> + toIntervalDay(N)` to samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv, metrics_15s and patterns (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:122-200). One env var therefore sets retention for logs, metrics, labels, traces and the 15s rollup at once. The `profiles` table is absent from Rotate and gets no TTL at all (unverified whether a plugin adds one).
- No TTL clause exists in any ctrl/qryn/sql/*.sql file (grep for 'TTL' returns nothing there). All TTL is applied at boot by ALTER, from initDB -> ctrl.Rotate (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:71-83). Two hooks matter for per-signal retention: (a) OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=true skips both Init and Rotate entirely (main.go:72-78), and (b) rotateTables writes the computed TTL string into the `settings` table under key v3_samples_days and short-circuits when the stored value is unchanged (rotate.go:73-76, 94), so a hand-applied per-type TTL on samples_v3 survives restarts until SAMPLES_DAYS or the tiered policy changes. gigapipe itself never emits a TTL with a WHERE/type predicate: rotateTTLStr is only `<expr> + toIntervalSecond(n) [TO DISK 'x'], ..., <drop expr>` (rotate.go:52-67).
- metrics_15s_mv has no type filter: it aggregates EVERY samples_v3 row, logs included, and carries `type` through with `GROUP BY fingerprint, timestamp_ns, type` (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:146-158). Its `bytes` column is `sumSimpleState(length(string))`, i.e. log-volume bytes. The PromQL read path (reader/promql/promql_transpiler/planner/bucket_producer.go:52-57 and downsample_values.go:32-35) applies NO type predicate to metrics_15s; metric/log separation there relies entirely on the fingerprint set coming from a type-filtered time_series_gin subquery (planner_stream_select.go:72-79).
- Fingerprints are computed from labels ONLY -- type is not an input (writer/utils/unmarshal/unmarshal.go:250-270, fingerprintLabels). A log stream and a metric series with an identical label set collide on one fingerprint and are distinguished only by the type column. For the label-enforcement isolation plan this is fine (op_project_id is a label, so it is in the fingerprint), but it means a type-less direct SQL query on samples_v3/metrics_15s can mix log and metric rows for the same labels.
- A per-request TTL override already exists in the writer but is dropped on the OSS insert path: the X-Ttl-Days HTTP header (writer/controller/middleware.go:167-207), the x-ttl-days gRPC metadatum (writer/grpc/tenant.go:53-58) and a `__ttl_days__` label (writer/utils/unmarshal/builder.go:333-338) all populate TimeSeriesData.MTTLDays / TimeSamplesData.MTTLDays (writer/model/insert_request.go:162,178). But the built-in insert statements are `INSERT INTO samples_v3 (type, fingerprint, timestamp_ns, string, value)` (insert/samples.go:59) and `INSERT INTO time_series (type, date, fingerprint, labels, metadata)` (insert/time_series.go:57) -- no ttl_days column, and no ttl_days column exists in ctrl/qryn/sql at all. So the value is collected and discarded unless a writer plugin (plugins.GetSamplesInsertServicePlugin, insert/samples.go:47-51) replaces the insert service. Treat per-request TTL as a closed-source/plugin feature, not something OpenPanel can use as-is.
- reader-side type constants are duplicated, not shared with the writer: reader/logql/logql_transpiler/shared/types.go:12-14 declares SAMPLES_TYPE_LOGS = 1, SAMPLES_TYPE_METRICS = 2, SAMPLES_TYPE_BOTH = 0. PromQL sets PlannerContext.Type = 2 as a hardcoded literal (reader/service/prom_queryable.go:170); LogQL leaves it 0, and GetTypes maps 0 -> LOGS before emitting `type IN (tp, 0)` (sql_misc.go:213-220).
- One reader query uses the `type_v2` ALIAS column rather than `type`: the LogQL volume/stats query filters `type_v2 IN (0, 1)` (reader/service/query_range.go:853). type_v2 is defined as `ALIAS type` on time_series, time_series_gin, samples_v3 and metrics_15s (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:162-174, and log_dist.sql:57-68 for the _dist tables), so it is the same data under a second name -- worth knowing if you grep for type filters.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's premise for per-signal retention holds and the mechanism is workable, but three details change the design. (1) A conditional TTL must key off `type IN (1,0)` vs `type IN (2,0)`, not `type=1` / `type=2`, because Loki-JSON entries carrying both a line and a value are stored as type 0 and every gigapipe reader treats 0 as belonging to both signals. If OpenPanel's gateway only ever pushes OTLP (logs -> 1, metrics -> 2) the type-0 case never arises, so the cleanest fix is to state that OpenPanel's ingest gateway must use the OTLP/remote-write/Loki-protobuf paths and never the Loki JSON push path — then the two-value assumption becomes true by construction rather than by luck. That belongs in the P1 ingest doc as a constraint, not a footnote. (2) Any hand-written conditional TTL on samples_v3 will be overwritten by gigapipe's own `ALTER TABLE samples_v3 MODIFY TTL ...` whenever the computed TTL string changes, since Rotate runs on every boot and compares against a value it stashes in the `settings` table under v3_samples_days. The plan needs an explicit position: either pin SAMPLES_DAYS to the longest per-signal retention and let OpenPanel own a supplementary per-type TTL applied out of band (accepting that a SAMPLES_DAYS change re-asserts the base TTL), or run gigapipe with OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=true and have OpenPanel own the entire schema lifecycle including migrations. The latter is more work but is the only version where OpenPanel's TTL is authoritative. (3) SAMPLES_DAYS is not scoped to samples_v3 — it also sets the TTL for tempo_traces and the label tables — so the plan's statement that traces get their own retention knob is not free; traces share the same integer unless OpenPanel manages that ALTER itself. Separately, the plan should not count on the X-Ttl-Days / __ttl_days__ per-request TTL: the writer parses it but the open-source insert path has no ttl_days column to write it to, so it is inert without a closed-source writer plugin. Finally, for the direct-SQL read path the plan contemplates: samples_v3's primary key is timestamp_ns alone, so filtering by op_project_id-derived fingerprints or by type is not index-assisted, and metrics_15s carries log rows — a direct query must filter type explicitly or restrict to a fingerprint set resolved through the type-filtered time_series_gin, exactly as gigapipe's own planners do.

## Investigation 27 — `partially_confirmed`

The claim is directionally right about intent but wrong about feasibility as stated, and its central premise is contradicted by gigapipe's own code. ClickHouse's conditional-TTL syntax is real in principle, but it appears nowhere in either repository and support on the pinned version (clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65, self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:68) could not be confirmed from anything on disk -- the only local ClickHouse binary is a dangling Homebrew symlink, so no parse test was possible. Far more decisive: gigapipe explicitly forces `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` on samples_v3 immediately before every `MODIFY TTL` (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:79), which disables row-level TTL deletion entirely -- a `DELETE WHERE type = 1` clause would delete nothing until that setting is reversed. And part-level retention cannot substitute, because samples_v3 partitions by day only, with `type` bolted on later as a non-key column (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:26-32). On the clobbering question the answer is "conditionally yes": `MODIFY TTL` replaces the whole TTL expression and runs on every gigapipe start (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:78), but it short-circuits when gigapipe's own `settings` bookkeeping row already matches the string it would write (rotate.go:73-76) -- so a hand-applied TTL survives ordinary restarts and dies on the first SAMPLES_DAYS or storage-policy change. `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=true` (main.go:67-72) disables both schema init and rotation wholesale and is the only clean opt-out.

It sets no merge-tree TTL defaults, so ClickHouse's own defaults for ttl_only_drop_parts / materialize_ttl_after_modify apply -- and neither is pinned anywhere in the repo.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's premise -- that a conditional TTL 'makes per-signal retention possible on a shared samples_v3 table' -- is defeated as written by gigapipe's own settings. gigapipe explicitly sets `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` on samples_v3 (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:79). Under that setting ClickHouse drops only whole expired parts and never removes individual rows at merge, so a `DELETE WHERE type = 1` clause would delete nothing. The plan must additionally flip `ttl_only_drop_parts` back to 0 (and keep it there), which is a real performance regression gigapipe deliberately chose to avoid.
- Part-level retention cannot substitute, because samples_v3 partitions by day only: `PARTITION BY toStartOfDay(toDateTime(timestamp_ns / 1000000000))` (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:31). `type` is not in the partition key -- it was bolted on later via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS type UInt8`. Every partition mixes logs and metrics.
- Yes, a hand-applied `ALTER TABLE samples_v3 MODIFY TTL ...` WOULD be clobbered by gigapipe's startup path -- `MODIFY TTL` replaces the whole TTL expression (rotate.go:87) and Rotate runs on every start (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:78) -- but not unconditionally. rotate.go:73-76 short-circuits when gigapipe's own `settings` bookkeeping row for `v3_samples_days` already equals the string it would write. So the clobber is config-change-triggered, not restart-triggered. Stating it as either 'always clobbered' or 'never clobbered' would be wrong.
- The exact syntax `TTL <expr> DELETE WHERE <condition>` is NOT used, tested, or referenced anywhere in either repository, and ClickHouse 25.10.2.65's support for it could not be confirmed from anything on disk. Neither repo vendors ClickHouse source or docs, and the only local ClickHouse binary (/opt/homebrew/bin/clickhouse -> Caskroom/26.6.1.1193-stable) is a dangling symlink whose target file does not exist, so no empirical parse test was possible. Treat the syntax and its version floor as UNVERIFIED and test it against 25.10.2.65 before the plan depends on it.
- 'Merge-time only' and 'materialisation cost' are correct in spirit but unverified from source here. In particular, whether `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL` triggers a mutation to materialize TTL metadata over existing parts (the `materialize_ttl_after_modify` behaviour) could not be confirmed from any file in either repo -- neither repo sets or mentions that setting. Do not assert it in the plan document as verified.
- 'gigapipe stores logs and metrics in the same samples_v3 table keyed by a type column with a global SAMPLES_DAYS setting' is confirmed, but the type column is tri-valued (0=UNDEF, 1=LOG, 2=METRIC) and type=0 rows are returned by BOTH logs and metrics queries (`type IN (requested, 0)`). A two-clause conditional TTL must explicitly account for type=0, or old pre-migration rows fall through to whichever clause happens to be the unconditional fallback.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe FORCES `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` on samples_v3 immediately before every `MODIFY TTL` (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:77-92). With that setting on, ClickHouse only drops whole parts whose TTL has fully expired; it does not rewrite parts to delete individual rows. A row-level `DELETE WHERE type = ...` clause would therefore be inert until that setting is flipped back to 0 -- and gigapipe re-sets it every time it re-applies rotation.
- samples_v3 partitions by day only -- `PARTITION BY toStartOfDay(toDateTime(timestamp_ns / 1000000000))` (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:26-32). The type column is added later by `ALTER TABLE {{.DB}}.samples_v3 ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS type UInt8` and is NOT in the partition key. So the cheap part-drop path can never separate logs from metrics; only row-level TTL (or a schema change to the partition key) can.
- gigapipe's Rotate runs on EVERY process start: cmd/gigapipe/main.go:66-81 (`initDB` -> `ctrl.Init` then `ctrl.Rotate`), ctrl/ctrl.go:39-53 -> maintenance.RotateAll -> rotateDB -> Rotate. `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL <str>` (rotate.go:87) REPLACES the entire TTL expression, so any hand-applied conditional TTL is wiped whenever this fires.
- The clobber is guarded, but only by a self-reported bookkeeping row, not by inspecting the table: rotate.go:73-76 reads `getSetting(db, dist, "rotate", "v3_samples_days")` from gigapipe's own `settings` table and returns early if the stored string equals the string it just computed. Consequence: a manual conditional TTL SURVIVES ordinary restarts (config unchanged), but is silently destroyed the moment SAMPLES_DAYS, the ttl_policy list, or storage_policy changes, or if the settings row is missing/lost. Corollary tactic: pre-seeding that settings row with the exact string gigapipe would compute makes it never touch TTL at all.
- There is a clean opt-out: `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES` (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:67-72, docs/configuration.md:56) skips BOTH ctrl.Init and ctrl.Rotate. Setting it true means OpenPanel owns the TTL permanently -- but also owns gigapipe's schema creation and every future schema migration, which is a real long-term cost.
- Rotate applies the SAME dropTTLDays to samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv, metrics_15s and patterns (rotate.go:122-212). Traces live in their own table (tempo_traces), so trace retention only needs a per-table TTL, not a conditional one. Only the logs-vs-metrics split genuinely needs `DELETE WHERE`.
- `type` is tri-valued, not binary: SAMPLE_TYPE_UNDEF=0, SAMPLE_TYPE_LOG=1, SAMPLE_TYPE_METRIC=2 (writer/model/insert_request.go:9-11), and the reader matches `type IN (requested, 0)` (reader/logql/logql_transpiler/clickhouse_planner/sql_misc.go:213-220, shared/types.go:12-14). Rows with type=0 -- including any parts written before the ADD COLUMN migration -- are visible to BOTH logs and metrics queries, so a two-clause conditional TTL must have a deliberate fallback clause for type=0.
- metrics_15s is an insert-triggered materialized view over samples_v3 (ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql, metrics_15s_mv). Deleting rows out of samples_v3 by TTL does NOT propagate to the rollup; metrics_15s carries its own separate TTL set from the same dropTTLDays. Per-signal retention has to be applied to both tables to be coherent.
- gigapipe's documented per-request TTL is a no-op in the OSS code. `X-Ttl-Days` / `x-ttl-days` and the `__ttl_days__` label are parsed (writer/controller/middleware.go:167-207, writer/grpc/tenant.go:53-58, writer/utils/unmarshal/builder.go:326-390) into `MTTLDays` (writer/model/insert_request.go:162,178) -- but MTTLDays appears in NO insert service: writer/service/insert/samples.go:57-58 inserts only `(type, fingerprint, timestamp_ns, string, value)`, and there is no ttl_days column anywhere in ctrl/qryn/sql/. Do not build per-project retention on that header.
- Replication only kicks in with CLUSTER_NAME set: main.go sets `Cloud = true` when CLUSTER_NAME is present, maintain.go:20-26 maps that to CLUST_MODE_CLOUD, and update.go:235-243 swaps MergeTree -> ReplicatedMergeTree; ALTERs then carry `ON CLUSTER` (rotate.go:68-71). OpenPanel's self-hosting compose sets no cluster env at all, so the default deployment is plain MergeTree and MODIFY TTL is a local metadata change.
- OpenPanel's own `modifyTTL` helper cannot be reused against gigapipe tables in a clustered install: it targets `${tableName}_replicated ON CLUSTER '{cluster}'` (packages/db/src/clickhouse/migration.ts:127-129), a naming convention gigapipe does not use -- gigapipe's replicated local table is just `samples_v3`, with `_dist` for the Distributed wrapper.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's "per-signal retention needs conditional ClickHouse TTL" line item is under-specified and, as written, would silently not work. Three changes are required. (1) Conditional TTL alone is insufficient: the plan must also `ALTER TABLE samples_v3 MODIFY SETTING ttl_only_drop_parts = 0`, and must own the fact that this is a deliberate performance regression against what gigapipe chose (rotate.go:79) -- expiring rows now force part rewrites at merge instead of cheap whole-part drops. Budget for that on a high-volume samples table. The alternative, arguably better, is to change samples_v3's PARTITION BY to include `type` so per-signal part-drop works with ttl_only_drop_parts=1 intact -- but that means owning the table's DDL outright, not ALTERing gigapipe's. (2) The plan must pick and document a strategy for gigapipe's startup rotation, because Rotate replaces the entire TTL expression on every start (main.go:78 -> rotate.go:87). Options, in descending cleanliness: run gigapipe with `OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=true` and have OpenPanel's own migration runner own the full gigapipe schema (clean, but OpenPanel then inherits every future gigapipe schema migration, and the ctrl/qryn/sql/*.sql files are explicitly "APPEND ONLY" versioned against a `ver` table); or pre-seed gigapipe's `settings` row for `v3_samples_days` with the exact string it would compute so the guard at rotate.go:74 always short-circuits (fragile, breaks on any gigapipe upgrade that changes the generated string); or accept re-applying the TTL after any SAMPLES_DAYS change. Doing nothing is not viable -- the TTL survives restarts but dies on the first config change. (3) Before any of this is committed to, someone must empirically verify `TTL <expr> DELETE WHERE <cond>` against clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65 specifically; it is not exercised anywhere in either repo and could not be tested here. Secondary: per-signal retention must be applied to metrics_15s as well as samples_v3 (the rollup MV is insert-triggered and unaffected by row deletes upstream), a fallback clause must cover type=0 rows, and trace retention needs no conditional TTL at all since tempo_traces is its own table. Finally, drop any dependence on gigapipe's X-Ttl-Days / __ttl_days__ per-request TTL -- it is parsed but never persisted.
