## Investigation 34 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived the answer from the type definition outward (grep for `FinalChart`, grep for every `trpc.chart.*` call in the renderer tree, grep for every `ChartEngine`/`AggregateChartEngine` call site) rather than walking the claim's list, and I reach the same verdict as the first engineer. Their evidence is accurate: I confirmed the `FinalChart` type, the 7-of-11 renderer split, the five engine call sites, `sankey` being a `protectedProcedure`, the `.strict()` MCP schema, the closed `event|formula` union, and the closed Postgres `ChartType` enum. The claim as written is wrong on the renderer count (7 of 11, not 11), wrong that ShareOverview and the embed widgets are FinalChart consumers at all, and wrong that the MCP tools work unchanged. Beyond their work I found four things that change the plan's cost estimate: `zReportInput` is a plain `z.object()` so any metrics discriminator is *silently stripped* by zod rather than rejected; `getReportDataCore` is exposed as a documented public REST endpoint (`GET /:projectId/reports/:reportId/data`), making it an external compatibility contract rather than just an internal call site; the server-side dispatch handles only funnel/metric/other, so retention, conversion and sankey reports already run through the wrong engine on every server path; and there is zero test coverage of the FinalChart shape anywhere in the repo, so a second engine has no conformance test to build against.

**Evidence**

- `packages/validation/src/types.validation.ts:75-107` — Confirmed verbatim. `Metrics = { sum; average; min; max; count: number | undefined; previous?: {...} }`, `IChartSerie = { id; names: string[]; event: { id?; name; breakdowns? }; metrics; data: { date; count; previous }[] }`, `FinalChart = { series: IChartSerie[]; metrics: Metrics }`. The first engineer's line numbers are right.
- `packages/db/src/engine/index.ts:27,84-86,352-360` — Only two producers, both `Promise<FinalChart>`: `executeChart` and `executeAggregateChart`, exported as `ChartEngine` and `AggregateChartEngine`. A repo-wide grep for `FinalChart` across all .ts/.tsx (excluding node_modules and dist) returns only 8 hits, in 4 files: format.ts, engine/index.ts, types.validation.ts, and one comment in packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:47. The type is genuinely narrow.
- `apps/start/src/components/report-chart/index.tsx:40-63` — Confirmed 11 renderers dispatched on `props.report.chartType`: linear, bar, area, histogram, pie, map, metric, funnel, retention, conversion, sankey.
- `apps/start/src/components/report-chart/` — Independent grep for every tRPC call under this directory settles the split: `chart.chart` in line/index.tsx:16, area/index.tsx:17, map/index.tsx:17, metric/index.tsx:16, histogram/index.tsx:17 (5); `chart.aggregate` in bar/index.tsx:17, pie/index.tsx:17 (2); `chart.funnel` funnel/index.tsx:23; `chart.cohort` retention/index.tsx:34; `chart.conversion` conversion/index.tsx:18; `chart.sankey` sankey/index.tsx:47. Exactly 7 of 11 reach FinalChart. Confirms the first engineer.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:456,498,554,588,612,636` — Procedure kinds confirmed by grep: `funnel: chartProcedure`, `conversion: chartProcedure`, `sankey: protectedProcedure.input(zReportInput)`, `chart: chartProcedure`, `aggregate: chartProcedure`, `cohort: chartProcedure`. Sankey is indeed the odd one out with no shareId path — the first engineer's finding holds.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:588-635` — Both procedures are `zReportInput.and(z.object({ shareId, id }))` and end in an unconditional `return ChartEngine.execute(chartInput)` / `return AggregateChartEngine.execute(chartInput)`. On the share path `chartInput` is built from `ctx.report` with only range/startDate/endDate/interval taken from client input — so share rendering is driven entirely by the persisted row, as claimed.
- `packages/validation/src/index.ts:233-308` — `zReportInput` is `z.object({...})` — NOT `.strict()` and NOT `.passthrough()`. Zod's default for a bare object is to STRIP unknown keys. This is the file that refutes the first engineer's reading of context.tsx: an added metrics discriminator does not 'reach the server with no frontend change needed' — it is silently dropped at the input validator until zReportInput itself is extended.
- `packages/validation/src/index.ts:143-158` — `zChartEventItem = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [zChartEventWithType, zChartFormula])` and `zChartSeries = z.array(zChartEventItem)`. Confirmed closed at two members; a metric series needs a third.
- `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:385-397,425-459` — `enum ChartType { linear bar histogram pie metric area map funnel retention conversion sankey }` confirmed as a closed Postgres enum. `model Report` has `events Json`, `unit String?`, `visibleSeries String[]`, `options Json?` — series are schemaless JSON, chartType is not.
- `apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.ts:459-468 and apps/api/src/controllers/insights.controller.ts:646-651` — NEW — the first engineer counted reports.service.ts as an internal call site but missed that it is publicly exposed. `fastify.route({ method: 'GET', url: '/:projectId/reports/:reportId/data', schema: { tags: TAGS, description: 'Get the data for a saved report.' }, handler: c.getReportData })`, whose handler is `reply.send(await getReportDataCore({...}))`. FinalChart is a documented external API response body here, not just an internal type.
- `packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:180-220` — `getReportDataCore` dispatches ONLY on `chartType === 'funnel'` → funnelService, `=== 'metric'` → AggregateChartEngine, else → ChartEngine. Retention, conversion and sankey reports therefore fall through to the event ChartEngine and return a FinalChart the UI would never render for those types. Same three-way fallthrough at packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:297-304 and :345-351, and apps/api/src/agents/tools/dashboard.ts:98-104.
- `apps/api/src/controllers/export.controller.ts:201-216 and apps/api/src/routes/export.router.ts:48-56` — Confirmed: `GET /charts` ('Export aggregated chart/analytics data...') → `ChartEngine.execute({ ...rest, projectId, series: eventSeries, chartType: 'linear', metric: 'sum' })`. A second public REST surface returning FinalChart.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/dashboard-management.ts:15-17,408-432` — Confirmed: `const reportSchema = zReport.omit({projectId,limit,offset}).strict().superRefine(...)`, used as the `report` input for both `create_report` and `update_report`. `.strict()` means an added discriminator is rejected outright here — the opposite failure mode from zReportInput's silent strip.
- `apps/start/src/routes/share.overview.$shareId.tsx:1-20,119-133 plus apps/start/src/components/overview/*.tsx` — STRENGTHENS the first engineer. I grepped every overview component: not one renders `<ReportChart>`. All eight widgets go through a separate `trpc.overview.*` router (stats, topPages, topGeneric, topGenericSeries, topEvents, topConversions, topLinkOut, userJourney, map, liveData). The `ReportChartProps` type in useOverviewWidget.tsx:11 is vestigial — its only consumer, overview-top-devices.tsx:41, actually queries `trpc.overview.topGeneric`. ShareOverview is not merely 'never renders saved reports'; the whole overview surface is a parallel data path.
- `packages/trpc/src/routers/widget.ts:1-14,118,141,184` — Confirmed no FinalChart. The router imports `ch, clix, db, eventBuffer, getSettingsForProject, TABLE_NAMES` and queries ClickHouse directly (e.g. `counter: publicProcedure` returns `await eventBuffer.getActiveVisitorCount(...)`). Zero references to ChartEngine/AggregateChartEngine. Embed widgets are a separate surface, as the first engineer said.
- `apps/start/src/components/grafana-grid.tsx:9-31` — Confirmed data-agnostic: `useReportLayouts` reads only `report.id` and `report.layout?.x/y/w/h` (optional chaining, with index-based fallbacks) and emits react-grid-layout layouts. Never touches chart data. Genuinely works unchanged.
- `apps/start/src/hooks/use-rechart-data-model.ts:19-52` — Confirmed the implicit contract: `series[0]?.data.map(({date}) => ...)` takes the x-axis grid from the FIRST series only, then inner `serie.data.reduce` matches later series by `if (item.date === date)` exact string equality. A metrics engine must emit an identical, identically-formatted, zero-filled date array on every series or points vanish silently.
- `packages/db/src/engine/ and packages/db/src/services/reports.service.test.ts` — NEW — no test coverage of the contract. The engine directory contains exactly one test, formula.test.ts, which tests `evaluateFormula`/`isValidFormula` arithmetic only. reports.service.test.ts contains only `describe('mergeGlobalFilters')` with 4 cases. A repo-wide search of every *.test.ts/*.test.tsx for FinalChart/executeChart/ChartEngine returns nothing. There is no conformance test a second engine can be written against.
- `apps/start/src/modals/view-chart-users.tsx:207-247 and packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:730-752` — Confirmed the dead-drilldown. `matchingChartSeries` filters `chartData.series.filter(s => s.event.id === selectedSerieId)`; the `getProfiles` query passes `series: []` and is `enabled: selectedReportSerie.type === 'event'` — so for a non-event series it never fires and the modal renders empty. Server-side `getProfiles` throws `new Error('Series must be an event')` and builds SQL over the events table via `sb.select.profile_id = 'DISTINCT profile_id'`.
- `apps/start/src/components/report-chart/line/chart.tsx:160-186` — Confirmed: `if (projectId) { items.push({ label: 'View Users', ... pushModal('ViewChartUsers', { type: 'chart', chartData: data, report: {...} }) }) }` — unconditional on projectId, with a hardcoded `chartType: 'linear', metric: 'sum'` in the synthesized report. Must be suppressed for metrics reports.
- `apps/start/src (ReportChart render sites)` — NEW — the claim and the first engineer both undercount ReportChart render sites. Grep finds: routes/share.report.$shareId.tsx:125, components/report/report-item.tsx:192 and :260 (ReportItem + ReportItemReadOnly, the latter used by ShareDashboard), modals/overview-chart-details.tsx:18, modals/insight-details.tsx:174, components/profiles/profile-charts.tsx:90 and :98, components/chat/tool-results/chat-report-result.tsx:75, plus ReportChartShortcut at modals/event-details.tsx:360 and routes/_app.$organizationId.$projectId.events._tabs.stats.tsx:49,73,117,161. All but report-item and share.report synthesize event-only reports, so the conclusion is unaffected — but ReportChart is the generic funnel far more widely than 'dashboards + shares'.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's "11 chart renderers" is wrong and I confirm the first engineer's 7. Verified by grepping every tRPC call under apps/start/src/components/report-chart/: 5 renderers call `chart.chart`, 2 call `chart.aggregate`, and funnel/retention/conversion/sankey call `chart.funnel`/`chart.cohort`/`chart.conversion`/`chart.sankey` respectively, each with a non-FinalChart result shape.
- The claim's "works everywhere unchanged" is false as stated. Each renderer hardcodes its procedure at the call site, and `chart`/`aggregate` end in an unconditional `return ChartEngine.execute(chartInput)` / `AggregateChartEngine.execute(chartInput)` (packages/trpc/src/routers/chart.ts:609,633). Nothing is unchanged unless routing is added server-side inside those two procedures.
- ShareOverview and the embed widgets are not FinalChart consumers, confirming the first engineer — and I can put it more strongly than they did. No overview component renders ReportChart at all; the entire overview surface is served by a separate `trpc.overview.*` router. The widget router imports only `ch, clix, db, eventBuffer` and never touches either engine.
- The MCP tools do not work unchanged, confirming the first engineer. `runReport` (packages/mcp/src/tools/analytics/reports.ts:297-304) and `runReportFromConfig` (:345-351) hardcode chartType→engine, and `reportSchema = zReport.omit(...).strict()` (dashboard-management.ts:15-17) rejects any added field on create_report/update_report.
- CORRECTION TO THE FIRST ENGINEER: their reading of apps/start/src/components/report-chart/context.tsx:53-63 is over-confident. They conclude a future metrics discriminator reaches the server "with no frontend change needed." `useChartInput` does forward everything but `visibleSeries`, but the server input is `zReportInput.and(...)` and `zReportInput` is a bare `z.object()` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:233), which strips unknown keys by default. The discriminator is silently discarded — a worse failure than rejection, because the report renders through the event engine with no error. The frontend needs no change; the schema does.
- CORRECTION TO THE FIRST ENGINEER: they describe reports.service.ts:178-219 as "a third server-side call site," understating it. `getReportDataCore` is the handler behind a documented public REST route, `GET /:projectId/reports/:reportId/data` (apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.ts:459-468, controller at insights.controller.ts:646-651). That makes FinalChart an external API contract on two REST endpoints, not one.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Retention, conversion and sankey reports are ALREADY mis-dispatched on every server-side path. `getReportDataCore` (reports.service.ts:203-219), `runReport` (mcp reports.ts:297-304), `runReportFromConfig` (:345-351) and the chat agent tool (apps/api/src/agents/tools/dashboard.ts:98-104) all branch only on funnel and metric, falling through to `ChartEngine.execute` for everything else. So a saved sankey or retention report fetched via MCP or the public reports/data endpoint returns a FinalChart produced by the event time-series engine — data the UI would never render for that chart type. The plan should not assume server-side report execution is currently equivalent to what the UI shows.
- There is no test anywhere in the repo that asserts the FinalChart shape. packages/db/src/engine/ contains one test file (formula.test.ts, arithmetic only); reports.service.test.ts covers only `mergeGlobalFilters`. Decision 4 of the plan rests on a contract with zero executable specification — a second engine can only be validated by eye. Writing a FinalChart conformance test suite against the event engine first is a cheap de-risking step the plan does not budget for.
- The metric-chartType divergence is real and bidirectional. The frontend routes chartType `metric` to `trpc.chart.chart` → ChartEngine (apps/start/src/components/report-chart/metric/index.tsx:16), while every server-side path routes `metric` to AggregateChartEngine (reports.service.ts:215, mcp reports.ts:302, agents/tools/dashboard.ts:102). A metrics engine must replicate this inconsistency on both paths or the same saved report will return different numbers in the dashboard than through MCP/REST.
- zReportInput strips silently while the MCP reportSchema rejects loudly. Any discriminator added for metric reports has to be landed in `zReportInput` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:233) before it is useful anywhere, and simultaneously in the MCP `.strict()` schema (dashboard-management.ts:15) before it can be written through MCP. Landing one without the other produces two different silent failure modes.
- The FinalChart render surface is wider than the claim lists. Besides shares and dashboards, `<ReportChart>` is rendered by modals/overview-chart-details.tsx:18, modals/insight-details.tsx:174, components/profiles/profile-charts.tsx:90,98, chat/tool-results/chat-report-result.tsx:75, and ReportChartShortcut in modals/event-details.tsx:360 and the events stats route (4 sites). All synthesize event-only reports today, so they inherit whatever routing decision lands in chart.chart/chart.aggregate — worth auditing so a metrics discriminator cannot leak into them.

**Impact on the plan.** Decision 4 still pays off, but the plan should stop describing it as "works everywhere unchanged" and state the actual scope: it buys 7 of 11 renderers, the dashboard grid, ReportLayout, ShareReport and ShareDashboard — conditional on the metrics dispatch being implemented server-side inside `chart.chart` and `chart.aggregate`, keyed off a persisted discriminator. Concretely the plan must add: (1) a new member to `zChartEventItem`'s discriminated union plus a discriminator field on `zReportInput` — without the latter the field is silently stripped by zod, not rejected, so this is a correctness prerequisite not a nicety; (2) branches at seven engine call sites, not five, because both public REST endpoints (`GET /export/charts` and `GET /:projectId/reports/:reportId/data`) return FinalChart to external consumers and are backward-compatibility surfaces; (3) removal of ShareOverview and the embed widgets from the claimed benefit list entirely — they are separate routers with no FinalChart in them; (4) an explicit MCP work item covering both `runReport`/`runReportFromConfig` dispatch and the `.strict()` reportSchema; (5) suppression of the "View Users" drilldown for metric reports, since `getProfiles` throws on non-event series and the modal silently renders empty; (6) either reuse of an existing ChartType enum value or a Prisma migration. I would also add a pre-work item the plan currently lacks: write a FinalChart conformance test against the event engine, because none exists and the "same type" guarantee is otherwise unenforced.

## Investigation 35 — `partially_confirmed`

The claim's three factual assertions are all true and I re-read each file from source; the first engineer's three completeness corrections (worker also traces, API also serves /metrics, packages/logger is itself a HyperDX integration point) are all correct and I confirmed each by a different route. Their bottom line — traces/logs are OTLP-push and plausibly repointable, metrics are prom-client pull and are not — is right, but their supporting evidence for the metrics half was weak and their framing of it is subtly wrong: gigapipe does not merely lack a scraper, it has a *deliberately disabled* one (`// go promscrape.RunPrometheusScraper(goCache, TsSvcs, MtrSvcs)` at writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:257, with no `promscrape` package left in the tree). Both engineers also missed the single most on-point line in the repo: the comment in *both* observability.ts files says "Metrics stay on prom-client/**Grafana**" — the code names the exact consumer the plan forbids. Following the repoint path into gigapipe's OTLP decoders then turned up three facts that break plan decision #2 as written: on OTLP **metrics** a resource attribute never reaches a sample series (it lands only on `target_info`), on OTLP **logs** a record-level attribute *overrides* the gateway's resource-level one, and only on **traces** does the resource attribute win. Finally, the SDK source genuinely is unreadable here (no node_modules, and the pnpm v11 store's files dir is empty), so "repointable" for traces and logs remains an assumption, not a verified fact.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts ... (traces only, gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY)" — true, but incomplete in exactly the way the first engineer said. `diff apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts apps/worker/src/utils/observability.ts` yields a single differing line (19). Tracing is wired in both services.
- "apps/worker/src/metrics.ts builds a prom-client registry" — true, but there are two Prometheus surfaces. apps/api/src/app.ts:371-372 registers fastify-metrics at `/metrics` in a no-prefix scope whenever `testing` is false. Confirmed independently via app.ts:362-364, where the swagger transform explicitly hides `/metrics`.
- "packages/logger handles pino + output interception" — understated. It is the third HyperDX integration point (getPinoTransport at :113, getPinoMixinFunction at :109) and the only OTLP *log* path. Additionally it names the current backend: line 85 says both logs and traces "land under the same service name in ClickStack".
- "so all three can be repointed at a local OTLP endpoint" — false for metrics, and UNVERIFIED for traces and logs. Metrics: prom-client is pull-only and gigapipe's scraper is commented out (writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:257) with the `promscrape` package removed from the tree, so nothing will fetch /metrics. Traces/logs: no node_modules and an empty pnpm store mean nobody in this session has read the HyperDX SDK; the repo passes `apiKey` and no URL, and no OTEL_* variable is read anywhere. "Repointable via config" is an untested hypothesis.
- I disagree with the FIRST ENGINEER's framing (not their conclusion) that "gigapipe has no Prometheus scraper anywhere in its tree." A `scrape_config` grep only rules out a config key. The scraper call exists as dead code — `// Run Prometheus Scaper` / `// go promscrape.RunPrometheusScraper(goCache, TsSvcs, MtrSvcs)` at writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:256-257 — with the referenced package deleted. "Deliberately disabled upstream" is a different planning fact from "never existed": it means re-enabling is an upstream-fork question, not a greenfield feature request.
- The claim's implicit premise that the current setup is signal-complete is wrong in a way that flatters it: because tsdown bundles ioredis/bullmq/pg (apps/api/tsdown.config.ts:7-13), today's traces cover roughly only undici/fetch. There is very little existing trace signal to repoint.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Plan decision #2 is BROKEN for metrics as literally written. gigapipe's OTLP metrics decoder routes every non-identifying resource attribute into `rs.targetAttrs`, which is consumed only by `emitTargetInfo()` (writer/utils/unmarshal/otlp_metrics.go:495-517) to write a separate `target_info` gauge. `seriesLabels()` (:239-268) builds each stored series from scope labels + DATA-POINT attributes + __name__/job/instance + extras, and never touches targetAttrs. So injecting `op_project_id{...}` as a mandatory PromQL matcher would match nothing. The gateway must stamp op_project_id as a per-DATA-POINT attribute, or fold it into service.namespace so it lands in `job` — and the query compiler must match on whichever is chosen. This is a security-boundary defect, not a cosmetic one.
- Plan decision #2 is BYPASSABLE for logs. In writer/utils/unmarshal/otlplogs.go:39-46, resource attributes are written into attrsMap first and log-RECORD attributes last, so a client-controlled record-level `op_project_id` silently overwrites the gateway's value. Overwriting only the resource attribute is insufficient; the gateway must strip or overwrite op_project_id at record level (and at scope level) too. Traces have the OPPOSITE precedence (writer/utils/unmarshal/otlp.go:81-84 appends resource attrs last, so resource wins) — so the three signals need three different enforcement rules, not one.
- gigapipe rejects DELTA-temporality Sum/Histogram/ExponentialHistogram data points (docs/otlp-metrics.md, "Rejected and dropped data": "gigapipe stores cumulative series only"), and does so via partial_success rather than an HTTP error — i.e. silently from the exporter's point of view. If P2 replaces prom-client with an OTLP metrics exporter, the temporality preference must be pinned to CUMULATIVE and partial_success responses must be surfaced, or metrics will vanish without an error.
- There is a shipped, zero-code path for the logs signal that the plan should consider before writing anything: LOG_EXPORTER=stdout is already a first-class mode (packages/logger/index.ts:10-14, and interceptProcessOutput's passthrough at :163), documented in-file as "pino writes JSON to stdout; an external collector ships it." It was added in commit 5bceac94 explicitly so "an external collector (own swarm/k8s) can take over shipping without duplicates." Note the trap the first engineer identified and I confirmed: the trace_id/span_id mixin at :109-111 is gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY alone, NOT on logExporter, so a stdout-mode deployment loses trace correlation unless a key is also present.
- Zero test coverage over all three components. packages/logger has no test file at all (the package is index.ts + package.json + tsconfig.json); neither observability.ts has one; and metrics.ts is only ever `vi.mock`ed away in worker job tests (cron.session-vacuum.test.ts:33, events.create-session-end.test.ts:39, cron.session-reaper.test.ts:41). Combined with the fact that this code is ~5 days old (commits 5bceac94 and d19c5298, both 2026-08-24), the plan should not treat the existing instrumentation as a hardened foundation.
- Both /metrics endpoints are currently exposed on the public internet in the self-hosted topology, and the plan will make that worse. `handle_path /api*` in self-hosting/caddy/Caddyfile.template:4-6 strips the prefix, so https://$DOMAIN/api/metrics serves the API's full prom-client dump unauthenticated; the worker's is behind Caddy basic_auth only. The worker registry has 10 async collect() hooks doing live Redis work (SMEMBERS/ZCARD per project), so an unauthenticated scrape is not free. If P0 introduces any internal scraper or bridge, this is the moment to put auth on both.
- `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry` is declared in four places — root package.json:33, packages/logger/package.json:10, apps/api/package.json:28, apps/worker/package.json:16 — all via `catalog:` (pnpm-workspace.yaml:87, pinned ^0.10.3). A stale root package-lock.json (npm, pinning ^0.8.1/0.8.2) also exists alongside pnpm-lock.yaml. Any swap to vanilla @opentelemetry/* touches all four plus the two `external:` arrays in the tsdown configs.
- The referenced design doc `logging-capture-plan.md` (cited from packages/logger/index.ts:9 and both observability.ts files) is not in the repository, and `docs/` does not exist at all. The plan's own docs/observability/ directory would be the first docs tree in the repo — and the missing logging-capture-plan is worth reconstructing there, since the current logger's single-shipping-path invariant is only recorded in comments pointing at a file that is gone.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim is safe to keep in the plan only as background, with its conclusion rewritten per signal: traces are OTLP-push and the most likely repoint, but the SDK's endpoint knob is UNVERIFIED (no node_modules, empty pnpm store) and must be spiked before P1 commits to it; logs already have a shipped collector handoff (LOG_EXPORTER=stdout) that needs no code, with the caveat that the trace-id mixin is gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY independently of it; metrics are a rewrite, not a repoint, because prom-client is pull-only and gigapipe's scraper is commented out with its package removed. More consequentially, the investigation surfaces a defect in load-bearing decision #2 that is independent of the self-instrumentation question and should be fixed before P1 ingest is designed: "overwrite an op_project_id RESOURCE attribute on ingest, inject op_project_id as a mandatory matcher on query" works only for traces. For metrics the resource attribute never reaches a queryable series label (it lands on target_info), so the matcher would silently match nothing; for logs a record-level attribute overrides the resource-level one, so the boundary is client-bypassable. The gateway needs three signal-specific enforcement rules — data-point-attribute (or job-label) stamping for metrics, record+scope+resource stripping for logs, resource stamping for traces — and the query compiler must match on whatever metrics actually store. Also add to P2: pin OTLP metrics temporality to CUMULATIVE and surface partial_success rejections. Finally, plan for zero existing test coverage on logger/observability/metrics and for four declaration sites of the HyperDX dependency.

## Investigation 36 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-checked every file the first engineer cited and each one says what they say it says — the type is verbatim correct (packages/validation/src/types.validation.ts:66-109), format.ts is the sole producer, and all four gigapipe citations (15s window rounding, 11000-point cap, writeMatrix emitting float-seconds plus string values in Go map order, s.Histograms skipped) are exact. Their verdict of partially_confirmed is right and I reach it independently. But their reasoning is wrong in two places and thin in four. Most consequentially, they framed the renderer question purely as a blocker and missed the mechanism that actually delivers the payoff: no chart component references FinalChart at all — every one types against IChartData = RouterOutputs['chart']['chart'] (apps/start/src/trpc/client.ts:16), which is structurally identical to FinalChart, so a new procedure returning FinalChart IS assignable to every `data: IChartData` prop. Conversely the real blocker is deeper than hard-coded procedures: ReportChartContextType.report is typed IReportInput (context.tsx:26) whose series is a required array of event|formula. And the sharpest fact neither of us should have missed: OpenPanel's `week` and `month` intervals — and DST-affected `day` buckets — are literally unrepresentable as a fixed PromQL `step`, so the gateway must re-bucket, not relabel.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/validation/src/types.validation.ts:66-109` — Confirmed verbatim. PreviousValue, Metrics = {sum, average, min, max, count: number|undefined, previous?: {...PreviousValue}}, IChartSerie = {id, names: string[], event: {id?, name, breakdowns?}, metrics, data: {date: string, count: number, previous: PreviousValue}[]}, FinalChart = {series: IChartSerie[]; metrics: Metrics}. The claim's quoted type is character-for-character correct.

A Prometheus range query's step is a fixed duration; calendar months are not, and neither is a DST-transition day (23h or 25h). So week, month and tz-correct day buckets cannot be obtained from gigapipe by choosing a step at all — the gateway must query at a finer step and re-aggregate itself. If a metrics engine emits ISO-8601 with Z — the natural thing when the source is UTC epoch seconds — the axis shifts by the viewer's UTC offset relative to event charts on the same dashboard, while still passing every string-equality check inside a single series.

The FinalChart contract — grid density, date-string format, previous alignment, metric semantics — is entirely unpinned by tests.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's second half, 'a Prometheus matrix response maps onto it cleanly', is the overstated part — I agree with the first engineer's verdict but for a harder reason than the seven they list. Three of OpenPanel's five intervals are not reachable from a PromQL range query at all: intervals = {minute, day, hour, week, month} (packages/constants/index.ts:236-242) and the engine buckets with toStartOfWeek(created_at, 1, '<tz>') / toStartOfMonth(created_at, '<tz>') (chart.service.ts:718-731), while Prometheus step is a fixed duration. Calendar months, calendar weeks and DST-affected days cannot be expressed as a step. The gateway must query at a finer step and re-aggregate into project-timezone calendar buckets itself. That is not a lossy edge — it is a required component the plan does not currently name.
- The first engineer's strongest correction — 'every chart renderer works unchanged is not true as written' — is right about the fetch layer but stops one file short of the mechanism that makes decision 4 pay off. No chart component imports FinalChart or IChartSerie; they all type against IChartData = RouterOutputs['chart']['chart'] (apps/start/src/trpc/client.ts:16). Because executeChart returns Promise<FinalChart>, those are the same type structurally, so returning FinalChart from a new procedure does make every inner Chart, the report table, the tooltip, and the MCP shaper accept it with no edit. The blocker is also deeper than they said: ReportChartContextType.report is IReportInput (context.tsx:26) with no data or fetcher override, and IReportInput.series is a required z.array(zChartEventItem) — so metric reports need either a widened input schema or a parallel provider, not just a swapped query hook.
- Their math.ts characterisation is half wrong. average explicitly guards !Number.isNaN(n) && Number.isFinite(n) (math.ts:8-18); only sum, min and max use bare mathjs isNumber (20-32). NaN/±Inf — which gigapipe WILL emit as the strings 'NaN'/'+Inf'/'-Inf' via strconv.FormatFloat — propagate through sum/min/max but not average. Since metrics.sum is the series sort key (format.ts:153) and the bar/pie denominator (bar/chart.tsx:59, pie/chart.tsx:81), their conclusion survives; the stated reason does not.
- Their reading of the MCP payoff case is backwards on one detail. reports.ts:71-75 says the engine zero-fills 'but take the union anyway so a short series can't silently truncate the axis', and the code does lookup.get(date) ?? 0 — shapeChart tolerates holes and does not assume a dense grid. It is a cleaner win for the plan than they credited.
- They assert count: undefined renders 'N/A' without checking whether undefined survives tRPC serialization. It does, but only because packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:57 sets transformer: superjson; under a plain JSON transformer the key would vanish. Worth recording as a dependency, not an accident.
- Neither their answer nor the claim mentions that a second output shape exists. ChartResponse (engine/types.ts:57-84) is documented as 'The final output format' and format.ts:16 carries 'TODO: Migrate frontend to use cleaner ChartResponse format', while FinalChart's own docstring says '(backward compatible)'. ChartResponse has zero references outside its declaration, so nothing is at risk today — but decision 4 stakes the metrics engine on a shape the codebase has already flagged for replacement, and the plan should say so.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Week, month, and DST-correct day buckets are unrepresentable as a PromQL step. The plan needs an explicit gateway-side re-bucketing stage: query gigapipe at a fixed sub-bucket step, then fold into toStartOfWeek(x,1,tz)/toStartOfMonth(x,tz)-equivalent calendar buckets in the project timezone before building FinalChart. Without it, metric reports silently cannot honour the interval picker for 6m/1y ranges.
- gigapipe's 11,000-points-per-series cap and 15s window quantisation (prom_query_range.go:55-70) interact badly with that re-bucketing: asking for a fine step over a long range to reconstruct month buckets is exactly what trips the cap. The gateway will need to chunk long windows into multiple range queries and stitch, or choose the coarsest step that still divides every calendar bucket — which for months it never does.
- The date string format must be chosen once and matched exactly to 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' naive project-local. It is consumed three different ways: exact string equality for grid alignment (use-rechart-data-model.ts:31, report-table-utils.ts:421), new Date(date).getTime() for x-axis position (use-rechart-data-model.ts:25 feeding axis.tsx:82 dataKey: 'timestamp', scale: 'utc'), and new Date(a.date).getTime() for sorting (group-by-labels.ts:55). Emitting ISO-with-Z passes the equality checks and still misplaces every point on the axis by the viewer's UTC offset. This deserves to be a named invariant in the plan, not a detail.
- There is no test coverage of the FinalChart contract anywhere in the repo — no test calls format() or asserts on a FinalChart. If the plan is going to make FinalChart a load-bearing interface between two engines, it should add contract tests as a P2 deliverable; today nothing stops either producer from drifting.
- ReportChartContextType (context.tsx:8-31) is the actual integration seam, not the renderer index files. Introducing an optional data/source field there, or widening report beyond IReportInput, is the minimal change that would make every existing renderer accept metric data. Worth costing explicitly in P2 rather than discovering during implementation.
- Because getPreviousMetric aligns previous-period points strictly by array index (format.ts:142) and previous-series by breakdown-value string (ps.name.slice(1).join(':::'), lines 93-98), the metrics gateway must produce previous-period series that are (a) dense on their own grid with the same point count as the current period, and (b) keyed by an identically-ordered label tuple. Prometheus holes in either window silently shift the whole comparison. Deterministic label ordering — which the plan already needs for stable ids — is a prerequisite for previous-period support, so those two work items are the same item.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's decision 4 survives and is well-founded: FinalChart really is the shape, and the payoff is real and larger than the first engineer allowed, because the entire chart component layer types against RouterOutputs['chart']['chart'] rather than any nominal type. Three things must change. First, P2 must add an explicit calendar re-bucketing stage between gigapipe's matrix and FinalChart — fixed PromQL steps cannot produce week, month, or DST-correct day buckets, so this is a required component, not a rounding concern, and it interacts with gigapipe's 11k-point cap in a way that forces window chunking. Second, the date-string format must be written into the plan as a hard invariant ('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss', naive, project-local), because it is consumed both by string equality and by JS new Date() for axis positioning, and an ISO-with-Z emission fails only the second one — invisibly. Third, the plan should name ReportChartContextType.report: IReportInput as the integration seam to widen, rather than assuming renderers are free; and it should record that FinalChart is marked 'backward compatible' with a live TODO pointing at the unused ChartResponse, plus that no test anywhere pins the FinalChart contract, so contract tests belong in P2.

I re-checked this from the runtime path (writer insert services, reader planner registry, git log, tests, docs) rather than from the DDL alone, and I independently confirm every piece of evidence the first engineer cited — the file paths, line numbers and quoted text all exist and say what they claim. Traces and profiles do live in their own ClickHouse tables (`ctrl/qryn/sql/traces.sql`, `profiles.sql`), fully separate from `samples_v3`, each with a `_dist.sql` and `_read_dist.sql` companion, all embedded in `sql.go` and all conditional on cluster mode. Their corrections about `tempo_traces` naming, table families, single database, conditional dist variants, and the shared `SAMPLES_DAYS` TTL are all correct as stated, and the profiles-have-no-TTL point is real. Where I disagree is one framing: `traces_input` is not the runtime ingest funnel — the string `traces_input` appears in no Go file in the repo; the writer inserts straight into `tempo_traces` and `tempo_traces_attrs_gin`. I also found four things they missed that bear directly on the plan: the `oid` tenant column exists only in the traces family and is never populated by the writer, logs/metrics/profiles have no `oid` at all, a per-request TTL hook exists but is dead in OSS, and `rules.sql` exists for the ruler with no read-dist variant.

Nothing in docs/ tells the operator this also drives tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv, metrics_15s and patterns.

There is no test covering rotate.go/Rotate or the maintenance script ordering — the TTL behaviour described above is untested in-repo.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- Correction to the FIRST ENGINEER, not to the claim: they wrote that `traces_input` is 'an ingest-only funnel'. That is a schema-level inference that the runtime contradicts. The identifier `traces_input` occurs in no Go file in the repository — only inside ctrl/qryn/sql/traces.sql itself. The live writer builds `INSERT INTO tempo_traces (trace_id, span_id, parent_id, name, timestamp_ns, duration_ns, service_name, payload_type, payload)` (writer/service/insert/tempo.go:86-93) and a second service writing straight to tempo_traces_attrs_gin (l.185-190). `traces_input` and its two MVs are dormant legacy schema. Profiles are the opposite: profile.go:93 really does write to the Null table `profiles_input` and let the four MVs fan out. Their advice ('any direct-SQL path must target tempo_traces') lands in the right place for the wrong reason.
- The claim's 'each with their own distributed and read-dist variants' is true of the FILES but not of a running single-node deployment. traces_dist.sql / profiles_dist.sql execute only under CLUST_MODE_DISTRIBUTED, and *_read_dist.sql only when CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER is set, differs from the write cluster, AND distributed mode is on (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/update.go:56-75, 92-108). I confirm the first engineer on this.
- Also true of the claim but worth stating plainly: 'their own tables' is not 'their own database'. Every DDL in all six files is `{{.DB}}.<table>`, and the reader composes dist names as `` `db.Config.Name`.<table><suffix> `` (reader/utils/tables/tables.go:100-121). Table separation buys zero tenancy isolation.
- The claim's naming is loose in two ways beyond `tempo_traces` vs `traces`: each signal is a table family (traces = tempo_traces + tempo_traces_attrs_gin + tempo_traces_kv + 3 MVs + a dead Null table; profiles = profiles + profiles_series + profiles_series_gin + profiles_series_keys + 4 MVs + profiles_input), and the sidecars are not small — tempo_traces_attrs_gin stores one row per attribute key/value per span.
- The unstated payoff of the claim — separate tables therefore per-signal retention — does not hold. Rotate() (rotate.go:122-212) derives one drop interval from one TTLDays/SAMPLES_DAYS (default 7) and applies the identical expression to samples_v3, time_series, time_series_gin, tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv, metrics_15s and patterns. I add that the tiering side is equally global: the `days []RotatePolicy` list built from TTLPolicy (maintain.go:119-127) is passed unchanged to every rotateTables call, so 'move to cold disk after N' is also one setting for all signals.
- profiles* gets no TTL and no storage policy at all — confirmed, it is absent from Rotate(). I add that profiles is also absent from the writer health check (qryn_writer_db.go:74-80) and that profiles_series_keys is absent from the reader table registry (tables.go:22-40). Profiles is the least-maintained signal in the codebase.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- gigapipe's only built-in tenant column is `oid`, it exists ONLY in the traces family (tempo_traces, tempo_traces_attrs_gin, tempo_traces_kv), and the writer never populates it — `oid` is missing from both INSERT column lists in writer/service/insert/tempo.go, so every span lands with the schema DEFAULT '0'. `grep -n oid ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql` returns nothing (no oid on time_series, samples_v3, time_series_gin, metrics_15s, patterns) and profiles.sql has no oid either. This is direct support for the plan's decision #2: there is no per-tenant column to lean on, so label enforcement really is the only available boundary. It also means the plan must never describe oid as a fallback or defence-in-depth layer — populating it would require the closed traces-insert plugin hook at tempo.go:79-82 (`plugins.GetTracesInsertServicePlugin()`).
- Because tempo_traces is `ORDER BY (oid, trace_id, timestamp_ns)` and `PARTITION BY (oid, toDate(...))` with oid constant '0', the leading sort-key column and the first partition-key component are degenerate for every OpenPanel deployment. Trace queries filtered by an op_project_id resource attribute will therefore hit tempo_traces_attrs_gin (key/val) rather than the primary index. The plan's trace-query performance section should account for that; a per-project ClickHouse projection or an `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ORDER BY` is not possible on an existing MergeTree sort key without a rebuild.
- gigapipe already ships a per-request retention hook that is inert in OSS: HTTP `X-Ttl-Days` (writer/controller/middleware.go:167), gRPC `x-ttl-days` (writer/grpc/tenant.go:53), and a `__ttl_days__` special label (writer/utils/unmarshal/builder.go:333) all populate `MTTLDays` on the insert structs (writer/model/insert_request.go:162,178) — but no insert service reads that field and neither samples_v3 nor time_series has a ttl_days column. The plan should NOT bank on these headers for per-project or per-signal retention; it must apply its own conditional `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL` as the plan already anticipates, and must expect Rotate() to fight it whenever the SAMPLES_DAYS-derived string changes (rotate.go:73-76 only skips while the stored settings row matches).
- The plan's position that 'gigapipe's ruler is recording-only' has a schema consequence nobody has costed: rules.sql and rules_dist.sql exist and are applied unconditionally (sql.go:32-36; update.go k=10/11), creating a `{{.DB}}.rules` table in the SAME database as the telemetry, with the comment 'Ruler rule-group storage (recording/alerting rule groups).' There is NO rules_read_dist.sql, so a cross-cluster read deployment has no distributed read path for rule groups. If alert evaluation lives in OpenPanel's worker, this table is either unused dead weight or a second source of truth alongside NotificationRule — the plan should say explicitly which.
- Writer cluster-suffix handling is inconsistent and hardcoded. tempo.go:87-88 appends a literal `"_dist"` when ClusterName != "", ignoring distconfig / CLICKHOUSE_READ_DIST_SUFFIX; profile.go never appends any suffix; and the health check at qryn_writer_db.go:78-80 hardcodes `_dist` names too. Irrelevant for a single-node OpenPanel deployment, but it caps how far the 'gigapipe as internal service' story scales without patching gigapipe.
- There is no test anywhere in the repo covering Rotate(), the maintenance script ordering, or TTL application — the only tests touching these tables are four reader transpiler tests (traceql planner, logql labels joiner, promql transpiler/vector_range). Every retention behaviour the plan depends on is asserted only by reading the source, so OpenPanel should verify the resulting TTLs against a live ClickHouse in P0 rather than trusting the code path.
- log.sql also creates `samples_read` and `samples_read_v2_2` (lines 45-60), Merge-engine views over `^(samples|samples_v2)$` and `^(samples_read_v2_1|samples_v3)$`. These are legacy migration read paths in the logs/metrics family. Not part of the claim, but any storage inventory or 'which tables exist' documentation for the plan should list them so they are not mistaken for stray tables.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan's five load-bearing decisions has to change; the claim as written is safe to keep once corrected. Three concrete edits to the plan text: (1) name the tables correctly and by family — `tempo_traces` + `tempo_traces_attrs_gin` + `tempo_traces_kv` for traces, `profiles` + `profiles_series` + `profiles_series_gin` + `profiles_series_keys` for profiles — and drop any suggestion that `traces_input` is on the write path, since the writer bypasses it entirely; (2) stop implying that separate tables give per-signal retention, and instead state that ALL rotated tables share one `SAMPLES_DAYS`-derived drop interval AND one `TTLPolicy` tiering schedule, that profiles receives neither, and that the `X-Ttl-Days` / `__ttl_days__` per-request TTL hook is parsed but never persisted in OSS — so the plan's own conditional-TTL work is mandatory and must be re-applied whenever SAMPLES_DAYS changes; (3) add an explicit note under decision #2 that gigapipe's built-in `oid` tenant column exists only on the traces family and is never written, and does not exist at all for logs, metrics or profiles — which both strengthens the case for label enforcement and forecloses any oid-based defence-in-depth. Two smaller adds: the P5 alerting section should say what happens to gigapipe's own `{{.DB}}.rules` table given OpenPanel owns evaluation, and the P4 trace-query section should account for `oid` being a degenerate leading sort/partition key so project-scoped trace lookups fall to the GIN sidecar.

## Investigation 38 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-checked every line the first engineer cited and each one exists and says what they say it says. Their verdict is correct: the transport half of the claim is exact (X-CH-DSN at writer/controller/middleware.go:165, x-ch-dsn at writer/grpc/tenant.go:42, both stored under utils.ContextKeyDSN and threaded into ResolveLogServices/ResolveTraceServices/ResolveProfileServices/ResolveMetricServices), while "routing inserts to that DSN" is wrong — the value is an opaque id compared against svc.GetNodeName() in writer/service/registry/static.go:55-69, with a fail-open random fallback, and it can only ever select among insert services opened at boot from config.DATABASE_DATA. Two corrections to their write-up. First, their absolute statement "there is no code path anywhere in the writer that opens a connection from a caller-supplied DSN" is too strong as phrased: writer/chwrapper does contain caller-supplied-DSN dialing primitives (NewSmartDatabaseAdapterWithXDSN / NewSmartDatabaseAdapterWithDSN at factory.go:246-268, dispatched in adapter.go:34-53, with NewGeneralPurposeClientWithXDSN / NewWriterClientWithXDSN parsing an "x-" prefixed DSN at factory.go:71-77 and 171-183). They are real and they dial — they are simply never called from any request path (only writer/chwrapper/unit_test.go and writer/e2e_test.go.bak). The accurate statement is "unwired", not "nonexistent", and their existence is what makes the header's name and the docs wording historically coherent. Second, and more consequential for the plan: X-Ttl-Days is parsed and propagated but is a dead letter in OSS — no insert service writes a ttl_days column.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- Agree with the first engineer's core correction: "routing inserts to that DSN" is wrong. The value is matched against svc.GetNodeName() (writer/service/registry/static.go:58-63), i.e. the .Node field of a boot-configured database entry, and selects among already-open insert services only.
- Agree the selector is FAIL-OPEN: static.go:65-68 returns a uniformly random service for an empty or unrecognized id. It cannot be a security boundary.
- Agree selection is not atomic per request — each Get*Service re-randomizes (services_test.go:41-49 documents this) — and that portCHEnv (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:84-165) never sets .Node, so the header is inert under env-var configuration.
- CORRECTION TO THE FIRST ENGINEER: "There is no code path anywhere in the writer that opens a connection from a caller-supplied DSN" is overstated. writer/chwrapper/factory.go:246-268 (NewSmartDatabaseAdapterWithXDSN / NewSmartDatabaseAdapterWithDSN), dispatched by writer/chwrapper/adapter.go:34-53, do exactly that — factory.go:171-183 runs clickhouse.ParseDSN + ch.Dial on the caller string. They are present and functional; they are simply not reachable from any request path (callers: writer/chwrapper/unit_test.go:58,95 and writer/e2e_test.go.bak:857 only). The correct phrasing is "the primitive exists but is unwired to X-CH-DSN", which matters because a future gigapipe release or a fork could wire it in one line and silently turn the header into a real DSN.
- SCOPE SHARPENING: the claim is not universally inert. cmd/gigapipe/main.go:85 makes portCHEnv a no-op when DATABASE_DATA is already populated (config file). In a multi-entry config each node has its own database Name (writer/chwrapper/factory.go:20-31), so X-CH-DSN does then select a specific preconfigured ClickHouse database by node name. I could not verify the config-file schema for the Node key — the cloki-config v0.0.96 module is not in this machine's module cache and there is no vendor/ dir or sample YAML in the repo — so "a config file can set .Node" is UNVERIFIED, inferred from dbObject.Node being read at writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:49 and writer/chwrapper/factory.go:18.
- Minor robustness note the first engineer omitted: static.go:67 calls r.rand.Intn(len(svcs)) after the id loop with no length guard. If any signal's service slice is empty (nil), the getter panics rather than erroring — the fallback is fail-open in the normal case and fail-crash in the degenerate one.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The gigapipe ruler's own write-back path is hard-coded tenant-less: writer/controller/recording_writeback.go:30,34 pass "" to GetTimeSeriesService/GetSamplesService. Even in a hypothetical multi-node config, recording-rule output cannot be routed per tenant. This independently supports the plan's position that gigapipe's ruler must be treated as recording-only and that alert evaluation belongs in OpenPanel's worker.
- X-Ttl-Days is a dead letter in OSS. It is parsed (middleware.go:167-174), mirrored on gRPC (tenant.go:49-58), and materialised per row into MTTLDays (builder.go:357,388) — but no insert service writes a TTL column: samples_v3 gets (type, fingerprint, timestamp_ns, string, value), time_series gets (type, date, fingerprint, labels, metadata), metrics gets (type, fingerprint, timestamp_ns, value). Only a closed-source insert-service plugin (plugins.GetSamplesInsertServicePlugin, samples.go:48-51) could consume it. If the plan was considering per-request TTL headers as an escape hatch for per-signal retention, that option does not exist in OSS — the conditional-TTL-on-the-type-column approach the plan already names is the only route.
- The `type` UInt8 column that discriminates logs from metrics inside samples_v3 is confirmed on the write side (writer/service/insert/samples.go:24 and metrics.go:23, both acquiring "type"), but ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql:25-32 creates samples_v3 WITHOUT it — the column must be added by the maintenance/upgrade path (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/update.go). I did not trace which template adds it; treat the exact DDL of the deployed samples_v3 as UNVERIFIED and read it from a live instance before writing a conditional TTL expression against it.
- Signal isolation is deliberate and documented in-tree (writer/controller/services.go:9-20, "SIGNAL ISOLATION: each signal resolves ONLY its own services"), and metrics explicitly share samples+time_series with logs (services.go:58-65). That is first-party confirmation of the plan's premise that logs and metrics land in one table.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's decision 2 (label enforcement, not database-per-project) survives intact and is if anything better supported than the first engineer stated — not only is the reader single-database (reader/registry/static.go:33-38 ignores ctx entirely), but the writer's per-request selector is fail-open, non-atomic, unauthenticated per-tenant, and inert under env-var config. Any plan text should say the header selects a preconfigured NODE NAME, never "routes to a DSN", and must not describe it as a tenancy boundary. Two changes to make: (1) do not repeat the absolute claim that the writer cannot dial a caller-supplied DSN — writer/chwrapper carries dormant XDSN dialing, so the gateway must strip X-CH-DSN and x-ch-dsn from every proxied ingest request rather than relying on the header being harmless, and a gigapipe version bump should re-check whether that primitive got wired up. (2) Remove any reliance on X-Ttl-Days for per-signal retention: it is parsed but never persisted in OSS, so conditional ClickHouse TTL keyed on the samples_v3 `type` column is the only mechanism, and the deployed samples_v3 DDL should be read from a live instance first since ctrl/qryn/sql/log.sql does not declare that column.

## Investigation 39 — `partially_confirmed`

I reached the same verdict as the first engineer and every one of their ~20 citations checks out verbatim — I re-read each file independently. The `Client` model and the `getClientByIdCached` → `verifyPassword` → `getCache` machinery are real and reusable, `cors` really is on `Project` not `Client`, `validateSdkRequest` really never reads `client.type`, and the Export/Import/MCP validators really are deny-lists on `write`. But their answer understates the blast radius in one place and misses two surfaces entirely. First, `validateExportRequest` gates BOTH `/export` and `/insights` (apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.ts:52) — a new `telemetry` enum value is silently granted the Insights API too, which is the richest read surface (chart engine, profiles, groups, saved reports), not just Export/Import/MCP. Second, and more decisive for this plan: `validateSdkRequest` contains two paths that return an authenticated client with NO secret verification at all — `client.ignoreCorsAndSecret` (auth.ts:133-135) and an Origin match against `project.cors` (auth.ts:137-161, incl. `'*'`). Since client IDs are public values shipped in web SDK bundles and `Origin` is attacker-controlled from curl, reusing `validateSdkRequest` for telemetry would make the op_project_id security boundary bypassable with a public ID alone. The first engineer listed those lines but framed them as ordering ("short-circuits on…", "and only then verifies the secret") rather than as the reason a separate validator is mandatory rather than merely tidier. Third, they never checked docs or tests: the public docs enumerate exactly three client types and already contain a false claim about track-time type enforcement, and there is zero test coverage of `validateSdkRequest`.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:353-375` — Verified independently. `enum ClientType { read write root }` then `model Client { id String @id @default(dbgenerated("gen_random_uuid()")) @db.Uuid; name String; secret String?; type ClientType @default(write); projectId String?; project Project? @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade); organizationId String; ignoreCorsAndSecret Boolean @default(false); createdAt; updatedAt; @@map("clients") }`. No `cors` field. The first engineer's reading is exact.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- THE FIRST ENGINEER UNDERCOUNTED THE EXPOSED SURFACES. Their summary and corrections say a new `telemetry` enum value is granted "the Export, Import and MCP read surfaces". It is also granted the INSIGHTS API: apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.ts:36,52 imports and calls `validateExportRequest(req.headers)` in its own preHandler. Insights is the larger of the two read surfaces (chart engine, event names, profiles, groups, saved reports). The count is four surfaces, and the plan's mitigation list must include insights.router.ts / insights.controller.ts.
- THEY UNDERSTATED THE INGEST BYPASS. They describe auth.ts:133-161 procedurally ("short-circuits on client.ignoreCorsAndSecret", "matches client.project.cors", "and only then verifies the secret"). The security consequence is the load-bearing part and they never state it: BOTH paths `return client` without any secret verification (auth.ts:134, 155, 159). Client IDs are public (they ship in web SDK bundles and are accepted from the JSON body at auth.ts:52), and `Origin` is freely settable from a non-browser client. So for any project whose `cors` array is non-empty — or any client with `ignoreCorsAndSecret` — possession of the public client ID plus a spoofed Origin header is sufficient to authenticate as that project. That makes `validateSdkRequest` structurally unusable as the auth for a telemetry bearer token whose whole purpose is to be the source of truth for the injected `op_project_id`. This is not a nice-to-have refactor; it is why the separate validator is mandatory.
- THEY DID NOT CHECK DOCUMENTATION, AND THE DOCS ALREADY LIE ABOUT THIS. apps/public/content/docs/api/track.mdx:13 states "All requests require a `write` or `root` client", and apps/public/content/docs/api/authentication.mdx:10 states "Track API: Default client works with `write` mode". The code enforces neither — validateSdkRequest never reads client.type. Anyone reasoning from the docs (including a future implementer of this plan) would wrongly conclude ClientType already gates ingest. Three doc surfaces also enumerate exactly three types and must be edited: authentication.mdx:56-66 (a literal "three client types" table), mcp/index.mdx:53-62, features/mcp.json:72,140-141.
- THEY DID NOT CHECK TEST COVERAGE. There is no test file for apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts (only ids.test.ts and image-proxy.test.ts exist in that directory), and no test anywhere exercises validateSdkRequest. The only client-auth tests are packages/mcp/src/auth.test.ts — which mocks ClientType as a plain object literal at line 8, so a new Prisma enum value cannot break it — and apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.test.ts, which mocks getClientByIdCached with a single hard-coded `read` client. The allow-list retrofit they recommend therefore lands with no existing regression net, and each retrofitted validator needs a new negative test.
- MINOR CITATION SLIPS, none load-bearing: (a) `resolveClientProjectId` uses `db.project.findFirst`, not `findUnique` (packages/db/src/services/project.service.ts:186); `findUnique` with `{organizationId, id}` is export.controller.ts:35. (b) Their range "project.service.ts:163-198" overshoots the function, which ends at 197. (c) They cite one enum-ADD VALUE precedent; there are nine. (d) They assert the schema's `@default(write)` and `onDelete: Cascade` without showing the migrations that produced them — 20240411180951 and 20250225230336 respectively — worth having, because the ORIGINAL ClientType migration set `DEFAULT 'read'` and `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so reading only the first migration would mislead.
- SHARPENING, NOT A CONTRADICTION: the Import exposure is narrower than "Import surface" implies but qualitatively worse than a read. apps/api/src/controllers/import.controller.ts:13-27 pins `project_id: projectId` from `request.client?.projectId`, so a telemetry-typed client cannot import into another project — but it CAN insert arbitrary hand-crafted `IClickhouseEvent` rows straight into TABLE_NAMES.events for its own project, bypassing the entire track pipeline, isBotHook and session logic. Export is the one with org-wide breadth.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- `validateExportRequest` is the auth for `/insights` as well as `/export` (apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.ts:52). Any plan item that says "tighten the Export validator" must say "tighten the Export validator, which also guards Insights" — and the insights preHandler is an inline anonymous hook, not a shared one, so the fix has to be inside validateExportRequest itself or duplicated.
- The two secret-free return paths in validateSdkRequest (ignoreCorsAndSecret at auth.ts:134; Origin/cors match at auth.ts:155 and the `'*'` case at 159) mean the P1 ingest gateway MUST NOT call validateSdkRequest. A dedicated `validateTelemetryRequest` should be header-only (no body-derived credentials — auth.ts:52-56 pulls clientId/clientSecret out of `req.body` via ramda `path`, which is wrong for an OTLP protobuf body anyway), must require `client.secret` to be non-null, must require `client.type === ClientType.telemetry` as an allow-list, and must not consult project.cors at all.
- There is no rate limiter on the ingest routers. `activateRateLimiter` appears only in mcp.router.ts:12, manage.router.ts:21, export.router.ts:16 and insights.router.ts:48; track/event/profile/import have none, and apps/public/content/docs/api-reference/rate-limits.mdx documents that as intentional. A telemetry ingest endpoint modelled on track.router.ts inherits zero request-rate protection — relevant to the plan's P6 quotas item, which cannot lean on existing per-client limiting because none exists on the ingest side.
- `subscriptionHook` (apps/api/src/hooks/subscription.hook.ts:28-79) transfers cleanly to telemetry as the first engineer said — it only reads `req.client?.projectId`, no-ops when `process.env.SELF_HOSTED === 'true'`, replies 202 on windDownStep in {'blocked','final_warning'}, and fails open. Worth noting its typed Body is `ITrackHandlerPayload | DeprecatedPostEventPayload`, so the signature needs widening (or the type parameter loosening) to sit on an OTLP route, even though the body is never read.
- Cross-node token revocation is bounded by the 60s L1 LRU, not the 5-minute Redis TTL: `cachedFn.clear()` (packages/redis/cachable.ts:290-294) deletes only the local LRU and the Redis key, and the file's own comment says other nodes may serve stale for up to 60s. `manage.controller.ts` does call `getClientByIdCached.clear(...)` on create/update/delete, but that only helps the node that handled the request. For a telemetry token this is the revocation SLA and should be stated in the plan rather than discovered later.
- Because `onDelete: CASCADE` on clients.projectId is live (migration 20250225230336:23), deleting an OpenPanel project silently deletes its telemetry ingest tokens — while the telemetry rows already written into gigapipe's ClickHouse database under that op_project_id are NOT deleted by any Postgres cascade. The plan's retention/deletion section needs an explicit orphaned-telemetry story.
- `validateSdkRequest` requires `client.project` (auth.ts:94-96) and both `import.controller.ts:13` and `track.controller.ts` buildContext require `request.client?.projectId`, so every ingest surface today is project-scoped. If the plan wants an org-level telemetry collector token (one agent shipping for many projects, choosing the project per-request), none of the existing ingest machinery supports it — that needs `resolveClientProjectId`-style resolution plus a request-supplied projectId, which reopens the op_project_id trust question the plan closes by taking it from the token.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's position "telemetry ingest tokens reuse the existing Client/ClientType machinery" survives, but the first engineer's remediation list is incomplete in two ways that matter for a security boundary.

1. Widen the allow-list retrofit from three validators to four surfaces. Add `apps/api/src/routes/insights.router.ts:52` / `apps/api/src/controllers/insights.controller.ts:87` to the list of places that must explicitly reject `ClientType.telemetry`, alongside `validateExportRequest` (auth.ts:202), `validateImportRequest` (auth.ts:237) and `packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:99`. Because Export and Insights share one validator, the check belongs inside `validateExportRequest`. Prefer inverting all three deny-lists to allow-lists (`if (client.type !== read && client.type !== root) throw`) so the next enum value fails closed.

2. Escalate "write a new validator" from a tidiness recommendation to a hard requirement, with the reason recorded. `validateSdkRequest` authenticates on a public client ID plus a spoofable `Origin` header whenever `project.cors` is non-empty (auth.ts:137-161) or `ignoreCorsAndSecret` is set (auth.ts:133-135). The P1 gateway derives `op_project_id` — the entire tenancy boundary — from the authenticated token, so it must use a header-only `validateTelemetryRequest` that requires a non-null `client.secret`, verifies it, and never consults `project.cors`. Copy only `getClientByIdCached` + `verifyPassword` + the `getCache` pattern.

3. Add to the plan's change inventory: three documentation files (`apps/public/content/docs/api/authentication.mdx:56-66`, `docs/mcp/index.mdx:53-62`, `features/mcp.json:72,140-141`), and a correction to `docs/api/track.mdx:13` whose claim that track requires a write/root client is currently false — if the plan adds a type check to `validateSdkRequest`, that doc line becomes true and the change is a breaking one for any customer ingesting with a `read` client today, which needs calling out.

4. Add a testing line item to P1/P11: `apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts` has no test file at all, so every allow-list retrofit ships untested. Note also that `packages/mcp/src/auth.test.ts:8` mocks `ClientType` as an object literal, so it will not catch a missing case for the new value.

5. Record the 60s cross-node revocation lag (packages/redis/cachable.ts:155-157, 290-294) as the telemetry-token revocation SLA, and add an orphaned-telemetry story for project deletion, since clients cascade-delete with the project but ClickHouse rows do not.

## Investigation 40 — `partially_confirmed`

Every individual assertion in the claim is true and I read each file. But the claim is incomplete in three ways that matter to the plan, and its conclusion ("so all three can be repointed at a local OTLP endpoint") is wrong for one of the three signals. (a) Tracing is not API-only: apps/worker/src/utils/observability.ts is byte-for-byte identical to the API's except `getServiceName('worker')`, so the worker traces too. (b) prom-client is not worker-only: apps/api registers `fastify-metrics` at `/metrics` (apps/api/src/app.ts:22,372), gated only on the `testing` flag. (c) packages/logger is not merely "pino + output interception" — it imports `@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry` itself and is where the OTLP *log* shipping path lives (`HyperDX.getPinoTransport`, `HyperDX.getPinoMixinFunction`), a third HyperDX integration point wholly independent of the two observability.ts modules. Most importantly: traces and logs are OTLP-push and are plausibly repointable, but metrics are NOT — prom-client is pull-based and gigapipe has no Prometheus scraper anywhere in its tree, so "repointing" metrics is a rewrite (OTLP metrics exporter or a remote-write bridge), not a config change.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts:17-27` — Confirms the claim's first half exactly. `if (process.env.HYPERDX_API_KEY) { init({ apiKey: process.env.HYPERDX_API_KEY, service: getServiceName('api'), consoleCapture: false, disableLogs: true, disableMetrics: true, disableStartupLogs: true }); }` then `interceptProcessOutput(logger)`. Traces only (logs and metrics explicitly disabled), gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY. No endpoint/URL option is passed.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/utils/observability.ts:17-27` — CORRECTION to the claim: identical init() block, differing only in `service: getServiceName('worker')`. The worker also emits traces. The claim frames tracing as API-only.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/index.ts:4` — `import './utils/observability';` is the first import after `process.env.TZ = 'UTC'`. Same in /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/index.ts:1. The side-effect-module-first ordering the file comments require is actually honoured.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/metrics.ts:12,16` — `import client from 'prom-client'` then `export const register = new Registry()`. Confirms the claim. Registry holds ~30 metrics: job duration histogram, kafka reprocess counter, per-queue active/delayed/failed/completed/waiting gauges, seven buffer LLEN gauges, flush/add histograms and counters wired through `buf.flushObserver` / `buf.addObserver`, and session-lifecycle counters/gauges. Several gauges do live Redis work inside `collect()` (e.g. sessions_active_total does SMEMBERS + a ZCARD per project), so scrapes are not free.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/index.ts:26,36-37,39,73-83` — How the worker exposes /metrics: `import { register } from './metrics'`, then inside start(): `collectDefaultMetrics({ register })`, `const PORT = Number.parseInt(process.env.WORKER_PORT || '3000', 10)`, an Express app, and `app.get('/metrics', ...)` which sets `register.contentType` and writes `register.metrics()`. Plain Express, no auth on the route itself. Mounted after the bull-board router at '/'.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/app.ts:22,371-373` — CORRECTION: the API also serves Prometheus. `import metricsPlugin from 'fastify-metrics'` and, inside the public-API register scope (which has no prefix), `if (!testing) { instance.register(metricsPlugin, { endpoint: '/metrics' }); }`. So `/metrics` exists on the API too, always on outside tests.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/hooks/request-logging.hook.ts:4` — `const ignoreLog = ['/healthcheck', '/healthz', '/metrics', '/misc'];` — corroborates that /metrics is a real live route on the API, deliberately excluded from request logging.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/logger/index.ts:1,12-14,86-90,92-125` — packages/logger does more than pino. Line 1: `import * as HyperDX from '@hyperdx/node-opentelemetry'` (unconditional, at module top). Lines 12-14: `const logExporter = process.env.LOG_EXPORTER ?? (process.env.HYPERDX_API_KEY ? 'otlp' : 'stdout')`. Line 95: `const useHyperDX = logExporter === 'otlp' && !!process.env.HYPERDX_API_KEY`. Line 109: `mixin: process.env.HYPERDX_API_KEY ? HyperDX.getPinoMixinFunction : undefined`. Line 112-116: `transport: useHyperDX ? HyperDX.getPinoTransport(logLevel, { detectResources: true, service }) : ...`. getServiceName (86) joins LOG_PREFIX / name / NODE_ENV.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/logger/index.ts:149-163` — interceptProcessOutput: early-returns only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && !HYPERDX_API_KEY && LOG_EXPORTER === undefined` — i.e. it is ALWAYS on in production. `const passthrough = logExporter !== 'stdout'` decides whether raw lines are also teed to the original fd. Wraps process.stdout/stderr.write, line-splits, truncates at 8192 chars, tags `source: 'stdout'|'stderr'`, with a reentrancy guard.
