An OTLP/gRPC server also exists with the same MaxRecvMsgSize and gzip codec registered, and optional basic auth (writer/grpc/auth.go:39). So both OTLP transports the HyperDX SDK could use are served.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (repo-wide grep)` — A grep for `scrape_config|scrape_configs|ScrapeConfig` across all .go, .md and .yaml files in /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe returns ZERO files. gigapipe does not scrape Prometheus targets. This is the fact that breaks the claim's conclusion for metrics.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts initialises ... (traces only, gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY)" — correct, but the worker has an identical module (apps/worker/src/utils/observability.ts:17-24), differing only in getServiceName('worker'). Tracing is already wired in BOTH services, not just the API.
- "apps/worker/src/metrics.ts builds a prom-client registry" — correct, but prom-client is not worker-only. apps/api/src/app.ts:22,372 registers `fastify-metrics` at `/metrics` whenever `testing` is false. There are TWO Prometheus scrape endpoints in the product, on different HTTP servers (Express on the worker, Fastify on the API), with different registries.
- "packages/logger handles pino + output interception" — true but understated. packages/logger/index.ts:1 imports @hyperdx/node-opentelemetry unconditionally and is where the OTLP LOG export path lives (getPinoTransport at :113) and where trace<->log correlation is injected (getPinoMixinFunction at :109-111). It is a third, independent HyperDX coupling point, not just a pino wrapper. The two observability.ts modules explicitly disable the SDK's own log pipeline (disableLogs: true, consoleCapture: false) precisely because packages/logger owns that signal.
- "so all three can be repointed at a local OTLP endpoint" — false as stated for metrics, and unverified for traces/logs. Traces and logs are OTLP-push and are the plausible cases. Metrics are prom-client PULL over HTTP, and gigapipe has no scraper (zero scrape_config hits repo-wide), so nothing in gigapipe will ever fetch /metrics. Repointing metrics means either replacing prom-client with an OTLP metrics exporter, or writing a scrape->remote-write bridge, or running a collector/agent. That is code and infrastructure, not an env var.
- "gated on HYPERDX_API_KEY" understates how load-bearing that variable is. It gates THREE separate behaviours in three files: init() in both observability.ts (:17), the pino OTLP transport via `useHyperDX` (packages/logger/index.ts:95), and the trace_id/span_id mixin (:109). The mixin is gated on the raw key only, NOT on LOG_EXPORTER — so setting LOG_EXPORTER=stdout while a key is present still injects trace ids.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- EXACTLY WHAT REPOINTING TRACES REQUIRES — the endpoint is not configurable from OpenPanel source. init() is called with only apiKey/service/consoleCapture/disableLogs/disableMetrics/disableStartupLogs (observability.ts:17-24); no url, endpoint or baseUrl option is passed anywhere in either repo, and no OTEL_* variable appears anywhere in the OpenPanel tree. Whether @hyperdx/node-opentelemetry@0.10.3 honours OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is UNVERIFIABLE from this checkout: node_modules is not installed and the package is not in the local pnpm store (~/Library/pnpm/store/v11/links has no hyperdx entry). Do not write the plan assuming an env var will do it. Two source-grounded options: (a) if the SDK does honour OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, you still must supply a non-empty HYPERDX_API_KEY purely to pass the `if` gate at observability.ts:17, which is an ugly dependency on a vendor variable for a self-hosted stack; (b) replace the HyperDX init with a plain @opentelemetry/sdk-node OTLPTraceExporter pointed at gigapipe's /v1/traces (gigapipe/writer/router/tempo.go:12). Option (b) is cleaner and removes the vendor gate, but it forfeits getPinoMixinFunction and getPinoTransport unless those are replaced too.
- WHAT BREAKS IF YOU DROP HYPERDX_API_KEY WHILE SETTING LOG_EXPORTER — a real, readable duplicate-logging bug. With LOG_EXPORTER='otlp' and no key: logExporter='otlp' (index.ts:12), useHyperDX=false (:95), usePretty=false in production (:96), so `transport` is undefined and pino writes JSON to stdout. But `passthrough = logExporter !== 'stdout'` is TRUE (:163), so interceptProcessOutput ALSO tees every raw line to the original fd. Result: each non-pino line lands on stdout twice — once raw, once wrapped as pino JSON. The LOG_EXPORTER switch was designed as otlp-with-key vs stdout-without; a third state (otlp-to-a-local-collector, no HyperDX key) is not represented and misbehaves.
- WHAT BREAKS FOR CORRELATION — the plan's differentiator (session.id / profile.id propagation, log<->trace linking) depends on trace_id/span_id appearing on log lines, which comes solely from `mixin: process.env.HYPERDX_API_KEY ? HyperDX.getPinoMixinFunction : undefined` (index.ts:109-111). Remove the key and every log line loses its trace ids, silently. Any repointing plan must replace that mixin (e.g. with @opentelemetry/api trace.getActiveSpan().spanContext()) in the same change, not later.
- AUTO-INSTRUMENTATION IS STRUCTURALLY CRIPPLED BY tsdown, AND FIXING IT IS A BUILD CHANGE. Both tsdown configs bundle everything except a five-item allowlist. @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node (0.56.1 per lockfile) patches modules through shimmer/require-hooks at module-resolution time; a dependency inlined into dist/index.js is never resolved, so it is never patched. Today that means NO spans for ioredis, bullmq/groupmq, pg/Prisma or the ClickHouse client — the exact spans an observability product would want from itself. Only diagnostics_channel-based instrumentation (undici/fetch) survives. The fix the code comment names — moving ioredis/bullmq/pg into `external` — is a build-config change with real consequences (those packages must then exist in the runtime node_modules; the Dockerfiles do a separate `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod` for the runner, so this happens to hold, but it is a coupling worth stating).
- THE API IMAGE'S NODE_OPTIONS IS ALREADY TAKEN. apps/api/Dockerfile sets ENV NODE_OPTIONS="--report-on-fatalerror --report-on-signal --report-directory=/tmp". The standard OTel escape hatch for bundler-defeated instrumentation is a `--require`/`--import` preload via NODE_OPTIONS; doing that here means replacing the whole value and re-adding the three diagnostic-report flags, per-environment. apps/worker/Dockerfile sets no NODE_OPTIONS, so the two images need different treatment. Easy to get silently wrong.
- METRICS: TWO ENDPOINTS, TWO EXPOSURE POSTURES, NEITHER REACHABLE BY GIGAPIPE. Worker: Express `/metrics` on WORKER_PORT (default 3000, self-hosting relies on the default), reachable at worker.$DOMAIN behind Caddy basic_auth. API: fastify-metrics `/metrics` at the root of the public-API scope, reachable at $DOMAIN/api/metrics with NO auth (Caddy's `handle_path /api*` strips the prefix). Since gigapipe cannot scrape, the plan needs a decision it currently lacks: run a scraper sidecar that remote-writes to /v1/prom/remote/write, or add an OTLP metrics exporter alongside prom-client. Note the second path is not free either — several worker gauges execute Redis round-trips inside collect() (metrics.ts sessions_active_total does SMEMBERS plus one ZCARD per project), so a push-on-interval exporter changes when that cost is paid from 'when scraped' to 'every interval, always'.
- THE API's /metrics BEING PUBLIC AND UNAUTHENTICATED IS A PRE-EXISTING FINDING WORTH FLAGGING IN THE PLAN. app.ts:371-373 gates registration only on the `testing` flag; that register scope carries no auth hook, and the Caddyfile proxies /api* straight through. Whatever the plan does about telemetry, it should not widen this, and the P6 'quotas' phase is a natural place to fix it.
- A REFERENCED DESIGN DOC DOES NOT EXIST IN THE TREE. Both observability.ts files and packages/logger/index.ts cite 'logging-capture-plan.md'; the file is nowhere in the repo. `git log -S` shows the two originating commits: 5bceac94 'feat(logging): capture all process output through pino (logging-capture-plan)' and d19c5298 'feat(observability): initialize HyperDX tracing SDK in api and worker'. d19c5298's message states plainly that before it, 'Nothing called init() ... there were no traces and the pino mixin's trace_id/span_id were always empty' — so self-tracing is recent (Aug 2026) and has never run against a non-HyperDX backend. Treat it as unproven in production against any other endpoint.
- apps/start (the dashboard) has NO instrumentation of any kind — no pino, no @openpanel/logger, no OTel, no prom-client in its package.json, and no telemetry module under src/. The claim's 'all three' covers api, worker and the logger package; the dashboard is a fourth service that is entirely dark today.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan can keep its self-instrumentation premise, but must split it by signal instead of treating "repoint all three" as one task. Traces and logs: genuinely repointable, but the work is real — the HyperDX endpoint is not configurable from OpenPanel source (no url option passed, no OTEL_* var anywhere), so either confirm the SDK's env surface against installed node_modules before committing to it, or replace init() with a plain sdk-node OTLPTraceExporter and replace getPinoTransport/getPinoMixinFunction at the same time, since dropping HYPERDX_API_KEY silently kills trace_id/span_id on every log line and puts LOG_EXPORTER into an untested third state that double-logs. Metrics: remove "repoint" from the plan. prom-client is pull-based and gigapipe has no scraper, so P0/P1 needs an explicit decision — scraper sidecar remote-writing to /v1/prom/remote/write, or an OTLP metrics exporter added alongside prom-client — and must account for TWO endpoints (worker Express and API Fastify), not one. Separately, the plan should state up front that self-tracing today yields almost nothing useful: tsdown bundles ioredis/bullmq/pg, so no Redis, queue or database spans exist, and unbundling them is a build-config change (plus a NODE_OPTIONS conflict on the API image only). If dogfooding is meant to validate the trace waterfall in P4, that unbundling belongs in P0, not P6.

## Investigation 41 — `partially_confirmed`

gigapipe is indeed AGPL-3.0: /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE is the verbatim FSF AGPL v3 text (661 lines), and nfpm.yaml declares `license: "AGPLv3"`. The claim's operative facts about network-service use are supported by the licence text itself (§0 "Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying"; §5's "aggregate" clause; §13's obligation being conditioned on "if you modify the Program"). But the claim is materially incomplete in one direction that changes the whole posture: OpenPanel's own /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/LICENSE.md is BYTE-IDENTICAL to gigapipe's LICENSE (both md5 4ae09d45eac4aa08d013b5f2e01c67f6) — OpenPanel is itself AGPL-3.0. So the copyleft "implications for linking" that the claim gestures at largely do not bite: there is no proprietary side to contaminate on the server. There is also a real, separate inconsistency the plan should not inherit: /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/package.json:6 still declares `"license": "MIT"`, a leftover from scaffolding, contradicting LICENSE.md. This is a factual reading of two files, not legal advice.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:1-6` — Verbatim FSF text: "GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 19 November 2007 / Copyright (C) 2007 Free Software Foundation, Inc." 661 lines, no appended §7 additional terms (file ends with the standard "How to Apply" section at lines 620-661).
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/LICENSE.md (whole file)` — Identical 661-line AGPL v3 text. `md5 -q` on both files returns 4ae09d45eac4aa08d013b5f2e01c67f6 for gigapipe/LICENSE and openpanel/LICENSE.md — byte-for-byte the same licence. OpenPanel is AGPL-3.0, not a proprietary or permissively-licensed consumer of gigapipe.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/package.json:6` — `"license": "MIT",` — contradicts LICENSE.md. `git log -L6,6:package.json` shows it was introduced by 493e1b76 "added tooling (eslint, typescript and prettier)" replacing the empty `keywords`/`author` scaffold fields; LICENSE.md was added later (46d5d203, 2024-01-21). The root package is `"private": true` so it is not published, but the metadata says MIT.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/packages/sdks/*/LICENSE` — All seven SDK packages (astro, express, nextjs, nuxt, react-native, sdk, web) ship `MIT License / Copyright (c) 2026 OpenPanel`, matching `"license": "MIT"` in each package.json. These are the deliberately permissive, separately-distributed client libraries — they never touch gigapipe, so nothing in this plan affects them.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:87-89` — §0: "To 'convey' a work means any kind of propagation that enables other parties to make or receive copies. Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying." This is the textual basis for "OpenPanel calling gigapipe over HTTP is not conveying gigapipe".
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:540-551` — §13 Remote Network Interaction: "Notwithstanding any other provision of this License, IF YOU MODIFY THE PROGRAM, your modified version must prominently offer all users interacting with it remotely through a computer network ... an opportunity to receive the Corresponding Source of your version." The trigger is modification, and the obligation is to offer the source OF THE MODIFIED GIGAPIPE — not of OpenPanel.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:223-231` — §5 aggregate clause: "A compilation of a covered work with other separate and independent works, which are not by their nature extensions of the covered work, and which are not combined with it such as to form a larger program ... is called an 'aggregate' ... Inclusion of a covered work in an aggregate does not cause this License to apply to the other parts." Relevant to shipping gigapipe alongside OpenPanel in a compose bundle.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:233-238` — §6 Conveying Non-Source Forms: "You may convey a covered work in object code form ... provided that you also convey the machine-readable Corresponding Source under the terms of this License." This is what a self-built gigapipe Docker image pushed under an OpenPanel account would trigger.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/nfpm.yaml:16` — `license: "AGPLv3"` in the Debian/RPM packaging metadata, alongside `maintainer: "GIGAPIPE <support@gigapipe.com>"` and `vendor: "GIGAPIPE"`. Independent confirmation of the project's own licence declaration.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/README.md:251-255` — "#### License ... ©️ HEPVEST BV, All Rights Reserves. Released under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0". Names the copyright holder as HEPVEST BV — note the LICENSE file itself contains no filled-in copyright line (only the FSF's own 2007 line at :4 and the `<year> <name of author>` template at :633).
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe git history: 0207310, 7b21d53, 7580d08` — 0207310 (2021-01-03) "Create LICENSE" added a 21-line MIT licence. 7b21d53 (2021-10-27) "Update LICENSE" replaced it with the 661-line AGPLv3 text; its commit message reads "Parties interested in a more liberal license for the code are welcome to contact the team/authors to establish a dual-license agreement." 7580d08 is the "qryn -> gigapipe" rename; go.mod line 1 is still `module github.com/metrico/qryn/v5`.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (grep for SPDX/AGPL headers in *.go)` — No per-file licence headers: `grep -rn "SPDX\|GNU Affero\|AGPL" --include="*.go"` returns nothing, and `find -iname "*license*"` returns only ./LICENSE. There is no separately-licensed vendored subtree in the repo (view/ contains only static.go, static_no.go, view.go; the embedded `view/dist` is absent and gated behind the `view` build tag).
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:5,26,48,68,93,123,143` — The self-hosting bundle REFERENCES third-party images by name (caddy:2-alpine, postgres:14-alpine, redis:7.2.5-alpine, clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.10.2.65) and only ships its own three (lindesvard/openpanel-api:2, -dashboard:2, -worker:2). A compose file naming an upstream gigapipe image pulled by the operator follows the existing pattern; building and publishing an OpenPanel-branded gigapipe image would not.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel (find -name "*.go")` — Zero Go files in the OpenPanel repo. In-process linking against gigapipe is not physically possible with the current architecture — the only coupling available is HTTP/gRPC across a process boundary, which is exactly the §0 'no transfer of a copy' case.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/public/content/compare/plausible-alternative.json:327-329` — OpenPanel's own marketing content states its licence: `"openpanel": "Yes - AGPL-3.0"` ... `"notes": "Both are open source and AGPL-3.0 licensed."` Also apps/public/content/articles/self-hosted-product-analytics.mdx:24 lists OpenPanel as AGPL-3.0. The public position matches LICENSE.md, not package.json.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/TRADEMARK.md` — Trademark guidelines are separate from the copyright licence and already contemplate third parties bundling: prohibited uses include "bundling OpenPanel products with other software" under OpenPanel marks, with the remedy being rebranding — "Adherence to the terms of the open-source license for OpenPanel software products and code is mandatory." Trademark, not copyleft, is the lever OpenPanel actually reserves.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "which is compatible with running it as a separately-deployed network service" is right but for a reason the claim doesn't state. The support is textual: §0 (LICENSE:87-89) says mere network interaction with no transfer of a copy is not conveying, and §13 (LICENSE:540-546) conditions the source-offer duty on "if you modify the Program". Running an UNMODIFIED gigapipe binary behind apps/api triggers no §13 obligation at all.
- The claim's framing — gigapipe is AGPL, so watch out for implications — implies OpenPanel is on the other side of a licence divide. It is not. openpanel/LICENSE.md and gigapipe/LICENSE are the same bytes (md5 4ae09d45eac4aa08d013b5f2e01c67f6). Both projects are AGPL-3.0. Even the worst-case characterisation (a single combined work) is licence-compatible in the AGPL-3.0 → AGPL-3.0 direction, so the copyleft risk the sentence hints at is close to nil for the server-side codebase.
- "implications for linking" is the least applicable half of the claim. OpenPanel contains zero Go files; gigapipe is a standalone Go binary with an HTTP surface. There is no linking mechanism available. The concrete triggers are modification (§13) and image/binary redistribution (§6), not linking.
- The claim omits the two situations that DO change posture, which is what the plan actually needs: (a) if OpenPanel patches gigapipe — plausible, since plan decision #2 exists precisely because gigapipe's reader binds one ClickHouse DB at boot, and per-signal TTL and ruler behaviour may need changes — then §13 requires offering that modified gigapipe's Corresponding Source to users interacting with it over the network; (b) if OpenPanel builds and publishes its own gigapipe binary or Docker image (rather than referencing an upstream tag the way self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:5-68 references caddy/postgres/redis/clickhouse), §6 (LICENSE:233-238) requires conveying Corresponding Source with it.
- "gigapipe is AGPL-3.0" is true today but is not the project's original licence and is not marked in-tree. It was MIT until 7b21d53 (2021-10-27); there are no SPDX or licence headers in any .go file; and the LICENSE file carries no copyright-holder line — the holder (HEPVEST BV) appears only in README.md:255.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- OpenPanel is AGPL-3.0 by LICENSE.md but declares "license": "MIT" at package.json:6. Git history shows this came from the initial tooling commit (493e1b76), predating LICENSE.md (46d5d203, 2024-01-21) — a stale scaffold value, not a deliberate dual-licence. The root package is private:true so nothing is published under the wrong metadata, but any tool reading package.json (SBOM generators, licence scanners, the container-security/sbom tooling this environment has) will report OpenPanel as MIT. Worth flagging in the doc as a pre-existing inconsistency the observability work should not compound.
- The seven SDK packages under packages/sdks/* are genuinely MIT (own LICENSE files, own package.json license fields) and are the parts users embed in their own proprietary apps. Nothing in the observability plan touches them — telemetry ingest goes through apps/api. If a future phase ships an OTel-flavoured client SDK, the doc should state up front that it stays MIT and stays free of any gigapipe-derived code, so the permissive SDK boundary survives.
- gigapipe was relicensed MIT → AGPLv3 in 7b21d53, whose commit message invites dual-licence agreements ("Parties interested in a more liberal license for the code are welcome to contact the team/authors"). Since OpenPanel is itself AGPL-3.0, a commercial gigapipe licence is not needed for the plan as scoped; it would only become relevant if OpenPanel ever wanted to ship a closed-source variant. Whether such a licence is offered today, and on what terms, is not determinable from this repository.
- gigapipe's docs/contributing.md states "Gigapipe is a 100% clear-room, native implementation. Do not submit code copied or derived from other projects (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo...) ... PRs containing copied or derived code will be rejected regardless of license compatibility", echoed by README.md footnote [^1]. This matters for the plan's phase-3 position on raw PromQL: pulling @prometheus-io/lezer-promql into OpenPanel is a separate licence question (that package is Apache-2.0 upstream, but I did not verify it on disk — it is not currently a dependency), and it is emphatically not something to contribute back into gigapipe.
- gigapipe declares no per-file licence headers and no SPDX identifiers anywhere in its Go sources, and the AGPL text carries no filled-in copyright holder. If OpenPanel ever forks or patches gigapipe, §5(a)/(b) (LICENSE:202-208) require the modified work to carry prominent notices stating it was modified, with a date, and stating the AGPL release — obligations that a plain fork-and-patch workflow will not satisfy on its own given there are no existing headers to amend.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's licence section should be rewritten from "gigapipe is AGPL, which constrains us" to "both projects are AGPL-3.0 (identical licence text), so the combination is licence-compatible in every configuration this plan contemplates; the obligations that remain are operational, not architectural." Concretely: (1) state that OpenPanel is AGPL-3.0 too, citing LICENSE.md, so no reader concludes copyleft is a reason to keep gigapipe at arm's length — the arm's-length service boundary should be justified on the operational grounds the plan already gives (gigapipe's reader binds one ClickHouse database at boot, label enforcement is the isolation mechanism), not on licensing. (2) Add an explicit rule for P0: prefer running an UNMODIFIED upstream gigapipe image referenced by tag in self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml, matching how caddy/postgres/redis/clickhouse are already referenced at lines 5/26/48/68 — this keeps both §6 and §13 untriggered. (3) Add a decision gate: the moment the plan requires patching gigapipe (a real possibility for per-request DSN handling, conditional per-signal TTL, or ruler alert behaviour), §13 obligates publishing that fork's Corresponding Source to remote users, and §5(a)/(b) obligate modification notices — so a public openpanel/gigapipe fork repo becomes a P0 deliverable rather than an afterthought. Same if OpenPanel ever builds and pushes its own gigapipe image under lindesvard/*. (4) Drop "linking" from the risk framing entirely; OpenPanel has no Go code and cannot link gigapipe. (5) Note the package.json:6 MIT/LICENSE.md AGPL mismatch as a pre-existing repo-hygiene item so the observability docs are not the place where an incorrect licence claim gets propagated. Explicit caveat to carry into the doc: this is a reading of two licence files, not legal advice, and whether a given deployment forms "a single combined work" is a legal judgment no file on disk can settle.

## Investigation 42 — `partially_confirmed`

The claim's conclusion holds and the first engineer's evidence checks out line-for-line — I re-read every file they cited and found nothing misquoted. gigapipe's reader builds one process-global `model.IDBRegistry` at boot (`registry.Init()` -> `InitStaticRegistry()`, reader/registry/registry.go:20-47) from `config.Cloki.Setting.DATABASE_DATA`, fixing each database in `clickhouse.Auth.Database` at connection open (registry.go:63-67); the only implementation, `staticDBRegistry.GetDB(ctx)`, ignores its ctx and returns `s.databases[s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases))]` (reader/registry/static.go:33-38). Going the other direction (route -> service) strengthens the finding rather than weakening it: the read services that hold the registry are themselves constructed once at route-registration time, not per request (e.g. `service.CLokiQueriable{ServiceData: model.ServiceData{Session: dataSession}}` at reader/router/prometheus_query_range.go:49-51). The decisive fact neither the claim nor the first engineer states is that the writer's insert-service registry is built from the SAME `config.DATABASE_DATA` list the reader iterates (writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:45, writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:69,83), so you cannot add per-project databases for the writer's `X-CH-DSN` node-name lookup without simultaneously adding them to the reader's random-selection pool — the two paths are coupled through one config list, which kills database-per-project more cleanly than the read path alone does. Decision #2 (label enforcement) stands unchanged.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/registry.go:18-47` — Verified verbatim. `var Registry model.IDBRegistry` is a package global. `func Init()` does `p := plugins.GetDatabaseRegistryPlugin(); if p != nil { Registry = (*p)() }` and then, with no `return`, `Registry = InitStaticRegistry()` — the plugin registry is always discarded. `InitStaticRegistry` builds `dbMap[node.Config.Node]` and panics on empty: "We don't have any active DB session configured. Please check your config". Note the map is keyed by `Config.Node` (node name), not database name.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/registry.go:50-70` — Confirmed. `createDataDBSessions()` iterates `config.Cloki.Setting.DATABASE_DATA` and opens each with `clickhouse.Options{ Auth: clickhouse.Auth{ Database: dbObject.Name, Username: ..., Password: ... } }`. The database is baked into the connection's auth block at process start; no request-scoped value reaches it.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/static.go:33-38` — Confirmed verbatim, including the mutex the first engineer elided: `func (s *staticDBRegistry) GetDB(ctx context.Context) (*model.DataDatabasesMap, error) { s.mtx.Lock(); defer s.mtx.Unlock(); idx := s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases)); return s.databases[idx], nil }`. `ctx` is accepted and never read. This is the settling line.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/model/db_egistry.go:7-12` — Confirmed: `type IDBRegistry interface { GetDB(ctx context.Context) (*DataDatabasesMap, error); Run(); Stop(); Ping() error }`. Note the first engineer wrote `Ping()`; the real signature is `Ping() error`. Cosmetic, not material.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (repo-wide grep for IDBRegistry)` — Stronger than the first engineer stated. `grep -rn IDBRegistry --include='*.go' .` returns 15 hits: one interface definition, one implementation (`staticDBRegistry`, static.go:20), one global, and the rest are parameter/field types in routers and services. There is NO mock, fake, or alternate registry anywhere — including tests. Their hedge "in non-test code" was unnecessary.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/router/prometheus_query_range.go:46-66` — Runtime-path evidence the first engineer did not use. `RoutePrometheusQueryRange` constructs the PromQL engine, `service.CLokiQueriable{ServiceData: model.ServiceData{Session: dataSession}}` and `controllerv1.PromQueryRangeController{...}` ONCE at registration, then binds `ctrl.QueryRange` / `ctrl.QueryInstant` to the routes. The storage object holding the registry is a singleton for the process lifetime, so there is no per-request object to attach a tenant DB to either.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/reader.go:101-114` — `performV1APIRouting` calls `registry.Init()`, then `watchdog.Init(&model.ServiceData{Session: registry.Registry})` and passes the same global to RouteQueryRangeApis, RouteSelectLabels, RouteSelectPrometheusLabels, RoutePrometheusQueryRange, RouteTempo, RouteProf, PluggableRoutes. (The first engineer cited lines 100-111 and omitted RouteSelectPrometheusLabels from their list — immaterial.)
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/reader.go:66-83 and reader/utils/middleware/` — Confirmed. `applyMiddlewares` adds only LoggingMiddleware, CorsMiddleware (conditional), AcceptEncodingMiddleware, BasicAuthMiddleware (conditional). `ls reader/utils/middleware/` = accept_encoding.go, accept_encoding_test.go, basic_auth.go, basic_auth_test.go, cors_middleware.go, logging.go, xss_test.go. Nothing tenant-aware.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (repo-wide grep for X-Scope-OrgID / tenant in reader/)` — New check the first engineer did not run. `grep -rni 'X-Scope-OrgID|orgid|org_id|tenant' --include='*.go' reader/` returns exactly two hits, both generated protobuf comments in reader/prof/querier_grpc.pb.go:59,204 ("returns profile stats for the current tenant"). The only `X-Scope-OrgID` string in the whole repo is a comment at ruler/controller/controller.go:3: "single-tenant — no X-Scope-OrgID is read." The reader implements no Loki/Cortex tenancy header.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/plugins/tables_plugins.go:3-13 + reader/utils/tables/tables.go:59-70` — A SECOND dormant extension point the first engineer missed. `type TableNamesPlugin func() map[string]string` with `RegisterTableNamesPlugin`/`GetTableNamesPlugin`; consumed in `GetTableName(name)` which returns the plugin's mapping when non-empty. A fork could return db-qualified names here. But the signature takes no ctx and no request — it is process-global like the registry, so it still cannot do per-request selection. Repo-wide grep finds no registrant.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/plugins/plugins.go:53-62` — Confirmed: `type DatabaseRegistryPlugin func() model.IDBRegistry`, `RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin`, `GetDatabaseRegistryPlugin`. Repo-wide grep for these two names returns only the definitions plus the single call at reader/registry/registry.go:21 — no registrant anywhere, tests included.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:45-68 and writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:63-92` — THE ADDITION THAT MATTERS. `for _, dbObject := range config.DATABASE_DATA` builds one `DataDatabasesMap` + ClickHouse adapter per entry, and those become the insert services registered into `registry.NewStaticServiceRegistry(...)` (qryn_writer_db.go:224-232), keyed by `node.Node`. This is the SAME `DATABASE_DATA` list the reader iterates at reader/registry/registry.go:53. There is one shared database list process-wide: adding N project databases so the writer's X-CH-DSN node-name lookup can route them would put all N into the reader's random `GetDB` pool.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:65` — In-source acknowledgement from upstream: `// TODO: move this all into a separate /registry module and add plugin support to support dynamic database registries`. Dynamic per-tenant database registries are explicitly unimplemented, on the write side too.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/service/registry/static.go:54-68` — Confirms the first engineer's writer correction. `staticServiceRegistryGetService[T interface{ GetNodeName() string }](r, id, svcs)`: `if id != "" { for _, svc := range svcs { if svc.GetNodeName() == id { return svc, nil } } }` then unconditionally `idx := r.rand.Intn(len(svcs)); return svcs[idx], nil`. An unmatched X-CH-DSN silently falls back to a random node — it does not error.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/middleware.go:164-212 and writer/controller/services.go:40-65` — Confirmed: `dsn := strings.Clone(r.Header.Get("X-CH-DSN"))` -> `context.WithValue(ctx, utils.ContextKeyDSN, dsn)` -> `ResolveLogServices(dsn)` -> `Registry.GetSamplesService(dsn)` / `GetTimeSeriesService(dsn)`, i.e. straight into the node-name lookup above. Also note services.go:58-65: `ResolveMetricServices` delegates to `ResolveLogServices` with the comment "Metrics and logs share the same storage (samples + time series)" — first-party corroboration of the plan's per-signal-retention problem.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (grep X-CH-DSN / ContextKeyDSN repo-wide)` — Confirmed the write/read asymmetry independently: hits appear only under writer/ (controller/middleware.go:165,204,222,244; grpc/tenant.go:33,42,43; utils/context.go:12; plus grpc tests). Zero hits under reader/.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/router/init.go:74-100` — Confirmed: `session := readerregistry.Registry`, then `readerservice.NewQueryRangeService(&readermodel.ServiceData{Session: session})` and `&readerservice.CLokiQueriable{ServiceData: readermodel.ServiceData{Session: session}}`. The ruler evaluates against the same boot-time global. Also `distributed := len(cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA) > 0 && cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA[0].ClusterName != ""` — index [0] only, another place that assumes a single database.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:84-156` — Confirmed: `portCHEnv` returns early if `len(cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA) > 0`, else creates exactly one entry with `Name` = `CLICKHOUSE_DB` (default `"cloki"`), plus host/port/auth/TTLDays from env. The env/Docker path yields exactly one database process-wide.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (grep sighup|reload in reader/ and cmd/)` — New check: zero hits. There is no config-reload or SIGHUP path in the reader or the entrypoint, and `registry.Init()` is called once from reader/reader.go:103 (itself invoked once as a boot step at cmd/gigapipe/main.go:363). The database binding is fixed for the process lifetime — you cannot even add a project database without a restart.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/utils/tables/tables.go:72-118` — Confirmed: table names are unqualified (`samples_v3`, `time_series`, …) unless `db.Config.ClusterName != ""`, in which case the *_Dist names get ``fmt.Sprintf("`%s`.%s%s", db.Config.Name, ...)``. In the normal single-node case queries resolve against the connection's default database, reinforcing that the DB is a property of the boot-time connection.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (git, HEAD d4b91b1)` — Verified against the checked-out commit d4b91b1 "build(deps): bump github.com/sirupsen/logrus". `git log --oneline -- reader/registry/` shows six commits (55998f4, e05bf2d, c718e00, 7f3f274, ed2e8c2, 634c551); `git log -S 'GetDB(ctx' -- reader/` shows no commit that ever added request-scoped selection. History contains no per-request tenant read path.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's phrase "impossible on the read path" is one notch too strong as literally worded, and neither the claim nor the first engineer names the caveat: database-per-project is impossible within a SINGLE gigapipe reader process, but nothing stops you running N gigapipe processes, one per project database, since the database is a boot-time config value (reader/registry/registry.go:53-67). That is not viable for OpenPanel — it is one Go process, one ClickHouse connection pool, one HTTP port and one ruler per project — but the honest statement is "impossible in one process", not "impossible". The plan should say so, because "impossible" invites a reviewer to find the counterexample and distrust the rest.
- "Bound to a single ClickHouse database" is imprecise in the way the first engineer said, and I would sharpen it further: the boot-time pool is a `map[string]*model.DataDatabasesMap` keyed by `node.Config.Node` (reader/registry/registry.go:41-44), i.e. keyed by NODE NAME, not database name. Two DATABASE_DATA entries sharing a `Node` value silently collapse to one. The precise statement: the reader binds at boot to a fixed set of connections keyed by node name, each with its database fixed in the connection's auth block, and `GetDB` picks among them uniformly at random per call while ignoring its `ctx`.
- The first engineer's "a repo-wide grep for IDBRegistry finds exactly one implementation in non-test code" understates their own finding. The grep returns exactly one implementation FULL STOP — there is no mock or fake registry in tests either. The hedge is unnecessary and slightly weakens a stronger fact.
- The first engineer identified one dormant extension point (`RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin`) but missed a second: `RegisterTableNamesPlugin` / `GetTableNamesPlugin` (reader/plugins/tables_plugins.go:3-13), consumed by `GetTableName` at reader/utils/tables/tables.go:59-70, which could in principle return db-qualified table names and redirect queries at a different database. It does not rescue database-per-project either — its signature is `func() map[string]string` with no ctx and no request — but a plan that lists gigapipe's extension points should list both, and should note that BOTH are process-global, which is the real reason neither helps.
- Minor citation drift in the first engineer's evidence, all immaterial: `performV1APIRouting` is reader/reader.go:101-114 (they wrote 100-111) and their route list omits `router.RouteSelectPrometheusLabels`; the interface method is `Ping() error`, not `Ping()`; and they omitted that `GetDB` takes a mutex, which matters only in that the random pick is serialized across all in-flight requests.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The strongest argument against database-per-project is not the read path alone but the COUPLING: the writer's insert-service registry is constructed from the same `config.DATABASE_DATA` slice the reader iterates (writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:45 and qryn_writer.go:69,83 vs reader/registry/registry.go:53). So the tempting workaround — "use the writer's X-CH-DSN to route each project to its own database, and figure out reads later" — is self-defeating in a single process: every project database you add for the writer lands in the reader's random `GetDB` pool. The plan should lead decision #2's justification with this rather than with the reader in isolation.
- The read services holding the registry are singletons constructed at route-registration time, not per request (reader/router/prometheus_query_range.go:49-51; the ruler does the same at ruler/router/init.go:89-99). Even if a tenant were somehow placed in the request context, there is no per-request service object to carry it — which is why the ctx-aware `GetDB(ctx)` signature is a dead letter rather than a half-built feature.
- There is no config-reload or SIGHUP handling in reader/ or cmd/ (grep returns zero hits) and `registry.Init()` runs once from a boot step (reader/reader.go:103, invoked at cmd/gigapipe/main.go:363). Even the degenerate "one reader process per project" fallback would require a process restart to onboard a project. This is worth one line in the plan as further justification that label enforcement is the only workable isolation model.
- First-party corroboration for the plan's per-signal-retention position, from the writer rather than the schema: writer/controller/services.go:58-65 defines `ResolveMetricServices` as a pure delegation to `ResolveLogServices`, with the comment "Metrics and logs share the same storage (samples + time series), so this delegates to ResolveLogServices". That is gigapipe's own code stating logs and metrics land in the same tables, which is exactly why a single global SAMPLES_DAYS cannot express per-signal retention.
- Upstream acknowledges the gap in-source: `// TODO: move this all into a separate /registry module and add plugin support to support dynamic database registries` (writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:65). Useful for the plan's risk section — dynamic database registries are a known-unbuilt item on both paths, so a future gigapipe release adding them is plausible but cannot be assumed.
- `ruler/router/init.go:80` computes `distributed := len(cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA) > 0 && cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA[0].ClusterName != ""` and `writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:75` dials `config.DATABASE_DATA[0]` for its main connection. Several components hard-index entry [0], so a multi-entry DATABASE_DATA is not uniformly treated as a pool even where it is treated as one — another reason not to try to smuggle per-project databases in through that list.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan needs to change: decision #2 (label enforcement as the isolation mechanism, enforced at ingest by overwriting op_project_id and at query by mandatory matcher injection) is correctly grounded, and the first engineer's verdict was right. Two wording fixes are worth making in the written plan. First, replace "gigapipe's reader binds to a single ClickHouse database at boot" with "the reader binds at boot to a fixed set of connections whose databases are fixed in each connection's auth block, and selects among them at random per call while ignoring the request context" — and say "impossible in a single reader process" rather than flatly "impossible", noting the non-viable one-process-per-project alternative so a reviewer does not find it and doubt the analysis. Second, replace the parenthetical "only its writer accepts a per-request DSN" with the accurate mechanism: the writer's X-CH-DSN is matched against preconfigured NODE NAMES from the same DATABASE_DATA list the reader reads, with a silent random fallback when nothing matches (writer/service/registry/static.go:54-68) — and add the coupling argument, which is the real closer: per-project databases added for the writer would land in the reader's random selection pool, because both registries are built from one shared config list.

## Investigation 43 — `partially_confirmed`

gigapipe is AGPL-3.0 — confirmed independently: /Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE is 661 lines of unmodified FSF AGPL v3 (md5 4ae09d45eac4aa08d013b5f2e01c67f6), nfpm.yaml:16 says `license: "AGPLv3"`, README.md:255 names HEPVEST BV as holder, and 0 of 477 .go files carry any SPDX/AGPL header. The "compatible as a separately-deployed network service" half is supported by the text: §0 (LICENSE:87-89) says mere network interaction with no transfer of a copy is not conveying, and §13 (LICENSE:540-551) conditions the source-offer duty on "if you modify the Program". The first engineer's central correction is right and I independently reproduced it: openpanel/LICENSE.md is byte-identical to gigapipe/LICENSE (same md5), OpenPanel has no proprietary or enterprise-licensed subtree (no ee/, no BSL/ELv2/Business Source anywhere, every apps/* and packages/* package.json omits a license field), and zero Go files exist, so "linking" has no mechanism. But they missed the artifact that OpenPanel would actually run: the published ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe image is built with VIEW=1 and embeds a prebuilt dist.zip downloaded from a *different* repository (github.com/metrico/qryn-view), whose licence is not in this tree — so their statement "there is no separately-licensed vendored subtree in the repo" is true of the source but not of the shipped image. This is a factual reading of files on disk, not legal advice.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:1-6, 661 lines` — Verbatim FSF AGPL v3. `md5 -q` = 4ae09d45eac4aa08d013b5f2e01c67f6. `grep -n -i "qryn|gigapipe|hepvest|metrico" LICENSE` returns nothing (exit 1) — the copyright line is only the FSF's own "Copyright (C) 2007 Free Software Foundation, Inc." at :4 plus the `<year> <name of author>` template at :633. No §7 additional terms appended; file ends with the standard "How to Apply" section.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:87-89` — §0: "To \"convey\" a work means any kind of propagation that enables other parties to make or receive copies. Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying." Line numbers confirmed by sed -n '85,92p'.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:540-551` — §13 Remote Network Interaction, confirmed by sed -n '540,560p': "Notwithstanding any other provision of this License, if you modify the Program, your modified version must prominently offer all users interacting with it remotely through a computer network (if your version supports such interaction) an opportunity to receive the Corresponding Source of your version...". The trigger is modification; the parenthetical "(if your version supports such interaction)" is the clause that matters for a gigapipe kept behind apps/api.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/LICENSE:223-231, 233-238` — §5 aggregate clause and §6 Conveying Non-Source Forms, both confirmed verbatim at the cited lines by sed -n '220,240p'. §6: "You may convey a covered work in object code form under the terms of sections 4 and 5, provided that you also convey the machine-readable Corresponding Source under the terms of this License."
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/.github/actions/get-view/action.yml` — THE FINDING THE FIRST ENGINEER MISSED. The whole action is: `wget https://github.com/metrico/qryn-view/releases/download/$TAG/dist.zip && unzip -d view/dist -o dist.zip`. A prebuilt frontend from a SEPARATE repository is unzipped into view/dist at release time. Its licence is not present anywhere in the gigapipe tree and I could not verify it from disk — unverified.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/view/static.go:1-10` — `//go:build view` + `//go:embed dist` + `var Static embed.FS`. Combined with the Dockerfile's `ARG VIEW` / `if [ "$VIEW" = "1" ]; then go build -tags view`, this means the qryn-view bundle is compiled INTO the binary. `ls -a view/` shows only static.go, static_no.go, view.go — dist/ is absent from the checkout, so `go build -tags view` would fail on this tree without the CI fetch step.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/.github/workflows/build_release.yml:57-58, 120-121, 190-191, 205-215` — Every release path runs `- name: build qryn-view / uses: ./.github/actions/get-view` before building, and lines 209/214-215 push with `build-args: VIEW=1` to `ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe:latest` and `ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe:${ref_name}`. Two consequences: (a) an upstream image OpenPanel can simply reference by tag DOES exist — the first engineer argued the compose pattern without confirming this; (b) that upstream image contains the third-party UI bundle.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/Dockerfile:1-16` — `ARG VIEW` with an else branch: `go build -o gigapipe cmd/gigapipe/main.go` (no -tags view). Building without VIEW=1 yields a headless binary with no embedded third-party frontend — the right choice for this plan, since decision #1 says gigapipe is never exposed and the UI is dead weight.

Reproduced independently. `grep -n -i "openpanel|lindesv" LICENSE.md` returns only the FSF 2007 line: OpenPanel's LICENSE file ALSO has no filled-in copyright holder. `git log --diff-filter=A -- LICENSE.md` = 46d5d203, 2024-01-21.

Every apps/* and packages/* package.json except the seven SDKs omits `license` entirely, inheriting LICENSE.md.

A patched-but-unpublished gigapipe fork would contradict OpenPanel's own public position, independent of any legal analysis. (Line 118 of the same file also claims "all SDKs ship under an AGPL-3.0 license" — the SDKs are in fact MIT per packages/sdks/*/LICENSE, a third piece of licence-statement drift.)

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe git history: 0207310, 7b21d53, 7580d08` — Confirmed via `git log --follow -- LICENSE`. 0207310 (2021-01-03, PR #23) added a 21-line MIT LICENSE; 7b21d53 (2021-10-27, Lorenzo Mangani) replaced it with AGPLv3, commit body verbatim: "Parties interested in a more liberal license for the code are welcome to contact the team/authors to establish a dual-license agreement." - `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/go.mod:32-33, 42-44 (235 require lines)` — No vendor/ directory exists and no Go module cache is present on this machine, so third-party dep licences are UNVERIFIED from disk. **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The first engineer wrote "There is no separately-licensed vendored subtree in the repo (view/ contains only static.go, static_no.go, view.go; the embedded view/dist is absent and gated behind the view build tag)." That is true of the SOURCE TREE and false of the ARTIFACT. .github/actions/get-view/action.yml wgets a prebuilt dist.zip from github.com/metrico/qryn-view — a different repository — and unzips it into view/dist, and build_release.yml:209/214-215 pushes ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe with build-args VIEW=1. The image OpenPanel would pull embeds third-party frontend code whose licence is nowhere in the gigapipe tree. Mitigation is trivial and the plan should state it: build/run with VIEW unset (Dockerfile's else branch), which is correct anyway since decision #1 never exposes gigapipe's UI.
- The first engineer flattened a genuinely contested point. They wrote that §13's obligation is "to offer the source OF THE MODIFIED GIGAPIPE — not of OpenPanel," which is right, but did not flag that §13 says the offer runs to "all users interacting with it remotely through a computer network (if your version supports such interaction)" (LICENSE:541-544). Under decision #1 gigapipe is never exposed — end users talk to apps/api. Whether §13 reaches users proxied behind another service is unsettled and I cannot resolve it from files on disk; mark it unverified. It does not change the recommendation, because the conservative reading is cheap to satisfy: publish the fork.
- The metadata inconsistency is three files, not one. Enumerating every package.json turns up root:6 "MIT", self-hosting/package.json:10 "ISC", and tooling/publish/package.json:5 "MIT". self-hosting/package.json additionally lacks "private": true (root and tooling/publish both have it). self-hosting/ is the exact directory where a gigapipe compose service lands, so the plan will touch a package whose declared licence is ISC while the repo is AGPL-3.0.
- "implications for linking" is not merely the least applicable half of the claim — it is inapplicable. `find -name "*.go"` returns 0 in OpenPanel and there is no proprietary subtree (no ee/, no BSL/ELv2/Business Source anywhere in-tree) for copyleft to reach. The two real triggers are modification (§13) and image/binary redistribution (§6). The claim's word "redistribution" is the operative one and should not be dropped when the sentence is trimmed.
- "gigapipe is AGPL-3.0" is true today but is not marked in-tree: 0 of 477 .go files contain SPDX or AGPL headers, and the LICENSE file itself carries no copyright-holder line — only README.md:255 (HEPVEST BV) does. The same is true of OpenPanel's own LICENSE.md, which is the identical unmodified FSF template with no holder line, and README.md contains no licence statement at all. Neither project's licence file identifies its own copyright holder.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The clean deployment posture the plan should adopt, stated as three concrete constraints: (a) reference ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe:<pinned-tag> in self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml the way caddy/postgres/redis/clickhouse are referenced at lines 5/26/48/68 — never build and push an OpenPanel-branded gigapipe image, which is the §6 trigger; (b) if a custom build is unavoidable, build with VIEW unset so the qryn-view bundle is not embedded; (c) if gigapipe must be patched, publish the fork — decision #2 exists precisely because gigapipe's reader binds one ClickHouse DB at boot, so a patch is plausible, and per-signal TTL and ruler behaviour may need changes too.
- Whether §13 is triggered at all hinges entirely on one unresolved engineering question the plan has not yet settled: can label enforcement, per-signal TTL and recording-only ruler behaviour be achieved by CONFIGURATION, or do they require a gigapipe source patch? I did not verify this (out of scope for a licence check), but it is the single decisive variable for the AGPL posture and the plan should record it as such rather than treating the licence question as closed.
- gigapipe has no CONTRIBUTING file and no CLA. Upstreaming needed changes to metrico/gigapipe rather than maintaining a fork removes the §13 question entirely at zero licence cost, and there is no contributor-licence agreement standing in the way.
- A dual-licence route exists and is documented in gigapipe's own history: the relicensing commit 7b21d53 (2021-10-27) invites "parties interested in a more liberal license... to establish a dual-license agreement" with HEPVEST BV as sole named holder. Moot given OpenPanel is itself AGPL-3.0, but worth one line in the plan so nobody rediscovers it as a surprise.
- The licence-metadata drift is a documentation debt item the plan should not inherit and should not attempt to fix as part of the observability work: three package.json files (root, self-hosting, tooling/publish) contradict LICENSE.md, README.md states no licence at all, and apps/public/content/articles/open-source-web-analytics.mdx:118 claims the SDKs are AGPL-3.0 when packages/sdks/*/LICENSE are MIT. Separate cleanup PR.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's posture is sound and the licence is not a blocker, but three things should be written into it explicitly rather than left implicit. First, pin and reference the upstream ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe image rather than building and publishing an OpenPanel-branded one — that single choice keeps §6 out of play entirely, and I confirmed the upstream image exists to reference. Second, if any custom build happens, build without VIEW=1: the released image embeds a prebuilt frontend from github.com/metrico/qryn-view whose licence is not in the gigapipe tree and which I could not verify, and decision #1 never exposes gigapipe's UI anyway, so it is pure unverified surface for zero benefit. Third, the plan should record a standing rule: if gigapipe ends up patched — which decision #2's premise makes plausible — the fork gets published, and preferably upstreamed (no CLA stands in the way). Nothing here changes the architecture or phasing. The package.json/README/marketing licence drift is real but belongs in a separate cleanup PR, not this plan.

## Investigation 44 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-checked every file the first engineer cited and it all exists and says what they said. The four assertions in the claim are true: QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD enable HTTP basic auth (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:172-183 -> :321-326 -> reader/utils/middleware/basic_auth.go), 3100 is the default port (main.go:302-303, Dockerfile:14-15), docs/configuration.md documents the env surface, and MODE selects all/reader/writer/init_only (main.go:208-220, 306-311, 356-370). **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The first engineer's "OTLP/gRPC is multiplexed onto the same cleartext port" is stated without its mode gate. It is true only for MODE=all/writer/"". httpRoot (main.go:399-405) returns the bare router and a nil *http.Protocols for a reader-only node, so a reader mounts no gRPC dispatcher and does not advertise cleartext HTTP/2 at all. Pinned by tests at cmd/gigapipe/main_test.go:151-166 and 196-210, and stated in docs/otlp-grpc.md:8-14. For the plan this matters: if the metrics/logs read path runs as MODE=reader, that node is HTTP/1 only.
- They state as live fact that "view registers a catch-all '/'". It does not, in the image the plan will actually run. view.Init returns immediately unless HaveStatic, and HaveStatic is false in the default build (view/static_no.go:1-10, build tag `!view`); Dockerfile:4-9 passes `-tags view` only when the VIEW=1 build arg is set. The catch-all `mux.PathPrefix(prefix).Handler(fileServer)` (view/view.go:49) exists only in view-tagged builds. The bootSequence comment they quoted describes a constraint that is conditional on the build tag.
- Their gorilla/mux analysis is right about registration order but stops one step short. Router.Match builds the middleware chain only when a route matches (mux.go:143); Router.ServeHTTP falls through to `http.NotFoundHandler()` with no chain when nothing matches (mux.go:206-211). So on a default (non-view) build, requests to unregistered paths return 404 unauthenticated. Harmless in itself, but "the whole surface is behind basic auth" is not literally true, and any probe/monitor built on a 404 will not exercise auth.
- Their accurate-statement rewrite — "env vars are the primary and fully sufficient configuration surface, and they override the config file for everything portEnv touches" — over-reaches on the first half. docs/configuration.md:49 documents QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE, and cmd/gigapipe/main.go's portEnv never sets SYSTEM_SETTINGS.OTLPMaxMessageSize (grep: OTLPMaxMessageSize appears only under writer/). That variable must be bound generically inside cloki-config v0.0.96 — which is NOT on disk (no vendor/, and /Users/drew/go/pkg/mod/github.com/metrico/ does not exist). So there is a second env-var surface, of unknown extent and unknown naming rule, plus unknown default config-file search paths and unknown ReadConfig() behavior when no -config is passed. Mark this UNVERIFIED rather than asserting the env surface is fully known.
- Minor citation drift, none of it load-bearing: the port default is main.go:302-303 (not 301-303); the mux middleware loop is mux.go:143 (their 138-149 is the surrounding block); the auth `app.Use` call is main.go:323 inside the guard at :321-322.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Retention: the plan's position is CONFIRMED and one apparent shortcut is closed off. X-Ttl-Days / x-ch-dsn metadata does carry a per-request TTL into the writer (writer/controller/middleware.go:167-173, writer/grpc/tenant.go:53-58) and into the insert model (MTTLDays, writer/model/insert_request.go:162,178; TimeSeriesRequest.TTLDays :117), but nothing ever reads MTTLDays and no `ttl_days` column exists in ctrl/qryn/sql/*.sql. Real retention is a table-level `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL` from one global policy (ctrl/qryn/maintenance/rotate.go:87) driven by SAMPLES_DAYS (main.go:146-152). Per-signal retention therefore does need conditional TTL DDL, exactly as the plan says — X-Ttl-Days is not an alternative in this build.
- Security item for the ingest gateway (P1): X-CH-DSN (HTTP, writer/controller/middleware.go:165) and x-ch-dsn (gRPC, writer/grpc/tenant.go:42) select an arbitrary ClickHouse DSN per request, and the ONLY thing in front of them is the single shared basic-auth pair. X-Scope-Meta, X-Ttl-Days and X-Async-Insert are likewise attacker-controllable. apps/api must strip these headers from inbound client requests before proxying, and must never forward client headers wholesale. This sits alongside, not inside, the op_project_id label enforcement the plan already specifies.
- MODE=reader never runs initDB (main.go:306-311), and initDB is also skipped entirely when OMIT_CREATE_TABLES is truthy (main.go:64-71). A P0 compose that starts a reader before any writer/init_only node has created the schema will fail at query time, not at boot.
- Health checks: /ready calls watchdog.Check() and returns 500 on failure (shared/commonroutes/controller.go:11-21), and once auth is on it requires credentials. /config returns the literal "Not supported" (:23-26) — no credential leak, but also no config introspection — and /api/status/buildinfo returns a hardcoded version 0.0.1 (:28-34), so it cannot be used to pin the deployed gigapipe version. Version has to come from the image tag.
- Beyond CLICKHOUSE_READ_CLUSTER, four more env vars are read in production code but absent from docs/configuration.md: WEBAPPLOGPATH / WEBAPPLOGNAME (reader/utils/logger/logger.go:124,128) and CLOKIAPPLOGPATH / CLOKIAPPLOGNAME (writer/utils/logger/logger.go:132,136).
- The upstream repo pins its own boot-order and mode gating with tests (cmd/gigapipe/main_test.go, six tests covering bootSequence order, per-mode scope, servesGRPC and httpRoot). That is a useful stability signal for the plan: the mode semantics the plan depends on are asserted upstream and will not drift silently.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim is safe to keep as a plan premise, and the first engineer's verdict of partially_confirmed stands — but three of their supporting statements should be tightened before they are written into the doc. (1) Say OTLP/gRPC rides the shared cleartext port on writer/all nodes only; a MODE=reader node mounts no gRPC and no h2c, so if P0 ever splits reader and writer, the collector must target the writer. (2) Drop or qualify the "view catch-all /" detail — it is compiled out unless the image is built with VIEW=1, and the corollary is that on the default image unmatched paths 404 without auth. (3) Record the config surface as "env-var driven, with a -config file supported and a second, generically-bound QRYN_<SECTION>_<KEY> env family implemented inside cloki-config v0.0.96 whose source is not vendored — extent unverified" rather than "fully sufficient env surface". Two additions to the plan's own text: the P1 gateway must strip X-CH-DSN / X-Scope-Meta / X-Ttl-Days / X-Async-Insert from client requests (a shared basic-auth credential is the only thing guarding an arbitrary ClickHouse DSN), and the per-signal-retention section should note explicitly that X-Ttl-Days is inert in the OSS build, so conditional TTL DDL really is the only lever. Operationally, pin MODE explicitly and assert it at startup (a typo boots a silent no-op server), use lowercase true/false for every boolean env (boolEnv panics otherwise), and set both QRYN_LOGIN and QRYN_PASSWORD or the instance is fully open.

## Investigation 45 — `partially_confirmed`

I took the runtime/history/docs route (git log on the two commits that created this code, the shutdown path, the public docs site, gigapipe's own metrics surface) and reached the same verdict as the first engineer: every literal assertion in the claim is true, and the trailing conclusion "so all three can be repointed at a local OTLP endpoint" is false for metrics. I confirmed all of their corrections against source — the worker's observability.ts is byte-identical bar `getServiceName('worker')`, apps/api does register fastify-metrics at /metrics, and packages/logger is the third and independent HyperDX coupling point. They under-cited two things in their favour and got two things slightly wrong. In their favour: the source itself already settles the metrics question — the comment at apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts:9-10 (and the worker's, identically) reads "Metrics stay on prom-client/Grafana", and commit d19c5298's message says the same, so this is stated author intent, not just an inference from gigapipe's missing scraper. Against them: HYPERDX_API_KEY and LOG_PREFIX *are* documented self-hosting env vars on the public docs site, and neither they nor the claim noticed that nothing anywhere flushes or shuts down the OTel SDK on SIGTERM.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts:1-27 and /Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/utils/observability.ts:1-27` — Diffed both in full: identical except line 19 (`service: getServiceName('api')` vs `getServiceName('worker')`). Confirms the first engineer's correction (a). More decisive than anything they cited: the shared comment at lines 9-10 reads "Metrics stay\n// on prom-client/Grafana." and lines 7-8 "Traces only: logs ship via the pino transport and the output interceptor". The code's own comments already assign each signal to a fixed shipping path, so the claim's "all three can be repointed" contradicts stated in-file intent, not merely gigapipe's capabilities.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/api/src/app.ts:22, 362, 371-372` — Confirms correction (b) and adds one line they missed. :22 `import metricsPlugin from 'fastify-metrics';`. :371-372 inside the public-API register scope (no prefix): `if (!testing) { instance.register(metricsPlugin, { endpoint: '/metrics' }); }`. :362 the swagger `transform` hook explicitly special-cases `if (args.url === '/metrics')` to hide it from the OpenAPI document — independent corroboration that /metrics is a live API route, not a leftover.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/metrics.ts:12-16, 20-38, 40-50 (450 lines total)` — `import client from 'prom-client'`, `const Registry = client.Registry`, `export const register = new Registry()` — an explicit non-global registry. Metrics registered onto it include `job_duration_ms` (Histogram), `kafka_events_reprocessed_total` (Counter) and per-queue gauges built in a loop with `async collect()` bodies that call `queue.getActiveCount()` / `getDelayedCount()` at scrape time. Confirms the claim's second clause.
- `/Users/drew/projects/openpanel/apps/worker/src/index.ts:1, 21, 26, 36-40, 73-83` — Runtime path for the worker's scrape endpoint: `import './utils/observability';` is line 1; `import client from 'prom-client'` :21; `import { register } from './metrics'` :26; inside start(), `collectDefaultMetrics({ register })` :36-37, `WORKER_PORT || '3000'` :39, `const app = express()` :40; `app.get('/metrics', ...)` :73-83 sets `register.contentType` and writes `register.metrics()`. This is a deliberate architectural boundary, not an oversight to be config'd away.
- The claim's "already instruments itself" is true of the code and false of any deployment. Commit d19c5298 landed Aug 24 2026 (five days ago) and says in its own message that "Nothing called init() before ... there were no traces". HYPERDX_API_KEY appears nowhere in .env.example, self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml or self-hosting/coolify.yml, and it gates init() in both services plus useHyperDX and the pino mixin. So a stock self-hosted OpenPanel emits zero traces and ships logs to stdout today. The plan should read this as "the wiring exists, unexercised", not "a working pipeline to redirect".
- The first engineer's evidence line stating that HYPERDX_API_KEY / LOG_EXPORTER / LOG_PREFIX appear in no config is correct as scoped but misleading as framed. HYPERDX_API_KEY and LOG_PREFIX are documented public self-hosting environment variables at apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx:1174-1197. The HYPERDX_API_KEY entry is also stale — it says the key is "for sending logs to HyperDX", written before that key also began gating tracing. LOG_EXPORTER, the newest knob, is documented nowhere. Repointing telemetry is therefore a user-facing docs change, not purely an internal one.

The API side is an inference: apps/api/package.json declares fastify-metrics ^12.1.0 and no prom-client at all, and node_modules is not installed in this checkout (verified: no root, no apps/api, no node_modules/fastify-metrics), so fastify-metrics' registry behaviour could not be read from source. Mark it unverified — it is load-bearing for docs/observability/01-tenancy-and-security.md:1720-1721, which assumes a bare `new client.Counter(...)` in apps/api will be scraped.
- Their gigapipe grep (`scrape_config|scrape_configs|ScrapeConfig`) was too narrow to justify "ZERO files" as stated; a plain `scrape` grep does hit. The conclusion survives and is stronger than they put it: the only scraper artefact in the tree is a commented-out `// go promscrape.RunPrometheusScraper(goCache, TsSvcs, MtrSvcs)` at writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:257, with no promscrape package and no *scrape* directory anywhere. Someone once considered it and it is not there.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Nothing in either service flushes or shuts down the OpenTelemetry SDK. apps/api/src/utils/graceful-shutdown.ts:29-139 closes Fastify, MCP, Prisma, ClickHouse, BullMQ, Kafka and Redis and then calls process.exit(); a repo-wide grep for forceFlush / closeSDK / recordException / .shutdown across apps/api/src, apps/worker/src and packages/logger returns zero hits, and apps/worker/src/utils/graceful-shutdown.ts is a 9-line boolean with no close logic. Whatever the plan repoints traces at, a phase that adds OTLP tracing must add an explicit SDK shutdown step to the drain sequence or lose the last batch on every deploy and every SIGTERM.
- gigapipe itself exposes /metrics via promhttp over prometheus.DefaultGatherer (shared/commonroutes/routes.go:13-18, registered at cmd/gigapipe/main.go:319). Both sides of the proposed system publish Prometheus text and neither pulls it, so P0 needs an explicit decision about who scrapes: today the answer is 'an external Prometheus the plan says it wants to eliminate'. docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:1675 already touches this by ruling out re-exporting gigapipe's /metrics, but the underlying gap — no scraper in the target architecture — is not resolved by that.
- gigapipe's only authentication is HTTP Basic (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:323 applies middleware.BasicAuthMiddleware via app.Use; writer/grpc/server.go:101-103 is the gRPC equivalent). Meanwhile every HyperDX code path in OpenPanel is gated on a non-empty HYPERDX_API_KEY (both observability.ts:16, packages/logger/index.ts:95 and :109). Repointing traces or logs therefore requires setting a dummy API key whose only job is to flip three booleans, and whose value the SDK will place on the wire in a header format gigapipe's Basic middleware does not expect. I could not verify the SDK's header format (dependencies not installed), but the mismatch is a concrete P1 risk, not a config detail.
- packages/logger/index.ts:84-85 names the current destination: "so both signals land under the same service name in ClickStack". ClickStack is HyperDX's own ClickHouse-backed OSS stack. OpenPanel's existing self-telemetry target is already a ClickHouse observability backend, which strengthens the plan's premise but also means the migration is HyperDX-ClickStack-to-gigapipe, not greenfield — worth naming explicitly in the P1 doc.
- Three source comments (packages/logger/index.ts:9, apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts:9, apps/worker/src/utils/observability.ts:9) point readers at `logging-capture-plan.md` for the one-shipping-path-per-signal invariant. That file does not exist in the working tree and has never existed in git history. If the observability plan intends to preserve that invariant — it must, or logs land twice once a second OTLP path is added — it should restate the rule in docs/observability/ rather than inherit a dangling reference.
- The worker's per-queue gauges call BullMQ/Redis at scrape time inside `async collect()` (apps/worker/src/metrics.ts:45-60 and the buffer gauges further down), and apps/worker runs at `replicas: $OP_WORKER_REPLICAS` behind a round-robin Caddy vhost (self-hosting/docker-compose.template.yml:157-158, Caddyfile.template:11-18). docs/observability/10-ops-retention-billing.md:45 already reasons about this for the new stack-health gauges; worth noting the existing gauges have the same shape, so scrape cost and per-replica variance are pre-existing conditions the plan inherits rather than introduces.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan's five load-bearing decisions changes. What changes is the self-instrumentation phase's scope, and in three specific ways. (1) Metrics: keep the first engineer's conclusion, but cite apps/api/src/utils/observability.ts:9-10 ("Metrics stay on prom-client/Grafana") rather than only gigapipe's missing scraper — it is stated author intent, so the plan should say it is deliberately changing that decision. Concretely, self-metrics into gigapipe means one of: replace prom-client with an OTLP metrics exporter in both services, write a scrape-to-remote-write bridge in the worker, or accept that OpenPanel's own metrics stay on an external Prometheus. Pick one and put it in a phase; do not let "repoint" survive in prose. (2) Traces: whichever phase turns on OTLP tracing must also add an SDK flush/shutdown to apps/api/src/utils/graceful-shutdown.ts's drain sequence — today it ends in process.exit() with no flush, so the last span batch is lost on every deploy. This is new work neither prior analysis budgeted. (3) Docs: HYPERDX_API_KEY and LOG_PREFIX are published self-hosting env vars (apps/public/content/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx:1174-1197) and the HYPERDX_API_KEY entry is already stale; LOG_EXPORTER is undocumented. Any change to the telemetry env surface has a user-facing docs deliverable. Separately, note in the plan that tracing landed five days ago (commit d19c5298) and no self-hosting config sets the key, so there is no running trace pipeline to migrate — the P4 correlation work starts from zero traces in production, not from an existing stream. Finally, docs/observability/01-tenancy-and-security.md:1720-1721 assumes a bare `new client.Counter(...)` in apps/api is picked up by fastify-metrics; apps/api declares no prom-client dependency and node_modules is not installed here, so that assumption is unverified and should be checked against fastify-metrics v12 before it is relied on.

## Investigation 46 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived the answer from the runtime path, the test suite, CI and git history rather than re-reading their citations, and every file they cited exists and says what they said it says — I found no fabricated path, symbol or line range. The claim's four assertions are individually true: QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD drive HTTP basic auth (main.go:172-183, gated at 322-326, implemented in reader/utils/middleware/basic_auth.go and pinned by basic_auth_test.go), 3100 is the code default (main.go:301-303) and the published image's ENV, docs/configuration.md documents the env surface, and MODE selects all/reader/writer/init_only (main.go:207-220, 305-311, bootSequence at 353-370, pinned by main_test.go). So "partially_confirmed" is the right verdict. But the first engineer's own correction about config-vs-env precedence is itself wrong: portCHEnv returns early when a config file already supplied DATABASE_DATA (main.go:85-87), so the entire CLICKHOUSE_*/SAMPLES_DAYS/STORAGE_POLICY env block is silently ignored in that case — the config file wins, not env. I also found that the env surface extends beyond every os.Getenv in the repo via cloki-config's own binding (QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE is documented and referenced but read nowhere in the tree), and that module is not on disk, so that mechanism and any default config-file search paths remain unverified.
