**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "Configured entirely by environment variables" is wrong twice over, and the first engineer only caught half of it. A config file is supported (`-config` flag, cmd/gigapipe/main.go:51, consumed at main.go:290-296). More importantly, their statement that env vars "override the config file for everything portEnv touches" is FALSE for the largest block: `portCHEnv` opens with `if len(cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA) > 0 { return nil }` (main.go:85-87), so if a config file defines any database, every one of CLICKHOUSE_SERVER / CLICKHOUSE_PORT / CLICKHOUSE_DB / CLICKHOUSE_AUTH / CLICKHOUSE_PROTO / SELF_SIGNED_CERT / ADVANCED_SAMPLES_ORDERING / SAMPLES_DAYS / STORAGE_POLICY is silently ignored — the config file wins, not env. Precedence is per-block, not uniform.
- The env surface is larger than any `os.Getenv` in this repository, and neither engineer said so. `QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` is documented (docs/configuration.md:53) and named in code comments (writer/controller/otlp_metrics.go:31-32) but appears in NO `os.Getenv` call anywhere in the tree — it must come from `github.com/metrico/cloki-config`'s own generic env binding (a QRYN_<SECTION>_<KEY> scheme). That module is NOT present in the local module cache (`ls $(go env GOMODCACHE)/github.com/metrico` finds nothing), so I could not read it. UNVERIFIED, and it matters two ways: (a) other config-file keys may also be env-settable under that scheme, and (b) whether `clconfig.New(clconfig.CLOKI_READER, nil, "", "")` searches DEFAULT config-file paths when `-config` is absent is unknown. If it does, a stray file on the image could silently supply DATABASE_DATA and neutralize the ClickHouse env vars per the correction above.
- Basic auth is a single global credential pair with no tenancy whatsoever. Confirmed independently: `X-Scope-OrgID` is not read anywhere in the Go tree — the only hit is a comment, ruler/controller/controller.go:3 ("single-tenant — no X-Scope-OrgID is read"). There is no bearer/token scheme. This is a hard confirmation of the plan's decision 2: gigapipe supplies no tenancy primitive of its own.
- Docker default-port nuance: the first engineer's "in Docker PORT is always explicitly present" holds only for the PUBLISHED image. The root Dockerfile does set `ENV PORT 3100` (Dockerfile:13-14) and build_release.yml:210-215 builds ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe from `./Dockerfile`. But scripts/deploy/docker/Dockerfile — the one `make docker` and `make e2e-build` use (Makefile:22,27) — sets no PORT and no EXPOSE, so that image falls through to the code default at main.go:301-303.
- Auth-coverage nuance the first engineer overstated slightly: gorilla/mux applies router middleware to MATCHED routes only. Match builds the chain at match time (mux.go:138-149), so yes, /ready, /config, /metrics and /api/status/buildinfo are behind basic auth. But an unmatched path never gets a chain — ServeHTTP falls back to `http.NotFoundHandler()` at mux.go:209 with no middleware. Harmless (a bare 404), but the blanket "every request is authenticated" phrasing is not exact. Also, /config leaks nothing: it returns the literal string "Not supported" (shared/commonroutes/controller.go:23-26).

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Precedence between config file and env is per-block, not global. The ClickHouse/retention block is config-file-first (main.go:85-87); everything after it in portEnv is env-first. The plan should mandate an env-only deployment with no config file mounted (as test/integration/docker-compose.yml does) so precedence is never ambiguous — and should not repeat the first engineer's "env overrides the config file" as a general rule.
- UNVERIFIED and worth closing before P0: whether `clconfig.New(clconfig.CLOKI_READER, configPaths, "", "")` (main.go:294) searches default config-file paths when configPaths is empty, and what generic env-var scheme cloki-config exposes. The module github.com/metrico/cloki-config v0.0.96 (go.mod:40) is not in the local module cache, so nothing about it is confirmable from disk. The existence of QRYN_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_OTLP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE — documented and referenced in comments but never read by any os.Getenv in the tree — proves such a scheme exists.
- The reader picks its ClickHouse database at RANDOM per query and ignores request context (reader/registry/static.go:33-38). This is a firmer basis for the plan's label-enforcement decision than "the reader binds one database at boot": there is no request-scoped database selection to hook into at all.
- The write path honors caller-supplied X-CH-DSN / X-Ttl-Days / X-Scope-Meta on both HTTP (writer/controller/middleware.go:165-173) and gRPC (writer/grpc/tenant.go:42-58). The gateway must strip these headers from anything a customer sends, and must set them itself. This belongs in the plan's security boundary section alongside op_project_id overwriting.
- A per-series TTL mechanism exists but I could not confirm it is enforced: TimeSeriesRequest carries a TTLDays UInt16Column (writer/model/insert_request.go:116) fed from X-Ttl-Days, and writer/utils/unmarshal/builder.go:326-333 recognizes a special `__ttl_days__` label. I found NO TTL expression referencing a ttl_days column — rotation writes table-wide TTLs only (rotate.go:87,155-200), and `ttl_days` appears in no .sql file under ctrl/qryn/sql/. Before the plan commits to conditional ClickHouse TTL, someone should determine whether this per-series path actually drops data; it may be a cheaper route to per-signal retention, or dead weight.
- boolEnv (main.go:54-62) accepts only lowercase true/1/yes/y and false/0/no/n/"" and the callers panic on anything else — READONLY=TRUE or OMIT_CREATE_TABLES=True crash at boot. The ruler uses a different, more lenient parser that also accepts "on" (ruler/router/init.go:30-36). Confirmed; the self-hosting compose template must use lowercase for the boolEnv-parsed vars.
- Turning auth on turns it on for /metrics too (mux.go:138-149 builds the chain for any matched route). Any Prometheus scrape of gigapipe's own /metrics — including OpenPanel scraping itself — needs the credentials.

**Impact on the plan.** The claim is safe to keep in the plan with one word struck. Replace "configured entirely by environment variables" with "configured by environment variables, with an optional config file via -config; env and file precedence is per-block, so run env-only with no config file mounted." Delete the first engineer's generalization that env overrides the config file — false for the whole ClickHouse/retention block (main.go:85-87). Everything else in their verdict survived my re-check: 3100 default, MODE values, ruler-only-in-mode-all, CLOKI_* winning over QRYN_*, auth-off-by-default, no server-side TLS, one cleartext port for HTTP and OTLP/gRPC. Two additions the plan should absorb: (a) the gateway must STRIP X-CH-DSN / X-Ttl-Days / X-Scope-Meta from customer requests, since basic auth is the only gate on redirecting writes to an arbitrary ClickHouse DSN; (b) the reader's random per-query database selection (static.go:33-38) is the real reason database-per-project is off the table — cite that, not "binds at boot," when justifying label enforcement. Two open items before P0: what cloki-config does with default config paths and its generic env scheme (module absent from disk), and whether the per-series ttl_days column is actually enforced by any TTL expression.

gigapipe is AGPL-3.0 and every factual anchor the first engineer cited checks out: the LICENSE is 661 lines of verbatim FSF AGPL v3, nfpm.yaml:16 says AGPLv3, README.md:255 names HEPVEST BV, and OpenPanel's LICENSE.md is byte-identical (diff reports zero differences; md5 4ae09d45eac4aa08d013b5f2e01c67f6 both ways). Their verdict of partially_confirmed is right and their reading of §0/§5/§6/§13 is accurate. But they are wrong on two points and missed a third. They assert 'no separately-licensed vendored subtree in the repo' -- in fact reader/prof/profile.pb.go and reader/prof/google/v1/profile.pb.go carry Apache-2.0 Google headers and two cityhash102 files carry MIT headers (both AGPL-compatible, so posture unchanged, but the scan was over-confident). ## Investigation 48 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived this from the runtime path (queue payload -> worker job -> integration/email/ws fan-out) and from tests, git history and the Prisma schema, and I reach the same verdict as the first engineer. The union half is exactly right: `zNotificationRuleConfig` is a `z.discriminatedUnion('type', [...])` at packages/validation/src/index.ts:526-529, surfaced onto the `Json` column via `PrismaJson.IPrismaNotificationRuleConfig` (packages/db/src/types.ts:21), so adding a `metric` member is a pure type/validation change with no migration. The delivery half is right in its core: apps/worker/src/jobs/notification.ts never reads `rule.config.type` — it consumes only title/message/projectId/sendToApp/sendToEmail/integrationId/payload. Their two blocking caveats both check out verbatim: the payload gate at notification.ts:77-81, and the `NotificationRule['config']['events'][number]` union index at rule-card.tsx:21. But their claim that there is "no pending/firing/resolved... anywhere" is over-broad and wrong as stated: packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:674-739 defines `InsightState { active suppressed closed }` on `ProjectInsight` plus an append-only `InsightEvent` log with `eventKind "created" | "updated" | "severity_up" | "direction_flip" | "closed"`, and packages/db/src/services/insights/store.ts:85-200 implements the reopen/version/threadId state machine over it. That precedent exists in this repo, it is periodic rather than event-driven, and it deliberately bypasses NotificationRule entirely.

**Evidence**

- `packages/validation/src/index.ts:508-538` — Confirmed verbatim. `zNotificationRuleEventConfig` (508, `type: z.literal('events')`, `events: z.array(zChartEvent)`), `zNotificationRuleFunnelConfig` (517, `events: z.array(zChartEvent).min(1)`), `export const zNotificationRuleConfig = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [zNotificationRuleEventConfig, zNotificationRuleFunnelConfig]);` (526-529), type alias at 531, embedded as `config: zNotificationRuleConfig` in `zCreateNotificationRule` at 537. Both members share an `events` array.
- `packages/db/src/types.ts:21,23` — `type IPrismaNotificationRuleConfig = INotificationRuleConfig;` and `type IPrismaNotificationPayload = INotificationPayload;` inside `declare global { namespace PrismaJson }`. The zod union and the hand-written payload union ARE the typed shapes of the two Json columns — confirmed.
- `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:581-616` — `model NotificationRule` (581) and `model Notification` (599) confirmed field-for-field. Neither carries state, severity, cooldown, dedupe key or last-evaluated column. NEW: line 613 is `notificationRule NotificationRule? @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)` — deleting a rule cascade-deletes its entire Notification history, so alert history for a metric rule is destroyed on rule delete.
- `apps/worker/src/jobs/notification.ts:24-142` — Read the whole file. `rule.config.type` never appears. Order is: sendToApp -> `publishEvent('notification','created',notification); return;` (29-32); sendToEmail -> fan out to every non-deleted org member via `sendEmail('notification-rule', {title,message,projectName,dashboardUrl})`, `return` (34-65); `if (!notification.integrationId) throw` (67-69); `const payload = notification.payload; if (!isValidJson(payload)) { return new Error('Invalid payload'); }` (77-81); then `switch (integration.config.type)` over webhook/discord/slack (83-139), each building from `notification.title`/`notification.message`. The first engineer's reading is correct, including that line 80 RETURNS an Error rather than throwing, so BullMQ marks the job complete.
- `apps/worker/src/jobs/notification.ts:87-100` — Confirmed including the source comment `// We only transform event payloads for now (not funnel)` and the guard `integration.config.javascriptTemplate && payload.type === 'event'`. A `metric` payload falls to `body = payload` and is POSTed raw. Confirms the first engineer's citation exactly.
- `packages/db/src/services/notification.service.ts:29-37` — `export type INotificationPayload = { type: 'event'; event: IServiceCreateEventPayload } | { type: 'funnel'; funnel: IServiceEvent[] }` — confirmed. Note it is not merely 'needed for context': `ICreateNotification` (19-27) is `Pick<Notification, ...|'payload'|...>`, so this union is a hard TYPE constraint on `createNotification`; a metric payload does not compile until this union is extended.
- `packages/db/src/services/notification.service.ts:139-168` — `createNotification` builds `Prisma.NotificationUncheckedCreateInput` with `payload: stripNullChars(notification.payload) || undefined` (144), spreads `getIntegration(...)` (145), and at 149-154 `// Only create notifications for app` / `if (data.sendToApp) { await db.notification.create({ data }) }`. Then `triggerNotification(data)` enqueues `notificationQueue.add('sendNotification', { type, payload: { notification } })` (162-167). **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The first engineer's alert-state claim is over-broad and I disagree with it as written. They say 'there is no pending/firing/resolved, no for-duration, no cooldown and no last-fired marker anywhere'. That is true of NotificationRule/Notification, but false of the repository: packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:674-739 defines `InsightState { active suppressed closed }`, `firstDetectedAt`/`lastUpdatedAt`/`lastSeenAt`, `version`, `threadId`, `severityBand`, and an `InsightEvent` log with `eventKind` values 'created'|'updated'|'severity_up'|'direction_flip'|'closed'; packages/db/src/services/insights/store.ts:85-200 implements the reopen-and-version state machine over it. Their chosen precedent (cron.data-health.ts one-shot timestamps) is the weaker of the two that exist.
- Factual correction on worker concurrency: they wrote `workerOptions = { connection: getRedisQueue() }` (no concurrency/limiter). apps/worker/src/boot-workers.ts:230-236 passes `concurrency: getConcurrencyFor('notification')` to the notification Worker, defaulting to 1 and overridable via `NOTIFICATION_CONCURRENCY` (boot-workers.ts:88-102). The retry point (no `attempts`/`backoff`) is still correct.
- Line-number drift in packages/trpc/src/routers/notification.ts: `createOrUpdateRule` is 77-139 and `deleteRule` is 140-160, not the cited 74-158 / 132-158. The substance (only `.clear` at line 81; `deleteRule` never clears) is confirmed.
- The claim as stated is also incomplete on scope, in a way the first engineer only half-flagged: the payload union at notification.service.ts:29-37 is not merely 'needed to carry context' — `ICreateNotification` is `Pick<Notification, ...|'payload'|...>` (lines 19-27), so a metric payload is a compile error at `createNotification` until that union is extended. Two unions must change before any metric rule can even be constructed.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Alert history is destroyed on rule delete. packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:613 sets `notificationRule NotificationRule? @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)`. Combined with rows only being written when `sendToApp` (notification.service.ts:150-154), the plan's alert history is both partial and non-durable. If the plan wants a queryable incident record it should not live on the `Notification` table.
- The rule cache is staler than the 24 minutes the first engineer computed. packages/redis/cachable.ts:155-156 layers a 60s in-process LRU over Redis with the explicit comment that `clear()` invalidates Redis but 'other nodes may serve stale from LRU for up to this long'. So even a correctly-cleared rule edit takes up to 60s to reach every worker process, and an uncleared delete takes up to 24 minutes. For an on-call alert rule, 'I disabled it and it kept paging' is a real failure mode.
- There is no behavioral test coverage to regress against. The only test touching the path mocks `checkNotificationRulesForEvent` (apps/worker/src/jobs/events.incoming-events.test.ts:21); nothing exercises `notificationJob`, the payload gate, or the integration switch. Contrast with cron.wind-down.test.ts / cron.onboarding.test.ts, which do assert on `sendEmail` calls — that is the testing pattern a metric evaluator should follow.
- Both ingest paths converge on one function, which helps the plan. `createEventAndNotify` (events.incoming-event.ts:57-81) is the sole caller of `checkNotificationRulesForEvent`, and the Kafka consumer re-enters through the same `incomingEvent` (events.kafka-consumer.ts:171). A metric evaluator does not need to worry about a second ingest branch bypassing it.
- The in-app delivery path publishes the Prisma create INPUT, not the persisted row. notification.service.ts:156 passes `data` to `triggerNotification`, and notification.ts:30 publishes that same object over `publishEvent('notification','created', ...)`. apps/start/src/components/notifications/notification-provider.tsx:18 types it `useWS<Notification>` — a lie, since there is no `id` or `createdAt`. Harmless today (the toast reads only title/message) but it blocks 'click the alert toast to open the incident'.
- OpenPanel already runs two parallel notification systems, and the plan should pick one deliberately. NotificationRule -> Notification -> integrations is event-driven, stateless, per-hit. ProjectInsight -> InsightEvent -> weekly digest is periodic, stateful, deduped by (projectId, moduleKey, dimensionKey, windowKind, state), and never touches NotificationRule. A metric alert is structurally the second shape (periodic evaluation, firing/resolved, one page per incident not per sample) but needs the first shape's delivery channels. The honest framing is: reuse the delivery half, model the state half on insights.
- No precedent commit exists for adding a rule type. `git log -S"zNotificationRuleFunnelConfig"` returns only f65a6334, the original notifications feature — both union members shipped together. Every consumer written since has assumed a shared `events` array (rule-card.tsx:21, add-notification-rule.tsx:87-96), which is exactly what a `metric` member breaks.
- Unverified, flagged as such: I did not find any per-rule recipient list, per-rule mute/snooze, or notification-level rate limit anywhere in the notification path. Absence of a grep hit is weaker than a positive citation, so treat 'these do not exist' as probable rather than proven.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's position that P5 can reuse NotificationRule -> Notification -> delivery survives, but with four concrete work items that must be written into the phase rather than assumed away. (1) Two unions must be extended, not one: `zNotificationRuleConfig` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:526) and `INotificationPayload` (packages/db/src/services/notification.service.ts:29) — the latter is a compile-time gate on `createNotification`, and a metric alert MUST emit a non-null payload or it silently never reaches webhook/Discord/Slack (notification.ts:79-81) while still reporting job success. (2) The dashboard is not free: rule-card.tsx:21's `NotificationRule['config']['events'][number]` is a hard type error the moment a member lacks `events`, and add-notification-rule.tsx is structurally bound to `config.events` — budget a UI branch, not a cosmetic tweak. (3) The plan's assumption that alert state must be built from scratch should be revised: packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:674-739 and packages/db/src/services/insights/store.ts:85-200 already implement active/suppressed/closed with reopen, versioning, a stable `threadId`, and an append-only event log keyed by a composite unique. A metric alert should model firing/resolved on that (a `MetricAlertState` sibling of `ProjectInsight`) and use NotificationRule only as the delivery fan-out on transition — which also fixes the cascade-delete and in-app-only history problems, since alert history then lives on its own table rather than on `Notification`. (4) Operationally, the plan must state a rule-cache invalidation contract: `deleteRule` clears nothing and `cacheable`'s 60s L1 LRU survives `.clear()` across processes, so a disabled or deleted metric rule can keep firing for up to 24 minutes. Also fix the plan's inputs where the first engineer was imprecise: the notification worker does take concurrency (`NOTIFICATION_CONCURRENCY`, default 1) — the real gap is `attempts`/`backoff`, not concurrency.

## Investigation 49 — `partially_confirmed`

I reached the same conclusion by a different route and agree with the first engineer: the reader's operative behavior is exactly as claimed — database-per-project is impossible on gigapipe's read path — while the claim's wording ("a single ClickHouse database") is imprecise, since the reader binds at boot to a *pool* of connections and picks one at random per call, ignoring the ctx argument. My independent additions strengthen the conclusion beyond what they showed: the reader's service and controller objects are themselves constructed once at route-registration time (reader/router/*.go), so there is no per-request construction site at all, not merely a global registry; reader/config holds a single package-global `Cloki` config, so one process cannot even host two readers; and a repo-wide search shows `X-Scope-OrgID` — the header any Loki-compatible client would expect to carry a tenant — appears exactly once in the whole tree, in a ruler comment stating it is *not* read. The sharpest new finding is that configuring per-project databases is not merely unsupported but actively unsafe: the writer *can* be steered per-request to one of N boot-configured nodes by name, so N per-project DATABASE_DATA entries would write correctly while the reader served a uniformly random project's database on every one of the ~5 GetDB calls inside a single query. One correction to their evidence: their git attribution of the missing `return` to commit 634c551 is wrong; blame and `-S` both attribute it to 7580d08.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/static.go:33-38` — Verified verbatim. `func (s *staticDBRegistry) GetDB(ctx context.Context) (*model.DataDatabasesMap, error) { s.mtx.Lock(); defer s.mtx.Unlock(); idx := s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases)); return s.databases[idx], nil }`. `ctx` is accepted and never dereferenced. This is the decisive line and the first engineer quoted it correctly.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/registry.go:20-26, 53, 63` — Verified. `Init()` runs `p := plugins.GetDatabaseRegistryPlugin(); if p != nil { Registry = (*p)() }` and then, with no `return`, `Registry = InitStaticRegistry()` — the plugin registry is unconditionally discarded. `createDataDBSessions` iterates `config.Cloki.Setting.DATABASE_DATA` and fixes `Auth: clickhouse.Auth{Database: dbObject.Name, ...}` per connection at process start.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/router/query_range.go:11-19 (and prof.go:11, select_labels.go:10, tempo.go:10, prometheus_query_range.go:46, prometheus_labels.go:10, route_plugin.go:10)` — NEW — stronger than the first engineer's finding. `RouteQueryRangeApis(app *mux.Router, dataSession model.IDBRegistry)` builds `qrService := &service.QueryRangeService{ServiceData: model.ServiceData{Session: dataSession}}` and `qrCtrl := &controllerv1.QueryRangeController{...}` ONCE, at boot, then registers `qrCtrl.QueryRange` as the handler. Every reader route group does the same. So it is not just that the registry is a global — the service and controller objects that hold it are singletons created before the first request. **Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The claim's phrase "bound to a single ClickHouse database chosen at boot" is imprecise in the same way the first engineer identified, and I confirm their precision independently: the reader binds at boot to a fixed *pool* built from every entry in `config.Cloki.Setting.DATABASE_DATA` (reader/registry/registry.go:53), and `staticDBRegistry.GetDB` returns `s.databases[s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases))]` (reader/registry/static.go:33-38). Multiple entries are a replica pool, not tenants. In the env/Docker path exactly one entry ever exists (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:84-99).
- The claim points at the registry, but the constraint is bound tighter than that and the plan should know it: the reader's *services and controllers* are singletons built at route-registration time with the registry already embedded (reader/router/query_range.go:11-19 and the six sibling route files), and reader/config is a single package-global `Cloki`. So even a fork that made `GetDB` ctx-aware would still have one config and one route table per process. Database-per-project on the read path means one gigapipe reader process per project, not a per-request switch.
- "Offers no per-request tenant/DSN selection" is true in effect, but I confirm the first engineer's caveat that two dormant extension points exist — `plugins.RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin` (reader/plugins/plugins.go:53-62) and `RegisterPreRequestPlugin` (plugins.go:32, consumed at reader/controller/utils.go:143-156). I verified both are dead in this tree: `git log -S "DatabaseRegistryPlugin"` returns one commit and there is no registrant anywhere, and `Init()` discards any plugin registry for want of a `return`. I add that `writer/plugin/qryn_writer.go:65` carries a TODO to "add plugin support to support dynamic database registries" and `SYSTEM_SETTINGS.DynamicDatabases` (qryn_writer.go:106) only sizes a pool — i.e. dynamic databases are explicitly not built in OSS. Nothing here should be treated as a supported path.
- One factual correction to the first engineer's own evidence: they attribute the missing-`return` line to commit 634c551 ("refactor: replace dbRegistry with registry in routing logic"). `git blame -L 18,28 reader/registry/registry.go` attributes lines 18-26 to 7580d08 ("qryn -> gigapipe (#622)", 2025-04-07), and `git log -S "Registry = InitStaticRegistry()"` returns only 7580d08. 634c551 exists and is dated 2025-07-15 but did not introduce or alter that line. The historical conclusion is unaffected.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The reader/writer asymmetry is not just "the writer can't do it either" — it is an active hazard the plan should document as the reason database-per-project is rejected, not merely a limitation. The writer builds one insert service per DATABASE_DATA node (writer/plugin/qryn_writer_db.go:44-60, 117-121, 224) and `staticServiceRegistryGetService` will return the service whose `GetNodeName()` matches X-CH-DSN (writer/service/registry/static.go:55-68). So N per-project entries in DATABASE_DATA would make WRITES land in the right per-project database — while the reader, given the same config, returns a uniformly random one of the N on every GetDB call. Since GetDB is called roughly five times inside one query_range (reader/service/query_range.go:225,302,533,675,808) and eleven times across the profiling path (reader/service/prof.go), a single query would mix databases nondeterministically. A half-working config that silently cross-reads other projects is worse than no isolation, and is the strongest available argument for the plan's label-enforcement decision.
- `X-Scope-OrgID` — the header an operator would most plausibly reach for, since gigapipe advertises Loki drop-in compatibility — is not read anywhere. Its only appearance in the entire repository is `ruler/controller/controller.go:3` saying so explicitly. Worth stating in the plan doc, because "gigapipe is Loki-compatible, so Loki multi-tenancy must work" is exactly the assumption a reviewer will bring.
- `docs/otlp-grpc.md:36-59` heads its table "Multitenancy and per-request options" and lists `x-ch-dsn` as "Selects the tenant (ClickHouse DSN)". This doc covers the OTLP ingest path only, and the label is doubly misleading: it is not a DSN (it is a node name, writer/service/generic_insert.go:130-132) and there is no corresponding query-path mechanism. If the plan cites gigapipe's own docs for multitenancy, it should note that this sentence describes ingest-side node selection, not tenancy.
- Reader table-name resolution has a third global override the plan should not mistake for a routing hook: `GetTableName` consults `plugins.GetTableNamesPlugin()` (reader/utils/tables/tables.go:60-70), which is process-wide, not per-request. In non-cluster mode names stay unqualified and resolve against the connection's default database; in cluster mode they are qualified with `db.Config.Name` taken from boot config (tables.go:99-114). Both paths reconfirm that the database is a property of the boot-time connection.
- Unverified side observation, flagged rather than asserted: `CLokiQueriable.SetOidAndDB` (reader/service/prom_queryable.go:102-109) copies ServiceData/random/Ctx/Expr but drops the `Stats *StatsStore` field, while `RoutePrometheusQueryRange` is passed `config.Cloki.Setting.SYSTEM_SETTINGS.QueryStats` (reader/reader.go:109). I did not trace whether Stats is read after this copy, so I make no claim that query stats are broken — noting it only because the plan's metrics phase may want PromQL query statistics.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan needs to change; decision #2's core choice is correct and now better supported. Two edits to the plan's wording are warranted. First, the parenthetical "only its writer accepts a per-request DSN" should be restated as "only its writer accepts a per-request node selector (X-CH-DSN / x-ch-dsn), matched against the names of boot-configured ClickHouse nodes, with a silent random fallback when nothing matches" — it is not an arbitrary connection string. Second, the justification for rejecting database-per-project should be upgraded from "impossible on the read path" to "impossible on the read path AND unsafe to half-attempt": because the writer can route per-node while the reader picks at random per call, a per-project DATABASE_DATA config would write correctly and read from a random project's database several times within one query. The plan should also record that the only in-tree route to per-project databases is one gigapipe reader process per project (reader/config holds a single package-global config and routes are registered once), which does not scale and is presumably why label enforcement was chosen. Finally, the dormant `RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin` hook should be named in the doc as explicitly out of scope — it requires forking gigapipe's Go source, is discarded by `Init()` even if registered, and the neighbouring writer TODO confirms dynamic database registries are unimplemented upstream.

## Investigation 50 — `partially_confirmed`

I re-derived the answer from the runtime path (queue payload → worker → integration senders → email template) rather than from the type definitions, and I reach the same verdict as the first engineer, with four corrections to their evidence. The union half is exactly right: `zNotificationRuleConfig` is a `z.discriminatedUnion('type', [...])` at packages/validation/src/index.ts:526-529, and the Prisma `Json` column is typed by it via `PrismaJson.IPrismaNotificationRuleConfig`. The delivery half is right in its core assertion — nothing in apps/worker/src/jobs/notification.ts reads `rule.config.type`; it consumes only `sendToApp`, `sendToEmail`, `integrationId`, `title`, `message`, `payload` — but "without changes to delivery" is too strong for the same two reasons the first engineer gave (the `isValidJson(payload)` gate at notification.ts:79-81, and the second hand-written `INotificationPayload` union at notification.service.ts:29-37 that the Prisma create input is typed against). Where I disagree with them: (a) the notification worker DOES get a configurable concurrency (boot-workers.ts:231-235), contradicting their "no concurrency/limiter"; (b) the typed-JSON mechanism is a bespoke regex post-processor, not `prisma-json-types-generator`, whose generator block is commented out at schema.prisma:12-14; (c) a metric payload is only posted raw in webhook `javascript` mode — in the default mode the body is `{title, message}`, so payload data never reaches a default webhook at all; (d) minor line drift on `deleteRule`.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The first engineer's characterization of the notification worker as having 'no concurrency/limiter' is WRONG. apps/worker/src/boot-workers.ts:231-235 constructs it as `new Worker(notificationQueue.name, notificationJob, { ...workerOptions, concurrency })` with `concurrency = getConcurrencyFor('notification')`, which defaults to 1 and is tunable via a `NOTIFICATION_CONCURRENCY` env var (boot-workers.ts:94-106). The plan should treat alert delivery as serialized at 1 job per replica by default — that is a throughput constraint, not an absence of one.
- The typed-Json mechanism is NOT `prisma-json-types-generator`. That generator block is commented out at packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:12-14. The mapping is applied by a bespoke regex post-processor, packages/db/prisma/prisma-json-types.ts, run as the second half of `"codegen": "prisma generate && jiti prisma/prisma-json-types.ts"`. The first engineer's conclusion survives (a new union member is still a pure type change, no migration, no regen, because the generated files reference `PrismaJson.IPrismaNotificationRuleConfig` by name), but the plan should know the mechanism is hand-rolled — and that Patterns 4 and 5 of that script (lines 148-167) are not scoped to the field name, so they can mistype other Json fields in client.ts/models.ts if new typed Json columns are added.
- The first engineer wrote that a metric payload 'falls to the else and is posted raw' on webhooks. That is true only inside webhook `mode === 'javascript'` (notification.ts:89-100). In the DEFAULT webhook mode the body is `{ title, message }` (notification.ts:99-104), so a metric payload's structured data never reaches a default webhook at all — its only job there is to pass the `isValidJson` gate at 79-81. Anything richer than a sentence on webhook/Discord/Slack requires touching delivery code, which strengthens rather than weakens their overall correction.
- Minor line drift in their citations: `deleteRule` is at packages/trpc/src/routers/notification.ts:140-160, not 132-158; `notificationQueue`'s options are at queues.ts:281-289 (defaultJobOptions at 284-286), and the notification job file runs to line 139. Substance of each is confirmed.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- NEW: `createNotification` and `triggerNotification` have ZERO callers outside packages/db/src/services/notification.service.ts (verified by repo-wide grep). In particular the existing periodic alerting feature — the usage & data-health alerts from commit d0d9895b — bypasses the entire NotificationRule/Notification path and calls `sendEmail` directly from apps/worker/src/jobs/cron.data-health.ts, deduping on `Project.noDataNotifiedAt` / `Project.dataStoppedNotifiedAt`. So there is no existing cron→NotificationRule bridge in the repo to copy, and the one time-driven alert that does exist chose not to use this machinery. A metric evaluator would be the first periodic producer of `Notification` rows.
- NEW: `createOrUpdateRule` clears the rule cache at packages/trpc/src/routers/notification.ts:81, BEFORE the `update` (96) or `create` (120) executes. Any event evaluated in that window repopulates the Redis cache with the pre-edit rule set, which then persists for the full 24-minute TTL. Combined with the already-noted missing `.clear` in `deleteRule`, rule edits are not reliably live for up to ~24 minutes — acceptable for 'a signup happened', a real problem for 'CPU above 90%'.
- NEW: the rule config is never validated at read time. `getNotificationRulesByProjectId` (notification.service.ts:71-95) selects `config` straight from the Json column with no `zNotificationRuleConfig.parse`. The discriminated union is enforced only at the single tRPC write boundary (`zCreateNotificationRule`, the union's only consumer). A metric rule config written by any other path — a seed script, an MCP tool, a direct DB edit — is trusted unconditionally by the evaluator.
- NEW: there is no test coverage of the notification path. The only two test files that reference it (apps/worker/src/jobs/events.incoming-events.test.ts:21, events.create-session-end.test.ts:33) mock `checkNotificationRulesForEvent` and `getHasFunnelRules` away. Neither rule matching, nor `createNotification`, nor `notificationJob` delivery is exercised, so adding a third rule type carries no regression safety net.
- NEW: `Notification.integration` is declared `onDelete: Cascade` (packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:610-611). Deleting an integration deletes its notification history rows. Combined with the confirmed 'rows only persist when sendToApp' behavior, alert history for metric rules is doubly fragile.
- NEW: `notification.list` (packages/trpc/src/routers/notification.ts:18-42) is an unbounded `findMany` with `take: 5000` and no pagination or cursor. Metric alerts, which fire far more often than product events per rule, would push this to the cap quickly if in-app is enabled. Access control is fine — `protectedProcedure` includes `enforceAccess` (packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:176-180).
- CONFIRMED and worth restating: no alert state exists anywhere. Neither `NotificationRule` nor `Notification` has a state, severity, for-duration, cooldown, resolvedAt, or lastEvaluatedAt column (schema.prisma:581-618), and the closest precedent (cron.data-health.ts) is one-shot timestamps on the Project entity, not a pending/firing/resolved machine and not per-series. P5 must introduce that state; it cannot be inherited.

**Impact on the plan.** The plan's P5 position — "reuse the existing NotificationRule → Notification → integration delivery path" — is directionally sound and should stay, but the plan must budget four concrete pieces of work it currently implies are free. (1) Extend TWO unions, not one: `zNotificationRuleConfig` in packages/validation and the hand-written `INotificationPayload` in packages/db/src/services/notification.service.ts:29-37; a metric alert MUST emit a non-null payload or it silently no-ops for webhook/Discord/Slack while still completing its BullMQ job. (2) Budget UI work as mandatory, not optional: rule-card.tsx:21's `NotificationRule['config']['events'][number]` is a hard compile error the moment a member lacks an `events` array, and add-notification-rule.tsx is structurally bound to `config.events` (useFieldArray, submit guard, hardcoded two-option type picker). Either give the metric member a compatible shape or refactor those three call sites. (3) Accept that delivery CONTENT is a change even though delivery PLUMBING is not: default-mode webhooks, Discord and Slack all send only title+message, and the notification-rule email template carries only title/message/projectName/dashboardUrl — a metric alert with a value, threshold, series and deep link requires touching the template and the webhook body builder. (4) Own the operational gaps the path does not provide: no retries (`removeOnComplete: 10` only, 1 attempt), delivery concurrency of 1 per replica by default, rule-cache staleness up to 24 minutes on edit and delete, evaluation errors swallowed at the call site, notification rows persisted only when in-app is enabled, and all-org-members email recipients suppressible by a `product_alerts` unsubscribe. Also: there is no existing periodic→NotificationRule bridge to imitate — the repo's only cron alert deliberately bypasses this path — so P5 is building that bridge plus the alert state machine (pending/firing/resolved, for-duration, dedupe) from scratch, most likely as new columns in the style of `Project.noDataNotifiedAt` but keyed per rule and per series.

## Investigation 51 — `partially_confirmed`

The claim is right in its conclusion and slightly imprecise in its wording. gigapipe's reader builds one process-global `IDBRegistry` at boot (`registry.Init()` -> `InitStaticRegistry()`, reader/registry/registry.go:20-47) from the `DATABASE_DATA` config list, opening each ClickHouse connection with its database fixed in `clickhouse.Options.Auth.Database` (registry.go:63), and hands that single global to every route group (reader/reader.go:100-111). The only implementation, `staticDBRegistry.GetDB(ctx)`, accepts a context and never reads it — it returns `s.databases[s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases))]` (reader/registry/static.go:33-38) — so there is genuinely no per-request tenant or DSN selection on the read path, and the reader's middleware chain (Logging/Cors/AcceptEncoding/BasicAuth) contains nothing tenant-aware. Two precisions: the reader binds to a *pool* of connections chosen at random, not literally one database (though the env/Docker path only ever creates one, cmd/gigapipe/main.go:85-96); and a dormant `DatabaseRegistryPlugin` hook exists whose result `Init()` unconditionally discards for want of a `return`, with no registrant anywhere in the tree. Separately, the plan's parenthetical about the writer overstates it: `X-CH-DSN` is matched against preconfigured node NAMES and silently falls back to a random node, not dialed as a connection string.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/registry.go:20-26` — `func Init()` — the only entry point. `p := plugins.GetDatabaseRegistryPlugin(); if p != nil { Registry = (*p)() }` then, with no return, `Registry = InitStaticRegistry()`. The plugin-supplied registry is always discarded; the static one always wins.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/registry.go:36-47` — `InitStaticRegistry()` builds `dbMap[node.Config.Node]` from `createDataDBSessions()` and panics if empty: "We don't have any active DB session configured". Boot-time only; no request context reaches it.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/registry.go:53-70` — `createDataDBSessions` iterates `config.Cloki.Setting.DATABASE_DATA` and opens each connection with `clickhouse.Options{Auth: clickhouse.Auth{Database: dbObject.Name, ...}}`. The database is fixed in the connection's auth block at process start.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/static.go:33-38` — `func (s *staticDBRegistry) GetDB(ctx context.Context) (*model.DataDatabasesMap, error) { ...; idx := s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases)); return s.databases[idx], nil }` — `ctx` is accepted and never read. This is the decisive line: no per-request selection is possible.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/registry/static.go:20` — `var _ model.IDBRegistry = &staticDBRegistry{}` — a repo-wide grep for `IDBRegistry` finds exactly one implementation in non-test code; there is no dynamic/tenant registry variant.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/reader.go:100-111` — `performV1APIRouting` calls `registry.Init()` once, then passes the process-global `registry.Registry` to every route group (RouteQueryRangeApis, RouteSelectLabels, RoutePrometheusQueryRange, RouteTempo, RouteProf, PluggableRoutes). Every read surface shares one boot-time registry.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/reader.go:66-83` — `applyMiddlewares` — the reader's entire middleware chain is Logging, Cors, AcceptEncoding, BasicAuth. No tenant/DSN/org middleware. `ls reader/utils/middleware` shows only accept_encoding, basic_auth, cors, logging.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/utils/tables/tables.go:72-118` — `PopulateTableNames` leaves table names unqualified (`samples_v3`, `time_series`, …) unless `db.Config.ClusterName != ""`, in which case it prefixes ``fmt.Sprintf("`%s`.%s%s", db.Config.Name, ...)``. So in the normal single-node case queries resolve against the connection's default database — reinforcing that the DB is a property of the boot-time connection.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/model/db_egistry.go:7-12` — `type IDBRegistry interface { GetDB(ctx context.Context) (*DataDatabasesMap, error); Run(); Stop(); Ping() }` — the interface is ctx-aware, so a per-request registry is expressible; nothing in-tree implements one.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/plugins/plugins.go:53-62` — `type DatabaseRegistryPlugin func() model.IDBRegistry` with `RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin` / `GetDatabaseRegistryPlugin`. A repo-wide grep for `RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin` returns only this definition — no caller anywhere, tests included.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:85-96` — `portCHEnv`: `if len(cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA) > 0 { return nil }`, else one entry is created and `cfg.Setting.DATABASE_DATA[0].Name = db` where `db` is `CLICKHOUSE_DB` (default `"cloki"`). The container-config path produces exactly one database, process-wide.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/controller/middleware.go:165,204` — `dsn := strings.Clone(r.Header.Get("X-CH-DSN"))` … `ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, utils.ContextKeyDSN, dsn)`. Grepping `X-CH-DSN|x-ch-dsn|ContextKeyDSN` across the repo returns hits ONLY under writer/ (middleware, grpc/tenant.go, tests) — zero under reader/. The write/read asymmetry is real.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/service/registry/static.go:55-68` — `staticServiceRegistryGetService`: `if id != "" { for _, svc := range svcs { if svc.GetNodeName() == id { return svc, nil } } }` then unconditionally `idx := r.rand.Intn(len(svcs)); return svcs[idx], nil`. The writer's 'DSN' is a preconfigured node-name lookup with a silent random fallback, not an arbitrary connection string.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/writer/service/generic_insert.go:130-132` — `func (svc *InsertServiceV2) GetNodeName() string { return svc.DatabaseNode.Node }` — confirms the id matched against `X-CH-DSN` is the config `Node` name, not a URL.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/service/prom_queryable.go:88-107` — `CLokiQueriable.Querier` calls `c.ServiceData.Session.GetDB(c.Ctx)` per query; the neighbouring `SetOidAndDB(ctx, expr)` only copies ServiceData/random/Ctx/Expr — the 'Oid' (org id) in its name is vestigial and sets nothing. The PromQL read path has no tenant concept.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/router/init.go:74-90` — The ruler evaluates rules through `session := readerregistry.Registry` — the same boot-time global. Corroborated by docs/configuration.md:85-86: the ruler "is single-tenant and recording-only (alerting rules may be stored but are never evaluated)."
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/docs/otlp-grpc.md:36-59` — "Multitenancy and per-request options" documents `x-ch-dsn` / `X-CH-DSN` as "Selects the tenant (ClickHouse DSN)" — and this doc covers the OTLP **ingest** path only. There is no equivalent doc or header for the query path.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (HEAD d4b91b1a, 2026-08-29)` — Verified against the checked-out commit. `git log -S "Registry = InitStaticRegistry()"` shows the line introduced by 634c551 "refactor: replace dbRegistry with registry in routing logic" and unchanged since; no branch in history adds per-request selection.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- "Bound to a single ClickHouse database" is imprecise: the reader binds at boot to a *list* of connections (`config.Cloki.Setting.DATABASE_DATA`, iterated at reader/registry/registry.go:53), each with its own `Name`. `staticDBRegistry.GetDB` then picks one with `s.rand.Intn(len(s.databases))` (reader/registry/static.go:33-38). The precise statement is: the reader binds at boot to a fixed pool of ClickHouse connections and selects among them **at random per call, ignoring the `ctx` argument entirely**. Multiple entries are a replica/load-balancing pool, not tenants — GetDB is called many times within a single request (e.g. reader/service/query_range.go:225,302,533,675,808), so pointing entries at different databases would produce nondeterministic results within one query. In the env-var/Docker path only one entry ever exists: cmd/gigapipe/main.go:85-96 returns early if DATABASE_DATA is non-empty, otherwise creates exactly one entry with `Name` = `CLICKHOUSE_DB` (default `cloki`).
- "Offers no per-request tenant/DSN selection" is true in effect but there IS a dormant extension point the claim doesn't mention: `plugins.RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin` / `GetDatabaseRegistryPlugin` (reader/plugins/plugins.go:53-62) lets an out-of-tree build supply its own `IDBRegistry`, and the interface signature `GetDB(ctx context.Context)` (reader/model/db_egistry.go:8) is ctx-aware by design — combined with `RegisterPreRequestPlugin` (reader/plugins/plugins.go:32, consumed at reader/controller/utils.go:145) a fork could stuff a tenant into ctx and select a DB per request. In THIS tree it is dead twice over: nothing calls `RegisterDatabaseRegistryPlugin`, and `registry.Init()` unconditionally overwrites the plugin's registry with the static one — `if p != nil { Registry = (*p)() }` is immediately followed by `Registry = InitStaticRegistry()` with no `return` (reader/registry/registry.go:20-26). Exploiting it would require forking gigapipe's Go source, which is out of scope for running a stock image.
- The parenthetical in plan decision #2 — "only its writer accepts a per-request DSN" — is itself imprecise and overstates the writer. In the OSS tree the writer's `X-CH-DSN` header (writer/controller/middleware.go:165) / `x-ch-dsn` gRPC metadata (writer/grpc/tenant.go:42) is not a DSN that gets dialed; it is matched against the **node names** of preconfigured services: `staticServiceRegistryGetService` compares `id` to `svc.GetNodeName()` (writer/service/registry/static.go:55-68), which returns `svc.DatabaseNode.Node` from config (writer/service/generic_insert.go:130-132). A value that matches nothing does **not** error — it falls through to `svcs[r.rand.Intn(len(svcs))]`. So the writer also cannot be pointed at an arbitrary per-project database without a plugin (writer/plugins/plugins.go registers a `DatabaseSession` hook but no dynamic service-registry hook).

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- `staticDBRegistry.GetDB` is called MULTIPLE times per request (reader/service/query_range.go:225, 302, 533, 675, 808; reader/service/query_abels.go:43, 108, 189, 274; reader/service/tempo.go:145-347; reader/service/prof.go ×12), each time re-rolling `rand.Intn`. Even a hypothetical patch that made the pool per-tenant would break unless GetDB became sticky within a request. This is independent evidence that the multi-entry pool means 'interchangeable replicas', not 'different data'.
- The reader's `DataDatabasesMap.DSN` field is populated at boot (reader/registry/registry.go:82-101, building a `n-`/`c-` prefixed clickhouse:// or http(s):// string) but a grep for `.DSN` under reader/ returns ZERO reads. It is write-only dead state on the read path — do not mistake its presence for DSN support.
- SECURITY-RELEVANT for the plan: the writer's node selection fails OPEN. An `X-CH-DSN` value matching no configured node does not error — writer/service/registry/static.go:64-67 falls through to a random preconfigured service. If the plan ever leans on X-CH-DSN for isolation (even as defence-in-depth behind label enforcement), a typo or a stale node name silently writes to an arbitrary node instead of failing. Label enforcement must remain the sole boundary, exactly as decision #2 states.
- reader/registry/registry.go:20-26 is a latent bug worth reporting upstream (not fixing here): the `DatabaseRegistryPlugin` result is assigned and then immediately clobbered because the `if` block lacks a `return`. If OpenPanel ever wanted to pursue a per-request registry via the plugin hook, this one-line upstream fix would be a prerequisite — which strengthens rather than weakens the plan's decision to avoid database-per-project.
- The reader's only auth is HTTP Basic (reader/reader.go:78-82, a single global username/password from QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD or CLOKI_LOGIN/CLOKI_PASSWORD, cmd/gigapipe/main.go:168-180). There is no per-project credential the reader could key off even if a registry wanted one. This independently supports plan decision #1 (gigapipe never exposed; every read through apps/api).
- Non-cluster deployments query UNQUALIFIED table names (reader/utils/tables/tables.go:72-95), so the effective database is whatever `clickhouse.Options.Auth.Database` was set to at boot. A per-signal retention scheme that needs a second database (or cross-database reads) has no read-path expression at all — relevant to the plan's conditional-TTL position on samples_v3.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan has to change. The claim's operative conclusion — database-per-project is impossible on gigapipe's read path without forking Go source — is correct, so decision #2 (label enforcement as the security boundary) stands, and decisions #1, #3, #4, #5 are unaffected. Three wording edits are warranted in the plan document: (a) state the reader binds at boot to a fixed connection pool selected at RANDOM per call with `ctx` ignored, rather than "a single database", since a config file can legally hold several DATABASE_DATA entries and a reader who checks will find that; (b) drop or heavily qualify "only its writer accepts a per-request DSN" — the writer's X-CH-DSN is a node-NAME lookup against preconfigured services with a silent random fallback, not an arbitrary DSN, so the writer cannot reach a new per-project database either, which makes the case against database-per-project stronger than the plan currently argues; (c) add a footnote that a dormant, currently-dead `DatabaseRegistryPlugin` hook exists, so a future reader of the plan does not "discover" it and reopen the decision — note that reader/registry/registry.go:20-26 discards it and that using it means forking gigapipe.

## Investigation 52 — `confirmed`

Every part of the claim holds in the source on disk. gigapipe's ruler evaluates only rules with a non-empty `Record` field — `evaluateInterval` and `evaluateRecordingRule` are gated on `rule.IsRecording()` (ruler/manager.go:213, ruler/model.go:19), and an alerting rule (non-empty `Alert`) is accepted by the write API and stored verbatim in the YAML blob but is never scheduled, never evaluated, never written back, and is filtered out of the `/api/v1/rules` Prometheus-format response (ruler/manager.go:269). There is no Alertmanager client, no `/api/v1/alerts` endpoint, and no alert-state machinery anywhere in the repo. The ruler is single-tenant (the `rules` table has no `org_id` by explicit design comment, and the controller reads no `X-Scope-OrgID`), and it is off by default behind `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED`, whose `Enabled()` gate causes `Init` to return before any route is registered, so the rule endpoints are unregistered and 404. Two further constraints the claim does not state: the ruler only boots in mode `all`/`""` (not in split reader-only or writer-only nodes), and recording rules themselves are global — there is no per-tenant scoping of rule storage or evaluation.

**Evidence**

- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/ruler.go:1-8` — Package doc states it outright: "Package ruler stores recording-rule groups and evaluates recording rules on a schedule... It is single-tenant and recording-only: alerting rules are stored but never evaluated."
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/model.go:5-21` — `Rule` has both `Record` and `Alert` fields; `func (r Rule) IsRecording() bool { return r.Record != "" }`. Comment: "Alerting rules (non-empty Alert) may be accepted and stored by the write API but are never evaluated, since Grafana no longer manages datasource alerting rules."
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/manager.go:203-222` — `evaluateInterval` iterates every group at the matching interval and calls `m.evaluateRecordingRule(...)` only inside `if rule.IsRecording() {`. An alerting rule is simply skipped — no state machine, no `For` handling, no pending/firing tracking. `Rule.For` is stored (model.go:12) but read nowhere in evaluation.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/manager.go:265-272` — `GetPrometheusRules` skips non-recording rules (`if !rule.IsRecording() { continue }`) and hardcodes `Type: "recording"`, so alerting rules stored in a group are invisible in the `/api/v1/rules` JSON.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/manager.go:160-176` — `pruneHealth` builds the valid-key set only from `rule.IsRecording()` rules — the health map, the only per-rule runtime state the manager keeps, has no slot for an alerting rule.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/router/init.go:28-36` — `Enabled()` reads `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED` and returns true only for "1", "true", "yes", "on" (case-insensitive, trimmed); anything else — including unset — is false. Default is therefore disabled.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/router/init.go:66-104` — `Init` starts `if !Enabled() { return }` at line 67, well before `Route(app, lokiCtrl, promCtrl)` at line 104. No rule route is ever registered when the flag is off, so the paths fall through to the router's not-found handling. Two further early returns (lines 70, 74) log an error and skip route registration if `writercontroller.DbClient` or `readerregistry.Registry` is nil, producing the same 404 even when the flag is on.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/router/router.go:1-40` — Package doc: "Alerting endpoints are intentionally absent: gigapipe stores but never evaluates alerting rules." Registered paths are exactly the CRUD surface on `/loki/api/v1/rules`, `/api/prom/rules`, `/api/v1/rules`, plus the debug `GET /prometheus/api/v1/rules`. No `/api/v1/alerts`, no `/rules/{ns}` alert-state route.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/controller/controller.go:1-4, 37-56` — Package doc: "It is recording-rule focused and single-tenant — no X-Scope-OrgID is read." `SetRuleGroup` yaml-unmarshals the posted group and hands it straight to `c.Store.SetRuleGroup` — there is no validation rejecting or stripping alerting rules, confirming "may be stored".
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/service.go:41-58` — `SetRuleGroup` marshals the whole `RuleGroup` (alerting rules included) to YAML into the `config` column: `INSERT INTO rules (namespace, group_name, config, updated_at, is_valid, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?, now(), 1, ?)`. The only scoping dimensions are namespace, group_name and type ("loki"/"prom").
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ctrl/qryn/sql/rules.sql:1-16` — DDL comment: "org_id is intentionally omitted: gigapipe is single-tenant, matching time_series/samples_v3 which carry no tenancy column." Table is `ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at) ORDER BY (namespace, group_name, type)` — no tenant column at all.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/docs/configuration.md:84-92` — "The ruler evaluates LogQL and PromQL recording rules on a schedule... It is single-tenant and recording-only (alerting rules may be stored but are never evaluated). It runs only in modes `all`/`""`" and "`QRYN_RULER_ENABLED` — ... (default: disabled). When disabled, the rule endpoints (`/api/v1/rules`, `/loki/api/v1/rules`, `/api/prom/rules`) are **not** served and return `404`."
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main.go:357-372` — `bootSequence`: the writer step runs in modes all/writer/"", reader in all/reader/"", but the ruler step is gated `if in("all", "")` — a reader-only or writer-only node never calls `rulerrouter.Init` regardless of the env var.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/cmd/gigapipe/main_test.go:110-124` — `TestBootSequenceModesScope` asserts `mode "reader" must not start the ruler` and `mode "writer" must not start the ruler`, locking that gating in.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/manager_test.go:91-112` — `TestEvaluateInterval_SkipsNonMatchingIntervalAndAlertingRules` feeds a group `{Alert: "Down", Expr: "up == 0"}` at the evaluated interval and asserts zero evaluator calls and zero writes: "alerting rules must never be written back".
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/controller/controller_test.go:133-159` — `TestPrometheusRules_RecordingOnlyJSON` posts a group holding both a recording and an alerting rule and asserts the `/api/v1/rules` body must NOT contain "Down" — "alerting rule must not appear".
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/writeback.go:15-40, 55-61` — Recording-rule results are written back in-process via `writerController.PushPromWriteRequest` as a `prompb.WriteRequest`; label precedence is sample labels, then `maps.Copy(merged, ruleLabels)` (rule labels win), then `merged["__name__"] = record` (record name wins over both). Nothing here emits or routes an alert.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/reader/router/prometheus_labels.go:24-25` — The reader deliberately does not register `/api/v1/rules`: "/api/v1/rules is owned by the ruler module (recording rules), which registers it when enabled" — so nothing else claims the path when the ruler is off.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe (repo-wide grep)` — `grep -rn "/api/v1/alerts|alertmanager|Alertmanager" --include=*.go .` returns zero hits. There is no alert notification, grouping, silencing, or dispatch code in the repository.

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- Imprecise wording, not an error: "the ruler" is actually two independent `RuleManager` instances built in ruler/router/init.go:91 and :100 — a Loki/LogQL one (evaluated through `readerservice.NewQueryRangeService` → instant LogQL) and a Prometheus/PromQL one (evaluated through a `promql.NewEngine` over `readerservice.CLokiQueriable`). Both are recording-only; they share one `rules` table discriminated by a `type` column ('loki' | 'prom').
- "404 when disabled" is true but the 404 does not come from the ruler — it comes from whatever handles an unregistered path. In a default build the gorilla/mux NotFoundHandler produces it; in a build with the `view` tag (view/static.go:11 sets `HaveStatic = true`), view.Init registers a catch-all `mux.PathPrefix("/")` file server (view/view.go:50) which returns 404 for the non-existent file. Either way the observable result is 404, so the claim is safe to rely on.
- The claim omits a second, independent gate: even with `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED=true`, the ruler is only wired in mode `all` or `""` (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:365-367). A split deployment running gigapipe as separate reader and writer processes gets no ruler and no rule endpoints at all.
- "Single-tenant" is stronger than the claim implies and cuts against the plan's isolation model: it is not just that there is no org header — the `rules` table has no tenancy column at all (ctrl/qryn/sql/rules.sql:5-6), and `GetAllRuleGroups` (ruler/service.go:141) selects every group of a type with no filter. Recording rules are global to the gigapipe instance.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- The plan's conclusion is right and the source is unusually explicit about it: three separate package/file doc comments (ruler/ruler.go:4-6, ruler/manager.go:53-55, ruler/router/router.go:2-3) and two dedicated tests (ruler/manager_test.go:91, ruler/controller/controller_test.go:133) all encode "recording-only, alerting stored but never evaluated" as an intentional invariant, not an unfinished feature. It will not silently change under gigapipe.
- Alerting rules being *storable* is a small footgun for OpenPanel: a POST of a rule group containing `alert:` entries is accepted with 202 and persisted forever (ruler/controller/controller.go:37-56 does no validation), yet the rule silently never fires and never appears in `GET /api/v1/rules`. If OpenPanel ever proxies rule CRUD, it should reject `alert:` at the gateway rather than let a user store a rule that looks accepted and does nothing.
- Recording rules are a second isolation hole the plan's label-enforcement model does not obviously cover. Rule storage is keyed only by `(namespace, group_name, type)` (ctrl/qryn/sql/rules.sql:16) with no project dimension, and `evaluateInterval` evaluates every stored rule expression as written. If OpenPanel ever exposes recording rules per project, the gateway must (a) namespace-prefix or otherwise partition `namespace`/`group_name` to prevent one project overwriting another's group under ReplacingMergeTree, and (b) inject `op_project_id` into the rule *expression*, since nothing in the ruler injects it — the evaluator is handed the raw expr string.
- Recording-rule write-back label precedence matters for that injection: ruler/writeback.go:24-27 applies sample labels first, then rule static `labels` on top, then forces `__name__`. So a static `op_project_id` label on the rule will override whatever the query produced — usable as a belt-and-braces stamp, but it will happily mislabel cross-project data if the expression itself was not scoped.
- Ruler startup is best-effort, not fatal: if the writer's ClickHouse client or the reader registry is nil, Init logs "Ruler enabled but ... not initialized; ruler not started" and returns without registering routes (ruler/router/init.go:70-77). A manager whose `Start` fails logs an error too (init.go:109-111) and boot continues. OpenPanel cannot infer ruler health from process liveness; if it depends on recording rules it needs its own probe (e.g. `GET /api/v1/rules` returning 200 with the expected groups).
- The ruler re-reads all rule groups from ClickHouse on *every* evaluation tick as well as every poll (`m.reader.GetAllRuleGroups` at ruler/manager.go:205 and :311), and creates one goroutine + ticker per distinct group interval (ruler/manager.go:140-155). At OpenPanel scale (many projects × many rules) that is a `SELECT ... FINAL` per interval per rule-type, which is a real load consideration if recording rules are ever offered per project.
- Git history shows the ruler is recent and lightly iterated — `git log --oneline -- ruler/` returns only three commits, the feature commit being 8161607 "feat(ruler): recording-rules ruler with in-process write-back (#843)". There is no earlier alerting implementation that was removed, and no version of the code on disk in which alerting was evaluated.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan has to change — the claim is load-bearing for \"alert evaluation must live in OpenPanel's worker\" and it is fully supported by source. Two refinements are worth folding into the P5 (alerts) and P0 (stack) docs. First, state the ruler's mode constraint alongside the env flag: the ruler is only wired when gigapipe runs in mode `all`/`""` (cmd/gigapipe/main.go:365-367), so if the P0 topology ever splits gigapipe into separate reader and writer processes, recording rules disappear entirely — an argument for keeping the single unified process, or for accepting that recording rules are not available in a split topology. Second, if any later phase offers per-project recording rules (as a materialization/cost optimization behind metric reports), treat rule storage as a THIRD place project isolation must be enforced by OpenPanel: the `rules` table has no tenancy column and `GetAllRuleGroups` filters only on rule type, so the gateway must both partition `namespace`/`group_name` per project (else ReplacingMergeTree collisions across projects) and inject `op_project_id` into the rule expression itself, exactly as the query compiler does — the ruler will not do it. Until then, the safe P0/P5 position is to leave `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED` unset (its default), which also removes the rule endpoints from the internal surface area entirely.

## Investigation 53 — `confirmed`

Every clause of the claim holds, and the first engineer's evidence exists and says what they say it says — I re-checked each cited file independently and found no misquote. Evaluation is gated on `rule.IsRecording()` (which is only `Record != ""`) at manager.go:213, the Prometheus read filters non-recording rules at manager.go:269, the `For` field is written but never read at evaluation (its only two uses in the whole package are a "0s"→"" normalization in service.go:46-47), and a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `alertmanager|/api/v1/alerts|notifier|silence` across all .go files returns zero hits. The `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED` gate and the mode `all`/`""` gate are both real and independent. The one place I'd sharpen the claim is the "404 when disabled" clause: it is true for the default `go build`, but the officially published container image is built with the `view` tag, where a catch-all file server matches the path instead — so the response passes through BasicAuthMiddleware and becomes 401 for an unauthenticated caller.

**Evidence**

**Corrections to the claim as stated**

- The "404 when disabled" clause is build-dependent in a way the first engineer flagged but understated. They wrote "in a build with the `view` tag" as a hypothetical; in fact the officially published image ghcr.io/metrico/gigapipe:latest is built with VIEW=1 (build_release.yml:209-213 → Dockerfile:5-6 → `-tags view`), so the view catch-all is the DEFAULT for anyone running the container. That matters beyond aesthetics: because gorilla/mux only composes `Use()` middleware onto a MATCHED route, the catch-all match means the request now traverses BasicAuthMiddleware. With QRYN_LOGIN/QRYN_PASSWORD set, an unauthenticated GET /api/v1/rules returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge (reader/utils/middleware/basic_auth.go:35-38), not 404; only an authenticated caller sees the file server's 404. In the plain `go build` (no view tag, and note the release BINARIES at build_release.yml:70/:133 are in this category because `VIEW=1` there is an ignored env var, not `-tags view`), no route matches, middleware never runs, and you get a clean unauthenticated 404. Practical consequence: OpenPanel must not probe for HTTP 404 to detect whether the ruler is enabled — the status code is a function of build tag and auth config, not ruler state.
- Minor imprecision in "alerting rules may be stored but are never evaluated": an alerting-only group still causes work. `updateRoutines` (manager.go:121-132) builds its interval set from every group regardless of rule kind, so a group containing only alerting rules spawns and keeps alive a `time.Ticker` goroutine at its interval. The ticker fires, `evaluateInterval` runs a full `GetAllRuleGroups` query, and evaluates nothing. Harmless correctness-wise, but it is not free.
- I could not verify the default value of `ClokiReader.ViewPath`. The `github.com/metrico/cloki-config` module is not present in the local module cache and is not vendored, so whether `view.Init`'s prefix resolves to "/" (swallowing every unregistered path) or to a narrower configured path is UNVERIFIED. The view.Init code path is confirmed; the breadth of its catch-all is not. This only affects the 401-vs-404 nuance above, not the substance of the claim.

**Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Recording rules are an isolation hole under the plan's label-enforcement model, and it is worse than "rules are global". writeback.go:27 applies `maps.Copy(merged, ruleLabels)` AFTER copying the sample's labels — the rule's static `labels:` block wins over whatever the query returned. So a rule author who writes `labels: {op_project_id: "victim-project"}` mints series attributed to another project, and those series are then indistinguishable to the query-time mandatory matcher, which is the plan's entire security boundary (decision 2). Symmetrically, a rule whose expr aggregates without `by (op_project_id)` writes series carrying NO op_project_id at all, which the mandatory matcher will then never return — silently invisible data. If OpenPanel ever surfaces recording-rule authoring to users, rule text must be compiled and label-enforced server-side exactly like queries are, not passed through.
- A rule group with a missing or unparseable `interval` is silently never evaluated. `time.ParseDuration("")` errors, so `updateRoutines` (manager.go:125-129) logs and skips the group, and `evaluateInterval` (manager.go:208-211) `continue`s past it. Prometheus and Loki both default a group's interval to a global evaluation interval when omitted; gigapipe has no such default. A group posted through the Loki-compatible API without an explicit `interval:` will be accepted with 202, appear in GET responses, and never run. If OpenPanel writes rule groups programmatically it must always emit an explicit interval.
- Read amplification on the rules table is significant and unbounded by rule count. `evaluateInterval` calls `GetAllRuleGroups` (a `SELECT ... FINAL` over the whole rules table for that type) on EVERY tick of EVERY interval routine — not once per tick across routines — and `pollForChanges` does the same every `QRYN_RULER_POLL_INTERVAL` (default 30s), and `GetPrometheusRules` does it again on every `/api/v1/rules` GET. With two managers (loki + prom) and k distinct intervals, that is 2×(k+1) FINAL scans per shortest interval, plus one per API poll. If OpenPanel's dashboard polls rule status, budget for it.
- `evaluateRecordingRule` evaluates against `m.ctx` (manager.go:226), the manager-level context, not the `ctx` that `evaluateInterval` was handed from the interval routine. Cancelling a single interval routine (which `updateRoutines` does when an interval stops being used, manager.go:137) will not cancel an in-flight evaluation started by it; only `RuleManager.Stop()` will. `Stop()` does `m.wg.Wait()` (manager.go:114) after cancelling, so shutdown blocks until every in-flight rule query finishes — relevant to the 30s `shutdownTimeout` in main.go, since ruler Stop runs at step 2 of graceful shutdown, before the writer flush.
- The write-back is in-process, not HTTP. `inProcessWriter.Write` calls `writerController.PushPromWriteRequest` directly (writeback.go:54-58), which is why the ruler hard-requires mode `all`/`""` — it needs the writer's ClickHouse client and insert registry in the same process (init.go:70-73, and the `bootSequence` doc comment at main.go:346-352 spells out the ordering dependency). This is a structural reason the ruler cannot be split out or scaled independently, reinforcing the plan's position that alert evaluation belongs in OpenPanel's worker rather than being coaxed out of gigapipe.
- Confirmed the OpenPanel side of the plan's proposed replacement path exists: packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:581 `model NotificationRule` and :599 `model Notification`. I did not trace the delivery path beyond the model declarations.

**Impact on the plan.** Nothing in the plan needs to change on account of this claim — the position that "gigapipe's ruler is recording-only, so alert evaluation must live in OpenPanel's worker" is correct and well-supported. Two adjustments to how the plan states and uses it: (1) drop any reliance on HTTP 404 as a ruler-availability probe; the status code is 401 or 404 depending on build tag and basic-auth config, so detect ruler state from OpenPanel's own configuration instead. (2) If P6 or later ever exposes recording rules to users, treat rule text and the rule's static `labels` block as untrusted input subject to the same op_project_id compilation as queries — writeback.go:27 lets a rule's static labels overwrite the query's, so a hand-written rule can forge project attribution, which would breach the plan's decision-2 security boundary from the write side rather than the read side. Also make any programmatic rule-group writer always emit an explicit `interval`, since gigapipe silently drops groups without one.

## Investigation 54 — `confirmed`

I re-derived the claim from the runtime path (boot sequence → Init gate → manager scheduling → the single Evaluate call site) rather than from the package docs, and every part of it holds. The decisive fact the first engineer did not surface is that `m.evaluator.Evaluate` has exactly one call site in the entire non-test tree — ruler/manager.go:226, inside `evaluateRecordingRule`, which is only reachable through the `if rule.IsRecording()` gate at manager.go:213. There is no other path by which a stored rule expression can be executed, and `Alert` appears in no production code anywhere except its struct-field declaration in ruler/model.go:10. The `QRYN_RULER_ENABLED` gate, the 404-when-disabled behavior, and single-tenancy all check out as described. Two things they got slightly loose and one thing nobody flagged: gigapipe's own Makefile and e2e compose default the flag to true; a group of only alerting rules disappears entirely from /api/v1/rules rather than being partially filtered; and alerting rules ARE returned verbatim by the YAML read endpoints, so "never evaluated" does not mean "never visible".

Verified with `grep -rn --include="*.go" "\.Evaluate(" . | grep -v vendor | grep -v _test`, which returns this one line. It sits inside `evaluateRecordingRule`, whose sole caller is manager.go:214 under `if rule.IsRecording()`. This is stronger proof than the IsRecording gates alone: there is no second execution path a stored alerting rule could take.
- `/Users/drew/projects/gigapipe/ruler/manager.go:213-215` — `evaluateInterval` loops `for _, rule := range g.Rules { if rule.IsRecording() { m.evaluateRecordingRule(...) } }`. No else branch, no `For` handling, no pending/firing state. Confirms the first engineer's citation.

Opt-in via QRYN_RULER_ENABLED; runs in mode all/\"\" after the writer and reader initialize." **Also found (not part of the claim, but affects the plan)**

- Alerting rules are stored AND readable, just not evaluated. The YAML read endpoints (controller.go:58-111) return the stored group verbatim, so a POSTed alerting rule reappears on GET /loki/api/v1/rules. If OpenPanel ever proxies gigapipe's ruler CRUD, a user (or Grafana's Loki ruler UI) can create an alert rule, see it listed, and reasonably believe it is armed — it will silently never fire. If the plan exposes ruler CRUD at all, it must reject rules with a non-empty `alert` at the OpenPanel gateway rather than relying on gigapipe to reject them; gigapipe does not.
- A group containing only alerting rules vanishes entirely from /api/v1/rules, not just its rules: ruler/manager.go:291 `if len(promRules) == 0 { continue }` drops the group after the per-rule filter. So the Prometheus-format view and the YAML view of the same storage can disagree about whether a group exists at all.
- gigapipe's own tooling defaults the flag ON: Makefile:5 `export QRYN_RULER_ENABLED ?= true` and scripts/test/e2e/docker-compose.yml:23 `${QRYN_RULER_ENABLED:-true}`. "Default disabled" is true of the binary only. Since the ruler routes carry no auth of their own (the only middleware is global — logging, CORS, accept-encoding, and optional HTTP basic auth at cmd/gigapipe/main.go:315-324), an accidentally-enabled ruler in OpenPanel's self-hosting compose would expose unauthenticated, untenanted rule CRUD on the internal service. The plan should state explicitly that QRYN_RULER_ENABLED must be unset/false, and that the compose template must not be copied from gigapipe's.
- The write-back path is untenanted at the storage layer: ruler/writeback.go:59 → writer/controller/recording_writeback.go:30,34 resolve insert services with an empty id, and writer/service/registry/static.go is the only registry implementation present, so recording-rule results always go to the boot-configured database. Combined with global rule storage (ruler/service.go:145-149, no filter), a recording rule is an instance-wide object whose output series carry only whatever labels the query itself produced. If OpenPanel ever uses gigapipe recording rules for per-project rollups, the op_project_id label survives only if the rule expression explicitly preserves it (e.g. `sum by (op_project_id) (...)`) — nothing in the ruler enforces it, and rule labels at writeback.go:26 can even OVERWRITE a sample's op_project_id. That makes ruler recording rules a hole in the label-enforcement security boundary, independent of the alerting question.
- Minor precision on the first engineer's note that `Rule.For` is "read nowhere in evaluation": it is read once, at store time — ruler/service.go:44-48 normalizes "0s"/"0" to "" before marshaling. Correct as they scoped it (evaluation), but `For` is not entirely dead.

**Impact on the plan.** No change to the plan's position that alert evaluation must live in OpenPanel's worker — that position is correct and the source supports it more strongly than the first engineer showed (a single evaluator call site, and `Alert` read by zero production lines). Two additions the plan should absorb: (1) gigapipe's ruler must be explicitly disabled in OpenPanel's compose template, because gigapipe's own Makefile and e2e compose default it to true and its rule routes have no per-tenant auth; (2) if any ruler CRUD is ever surfaced, OpenPanel must reject alerting rules at the gateway, since gigapipe accepts, stores and re-serves them while never firing them — a silent-failure footgun. Separately, recording rules are a genuine gap in the label-enforcement boundary (global storage, global evaluation, boot-configured write target, rule labels able to overwrite op_project_id), so if the plan later wants server-side rollups it should build them in OpenPanel's worker rather than delegating to gigapipe's ruler.
